D. Shock Strut Seal Leak Inspection

NOTE: If the inspection finds a fault on the scraper ring you will have to replace the damaged scraper ring. NOTE: The inner cylinder must be removed from the outer cylinder shock strut to replace the scraper ring. SUBTASK 32-11-21-480-021 WARNING MAKE SURE THAT THE DOWNLOCK PINS ARE INSTALLED IN ALL OF THE LANDING GEAR. WITHOUT THE DOWNLOCK PINS, THE LANDING GEAR CAN RETRACT AND CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT. (1) Make sure that the downlock pins are installed in the nose and main landing gear (PAGEBLOCK 32-00-01/201). EFFECTIVITY ALL SUBTASK 32-11-21-210-001 (2) Inspect the shock struts for leakage. NOTE: A small quantity of hydraulic fluid that is isolated to the movable surface of the inner cylinder is not leakage. SUBTASK 32-11-21-210-002 (3) If you find leakage of the shock strut fluid on the inner cylinder, do the steps that follow to make sure that the shock strut is serviceable: (a) Check for leaks for 5 minutes: 1) Wipe the surface of the inner cylinder with a clean cloth to remove all of the fluid from the leak. 2) Monitor the inner cylinder where it meets the outer cylinder for 5 minutes. NOTE: The extension of the inner cylinder must not change during this time. 3) Make a record of the location and the number of drops that come from the seals during the 5 minutes. (b) Jack the inner gear cylinder by the gear jack pad (TASK 07-11-01-580-815 or TASK 07-11-03-580-801) or tow the airplane (TASK 09-11-00-580-801) to cause movement between the inner cylinder and outer cylinder. NOTE: If towed, the minimum distance the airplane must be moved is two airplane lengths. (c) Check for leaks for 5 minutes: 1) Wipe the surface of the inner cylinder with a clean cloth to remove all of the fluid from the leak. 2) Monitor the inner cylinder where it meets the outer cylinder for 5 minutes. NOTE: The extension of the inner cylinder must not change during this time. 3) Make a record of the location and the number of drops that come from the seals during the 5 minutes. (d) Calculate the average of the number of drops that came from the seals during both of the 5 minute measurements. SUBTASK 32-11-21-210-003 (4) If the leakage stopped, do the steps that follow: (a) Continue to monitor the strut for leakage on subsequent landings. 1) If you see more signs of leakage, do the entire leak check procedure again. NOTE: If you find a continuous leakage flow on subsequent landings the shock strut is not serviceable. CAUTION IF THE AIRPLANE MADE A LANDING WITH A DEFLATED OR FLAT STRUT, DO THE HARD LANDING INSPECTION. MAKE SURE THAT NO DAMAGE OCCURRED. A DEFLATED OR FLAT STRUT CAN CAUSE DAMAGE DURING A LANDING. (b) If you do not find leakage on subsequent landings, examine the fluid level of the shock strut within 5 days or 15 flight cycles, do this task: Main Landing Gear Shock Strut Fluid Check, TASK 12-15-31-610-801. NOTE: If the leakage has stopped, there is no additional action necessary. EFFECTIVITY ALL 1) If the shock strut is deflated or flat, do this task: Phase IA Inspection, TASK 05-51-01-210-801. SUBTASK 32-11-21-210-004 (5) If there was leakage but the average was less than 50 drops during the two 5 minute periods, do the steps that follow: NOTE: 20 drops is equal to 1.0 cc. (a) Continue to monitor the strut for leakage on subsequent landings. 1) If the leakage continues or increases do the entire seal check procedure again. 2) Continue to monitor the fluid level of the shock strut at no more than 5 day or 15 flight cycle intervals, until you replace the seals (TASK 12-15-31-610-801). CAUTION IF THE AIRPLANE MADE A LANDING WITH A DEFLATED OR FLAT STRUT, DO THE HARD LANDING INSPECTION. MAKE SURE THAT NO DAMAGE OCCURRED. A DEFLATED OR FLAT STRUT CAN CAUSE DAMAGE DURING A LANDING. (b) If you do not find leakage on subsequent landings, examine the fluid level of the shock strut within 3 days or 10 flight cycles (TASK 12-15-31-610-801). NOTE: If the leakage has stopped and the fluid level is correct, there is no additional action necessary. 1) If the shock strut is deflated or flat, do this task: Phase IA Inspection, TASK 05-51-01-210-801. SUBTASK 32-11-21-210-005 (6) If the average leakage was more than 50 drops during the two 5 minute periods, but was not continuous, do the steps that follow: NOTE: 20 drops is equal to 1.0 cc. CAUTION IF THE AIRPLANE MADE A LANDING WITH A DEFLATED OR FLAT STRUT, DO THE HARD LANDING INSPECTION. MAKE SURE THAT NO DAMAGE OCCURRED. A DEFLATED OR FLAT STRUT CAN CAUSE DAMAGE DURING A LANDING. (a) Do this task: Main Landing Gear Shock Strut Servicing, Airplane on the Ground, TASK 12-15-31-610-802. 1) If the shock strut is deflated or flat, do this task: Phase IA Inspection, TASK 05-51-01-210-801. (b) Continue to monitor the fluid level of the shock strut after each flight until you replace the seals. SUBTASK 32-11-21-210-006 (7) If the fluid leaked continuously during the 5 minute period, the shock strut is not serviceable and you must replace the shock strut seals.

32-11-37-600-801CORROSION PREVENTIONPDF p. 379

2. CORROSION PREVENTION

A. Consumable Materials

Reference Description Specification G00009 Compound - Organic Corrosion Inhibiting BMS3-23

B. General Philosophy

SUBTASK 32-11-37-610-004 (1) The basic corrosion prevention philosophy is to make periodic inspections to preclude or detect the early stages of corrosion. Missing fasteners, white powdery or discolored deposits are evidence of the existence of corrosion which should alert operators that some corrective action is required. A corrosion prevention program should be initiated to prevent the accumulation of corrosive products in order to minimize the occurrence of corrosion. SUBTASK 32-11-37-210-001 (2) After the suspected areas are cleaned, a thorough inspection helps to ensure that protective finishes provided during manufacture remain intact. SUBTASK 32-11-37-210-002 (3) Where corrosion exists (noticeable bulges of the skin or white deposits of corrosion products at fastener heads of joint edges), refer to Structural Repair Manual for details of corrosion removal. SUBTASK 32-11-37-210-003 (4) For minor corrosion, to minimize the downtime of the airplane, the corrosion products should be cleaned off, followed by the application of a corrosion inhibiting compound into the affected area to slow the corrosion process. The finish system should be restored at the next maintenance opportunity.

C. Prevention Treatment

SUBTASK 32-11-37-610-001 (1) Do these steps for prevention treatment: (a) At the next maintenance opportunity, corrosion prevention treatment should be accomplished to the main landing gear. EFFECTIVITY ALL CAUTION DO NOT APPLY CORROSION INHIBITING COMPOUND ON GREASED JOINTS OR SEALED BEARINGS. THESE COMPOUNDS DISSOLVE GREASE AND OTHER LUBRICANTS. THEY ARE PENETRATING COMPOUNDS AND CAN GET AROUND THE SEALS AND INTO THE BEARINGS. (b) After application of corrosion inhibiting compound, G00009 all grease fittings in the treated areas should be regreased. NOTE: Apply corrosion inhibiting compound, G00009, to exposed outer surfaces only. Do not disassemble parts to apply the corrosion inhibiting compound. Do not spray into joints, linkages, pulleys, cables or bearings. (c) If you cleaned with high pressure water, apply the corrosion inhibitor again. NOTE: Make sure that the pressure of the water is not more than 50 psi. (d) Shock Struts (Oleo). Apply water displacing corrosion inhibiting compound, G00009 to exterior areas of the inner and outer cylinder with broken finish systems. All lugs, lug faces, connecting pin fasteners, and strut door attachments should be sprayed with corrosion inhibitor. (e) Axles. Apply water displacing corrosion inhibiting compound, G00009 to outside surfaces of the axles except journal and bearing surfaces. Make suitable nozzle extension and spray the inside surfaces of the axles with corrosion inhibiting compound, G00009 after protecting electrical wire and connectors. (f) Side Struts. Apply water displacing corrosion inhibiting compound, G00009 to surface areas with broken finish systems on both the upper and lower side struts. All lugs, lug faces, connecting pins and fasteners should be sprayed with corrosion inhibiting compound, G00009. (g) Walking Beam. Apply water displacing corrosion inhibiting compound, G00009 to surface areas with broken finish systems. (h) Door Hinges. Remove debris from recessed areas of door and apply water displacing corrosion inhibiting compound, G00009 to all hinge fittings. Relubricate hinge pins as necessary after application of corrosion inhibiting compound, G00009. (i) Miscellaneous. Lugs, lug faces and connecting pins of links, actuators and lock mechanisms connecting above mentioned components should also be sprayed with corrosion inhibiting compound, G00009. (j) The installation of mylar tape under corrosion resistant steel clamps is recommended at overhaul to minimize risk of galvanic corrosion should the finish be damaged.

D. Frequency of Application

SUBTASK 32-11-37-610-003 (1) Frequency of corrosion prevention application is as follows: (a) Periodic inspection is required to areas identified as susceptible to corrosion and should be consistent to the schedules identified in the Maintenance Planning Document. Operators must be aware of reported problems and areas of occurrence. (b) Annual application of corrosion inhibiting compound, G00009 is necessary to areas identified or as required by washing cycles.

EFFECTIVITY ALL SUBTASK 32-11-51-640-003 (3) Lubricate the chrome plated surfaces of the apex pin [31], lower torsion link pin [51], and cross bolt [52] with grease, D00633. SUBTASK 32-11-51-160-004 (4) Remove all unwanted grease, D00633. SUBTASK 32-11-51-080-002 (5) Remove the rope that holds the spacer [53] to the inner cylinder [47]. SUBTASK 32-11-51-420-010 (6) Connect the lower torsion link [22] to the inner cylinder [47]. (a) Put the lower torsion link [22] in its position on the inner cylinder [47]. (b) Put the lower torsion link pin [51] through the clevis on the inner cylinder [47] and spacer [53]. (c) Align the hole in the lower torsion link pin [51] with hole in the spacer [53] for the installation of the cross bolt [52]. (d) Put the cross bolt [52] through the spacer [53] and lower torsion link pin [51]. (e) Install the washer [50] and nut [49] on the cross bolt [52]. (f) Tighten the nut [49] to 160 in-lb (18 N·m) - 190 in-lb (21 N·m). (g) Install the cotter pin [48] in the cross bolt [52]. 1) If it is necessary, loosen the nut [49] to the nearest castellation to align the hole for the cotter pin [48]. SUBTASK 32-11-51-080-003 (7) Remove the rope that holds the upper torsion link [5] to the outer cylinder [33]. SUBTASK 32-11-51-420-011 (8) Connect the upper torsion link [5] and lower torsion link [22]. (a) Align the apex holes in the upper torsion link [5] and lower torsion link [22]. (b) Put the spacer [30] in its position between the upper torsion link [5] and lower torsion link [22]. (c) Put the apex pin [31] through the upper torsion link [5], spacer [30], and lower torsion link [22]. CAUTION MAKE SURE THAT YOU INSTALL THE SLEEVES IN THE CORRECT LOCATIONS. IF YOU INSTALL THE SLEEVES IN THE INCORRECT LOCATIONS, VIBRATION CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO COMPONENTS OF LANDING GEAR. (d) Install the tapered sleeve [54] in the lower torsion link [22], washer [29], bracket [28], and apex nut [24] on the apex pin [31]. NOTE: There may be a gap between the torsion link and apex joint. This condition is part of a normal shimmy damper installation. NOTE: The shimmy damper installation has a straight sleeve and tapered sleeve. The straight sleeve is longer than the tapered sleeve. (e) Tighten the apex nut [24] to 50 ft-lb (67.8 N·m) - 58 ft-lb (78.6 N·m). 1) Advance the apex nut [24] to the nearest castellation that aligns with the hole in the apex pin [31]. EFFECTIVITY ALL a) Make sure that the final torque is not more than 150 ft-lb (203 N·m). (f) Install the retention bolt [23] through the apex nut [24] and apex pin [31]. (g) Make sure that the electrical conduit and apex nut [24] do not contact one another. 1) Make sure that the electrical conduit is at an angle of 50 +0/-5 degrees from the bottom of the bracket [28]. 2) Make sure that the nut [55] is tightened to 70 ±5 in-lb (8 ±1 N·m). (h) Install the washers [25] and nut [27] on the bolt [23]. (i) Install the cotter pin [26] in the bolt [23]. 1) If it is necessary, loosen the nut [27] to the nearest castellation to align the hole for the cotter pin [26]. (j) Apply compound, A00226, to the nut [27] such that tampering must cause the seal to break. SUBTASK 32-11-51-420-020 (9) Do this task: Main Landing Gear Shimmy Damper Installation, TASK 32-11-81-400-801. SUBTASK 32-11-51-420-012 (10) Connect the bracket [42] and bracket [44] to the lower torsion link [22]. (a) Put bracket [42], bracket [44], and spacer [43] in their position on the lower torsion link [22]. (b) Install the washers [41] on the bolts [40]. (c) Put the bolts [40] through the bracket [42], spacer [43], lower torsion link [22], and bracket [44]. (d) Install the washers [45] and nuts [46] on the bolts [40]. F. Main Landing Gear Upper Side Strut Removal

SUBTASK 32-11-61-020-002 (1) Disconnect the upper side strut [3] from the downlock strut [1]. (a) Remove the pin [6] from the downlock link pin [2]. (b) Remove the nut [5] and the washer [4] from the downlock link pin [2]. (c) Remove the downlock link pin [2] to disconnect the upper side strut [3] from the downlock strut [1]. NOTE: Use the thread protector, C32029-13, SPL-1369, for the downlock link pin [2] when you do this step. SUBTASK 32-11-61-020-003 (2) Disconnect the upper side strut [3] from the lower side strut [8]. (a) Remove the cotter pin [13], nut [14], and washer [12] from the bolt [11]. (b) Remove the bolt [11] from the side strut pin [7]. (c) Use a rope to support the upper end of the lower side strut [8] and attach the rope to the outboard side of the reaction link assembly [15]. NOTE: The lower side strut weighs approximately 48.3 lb (21.91 kg). (d) Remove the end cap [9] from the side strut pin [7]. (e) Remove the side strut pin [7] to disconnect the upper side strut [3] from the lower side strut [8]. NOTE: Use the slug driver, C32029-11, SPL-1367, for the side strut pin [7] when you do this step. EFFECTIVITY ALL SUBTASK 32-11-61-020-004 (3) Disconnect the upper side strut [3] from the reaction link assembly [15]. (a) Remove the pin [19], nut [18], and washer [17] from the cross bolt [16]. (b) Remove the cross bolt [16] from the side strut pin [22]. (c) Remove the side strut nut [20], and the side strut washer [21] from the side strut pin [22]. NOTE: Use wrench adapter, C32029-3 or C32029-93, SPL-1359, to hold the head of the side strut pin [22] when you loosen the side strut nut [20]. (d) Remove the side strut pin [22] that holds the upper side strut [3] to the reaction link assembly [15]. NOTE: Use the thread protector, C32029-12 or C32029-101, SPL-1368, for the side strut pin [22] when you do this step. SUBTASK 32-11-61-020-007 (1) Disconnect the lower side strut [8] from the pushrod [41]. (a) Remove the cotter pin [55], nut [42], and washer [43] from the bolt [46]. 1) Discard the cotter pin [55]. EFFECTIVITY ALL (b) Remove the bolt [46], washer [44], and bushing [45] to disconnect the lower side strut [8] from the pushrod [41]. (c) Isolate the pushrod [41] from the lower side strut [8]. SUBTASK 32-11-61-480-004 (2) Use a rope to hold the pushrod [41] and the inner door in its position. SUBTASK 32-11-61-020-008 (3) Disconnect the lower side strut [8] from the shock strut [51]. (a) Remove the pin [49], nut [50], and washer [48] from the cross bolt [47]. (b) Remove the cross bolt [47] from the side strut pin [52]. (c) Remove the side strut nut [54] and the side strut washer [53] from the side strut pin [52]. (d) Remove the side strut pin [52] to disconnect the lower side strut [8] from the shock strut [51]. NOTE: Use the thread protector, C32029-14, SPL-1370, for the side strut pin [52] when you do this step. SUBTASK 32-11-61-020-009 (4) Disconnect the lower side strut [8] from the upper side strut [3]. (a) Remove the cotter pin [13], nut [14], and washer [12] from the bolt [11]. (b) Remove the bolt [11] from the side strut pin [7]. (c) Remove the end cap [9] from the side strut pin [7]. (d) Use a rope to support the upper end of the lower side strut [8] and attach the rope to the outboard side of the reaction link assembly [15]. NOTE: The lower side strut weighs approximately 48.3 lb (21.91 kg). (e) Remove the side strut pin [7] to disconnect the upper side strut [3] from the lower side strut [8]. SUBTASK 32-11-61-020-016 (5) Carefully lower and remove the lower side strut [8] from the airplane. NOTE: The lower side strut [8] weighs approximately 48.3 lb (21.91 kg).

(n) Install the new pin [49] in the cross bolt [47]. 1) Make sure that the pin [49] is installed in accordance with the type B preferred installation method (TASK 20-10-44-400-801). WARNING USE NITRILE GLOVES FOR SKIN PROTECTION WHEN YOU USE COR￾BAN 27L. IF IT GETS ON YOUR SKIN, IMMEDIATELY REMOVE IT WITH WATER. IF THIS MATERIAL GETS IN YOUR EYES, IMMEDIATELY FLUSH YOUR EYES WITH WATER. GET MEDICAL AID. THIS MATERIAL CONTAINS FLAMMABLE AGENTS WHICH CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONNEL. (o) Check the interior of side strut pin [52] and repair the application of corrosion preventive Cor-Ban 27L Compound, G50237, as required. SUBTASK 32-11-61-080-002 (7) Remove the rope that holds the pushrod [41] in its position. SUBTASK 32-11-61-420-007 (8) Connect the lower side strut [8] to the pushrod [41]. (a) Lubricate the shank of the bolt [46] and bushing [45] with grease, D00633. (b) Remove all unwanted grease, D00633. (c) Align the hole in the pushrod [41] with the hole in the lower side strut [8]. (d) Put the bushing [45] through the lower side strut [8] and the pushrod [41]. (e) Install the washer [44] on the bolt [46]. (f) Put the bolt [46] through the lower side strut [8] and the pushrod [41]. (g) Install the washer [43] and nut [42] on the bolt [46]. (h) Hand tighten the nut [42] until after final adjustments to the doors are made in the subsequent steps. EFFECTIVITY ALL SUBTASK 32-11-61-820-001 (9) If the length of pushrod [41] is changed, do the step that follows: NOTE: No adjustment to the doors is necessary if the pushrod was not changed. (a) Do this task: Main Landing Gear Shock Strut Door Adjustment, TASK 32-13-11-820-801. SUBTASK 32-11-61-420-015 (10) Tighten the nut [42]. (a) Install the new cotter pin [55] in the hole of the bolt [46]. (b) If it is necessary, loosen the nut [42] to the nearest castellation to align the holes for the cotter pin [55].

I. Put the Airplane Back to Its Usual Condition

SUBTASK 32-11-61-420-013 (1) Do this task: Main Gear Downlock Spring Installation, TASK 32-32-91-400-801. SUBTASK 32-11-61-640-002 (2) Lubricate the lube fittings on the lower side strut, do this task: Main Landing Gear Upper End Components Servicing, TASK 12-21-11-640-801. SUBTASK 32-11-61-780-003 (3) For hydraulic system A, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Pressurization, TASK 29-11-00-860-801. SUBTASK 32-11-61-710-006 (4) Do this task: Main Landing Gear Operational Test, TASK 32-32-00-710-801. NOTE: It is optional to perform the Main Landing Gear Test - Component Replacement, TASK 32-32-00-710-802 instead of the operational test if a hydraulic cart is not available. SUBTASK 32-11-61-580-007 (5) Do this task: Lower the Airplane Off the Jacks, TASK 07-11-01-580-816.

F. Main Landing Gear Side Strut Removal

SUBTASK 32-11-61-020-011 (1) Disconnect the upper side strut [3] from the downlock strut [1]. (a) Remove the pin [6] from the downlock link pin [2]. (b) Remove the nut [5] and the washer [4] from the downlock link pin [2]. EFFECTIVITY ALL (c) Remove the downlock link pin [2] to disconnect the upper side strut [3] from the downlock strut [1]. NOTE: Use the thread protector, C32029-13, SPL-1369, for the downlock link pin [2] when you do this step. SUBTASK 32-11-61-020-012 (2) Disconnect the lower side strut [8] from the pushrod [41]. (a) Remove the cotter pin [55], nut [42], and washer [43] from the bolt [46]. 1) Discard the cotter pin [55]. (b) Remove the bolt [46], washer [44], and bushing [45] to disconnect the lower side strut [8] from the pushrod [41]. (c) Isolate the pushrod [41] from the lower side strut [8]. SUBTASK 32-11-61-480-007 (3) Use a rope to hold the pushrod [41] and the inner door in its position. SUBTASK 32-11-61-020-013 (4) Disconnect the lower side strut [8] from the shock strut [51]. (a) Remove the pin [49], nut [50], and washer [48] from the cross bolt [47]. (b) Remove the cross bolt [47] from the side strut pin [52]. (c) Remove the side strut nut [54] and the side strut washer [53] from the side strut pin [52]. (d) Remove the side strut pin [52] to disconnect the lower side strut [8] from the shock strut [51]. NOTE: Use the thread protector, C32029-14, SPL-1370, for the side strut pin when you do this step. SUBTASK 32-11-61-020-014 (5) Disconnect the upper side strut [3] from the reaction link assembly [15]. (a) Remove the pin [19], nut [18], and washer [17] from the cross bolt [16]. (b) Remove the cross bolt [16] from the side strut pin [22]. (c) Remove the side strut nut [20] and the side strut washer [21] from the side strut pin [22]. NOTE: Use wrench adapter, C32029-3 or C32029-93, SPL-1359, to hold the head of the side strut pin [22] when you loosen the side strut nut [20]. (d) Remove the side strut pin [22] that holds the upper side strut [3] to the reaction link assembly [15]. NOTE: Use the thread protector, C32029-12 or C32029-101, SPL-1368, for the side strut pin when you do this step. SUBTASK 32-11-61-020-015 (6) Remove the assembly of the upper side strut [3] and the lower side strut [8] from the airplane. NOTE: The side strut assembly weighs approximately 90.11 lb (40.87 kg).

H. Main Landing Gear Side Strut Installation

SUBTASK 32-11-61-420-008 (1) Connect the upper side strut [3] to the reaction link assembly [15]. (a) Lubricate the chrome plated surfaces of the side strut pin [22] with the grease, D00633. (b) Remove all unwanted grease, D00633. (c) Put the upper side strut [3] in its position for connection to the reaction link assembly [15]. CAUTION MAKE SURE THAT THE HEAD OF THE PIN POINTS IS IN THE FORWARD DIRECTION. IF THE HEAD OF THE PIN POINTS IS IN AFT DIRECTION, DAMAGE TO COMPONENTS AND THE AIRPLANE STRUCTURE WILL OCCUR. (d) Put the side strut pin [22] through the upper side strut [3] and reaction link assembly [15]. 1) Make sure that the head of the side strut pin [22] points in the forward direction. a) Use a thread protector, C32029-12 or C32029-101, SPL-1368, for the side strut pin. WARNING USE NITRILE GLOVES FOR SKIN PROTECTION WHEN YOU USE COR￾BAN 27L. IF IT GETS ON YOUR SKIN, IMMEDIATELY REMOVE IT WITH WATER. IF THIS MATERIAL GETS IN YOUR EYES, IMMEDIATELY FLUSH YOUR EYES WITH WATER. GET MEDICAL AID. THIS MATERIAL CONTAINS FLAMMABLE AGENTS WHICH CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONNEL. CAUTION DO NOT APPLY CORROSION-INHIBITING COMPOUND ON GREASE JOINTS, OR SEALED BEARINGS. THESE COMPOUNDS REMOVE GREASE AND OTHER LUBRICANTS. THEY ARE PENETRATING COMPOUNDS. THEY WILL MOVE AROUND THE SEALS AND INTO THE BEARINGS. THIS WILL CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE BEARINGS, AND JOINTS. (e) Apply a thin layer of the corrosion preventive Cor-Ban 27L Compound, G50237, or corrosion inhibiting material, G50136, to these items: 1) Do not apply corrosion preventive compound to the chrome plated surfaces. 2) The threads and thread reliefs of the side strut pin [22] and cross bolt [16]. 3) The threads of the side strut nut [20] and nut [18]. 4) The faces of the side strut washer [21] and washer [17]. (f) Remove all unwanted corrosion preventive Cor-Ban 27L Compound, G50237. (g) Install the side strut washer [21] and side strut nut [20] on the side strut pin [22]. EFFECTIVITY ALL (h) Tighten the side strut nut [20] to 600 in-lb (67.8 N·m) - 900 in-lb (101.7 N·m). 1) Use a wrench adapter, C32029-3 or C32029-93, SPL-1359, to hold the head of the side strut pin when you tighten the side strut nut. (i) If it is necessary, loosen the side strut nut [20] to the nearest castellation to align the hole for the cross bolt [16]. (j) Install the cross bolt [16] in the side strut pin [22]. (k) Install the washer [17] and nut [18] on the cross bolt [16]. (l) Tighten the nut [18] to 30 in-lb (3.4 N·m) - 50 in-lb (5.6 N·m). (m) If it is necessary, loosen the nut [18] to the nearest castellation to align the holes for the new pin [19]. (n) Install the new pin [19] in the cross bolt [16]. SUBTASK 32-11-61-420-009 (2) Connect the lower side strut [8] to the shock strut [51]. (a) Lubricate the chrome plated surfaces of the side strut pin [52] with grease, D00633. (b) Remove all unwanted grease, D00633. (c) Put the lower side strut [8] in its position for attachment to the shock strut [51]. (d) Put the side strut pin [52] through the lower side strut [8] and clevis on the shock strut [51]. 1) Use a thread protector, C32029-14, SPL-1370, for the side strut pin. WARNING USE NITRILE GLOVES FOR SKIN PROTECTION WHEN YOU USE COR￾BAN 27L. IF IT GETS ON YOUR SKIN, IMMEDIATELY REMOVE IT WITH WATER. IF THIS MATERIAL GETS IN YOUR EYES, IMMEDIATELY FLUSH YOUR EYES WITH WATER. GET MEDICAL AID. THIS MATERIAL CONTAINS FLAMMABLE AGENTS WHICH CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONNEL. CAUTION DO NOT APPLY CORROSION-INHIBITING COMPOUND ON GREASE JOINTS, OR SEALED BEARINGS. THESE COMPOUNDS REMOVE GREASE AND OTHER LUBRICANTS. THEY ARE PENETRATING COMPOUNDS. THEY WILL MOVE AROUND THE SEALS AND INTO THE BEARINGS. THIS WILL CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE BEARINGS, AND JOINTS. (e) Apply a thin layer of the corrosion preventive Cor-Ban 27L Compound, G50237, or corrosion inhibiting material, G50136, to these items: 1) Do not apply corrosion preventive compound to the chrome plated surfaces. 2) The threads and thread reliefs of the side strut pin [52] and cross bolt [47]. 3) The threads of the side strut nut [54] and nut [50]. 4) The faces of the side strut washer [53] and washer [48]. (f) Remove all unwanted corrosion preventive Cor-Ban 27L Compound, G50237. (g) Install the side strut washer [53] and side strut nut [54] on the side strut pin [52]. (h) Tighten the side strut nut [54] to 95 ft-lb (128.8 N·m) – 115 ft-lb (155.9 N·m). 1) Use a wrench adapter, C32029-39 or C32029-95, SPL-1361, to hold the head of the side strut pin when you tighten the side strut nut. EFFECTIVITY ALL CAUTION MAKE SURE THAT YOU INSTALL THE CROSS BOLT WITH THE BOLT HEAD INBOARD. A CHAFF DAMAGE CAN OCCUR TO THE SHEATHING ON THE CABLE OF THE GROUND SPOILER INTERLOCK IF THE COTTER PIN END OF THE BOLT IS INBOARD. (i) Install the cross bolt [47] with the bolt head inboard in the side strut pin [52]. 1) Make sure that the bolt head points inboard. NOTE: Pin can interfere with ground spoiler interlock valve cable and cause premature failure of the cable. (j) If it is necessary, loosen the side strut nut [54] to the nearest castellation to align the hole for the cross bolt [47]. (k) Install the washer [48] and nut [50] on the cross bolt [47]. (l) Tighten the nut [50] to 20 in-lb (2.3 N·m) - 24 in-lb (2.7 N·m) more than the run on torque. (m) If it is necessary, loosen the nut [50] to the nearest castellation to align the hole for the new pin [49]. CAUTION MAKE SURE THAT THE COTTER PIN IS INSTALLED CORRECT. A CHAFF CONDITION CAN OCCUR TO THE SHEATHING ON THE CABLE OF THE GROUND SPOILER INTERLOCK. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY, DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR. (n) Install the new pin [49] in the cross bolt [47]. 1) Make sure that the pin [49] is installed in accordance with the type B preferred installation method (TASK 20-10-44-400-801). (o) Check the interior of side strut pin [52] and reapply corrosion preventive Cor-Ban 27L Compound, G50237, as required. C. General

SUBTASK 32-11-61-200-002 (1) This task gives the maximum design and wear clearances for the side strut assembly for the main landing gear. NOTE: A certain amount of free play is allowable as a result of design tolerances for all joints on the side strut assembly.

(a) Make sure the all joints on the side strut assembly for the main landing gear are within the maximum design or wear clearances. (b) If the joint exceeds the maximum wear clearance then replace or repair the applicable part. 32-11-62-000-801Main Landing Gear Side Brace Assembly RemovalPDF p. 451

2. Main Landing Gear Side Brace Assembly Removal (Figure 401 and Figure 402)

A. General

(1) This task gives the instructions to remove the Main Landing Gear (MLG) side strut assembly along with the MLG reaction link assembly. (2) The MLG side strut assembly along with the MLG reaction link assembly is referred to as the MLG side brace assembly.

B. References

Tool part numbers that are replaced or non-procurable are preceded by "Opt:", which stands for Optional. D. Location Zones

Zone Area 133 Main Landing Gear Wheel Well, Body Station 663.75 to Body Station 727.00 - Left 134 Main Landing Gear Wheel Well, Body Station 663.75 to Body Station 727.00 - Right 713 Nose Landing Gear 734 Left Main Landing Gear 744 Right Main Landing Gear

E. Prepare for the Removal

SUBTASK 32-11-62-480-001 WARNING MAKE SURE THAT THE DOWNLOCK PINS ARE INSTALLED ON ALL THE LANDING GEAR. WITHOUT THE DOWNLOCK PINS, THE LANDING GEAR COULD RETRACT AND CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT. (1) If the downlock pins are not installed on all the landing gear, do this task: Landing Gear Downlock Pins Installation, TASK 32-00-01-480-801. SUBTASK 32-11-62-580-001 (2) Do this task: Lift the Airplane with the Jacks, TASK 07-11-01-580-815. SUBTASK 32-11-62-860-001 (3) Remove the power from the hydraulic systems A and B, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Power Removal, TASK 29-11-00-860-805. SUBTASK 32-11-62-860-002 (4) Remove the pressure from the hydraulic reservoirs, do this task: Hydraulic Reservoirs Depressurization, TASK 29-09-00-860-802 or Hydraulic Reservoirs Depressurization, TASK 29-09-00-860-808.

F. Main Landing Gear Side Brace Assembly Removal

SUBTASK 32-11-62-020-001 (1) Do these steps to disconnect the lower side strut [2] from the pushrod [3]. (a) Remove the nut [4] and washer [5] from the bolt [8]. (b) Remove the bolt [8], washer [6], and bushing [7] to disconnect the lower side strut [2] from the pushrod [3]. (c) Isolate the pushrod [3] from the lower side strut [2]. (d) Use a rope to hold the pushrod [3] and the inner door in its position. SUBTASK 32-11-62-020-002 (2) Do these steps to disconnect the lower side strut [2] from the shock strut [13]. (a) Remove the cotter pin [11], nut [12], and washer [10] from the cross bolt [9]. (b) Remove the cross bolt [9] from the side strut pin [14]. (c) Remove the side strut nut [16] and side strut washer [15] from the side strut pin [14]. (d) Remove the side strut pin [14] to disconnect the lower side strut [2] from the shock strut [13]. NOTE: Use the thread protector, C32029-14, SPL-1370, for the side strut pin [14] when you do this step. (e) Use the strap assembly to temporarily hold lower side strut [2] in its position. EFFECTIVITY ALL SUBTASK 32-11-62-480-003 (3) Do these steps to install the strut support assembly to the side brace assembly [1]. NOTE: The strut support assembly is part of the side strut dolly, SPL-19644. For installation instructions, refer to the tool placard. (a) Install the protective pad on the lower side strut [2]. (b) Use the transportation equipment, SPL-8264 to lift the strut support assembly into position under the side brace assembly [1]. 1) Install the ball lock pins to lock the strut support assembly. NOTE: The two side ball lock pins lock the strut support assembly to the transportation equipment, SPL-8264. The top ball lock pin locks the rotation of the strut support assembly. You can remove the top ball lock pin to rotate the strut support assembly. 2) If the strut support assembly is installed on the cart assembly, remove the thumb screws before you lift the strut support assembly away from the cart assembly. NOTE: Do not lift the cart assembly with the strut support assembly. (c) Secure the side brace assembly [1] to the strut support assembly. 1) Install the strap assembly that holds the side brace assembly [1] to the strut support assembly. 2) Tighten the swivel screws that secure the side brace assembly [1] to the strut support assembly. SUBTASK 32-11-62-020-003 (4) Do these steps to disconnect the reaction link assembly [17] from the trunnion [18]: (a) Remove the cotter pin [23], nut [22], and washer [21] from the cross bolt [19]. (b) Remove the cross bolt [19] from the trunnion pin [20]. (c) Remove the end cap [24] from the trunnion pin [20]. (d) Remove the trunnion pin [20] that attaches the reaction link assembly [17] to the trunnion [18]. 1) Use the slug driver assy, C32029-8, SPL-1364, when you do this task. SUBTASK 32-11-62-020-008 (5) Remove and discard the lockwire from the electrical harnesses [26]. SUBTASK 32-11-62-020-004 (6) Disconnect the electrical harnesses [26]. SUBTASK 32-11-62-020-005 (7) Do these steps to disconnect the hydraulic line [28] and hydraulic line [28A] from the hydraulic tubes [27]: (a) Disconnect the hydraulic line [28] and hydraulic line [28A] from the hydraulic tubes [27]. (b) Install caps on the hydraulic line [28] and hydraulic line [28A]. (c) Put tags on the hydraulic line [28] and hydraulic line [28A] to prevent the crossing of the lines during the installation. (d) Install caps on the hydraulic tubes [27]. SUBTASK 32-11-62-020-006 (8) Do these steps to remove the hanger link assembly [29] from the supporting structure: (a) Remove the cotter pin [30], nut [31], and washer [32] from the cross bolt [33]. EFFECTIVITY ALL (b) Remove the cross bolt [33] from the hanger link assembly pin [36]. (c) Remove the nut [34] and washer [35] from the hanger link assembly pin [36] with wrench adapter, C32029-31 or C32029-99, SPL-11946. (d) Remove the hanger link assembly pin [36] and bushing [37] that attaches the hanger link assembly [29] to the supporting structure. (e) Use the strap assembly to hold lower side strut [2] to the hanger link assembly [29]. SUBTASK 32-11-62-020-007 (9) Use the transportation equipment, SPL-8264 to lower the strut support assembly along with the side brace assembly [1] into position on the cart assembly. (a) If it is necessary, disconnect the lower end of the support rod [50] and support rod [51] from the wheel well structure. 1) Remove the bolt [52], washer [53], bushing [54], washer [55], and nut [56]. (b) Install the top ball lock pin to lock the rotation of the strut support assembly. (c) Install the thumb screws to secure the strut support assembly to the cart assembly. (d) Remove the two side ball lock pins. NOTE: The two side ball lock pins lock the strut support assembly to the transportation equipment, SPL-8264. (e) Remove the transportation equipment, SPL-8264.

3. Main Landing Gear Side Brace Assembly Installation (Figure 401 and Figure 402)

F. Prepare for the Installation

SUBTASK 32-11-62-480-004 WARNING MAKE SURE THE DOWNLOCK PINS ARE INSTALLED ON ALL THE LANDING GEAR. WITHOUT THE DOWNLOCK PINS, THE LANDING GEAR COULD RETRACT AND CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONNEL AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT. G. Main Landing Gear Side Brace Assembly Installation

SUBTASK 32-11-62-480-005 CAUTION BE CAREFUL WHEN YOU MOVE THE SIDE BRACE ASSEMBLY INTO ITS POSITION. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY, DAMAGE TO THE COMPONENTS CAN OCCUR. (1) Use the transportation equipment, SPL-8264 to lift the strut support assembly along with the side brace assembly [1] into position on the MLG. NOTE: The strut support assembly is part of the side strut dolly, SPL-19644. For installation instructions, refer to the tool placard. (a) If not already done, install the protective pad on the lower side strut [2]. (b) If not already done, secure the side brace assembly [1] to the strut support assembly. 1) Install the strap assembly to hold the side brace assembly [1] to the strut support assembly. 2) Tighten the swivel screws to secure the side brace assembly [1] to the strut support assembly. (c) Install the ball lock pins to lock the strut support assembly. NOTE: The two side ball lock pins lock the strut support assembly to the transportation equipment, SPL-8264. The top ball lock pin locks the rotation of the strut support assembly. You can remove the top ball lock pin to rotate the strut support assembly. EFFECTIVITY ALL (d) If the strut support assembly is installed on the cart assembly, remove the thumb screws before you lift the strut support assembly away from the cart assembly. NOTE: Do not lift the cart assembly with the strut support assembly. SUBTASK 32-11-62-420-001 (2) Do these steps to connect the reaction link assembly [17] to the trunnion [18]: (a) Lubricate the chrome plated surfaces of the trunnion pin [20] and the end cap [24] with grease, D00633. (b) Position the outboard end of the reaction link assembly [17] for attachment to the trunnion [18]. (c) Put the trunnion pin [20] through the reaction link assembly [17] and the trunnion [18]. (d) Install the end cap [24] on the trunnion pin [20]. (e) Put the cross bolt [19] through the trunnion pin [20] and the end cap [24]. (f) Apply a thin layer of the corrosion preventive Cor-Ban 27L Compound, G50237, (preferred) or corrosion inhibiting material, G50136, (alternate) to these items: 1) Do not apply corrosion preventive compound to the chrome plated surfaces. 2) The threads and thread reliefs of the cross bolt [19]. 3) The threads of the nut [22]. 4) The faces of the washer [21]. (g) Remove all unwanted corrosion preventive Cor-Ban 27L Compound, G50237. (h) Install the washer [21] and nut [22] on the cross bolt [19]. (i) If it is necessary, loosen the nut [22] to the nearest castellation that aligns with the hole for the cotter pin [23]. (j) Install the cotter pin [23] in the cross bolt [19]. SUBTASK 32-11-62-420-003 (4) Do these steps to connect the hydraulic line [28] and hydraulic line [28A] to the hydraulic tubes [27]: (a) Remove the caps from the hydraulic line [28], hydraulic line [28A] and hydraulic tubes [27]. (b) Connect the hydraulic line [28] and hydraulic line [28A] to the hydraulic tubes [27]. (c) Torque the hydraulic line [28] to 140 ±7 in-lb (16 ±1 N·m). (d) Torque the hydraulic line [28A] to 270 ±14 in-lb (31 ±2 N·m). (e) Remove the tags from the hydraulic line [28] and hydraulic line [28A]. (b) Remove all unwanted grease, D00633. (c) Put the lower side strut [2] in its position for attachment to the shock strut [13]. SUBTASK 32-11-62-420-005 (8) Do these steps to tighten the fasteners at the hanger link assembly pin [36]: (a) Use wrench adapter, C32029-31 or C32029-99, SPL-11946, to hold hanger link assembly pin [36] to tighten nut [34]. (b) Torque the nut [34] to 95 ft-lb (128.80 N·m) – 115 ft-lb (155.92 N·m) and loosen the nut to align the nearest castellation if it is necessary. (c) Install the cross bolt [33] in the hanger link assembly pin [36]. EFFECTIVITY ALL (d) Install the nut [31] and washer [32] to the cross bolt [33]. (e) Torque the nut [31] to 20 in-lb (2.3 N·m) – 24 in-lb (2.7 N·m) above run-on torque. (f) If it is necessary, loosen the nut [31] to the nearest castellation that aligns with the hole for the cotter pin [30]. (g) Install the cotter pin [30] in the cross bolt [33]. SUBTASK 32-11-62-420-006 (9) Do these steps to tighten the fasteners at the side strut pin [14]: (a) Torque the side strut nut [16] to 95 ft-lb (128.80 N·m) – 115 ft-lb (155.92 N·m). NOTE: Use the wrench adapter, C32029-39 or C32029-95, SPL-1361, to hold the head of the side strut pin [14] when you tighten the side strut nut [16]. (b) If it is necessary, loosen the side strut nut [16] to the nearest castellation to align the hole for the cross bolt [9]. (c) Install the cross bolt [9] with the bolt head inboard in the side strut pin [14]. 1) Make sure that the bolt head points inboard. NOTE: Pin can interfere with Ground Spoiler Interlock Valve Cable and cause premature failure of the cable. (d) Install the washer [10] and nut [12] on the cross bolt [9]. (e) Torque the nut [12] to 20 in-lb (2.26 N·m) – 24 in-lb (2.71 N·m) more than the run-on torque. (f) If it is necessary, loosen the nut [12] to the nearest castellation to align the hole for the cotter pin [11]. CAUTION MAKE SURE THAT THE COTTER PIN IS INSTALLED CORRECT. A CHAFF CONDITION CAN OCCUR TO THE SHEATHING ON THE CABLE OF THE GROUND SPOILER INTERLOCK. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY, DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR. (g) Install the cotter pin [11] in the cross bolt [9]. 1) Make sure that you install the cotter pin [11] in accordance with TASK 20-10-44-400-801. (b) Loosen the swivel screws that secure the side brace assembly [1] to the strut support assembly. SUBTASK 32-11-62-080-002 (11) Use the transportation equipment, SPL-8264 to lower the strut support assembly into position on the cart assembly. (a) Install the top ball lock pin to lock the rotation of the strut support assembly. (b) Install the thumb screws to secure the strut support assembly to the cart assembly. (c) Remove the two side ball lock pins. NOTE: The two side ball lock pins lock the strut support assembly to the transportation equipment, SPL-8264. EFFECTIVITY ALL (d) Remove the transportation equipment, SPL-8264. SUBTASK 32-11-62-420-009 (12) If removed, connect the lower end of the support rod [50] and support rod [51] from the wheel well structure. (a) Install the bolt [52], washer [53], bushing [54], washer [55], and nut [56]. SUBTASK 32-11-62-420-008 (13) Do these steps to connect the lower side strut [2] to the pushrod [3]: (a) Remove the rope that holds the pushrod [3] in its position. (b) Lubricate the nut [4], washer [5], and bolt [8] with grease, D00633. (c) Remove all unwanted grease, D00633. (d) Align the hole in the pushrod [3] with the hole in the lower side strut [2]. (e) Put the bushing [7] through the lower side strut [2] and the pushrod [3]. (f) Install the washer [6] on the bolt [8]. (g) Put the bolt [8] through the lower side strut [2] and the pushrod [3]. (h) Install the washer [5] and nut [4] on the bolt [8]. (i) Hand tighten the nut [4] until after final adjustments to the doors are made in the subsequent steps. SUBTASK 32-11-62-820-001 (14) If you changed the length of pushrod [3], do the step that follows: NOTE: No adjustment to the doors is necessary if the pushrod was not changed. (a) Do this task: Main Landing Gear Shock Strut Door Adjustment, TASK 32-13-11-820-801.

H. Put the Airplane Back to Its Usual Condition

SUBTASK 32-11-62-640-001 (1) Lubricate the lube fittings on the MLG side brace assembly, do this task: Main Landing Gear Upper End Components Servicing, TASK 12-21-11-640-801. SUBTASK 32-11-62-860-004 (2) For hydraulic system A, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Pressurization, TASK 29-11-00-860-801. SUBTASK 32-11-62-710-001 (3) Do this task: Main Landing Gear Operational Test, TASK 32-32-00-710-801. NOTE: It is optional to perform the Main Landing Gear Test - Component Replacement, TASK 32-32-00-710-802 instead of the operational test if a hydraulic cart is not available. SUBTASK 32-11-62-790-001 (4) Do a check of the hydraulic connections for leakage. SUBTASK 32-11-62-580-002 (5) Do this task: Lower the Airplane Off the Jacks, TASK 07-11-01-580-816.

D. Prepare for the Removal

SUBTASK 32-11-71-480-001 WARNING MAKE SURE THE DOWNLOCK PINS ARE INSTALLED ON ALL THE LANDING GEAR. WITHOUT THE DOWNLOCK PINS, THE LANDING GEAR CAN RETRACT AND CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT. (1) If the downlock pins are not installed on all the landing gear, do this task: Landing Gear Downlock Pins Installation, TASK 32-00-01-480-801. SUBTASK 32-11-71-580-002 (2) Do this task: Lift the Airplane with the Jacks, TASK 07-11-01-580-815. SUBTASK 32-11-71-860-005 (3) Remove the power from the hydraulic systems A and B, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Power Removal, TASK 29-11-00-860-805. SUBTASK 32-11-71-860-001 (4) Remove the pressure from the hydraulic reservoirs, do this task: Hydraulic Reservoirs Depressurization, TASK 29-09-00-860-802 or Hydraulic Reservoirs Depressurization, TASK 29-09-00-860-808.

E. Main Landing Gear Reaction Link Assembly Removal

SUBTASK 32-11-71-020-001 (1) Do this task: Main Gear Downlock Springs Removal, TASK 32-32-91-000-801. SUBTASK 32-11-71-020-002 (2) Do these steps to disconnect the hydraulic line [37] and hydraulic line [37A] from the hydraulic tubes [2]: (a) Disconnect the hydraulic line [37] and hydraulic line [37A] from the hydraulic tubes [2] attached to the bracket assembly [38]. (b) Install the caps/plugs, STD-14686, on the hydraulic line [37] and hydraulic line [37A]. (c) Put tags on the hydraulic line [37] and hydraulic line [37A] to prevent the crossing of the lines during the installation. (d) Disconnect the hydraulic tubes [2] from the downlock actuator [4]. (e) Install the caps/plugs, STD-14686, on the hydraulic tubes [2]. EFFECTIVITY ALL (f) Install the caps/plugs, STD-14686, on the unions in the ports of the downlock actuator [4]. SUBTASK 32-11-71-020-003 (3) Do these steps to disconnect the reaction link assembly [1] from the downlock actuator [4]: (a) Remove the cotter pin [11], nut [10], and the washer [9] from the rod end pin [6]. (b) Remove the rod end pin [6] that attaches the head end of the downlock actuator [4] to the reaction link assembly [1]. (c) Remove the washers [7] and washers [8]. (d) Slowly lower the head end of the downlock actuator [4] to the upper end of the upper side strut [21]. (e) Use a tape to attach the head end of the downlock actuator [4] to the upper end of the upper side strut [21]. NOTE: This task will prevent the downlock actuator from moving when you do the subsequent steps. SUBTASK 32-11-71-020-004 (4) Do these steps to disconnect the reaction link assembly [1] from the upper lock link [5]: (a) Remove the cotter pin [16] from the downlock link pin [13]. (b) Remove the nut [15] and the washer [14] from the downlock link pin [13]. 1) Use the wrench adapter wrench adapter, C32029-4 or C32029-94, SPL-1360, to hold the head of the downlock link pin [13] when you loosen the nut [15]. (c) Remove the downlock link pin [13] that attaches the reaction link assembly [1] to the upper lock link [5]. 1) Use the thread protector, C32029-13, SPL-1369, when you do this step. SUBTASK 32-11-71-020-005 (5) Do these steps to disconnect the reaction link assembly [1] from the upper side strut [21]: (a) Remove the cotter pin [23], nut [22] and washer [24] from crossbolt [17]. (b) Remove the crossbolt [17] from the side strut pin [20]. (c) Remove the side side strut nut [18] and the side strut washer [19] from the side strut pin [20]. 1) Use the wrench adapter wrench adapter, C32029-3 or C32029-93, SPL-1359, to hold the head of the side strut pin [20] when you loosen the side strut nut [18]. (d) Attach a strap to the upper end of the upper side strut [21]. 1) If you will not remove the hanger link assembly [35], attach a strap to the upper end of the upper side strut [21] and loop the strap over the hanger link assembly [35]. Route the strap such that it will not interfere with removal of the reaction link assembly [1]. 2) If you will remove the hanger link assembly [35], attach a strap to the upper end of the upper side strut [21] and loop the strap over the main landing gear beam support hanger, located aft of the hanger link assembly [35]. Route the strap such that it will not interfere with removal of the reaction link assembly [1]. EFFECTIVITY ALL WARNING YOU MUST HAVE TWO PERSONNEL TO LIFT THIS COMPONENT. THE COMPONENT IS HEAVY. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY, INJURY TO PERSONNEL CAN OCCUR. (e) Remove the side strut pin [20] that attach the reaction link assembly [1] to the upper side strut [21]. NOTE: The reaction link assembly [1] weighs approximately 63.2 lb (28.7 kg). 1) Use the thread protector, C32029-12 or C32029-101, SPL-1368, when you do this step. SUBTASK 32-11-71-020-006 (6) Do these steps to disconnect the reaction link assembly [1] from the hanger link assembly [35]: (a) Remove the pin assembly [31] from the reaction link assembly [1]. (b) Remove the cotter pin [28], nut [29] and washer [30] from the crossbolt [25]. (c) Remove the crossbolt [25] from the end cap [27]. (d) Remove the washer [26] from the crossbolt [25]. (e) Isolate the end cap [27], bracket assembly [38], hydraulic tube [2], electrical harness [12], and the spacer [32] and spacer [36] as an assembly from the reaction link assembly [1]. (f) If it is necessary to disconnect the electrical harness [12], do this step: 1) Disconnect the electrical harness [12] by removing the bolts for the bracket which holds the sensor to the upper lock link [5]. (g) Remove the hanger link pin [34] that attaches the reaction link assembly [1] to the hanger link assembly [35]. 1) Use the slug driver slug driver assy, C32029-8, SPL-1364, when you do this step. SUBTASK 32-11-71-020-013 (7) If it is necessary, do the following steps to remove the hanger link assembly [35] from the supporting structure: (a) Remove the cotter pin [53], nut [52] and washer [51] from the crossbolt [50]. (b) Remove the cross bolt [50] from the hanger link assembly pin [46]. (c) Remove the nut [49] and washer [48] from the hanger link assembly pin [46] with wrench adapter, C32029-31 or C32029-99, SPL-11946. NOTE: The nut [54], washer [55], and washer [56] are not necessary to be removed when remove the hanger link assembly pin [46]. (d) Remove the hanger link assembly pin [46] and spacer [47] that attaches the hanger link assembly to the supporting structure. (e) Remove the hanger link assembly [35]. SUBTASK 32-11-71-020-007 (8) Do these steps to disconnect the reaction link assembly [1] from the trunnion [41]: (a) Remove the cotter pin [44], nut [43] and washer [42] from the crossbolt [39]. (b) Remove the crossbolt [39] from the trunnion pin [40]. (c) Remove the end cap [45] from the trunnion pin [40]. (d) Remove the trunnion pin [40] that attaches the reaction link assembly [1] to the trunnion [41]. 1) Use the slug driver slug driver assy, C32029-8, SPL-1364, when you do this task. EFFECTIVITY ALL SUBTASK 32-11-71-020-008 WARNING YOU MUST HAVE TWO PERSONNEL TO LIFT THIS COMPONENT. THE COMPONENT IS HEAVY. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY, INJURY TO PERSONNEL CAN OCCUR. (9) Remove the reaction link assembly [1] from the airplane. NOTE: The reaction link assembly weighs approximately 63.2 lb (28.7 kg).

SUBTASK 32-11-71-420-005 (7) Do these steps to connect the hydraulic tubes [2] to the downlock actuator [4]: (a) Remove the caps from the unions in the ports of the downlock actuator [4]. (b) Remove the caps from the hydraulic tubes [2]. (c) Connect the hydraulic tubes [2] to the downlock actuator [4]. (d) Tighten the hydraulic tubes [2] to 140 ±7 in-lb (15.8 ±0.8 N·m). (e) Loosen the hydraulic tubes [2] and re-tighten them to 133 in-lb (15.0 N·m) - 147 in-lb (16.6 N·m). SUBTASK 32-11-71-420-006 (8) Do these steps to connect the hydraulic line [37] and hydraulic line [37A] to the hydraulic tubes [2] that are attached to the bracket assembly [38]: (a) Remove the caps from the hydraulic line [37] and hydraulic line [37A]. (b) Connect the hydraulic line [37] and hydraulic line [37A] to the hydraulic tubes [2]. (c) Tighten the hydraulic line [37] to 140 ±7 in-lb (15.8 ±0.8 N·m). (d) Tighten the hydraulic line [37A] to 270 ±14 in-lb (30.5 ±1.6 N·m).

H. Main Landing Gear Reaction Link Assembly Installation Test

SUBTASK 32-11-71-420-007 (1) Do this task: Main Gear Downlock Spring Installation, TASK 32-32-91-400-801. SUBTASK 32-11-71-710-001 (2) Do this task: Main Gear Downlock Actuator Installation, TASK 32-32-51-400-801. SUBTASK 32-11-71-860-006 (3) Do this task: Hydraulic Reservoirs Pressurization, TASK 29-09-00-860-801. SUBTASK 32-11-71-860-004 (4) Do this task: Main Landing Gear Operational Test, TASK 32-32-00-710-801. NOTE: If a hydraulic cart is not available, it is optional to perform the Main Landing Gear Test - Component Replacement, TASK 32-32-00-710-802 instead of the operational test. SUBTASK 32-11-71-210-001 (5) Do a check of the hydraulic connections for leakage.

I. Put the Airplane Back to Its Usual Condition

SUBTASK 32-11-71-860-002 (1) For hydraulic system A, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Power Removal, TASK 29-11-00-860-805. SUBTASK 32-11-71-580-003 (2) Do this task: Lower the Airplane Off the Jacks, TASK 07-11-01-580-816.

F. Main Landing Gear Manifold Assembly Installation

SUBTASK 32-11-81-420-015 (1) Make sure the matting surfaces on the manifold assembly [4] and on the shimmy damper [1] are clean. SUBTASK 32-11-81-480-017 (2) Remove the plug from the new manifold assembly [4] and from the shimmy damper [1], if they are installed. SUBTASK 32-11-81-480-018 (3) Do these steps to install the transfer tube [12]: (a) Install the new packing [10]and the new rings [9,11]on the transfer tube [12] in their two locations. (b) Lubricate the transfer tube transfer tube [12], the packings [10], and the backup rings [9,11] with hydraulic fluid, D00153. (c) Install the transfer tube transfer tube [12] in its location in the shimmy damper [1]. SUBTASK 32-11-81-480-019 (4) Do these steps to install the manifold assembly [4]: (a) Put the manifold assembly [4] in its location on the shimmy damper [1] (and the transfer tube [12]). (b) Install the bolts [5] and the washers [6] to connect the manifold assembly [4] to the shimmy damper [1]. NOTE: The Shimmy Damper Housing contains inserts at the manifold bolt locations. (c) Install lockwire on the compensator to the closest bolt [5] for the manifold assembly [4]. SUBTASK 32-11-81-020-010 (5) If the new manifold assembly [4] does not have a reducer [2] installed, do these steps: (a) Remove the plug from the port in the manifold assembly, if one is installed. (b) Lubricate the hydraulic reducer [2] and the new packing [3] with hydraulic fluid, D00153. (c) Install the packing [3] on the hydraulic reducer [2]. EFFECTIVITY ALL (d) Install the reducer [2] in the manifold assembly [4]. SUBTASK 32-11-81-480-020 (6) Remove the cap from the reducer [2], if one is installed. SUBTASK 32-11-81-420-016 (7) Connect the hydraulic line to the manifold assembly [4] on the hydraulic shimmy damper [1]. SUBTASK 32-11-81-420-017 (8) Do this task: Hydraulic Shimmy Damper - Bleeding, TASK 32-11-81-870-801. (a) Look for leaks at the manifold connection and the hydraulic line connection when you bleed the shimmy damper [1].

F. Main Landing Gear Hydraulic Shimmy Damper Removal

SUBTASK 32-11-81-020-001 (1) Disconnect the hydraulic line from the manifold assembly [2] on the shimmy damper assembly [1]. SUBTASK 32-11-81-020-002 (2) If the replacement shimmy damper assembly [1] does not have a reducer [3] installed in the manifold assembly [2], do these steps: (a) Remove the reducer [3] and packing [4] from the shimmy damper assembly [1]. (b) Discard the packing [4]. (c) Install the reducer [3] with a cap and new packing [4] in the port of the manifold assembly [2] of the replacement shimmy damper assembly [1]. (d) As an alternative, install a plug in the port of the manifold assembly [2]. SUBTASK 32-11-81-020-024 (3) Remove the left hand inboard or right hand outboard wheel and tire assembly, do this task: Main Landing Gear Wheel and Tire Assembly Removal, TASK 32-45-11-000-801. SUBTASK 32-11-81-020-003 (4) Do this task: Main Landing Gear Torsion Link Disconnection, TASK 32-11-51-020-801. SUBTASK 32-11-81-020-004 (5) Remove the shimmy damper assembly [1] from the upper torsion link [18]. (a) Remove the lockwire from the bolts [16]. (b) Remove the bolts [16], washers [17], washers [22], and straight sleeve [21] that holds the shimmy damper assembly [1] to the upper torsion link [18]. NOTE: The washer [22] may not be on all aircraft. The washer [22] can be used on all aircraft. Refer to 737-SL-32-135.

SUBTASK 32-11-81-420-002 (1) Prepare the following parts for installation: WARNING USE NITRILE GLOVES FOR SKIN PROTECTION WHEN YOU USE COR￾BAN 27L. IF IT GETS ON YOUR SKIN, IMMEDIATELY REMOVE IT WITH WATER. IF THIS MATERIAL GETS IN YOUR EYES, IMMEDIATELY FLUSH YOUR EYES WITH WATER. GET MEDICAL AID. THIS MATERIAL CONTAINS FLAMMABLE AGENTS WHICH CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONNEL. NOTE: If Cor-Ban 27L Compound, G50237, is not available, you can use corrosion inhibiting material, G50136, as an approved alternate. NOTE: The washer [22] may not be on all aircraft. The washer [22] can be used on all aircraft. Refer to 737-SL-32-135. (b) Apply a thin layer of grease, D00633, to the outside diameter of the straight sleeve [21]. 1) Make sure that you install the bolt [16], washer [17], washer [22], and straight sleeve [21] immediately while the compound is wet. WARNING USE NITRILE GLOVES FOR SKIN PROTECTION WHEN YOU USE COR￾BAN 27L. IF IT GETS ON YOUR SKIN, IMMEDIATELY REMOVE IT WITH WATER. IF THIS MATERIAL GETS IN YOUR EYES, IMMEDIATELY FLUSH YOUR EYES WITH WATER. GET MEDICAL AID. THIS MATERIAL CONTAINS FLAMMABLE AGENTS WHICH CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONNEL. (c) Apply a thin layer of primer, C00259, Cor-Ban 27L Compound, G50237, or corrosion inhibiting material, G50136, to the shimmy damper face common to the upper torsion link. EFFECTIVITY ALL 1) Make sure that no compound is in or on the piston shaft of the damper. (d) Remove excess compound. SUBTASK 32-11-81-420-020 (2) Hold the hydraulic shimmy damper assembly [1] in its location on the upper torsion link [18]. SUBTASK 32-11-81-420-003 CAUTION MAKE SURE THAT YOU INSTALL THE SLEEVES IN THE CORRECT LOCATIONS. IF YOU INSTALL THE SLEEVES IN THE INCORRECT LOCATIONS, VIBRATION CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO COMPONENTS OF LANDING GEAR. (3) Loosely install the bolts [16], washers [17], washers [22], and straight sleeve [21] to hold the hydraulic shimmy damper to the upper torsion link [18]. NOTE: The shimmy damper installation has a straight sleeve and a tapered sleeve. The straight sleeve is longer than the tapered sleeve. SUBTASK 32-11-81-420-004 CAUTION MAKE SURE THAT YOU INSTALL THE SLEEVES IN THE CORRECT LOCATIONS. IF YOU INSTALL THE SLEEVES IN THE INCORRECT LOCATIONS, VIBRATION CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO COMPONENTS OF LANDING GEAR. (4) Do this task: Main Landing Gear Torsion Link Connection, TASK 32-11-51-400-803. (a) When you connect the torsion links, do not tighten the apex nut [9] completely or install the retention bolt [8] for the apex nut [9]. SUBTASK 32-11-81-420-022 (5) Tighten the bolts [16] for the hydraulic shimmy damper, in a cross pattern, to 450 in-lb (50.8 N·m) - 550 in-lb (62.1 N·m). (a) Install MS20995NC32 lockwire, G50347, on the bolts [16] with the double-twist method. SUBTASK 32-11-81-420-019 (6) Tighten the apex nut [9] to 50 ft-lb (67.8 N·m) - 58 ft-lb (78.6 N·m). (a) Advance the apex nut [9] to the nearest castellation that aligns with the hole in the apex pin [19]. (b) Tighten the apex nut [9] to a final torque of 150 ft-lb (203.4 N·m) maximum. (c) Install the retention bolt [8], washers [10], nut [12], and new pin [11]. SUBTASK 32-11-81-020-005 (7) If the new hydraulic shimmy damper assembly [1] does not have a reducer [3] and new packing [4] installed in the manifold assembly [2], do these steps: (a) Remove the plug from the port in the manifold assembly [2], if one is installed. (b) Lubricate the hydraulic reducer [3] and packing [4] with hydraulic fluid, D00153. (c) Install the packing [4] on the hydraulic reducer [3]. (d) Install the reducer [3] in the manifold assembly [2]. SUBTASK 32-11-81-480-004 (8) Remove the cap on the reducer [3], if one is installed. SUBTASK 32-11-81-420-007 (9) Connect the hydraulic line to the reducer [3] on the shimmy damper manifold assembly [2]. EFFECTIVITY ALL SUBTASK 32-11-81-420-026 (10) Install the left hand inboard or right hand outboard wheel and tire assembly, do this task: Main Landing Gear Wheel and Tire Assembly Installation, TASK 32-45-11-400-801. SUBTASK 32-11-81-420-008 (11) Do this task: Hydraulic Shimmy Damper - Bleeding, TASK 32-11-81-870-801. (a) Look for leaks at the hydraulic connection when you bleed the shimmy damper assembly [1].

(1) This task provides instructions to bleed the hydraulic shimmy damper. (2) The hydraulic shimmy damper has an internal piston with areas for hydraulic fluid on the two sides of the piston. To bleed the shimmy damper it is necessary to remove the air from the two fluid areas.

F. Hydraulic Shimmy Damper Bleeding

SUBTASK 32-11-81-480-006 WARNING MAKE SURE THE DOWNLOCK PINS ARE INSTALLED ON ALL THE LANDING GEAR. WITHOUT THE DOWNLOCK PINS, THE LANDING GEAR CAN RETRACT AND CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT. (1) If the downlock pins are not installed in the nose and main landing gear, do this task: Landing Gear Downlock Pins Installation, TASK 32-00-01-480-801. SUBTASK 32-11-81-860-003 (2) If the bleed plugs [5] need new packings [6], do these steps: (a) For the A hydraulic system, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Power Removal, TASK 29-11-00-860-805. (b) Remove the lockwire from the bleed plugs [5]. (c) Remove the bleed plug [5] from the shimmy damper assembly [1]. NOTE: Hydraulic return pressure that remains after you have depressurized system A will force fluid out the bleed port when you remove the bleed plug. (d) Install the packing [6] on the bleed plug [5]. (e) Install the bleed plug [5] in its location on the shimmy damper assembly [1]. (f) Tighten the bleed plug [5] to 140 ±14 in-lb (16 ±2 N·m). SUBTASK 32-11-81-790-001 WARNING KEEP PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT CLEAR OF THE FLIGHT CONTROL SURFACES. THESE COMPONENTS CAN MOVE SUDDENLY WHEN YOU PUT THE AIRPLANE IN AIR MODE. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT. (3) For the A hydraulic system, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Pressurization, TASK 29-11-00-860-801. SUBTASK 32-11-81-480-008 (4) Make sure that the tires have chocks installed around them. SUBTASK 32-11-81-840-001 (5) Do the steps that follow to bleed the air from the shimmy damper assembly [1] at the two bleed plugs [5]: (a) Bleed one side of the hydraulic shimmy damper piston: NOTE: The shimmy damper hydraulic pressure is supplied from the return lines of hydraulic system (system A), to bleed the damper it is necessary to cycle the landing gear control lever. EFFECTIVITY ALL WARNING MAKE SURE THE DOWNLOCK PINS ARE INSTALLED ON ALL THE LANDING GEAR. WITHOUT THE DOWNLOCK PINS, THE LANDING GEAR COULD RETRACT AND CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONNEL AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT. 1) Move the landing gear control handle to the UP position. 2) Open one of the two bleed plugs [5]. NOTE: You can open either the left or the right bleed plugs. 3) Move the landing gear control handle to the DOWN position. 4) Close the bleed plug [5] to 140 ±14 in-lb (16 ±2 N·m). (b) Continue to move the landing gear control handle and open and close the bleed plug as stated above until the air is gone from the fluid flow. (c) Bleed the other side of the hydraulic shimmy damper piston through the bleed plug that remains: 1) Do the steps that follow to bleed the shimmy damper assembly [1] from the other bleed plug [5]: a) Move the landing gear control handle to the UP position. b) Open the other bleed plug [5]. c) Move the landing gear control handle to the DOWN position. d) Close the bleed plug [5] to 140 ±14 in-lb (16 ±2 N·m). (d) Continue to move the landing gear control handle and open and close the bleed plug as stated above until the air is gone from the fluid flow. SUBTASK 32-11-81-420-023 (6) Install the MS20995NC32 lockwire, G50347, on the bleed plugs [5] using the double twist method. SUBTASK 32-11-81-860-004 (7) For the A hydraulic system, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Power Removal, TASK 29-11-00-860-805. SUBTASK 32-11-81-860-015 (8) Check the PSEU for faults generated by the bleeding procedure and clear them. NOTE: When the landing gear control lever is moved to bleed the shimmy damper, the gear lock sensors will not transition their state. This will cause faults to be stored in the PSEU and cause the PSEU light to illuminate.

F. Main Landing Gear Forward Trunnion Bearing Assembly Installation

SUBTASK 32-11-83-420-001 (1) Install the forward trunnion bearing assembly [1]: (a) Apply a thin layer of corrosion inhibiting material, G50136, to the fuse pins [6] as follows: 1) The outer diameters. 2) The threads. 3) The head mating surfaces. (b) Apply two layers of primer, C00259, to the special washers [7]. (c) Put the housing assembly [8] in its position for the connection to the forward trunnion support. NOTE: The zerk fitting on the housing assembly [8] will point up and aft. (d) Align the holes in the housing assembly [8] to the holes in the forward trunnion support. (e) Install the special washers [7] as follows: 1) Clean any corrosion inhibiting material, G50136, from surfaces where sealant, A00247, or sealant, A50009, is applied. NOTE: Cross contamination is not permitted. CAUTION DO NOT APPLY SEALANT TO WASHER SURFACES THAT TOUCH WITH THE PIN HEADS OR NUTS. THIS CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE EQUIPMENT. 2) Apply sealant as follows: a) If plain special washers [7] are installed, apply sealant, A00247, or sealant, A50009, to one side of the special washer [7] that will be mating to the forward trunnion support. b) If countersunk special washers [7] are installed, apply sealant, A00247, or sealant, A50009, to the non-countersunk side. <1> For each countersunk special washer [7], turn the non-countersunk side against the forward trunnion support. 3) Install the special washers [7] on the forward trunnion support. 4) Visually align the special washers [7] with the forward trunnion support bore. NOTE: Washers are to stay aligned with the fuse pins during installation of the fuse pins. (f) Apply a thin layer of corrosion inhibiting material, G50136, to the mating surfaces of the special washers [7] to the fuse pin bolt heads or nuts [9]. (g) Put the fuse pins [6] through the special washers [7], forward trunnion support, and housing assembly [8]. (h) Use a clean cloth to clean unwanted corrosion inhibiting material, G50136, from the threads of the fuse pins [6]. (i) Apply Pure Nickel Special compound, D00006, to the inner surfaces of nuts [9] and to the threads of the fuse pins [6]. (j) Install the nuts [9] on the fuse pins [6]. (k) Check that the run-up torque on the nuts [9] is 117 in-lb (13.2 N·m) or greater. EFFECTIVITY ALL 1) If the run-up torque is less than 117 in-lb (13.2 N·m), replace the nuts [9]. (l) Tighten the nuts [9] to 1300 in-lb (146.9 N·m) - 1350 in-lb (152.5 N·m). 1) Make sure that the special washers [7] stay aligned with the support bore when you tighten each nut [9]. 2) Do a visual inspection that the special washers [7] are centered. 3) Re-tighten the nuts [9] to 1300 in-lb (146.9 N·m) - 1350 in-lb (152.5 N·m). NOTE: Re-tighten the nuts before the squeeze-out life of the sealant. NOTE: Wait a minimum 10 minutes for sealant with a squeeze out life less than or equal to 48 hours. Wait a minimum 60 minutes for sealant with a squeeze out life greater than 48 hours. (m) Use a clean cloth to clean unwanted corrosion inhibiting material, G50136, at the outer edges of the special washers [7]. (n) Clean any corrosion inhibiting material, G50136, from surfaces where sealant, A00247, or sealant, A50009, is applied. NOTE: Cross contamination is not permitted. (o) Apply a fillet seal to the edge of the special washers [7] with sealant, A00247, or sealant, A50009. (p) Put the rods [4] into the fuse pins [6]. (q) Install the fuse pin caps [3], washers [5], and nuts [2] on the ends of the rods [4]. (r) Tighten the nuts [2] to 50 in-lb (5.6 N·m) - 80 in-lb (9.0 N·m). SUBTASK 32-11-83-420-003 (2) Install the clamp [10], screws [11], and washers [12] on the hydraulic flow regulator. SUBTASK 32-11-83-420-004 (3) Install the clamp block assemblies [17]. (a) Install the clamp blocks [22] and channels [21] to the tubing. (b) Install the spacers [20], washers [19] and screws [18] to the clamp block assemblies [17] and nutplates [23] to secure to the structure. SUBTASK 32-11-83-420-005 (4) Install the fairlead [13] and fairlead [24] to the brackets.. (a) Install the fairlead [13] to the bracket with bolts [14], washers [15] and nuts [16]. (b) Tighten the bolts [14] 20 in-lb (2.3 N·m) - 25 in-lb (2.8 N·m). (c) Install the fairlead [24] to the bracket with the bolts [25], washers [26] and nuts [27]. (d) Tighten the bolts [25] 20 in-lb (2.3 N·m) - 25 in-lb (2.8 N·m). (e) Visually inspect the cables at the fairlead [13] and fairlead [24] upon reinstallation to the brackets for any damage. SUBTASK 32-11-85-420-018 (1) Do the following steps to install the axle sleeve [37]: (a) Apply a generous coating of grease, D00633, to the lands of the axle assembly [1], where the axle sleeve [37] inside diameters set. (b) Heat the axle sleeve [37] to 375 ±25°F (191 ±14°C). (c) Align the retention pin holes in the axle sleeve [37] and the axle assembly [1] before installing the sleeve on the axle assembly [1]. NOTE: The axle sleeve will rapidly shrink to normal size and seize the axle, preventing further pin alignment efforts. SUBTASK 32-11-85-420-019 (2) Do the following steps to install the axle sleeve retention pin [38]: WARNING USE NITRILE GLOVES FOR SKIN PROTECTION WHEN YOU USE COR￾BAN 27L. IF IT GETS ON YOUR SKIN, IMMEDIATELY REMOVE IT WITH WATER. IF THIS MATERIAL GETS IN YOUR EYES, IMMEDIATELY FLUSH YOUR EYES WITH WATER. GET MEDICAL AID. THIS MATERIAL CONTAINS FLAMMABLE AGENTS WHICH CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONNEL. (a) Apply corrosion preventive Cor-Ban 27L Compound, G50237 (preferred), or corrosion inhibiting material, G50136 (alternate), to the retention pin hole in the axle assembly [1], and the hole in the axle sleeve [37]. 1) If corrosion inhibiting compound is not available, use sealant, A00247, as an approved alternate. (b) Install the axle sleeve retention pin [38] by lightly pressing or tapping the pin into place. The head of the pin must be flush or below the outside diameter of the axle sleeve [37]. SUBTASK 32-11-85-020-014 (3) Remove all unwanted corrosion preventive Cor-Ban 27L Compound, G50237. SUBTASK 32-11-85-420-026 (4) Do these steps to install the brake sleeve [2]: (a) Apply a light coating of grease, D00633, to the lands of the axle assembly [1] and the axle assembly sleeve, where the brake sleeve [2] inside diameters set. NOTE: Avoid use of too much grease on the brake sleeve [2]. (b) Heat the brake sleeve [2] to 375 ±25°F (191 ±14°C). (c) Install the brake sleeve [2] on the axle assembly [1]. (d) Remove all unwanted grease, D00633. SUBTASK 32-11-85-420-020 (5) Do these steps to install the wiring assembly [39] in the axle assembly [1]: (a) Before you connect the electrical connector to the inner cylinder assembly [3], examine the connector for corrosion. EFFECTIVITY ALL WARNING DO THE STEPS BELOW IF THE AIRPLANE OPERATES WHERE DEICING FLUID THAT CONTAINS POTASSIUM FORMATE OR POTASSIUM ACETATE IS USED. ALSO, DO THE STEPS FOR ALL AIRPLANES THAT YOU FOUND CORROSION IN THE ELECTRICAL CONNECTORS IN THE MAIN WHEEL WELL. THE ELECTRICAL CONNECTORS ARE IN A SYSTEM THAT IS NECESSARY FOR SAFE FLIGHT. (b) If there was corrosion, refer to SWPM 20-60-03 to correct the problem. (c) Apply D5026NS or ZC-026 compound, G50171, to the connector (SWPM 20-60-03). (d) Push the wiring through the hole on the inner cylinder assembly [3] and into the axle assembly [1]. (e) Clean the mating surfaces of the fitting [4] and conduit nut [5] with alcohol, B00130, and cloth, G51677. (f) Apply compound, D50004 (preferred), or Cor-Ban 27L Compound, G50237 (alternative), to the threads of the fitting [4] and conduit nut [5]. (g) Tighten the fitting [4] to 45 in-lb (5.1 N·m) - 55 in-lb (6.2 N·m). (h) Tighten the conduit nut [5] to 70 in-lb (8 N·m) - 90 in-lb (10 N·m) to connect the conduit assembly [40] to the inner cylinder assembly [3]. (i) Install MS20995NC20 lockwire, G02166, on the fitting [4] and conduit nut [5]. SUBTASK 32-11-85-420-021 (6) Install the in-axle assemblies (TASK 32-42-11-400-801). SUBTASK 32-11-85-420-022 (7) Do this task: Main Landing Gear Brake Installation, TASK 32-41-41-400-801. NOTE: This procedure will also install the wheel and tire assemblies. (a) Make sure that the correct wires are connected to the correct in-axle assembly. SUBTASK 32-11-85-600-002 (8) For the grease fittings on the upper torsion link and the lower torsion link [18], do this task: Main Landing Gear Lower End Components Servicing, TASK 12-21-11-640-802.

SUBTASK 32-11-85-020-015 (1) Do this task: Main Landing Gear Brake Removal, TASK 32-41-41-000-801. NOTE: This procedure will also remove the wheel and tire assemblies. SUBTASK 32-11-85-300-001 (2) Remove lockbolt and nut. SUBTASK 32-11-85-300-002 CAUTION DO NOT APPLY TOO MUCH FORCE WHEN YOU REMOVE THE BRAKE SLEEVE. IF YOU USE TOO MUCH FORCE, DAMAGE TO THE AIRPLANE AND THE SUPPORT EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR. (3) Remove the sleeve from the axle with an approved puller puller equipment, SPL-1864 (Main Landing Gear Axle Sleeve Removal, TASK 32-11-85-000-802). (a) If it is necessary, you can increase the temperature of the sleeve to approximately 200 degrees F. NOTE: Applied heat can decrease the force necessary for the removal. SUBTASK 32-11-85-300-003 (4) Use an abrasive, B00137 or abrasive cloth, B00102 or abrasive, B00138 and remove the plating by hand. NOTE: Do not use power tools. The maximum mismatch is 0.003 inch. SUBTASK 32-11-85-300-004 (5) Make sure you do not remove more than 0.003 in. (0.076 mm) of base metal. (6) If you find any cracks, continue to remove the plating and the base metal until the cracks will be smooth. SUBTASK 32-11-85-300-005 (7) Apply an coating, C00250 or coating, C00251 (Ref. Chapter 51, Heat, Weather, and Oil Resistant Inorganic Protective Coating). SUBTASK 32-11-85-300-006 (8) Apply a thick layer of grease, D00633 to the axle lands. NOTE: Do not remove too much grease, D00633 from the inside diameter of the axle sleeve after installation. SUBTASK 32-11-85-420-024 (9) Do this, do this task: Main Landing Gear Axle Installation, TASK 32-11-85-420-801. SUBTASK 32-11-85-300-007 (10) Align the bolt holes in the axle and the sleeve. EFFECTIVITY ALL (a) Install the lockbolt. SUBTASK 32-11-85-300-008 (11) Verify the diameter of the bearing supports after the sleeve installation. NOTE: The outer diameter of the small bearing support must not be more than 4.3293 inches. The outer diameter of large bearing support must not be more than 4.7491 inches.

32-11-85-300-802Repair of the Axle Sleeve of the Main Landing GearPDF p. 552

3. Repair of the Axle Sleeve of the Main Landing Gear (Figure 801, Figure 802)

A. Location Zones

Zone Area 734 Left Main Landing Gear 744 Right Main Landing Gear

B. Axle Sleeve of the Main Landing Gear Repair

SUBTASK 32-11-85-300-009 (1) Do a check on the wear limits of the bearing boss. (a) Examine the diameters of the inboard and outboard bearing boss for worn areas as shown on Figure 802. 1) If worn areas on the bearing boss is more than the specified wear limits and the clearance between the bearing and boss is more than 0.006 in. (0.152 mm), remove the axle sleeve and replace or rework. 2) If worn areas on the bearing boss is more than the specified wear limits and the clearance between the bearing and boss is not more than 0.006 in. (0.152 mm), the axle sleeve can continue to be in service for 65 hours flying time before removal for replacement or repairs. SUBTASK 32-11-85-300-010 (2) Repair the local damage on the bearing surfaces. (a) Remove the sharp edges and make a smooth finish on the damage to a 0.50 in. (12.70 mm) radius. 1) Do not reduce the wall thickness by more than 0.025 in. (0.635 mm) or more than 30 % of each of the total bearing area of any 90 degree segment. NOTE: The outboard bearing area can be counted separately from the inboard bearing area. (b) If damage is on the antirotation bolt hole, replace the sleeve or contact to make an analysis of a possible repair.

E. Main Landing Gear Downlock Strut Removal

SUBTASK 32-11-89-020-002 (1) Do these steps to disconnect the hydraulic lines [2] from the downlock actuator [4]: (a) Put tags on the hydraulic lines [2] to prevent the crossing of the hydraulic lines [2] during the installation. (b) Disconnect the hydraulic lines [2] from the downlock actuator [4]. (c) Install the cap/plug, STD-14686, on the hydraulic lines [2]. (d) Remove and discard the packings [3]. (e) Install the cap/plug, STD-14686, in the ports of the downlock actuator [4]. SUBTASK 32-11-89-020-008 (2) Use a downlock release lever, SPL-12498, to manually release the Main Landing Gear (MLG) downlock mechanism. SUBTASK 32-11-89-020-003 (3) Do these steps to disconnect the rod end of the downlock actuator [4] from the downlock strut [5]: (a) Remove the spacer [7] from the rod end pin [8]. (b) From the forward side, remove the rod end pin [8] that holds the rod end of the downlock actuator [4] to the downlock strut [5]. (c) Remove the spacers [9] and washers [10]. (d) Slowly lower the rod end of the downlock actuator [4] to the upper end of the upper side strut. (e) Use a tape to attach the rod end of the downlock actuator [4] to the upper end of the upper side strut. NOTE: This will prevent the downlock actuator from moving when you do the subsequent steps. SUBTASK 32-11-89-020-004 (4) Do these steps to disconnect the electrical harnesses [11] from the downlock strut [5]: EFFECTIVITY ALL (a) Remove the nuts [20], washers [19], and bolts [18] to disconnect the brackets [17] from the downlock strut [5]. 1) Remove the brackets [17] with the sensors attached. (b) Isolate the brackets [17] from the downlock strut [5]. SUBTASK 32-11-89-080-001 (5) Remove the downlock pin from the MLG in order to remove the downlock strut [5] (TASK 32-00-01-080-801). SUBTASK 32-11-89-020-005 (6) Do these steps to disconnect the downlock strut [5] from the reaction link assembly [6]: (a) Remove the pin [22] from the downlock link pin [12]. (b) Remove the nut [21] and washer [23] from the downlock link pin [12]. 1) Use a wrench adapter, C32029-4 or C32029-94, SPL-1360, to hold the head of the downlock link pin [12] when you loosen the nut [21]. (c) Remove the downlock link pin [12] that holds the downlock strut [5] to the reaction link assembly [6]. 1) Use a thread protector, C32029-13, SPL-1369. SUBTASK 32-11-89-020-006 (7) Do these steps to disconnect the downlock strut [5] from the upper side strut: (a) Remove the pin [16] from the downlock link pin [13]. (b) Remove the nut [15] and washer [14] from the downlock link pin [13]. (c) Remove the downlock link pin [13] that holds the downlock strut [5] to the upper side strut. 1) Use a thread protector, C32029-13, SPL-1369. SUBTASK 32-11-89-020-007 (8) Remove the downlock strut [5] from the airplane. SUBTASK 32-11-89-580-001 (9) If the removal of the downlock strut [5] is difficult do this task to decrease the weight on the gear: Lift the Main Landing Gear Axles with the Axle Jacks, TASK 07-11-03-580-801.
