H. Strut Torsion Links and Install Tooling Disassembly

SUBTASK 32-21-11-020-010 (1) Disconnect the lower torsion link [49] from the inner cylinder [12] as follows: (a) Use a jack to hold the inner cylinder [12] in its position in the outer cylinder [9], or when moving the inner cylinder [12] out of or into the outer cylinder [9] unless otherwise directed (TASK 07-11-03-580-802). (b) Remove the pin [52], nut [51], and washer [41] from the torsion link pin [42]. (c) Remove the torsion link pin [42] to disconnect the lower torsion link [49] from the inner cylinder [12]. (d) Supply a rope or other suitable tieback for the lower torsion links [49] to hold them out of the work area. SUBTASK 32-21-11-020-029 WARNING SHOCK STRUT FLUID MAY LEAK FROM THE GLAND NUT AREA WHEN THE GLAND NUT IS LOOSENED AND MOVED DOWN THE INNER CYLINDER. SHOCK STRUT FLUID MAY CAUSE HARM TO PERSONNEL. USE LINT FREE CLOTH PADS TO ABSORB LEAKAGE. (2) Disconnect the gland nut [17] from the outer cylinder [9] as follows: EFFECTIVITY ALL (a) Measure and write down, the dimension from the gland nut [17] lower surface to the outer cylinder [9] lower surface. NOTE: This measurement will be used to make sure of the proper stack up of the lower bearing carrier components upon reinstallation in the outer cylinder. (b) Remove the lockwire from bolt [14]. (c) Remove the bolts [14], washers [15], and lockplate [16] to release the gland nut [17]. (d) Wrap towels around the inner cylinder [12], one on top of the other, to absorb fluid when you slowly loosen the gland nut [17]. 1) Use a bucket to catch the fluid dripping from the towel. (e) Use a gland nut wrench, SPL-1867, to slowly loosen the gland nut [17] until the fluid begins to flow from the outer cylinder [9]. 1) When the fluid flow stops, disconnect the gland nut [17] from the outer cylinder [9]. (f) Hold the gland nut [17] in its position against the outer cylinder [9] after you have disconnected it from the outer cylinder [9]. SUBTASK 32-21-11-480-006 (3) Install the scraper retainer [79] (scraper retainer, C32016-4 or -67, SPL-1378) and scraper lock assembly [74] on the gland nut [17]. NOTE: This will make sure that the scraper ring for the gland nut does not come out of its groove. (a) Install the scraper retainer [79]. (b) Install the scraper lock assembly [74] to hold the scraper retainer [79] in its position on the gland nut [17]. SUBTASK 32-21-11-020-030 (4) Move the gland nut [17] down to the bottom of the inner cylinder [12]. (a) If the scraper ring [24] comes out of its groove, use the scraper plunger [80] and scraper reducer [81] to install the scraper ring [24] back in its groove. SUBTASK 32-21-11-020-031 (5) Move lower bearing carrier [23] as follows: (a) Loosely install the seal puller assembly [73] around the inner cylinder [12]. (b) Push the seal puller assembly [73] up, such that it will install correctly at the bottom of the outer cylinder [9]. (c) Align the holes in the seal puller assembly [73] with the holes in the lower bearing carrier [23] for the puller screws [78]. (d) Install the carrier puller screw [78] to hold the seal puller assembly [73] to the lower bearing carrier [23]. (e) Tighten the retainer screws on each side of the seal puller assembly [73]. (f) Use the jack to lift the inner cylinder [12] until the scraper lock assembly [74] is approximately 6 in. (15 cm) below the seal puller assembly [73]. (g) Install the strap assembly [75] around the axle and connect the ends to the shoulder bolts on each side of the seal puller assembly [73]. (h) Use the jack to lower the inner cylinder [12] until the lower bearing carrier [23] is completely out of the outer cylinder [9]. 1) Do not lower more than necessary. EFFECTIVITY ALL (i) Move the lower bearing carrier [23] by hand down on top of the gland nut [17]. NOTE: The bearing carrier pin may fall to ground during the movement of the lower bearing carrier down the inner cylinder. (j) Remove the bearing carrier pin [30] and retain for re-installation. (k) Remove the inner cylinder [12] from the outer cylinder [9]: WARNING MAKE SURE A MINIMUM OF TWO PERSONS WILL HOLD THE INNER CYLINDER WHEN YOU DO THE SUBSEQUENT STEPS. THE INNER CYLINDER IS HEAVY. INJURY TO PERSONS OR DAMAGE TO THE EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR IF THE INNER CYLINDER IS NOT HELD PROPERLY. 1) Use two people to lift the inner cylinder [12] off of the jack. 2) Move the jack away from the area. WARNING KEEP THE CYLINDER UP RIGHT. THE INNER CYLINDER CONTAINS SHOCK STRUT FLUID WHICH MAY FLOW OUT. USE A CONTAINER TO CAPTURE ANY REMAINING FLUID. THE FLUID CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONNEL OR EQUIPMENT. 3) Lower the inner cylinder [12] out of the outer cylinder [9]. (l) Pour the remaining shock strut fluid into a suitable 5 gal (19 l) container. NOTE: Total strut fluid is approximately 0.88 gal (3.3 l). NOTE: Debris from normal operation sometimes accumulates in the shock strut fluid. If necessary, the inner cylinder may be flushed with fluid, D00467, to ensure there is no debris upon reassembly. (m) Move the inner cylinder [12], lower bearing carrier [23], and gland nut [17] to a suitable location for further disassembly. NOTE: Two persons can transport the inner cylinder by holding the assembly by the axles and holding the inner cylinder upright. SUBTASK 32-21-11-840-003 (6) Use a plastic bag of suitable proportions to cover the open inner cylinder [12] and outer cylinder [9] when you are not directly working on them, to exclude the possibility of dirt or debris getting inside the cylinders.

I. Inner Cylinder Components Disassembly

SUBTASK 32-21-11-020-014 (1) Remove the upper bearing assembly [8] and recoil valve assembly from the top of the inner cylinder [12]: (a) Remove the insert [8A] from the upper bearing halve [85]. 1) Pull the insert [8A] apart slightly and slide it up and off the upper bearing halves [85]. 2) Inspect the insert [8A] for damage and excessive wear. a) The insert [8A] thickness must be greater than or equal to 0.0865 in. (2.1971 mm). b) Replace the insert [8A] if necessary. (b) Remove the upper bearing halve [85] from the inner cylinder [12]. EFFECTIVITY ALL (c) Remove the recoil valve [87] and ring [86]. SUBTASK 32-21-11-020-015 (2) Remove the upper centering cam [10] and lower centering cam [11] from the inner cylinder [12]. (a) Remove the dowel retaining circlip [88] and dowel [89] from the inner cylinder [12]. SUBTASK 32-21-11-020-032 (3) Remove the lower bearing carrier [23] from the inner cylinder [12]. (a) Use rubber mallet and lightly hit the bottom of the seal puller assembly [73] until the lower bearing carrier [23] can be pulled off at the top of the inner cylinder [12]. NOTE: The lower bearing carrier is coated with a dry lubricant film. The film may be worn and appear uneven, this is not cause for bearing carrier replacement. (b) Remove the puller screw [78] to disconnect the seal puller assembly [73] from the lower bearing carrier [23]. (c) Remove the seal puller assembly [73] from the lower bearing carrier [23]. (d) Remove the lower bearing insert [93] from the lower bearing carrier [23]. 1) Inspect the lower bearing insert [93] for damage and excessive wear. a) The lower bearing insert [93] must be greater than or equal to 0.0865 in. (2.1971 mm). b) Replace the lower bearing insert [93] if necessary. (e) Install the lower bearing insert [93] on the lower bearing carrier [23]. SUBTASK 32-21-11-020-033 (4) Remove the seal retainer [18]: (a) Move the seal retainer [18] away from the lower bearing carrier [23] to get access to the elastomer ring [19].

J. Active Dynamic Seal, Active Static Seal, and Spare Seals Replacement

NOTE: Perform this task in a sheltered and clean environment. Make sure that all fay surfaces of components have been cleaned and are free of debris before re-assembly. NOTE: You may disassemble the lower bearing carrier components all at once to aid in cleaning of the lower bearing carrier before reassembly. SUBTASK 32-21-11-900-007 (1) Install a new scraper ring [24] on the gland nut [17] if there is any sign of damage or wear on the old scraper ring [24]: NOTE: The scraper ring prevents dirt and debris from entering the shock strut when the inner cylinder and outer cylinder compress. (a) Remove the gland nut [17] from the inner cylinder [12]. (b) Remove the scraper retainer [79] and scraper lock assembly [74] from the gland nut [17]. (c) Remove the old scraper ring [24] from its groove on the gland nut [17]. (d) Install the new scraper ring [24] in its groove on the gland nut [17]. 1) Make sure that to use the correct scraper configuration to be installed in its groove on the gland nut [17]. NOTE: There are two possible scraper configurations used for installation (Figure 803). EFFECTIVITY ALL SUBTASK 32-21-11-480-007 (2) Install the scraper retainer [79] and scraper lock assembly [74] on the gland nut [17]. NOTE: This will make sure that the new scraper ring for the gland nut does not come out of its groove. (a) Install the scraper retainer [79] on the gland nut [17]. (b) Install the scraper lock assembly [74] to hold the scraper retainer [79] in its position on the gland nut [17]. SUBTASK 32-21-11-900-009 (3) Replace the excluder [25] on the lower bearing carrier [23] if there is a sign of damage or wear. NOTE: The excluder prevents dirt and debris from damaging the active static seal. (a) Remove the excluder [25] from its groove in the lower bearing carrier [23]. (b) Install the new excluder [25] in its groove in the lower bearing carrier [23]. 1) Put the excluder [25] in a sealed plastic bag and submerge the bag in hot water (not boiling) for 3-5 minutes. 2) Apply a thin layer of fluid, D50022, (preferred) or fluid, D00467, (alternate) onto the excluder [25]. 3) Put shock fluid, D50022, (preferred) or fluid, D00467, (alternate) on the surface on that the excluder [25] will move. 4) Position the excluder [25] evenly on the carrier with the spring facing down (toward the gland nut [17]). a) Zip ties can be used to help with this step. 5) Carefully slide the excluder [25] into position in it's carrier groove. 6) Make sure that you move the seal evenly down the carrier and do not allow it to roll over. 7) Make sure that the excluder stay in it's proper position until it reaches room temperature and has conformed to it's original shape. a) A compression ring can be used to lightly hold the excluder [25] in it's place until it reaches room temperature. SUBTASK 32-21-11-900-003 (4) Replace the active static seal [28] (Figure 803): CAUTION MAKE SURE THAT YOUR HANDS, TOOLS AND THE WORK AREA ARE CLEAN BEFORE YOU HANDLE THE ELASTOMER SEALS. SOME GREASES CAN CAUSE THE ELASTOMER SEALS TO SWELL. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY, SEAL LEAKS CAN OCCUR. (a) Remove the backup rings [29] from the active static seal [28]. (b) Remove the active static seal [28] from its groove on the lower bearing carrier [23]. EFFECTIVITY ALL CAUTION DO NOT APPLY VASELINE OR PETROLATUM TO THE SEALS. THIS CAN CAUSE THE SEAL MATERIAL TO BECOME LARGER. DAMAGE TO THE SEALS CAN OCCUR. (c) You may apply a very thin layer of fluid, D00467,or AFS-682 lubricant, D00589, to the new active static seal [28] and backup rings [29] to aid in keeping the rings in position during installation. NOTE: The material is a very thick, sticky material and heavy amounts can cause the bearing carrier to be difficult to re-install. 1) Use the minimum quantity of AFS-682 lubricant, D00589, necessary to keep the parts in position. 2) Remove excess AFS-682 lubricant, D00589. NOTE: Use of excess AFS-682 lubricant, D00589, can cause problems with assembly of the components. (d) Install the new active static seal [28] in its groove on the lower bearing carrier [23]. CAUTION MAKE SURE THE RADIUSED EDGE OF THE BACKUP RING IS INSTALLED AGAINST THE SEAL. IF NOT INSTALLED WITH THE RADIUSED EDGE AGAINST THE SEAL, THE SEALS WILL LEAK AFTER ASSEMBLY. (e) Install the first backup rings [29] on the active static seal [28] with the rounded edge of the backup rings [29] against the seal. (f) Install the second backup rings [29] with the split in the opposite positions on the diameter of the lower bearing carrier [23] as of the split of the first backup rings [29] installed. SUBTASK 32-21-11-900-004 (5) Replace the spare static seals [27]: CAUTION MAKE SURE THAT YOUR HANDS, TOOLS AND THE WORK AREA ARE CLEAN BEFORE YOU HANDLE THE ELASTOMER SEALS. SOME GREASES CAN CAUSE THE ELASTOMER SEALS TO SWELL. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY, SEAL LEAKS CAN OCCUR. (a) Install the new spare static seals [27] in its groove on the lower bearing carrier [23]. 1) Make sure that the spare static seal [27] is in the correct position (View A, Figure 803). SUBTASK 32-21-11-900-005 CAUTION MAKE SURE THAT THE BACKUP RING, THE CAP, AND THE SEAL STAY TOGETHER WHILE YOU INSTALL THE SEAL. IF THE BACKUP RING, THE CAP, AND THE SEAL MOVE APART, THEY WILL NOT INSTALL CORRECTLY. THIS CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE SEAL, THE CAP, AND THE BACKUP RING. (6) Replace the active dynamic seal: (a) Remove the cap seal [20], backup ring [21], and elastomer ring [19] from the inner groove on the lower bearing carrier [23]. EFFECTIVITY ALL CAUTION DO NOT APPLY VASELINE OR PETROLATUM TO THE SEALS. THIS CAN CAUSE THE SEAL MATERIAL TO BECOME LARGER. DAMAGE TO THE SEALS CAN OCCUR. (b) You may apply a thin layer of fluid, D00467, or AFS-682 lubricant, D00589, to the elastomer ring [19], cap seal [20], and backup ring [21] to aid in keeping the backup rings [21] in position during installation. NOTE: The material is a very thick, sticky material and heavy amounts can cause the bearing carrier to be difficult to re-install. 1) Use the minimum quantity of AFS-682 lubricant, D00589, necessary to keep the parts in position. 2) Remove excess AFS-682 lubricant, D00589. NOTE: Use of excess AFS-682 lubricant, D00589, can cause problems with assembly of the components. (c) The three parts of the active dynamic seal can be assembled on the inner cylinder [12] and then placed in the dynamic seal groove of the lower bearing carrier [23] or the parts can be installed in the groove one at a time. (d) Install the backup ring [21] of the new dynamic seal in the inner groove for the active dynamic seal. NOTE: The edge radius should be facing up and towards the elastomer ring. (e) Install the cap seal [20] in the inner groove for the active dynamic seal. (f) Install the elastomer ring [19] in its groove on the lower bearing carrier [23] (View B, Figure 803). NOTE: The wide seal edge is pointed toward the bottom of the lower bearing carrier. SUBTASK 32-21-11-900-008 (7) Replace the spare dynamic seal [26]: (a) Install a spare dynamic seal [26] if there is no spare dynamic seal in the spare seal groove on the lower bearing carrier [23]. (b) Install the spare dynamic seal backup ring [22] in the spare seal groove on the lower bearing carrier [23]. SUBTASK 32-21-11-420-021 (8) Install the seal retainer [18] or optional seal retainer [97] (seal retainer, C32016-55, SPL-23426): NOTE: You may use optional seal retainer to aid in properly installing the dynamic seal. (a) Put the seal retainer [18] in its position on the lower bearing carrier [23]. (b) Make sure that the seal retainer [18] is flush to the lower bearing carrier [23] all around the circumference before installing the bearing carrier pin [30] in place. NOTE: If the seal retainer is not flush, the active dynamic seal and backup rings may not be installed correctly. (c) You may apply a thin layer of AFS-682 lubricant, D00589, to the bearing carrier pin [30] to hold them in place while the lower bearing carrier [23] is re-installed into the outer cylinder [9]. NOTE: AFS-682 lubricant, D00589, will help keep the bearing carrier pins in position. EFFECTIVITY ALL 1) Use the minimum quantity of AFS-682 lubricant, D00589, needed to retain the pins. NOTE: The material is a very thick, sticky material and heavy amounts can cause the bearing carrier to be difficult to re-install. 2) Remove excess AFS-682 lubricant, D00589. CAUTION DO NOT FORCE THE RETENTION PINS INTO PLACE. THE PINS SHOULD FIT FREELY. FORCING THE PINS INTO PLACE CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE SEAL RETAINER. (d) Install the bearing carrier pins [30] to retain the seal retainer [18] to the lower bearing carrier [23]. 1) If the bearing carrier pin [30] are not free during installation, make sure that the seal retainer [18] is flush to the bearing carrier, then reinsert the pins. 2) If the seal retainer [18] is not flush, the active dynamic seal may have not been installed correctly. (e) Install the optional seal retainer [97] (seal retainer, C32016-55, SPL-23426). 1) Put the seal retainer [97] (seal retainer, C32016-55, SPL-23426) in its position on the lower bearing carrier [23]. 2) Install the retainer pin [94] (retainer pin, C32016-56, SPL-13125) to connect the seal retainer to the lower bearing carrier [23]. 3) Install the rubber band [95] (rubber band, C32016-58, SPL-13129) to hold the retainer pin [94] (retainer pin, C32016-56, SPL-13125) in position. SUBTASK 32-21-11-840-002 WARNING MAKE SURE A MINIMUM OF TWO PERSONS WILL HOLD THE INNER CYLINDER WHEN YOU DO THE SUBSEQUENT STEPS. THE INNER CYLINDER IS HEAVY. INJURY TO PERSONS OR DAMAGE TO THE EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR IF THE INNER CYLINDER IS NOT HELD PROPERLY. (9) Hold the inner cylinder [12] in a vertical position. SUBTASK 32-21-11-480-011 (10) Coat the dynamic seal guide [84] and lower bearing carrier [23] with fluid, D00467. SUBTASK 32-21-11-480-008 (11) Install the dynamic seal guide [84] at the top of the inner cylinder [12]. SUBTASK 32-21-11-420-022 (12) Install the lower bearing carrier [23]: NOTE: You can install the lower bearing carrier into the dynamic seal guide at the workbench and then install the dynamic seal guide with the lower bearing carrier onto the top of the cylinder. CAUTION MAKE SURE THAT THE BACKUP RINGS AND THE SEAL STAY TOGETHER WHEN YOU MOVE THE LOWER BEARING CARRIER. IF THE BACKUP RINGS AND THE SEAL MOVE APART, THEY WILL NOT INSTALL CORRECTLY. THIS CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE SEAL AND THE BACKUP RINGS. (a) Put the lower bearing carrier [23] in its position for installation on the inner cylinder [12]. EFFECTIVITY ALL (b) Use a rubber mallet and lightly hit the top of the lower bearing carrier [23] until it passes the dynamic seal guide [84]. (c) Move the lower bearing carrier [23] down to the bottom of the inner cylinder [12]. 1) Use ram assembly [96] (ram assembly, C32016-47, SPL-13126) as necessary to help install the lower bearing carrier [23] onto the inner cylinder [12]. 2) If you used optional seal retainer [97] for the installation, then remove the rubber band [95], retainer pin [94] and seal retainer [97]. 3) After removing the optional seal retainer [97], look down into the lower bearing carrier [23] and examine the dynamic seal. a) Make sure that the dynamic seal appears fully seated. 4) Install the production seal retainer [18] and bearing carrier pin [30] onto the lower bearing carrier [23]. SUBTASK 32-21-11-020-035 (13) Remove the dynamic seal guide [84] from the inner cylinder [12].

K. Inner Cylinder Components Assembly

SUBTASK 32-21-11-420-023 (1) Install the following items: (a) Install the lower centering cam [11] on the inner cylinder [12]. NOTE: There are two dowel pins loosely attached to the lower centering cam. These dowel pins must be aligned with the recesses inside the outer cylinder when you assemble the inner cylinder and outer cylinder assemblies in the subsequent steps. Align the centering cam dowel pins with the strut axle, or the gland nut lockable recesses on the outer cylinder to align the pins to the pin recesses. The dowel pins are designed to be loosely held in place with 0.005 in. (0.13 mm) - 0.015 in. (0.38 mm) dowel movement after the rivet is in place. (b) Put the upper centering cam dowels [89] in position on the inner cylinder [12] (Figure 804). 1) Make sure that each dowel is centered and flush in it's centering cam groove. NOTE: The dowels should also be positioned above the lip, on the inner cylinder, to allow the circlip to later move into it's installed position. (c) Put the dowel retaining circlip [88] approximately mid-point on the dowels [89] to hold the dowels [89] in position on the inner cylinder [12]. (d) Install the upper centering cam [10] on the inner cylinder [12]. 1) Carefully push the dowel retaining circlip [88] down the dowels [89], with the upper centering cam [10], until the dowels are in place in the upper centering cam [10]. NOTE: The dowel retaining circlip will snap over the bottom of the dowels into the circlip groove, that retains the dowels up inside the upper centering cam. (e) Install the upper bearing assembly [8] and recoil valve [87] on the inner cylinder [12]: 1) Install the ring [86] on the recoil valve [87], if it was removed. 2) Install the recoil valve [87] and ring [86] on top of the upper centering cam [10]. 3) Install the upper bearing halve [85] on the inner cylinder [12]. (f) Install the insert [8A] on the upper bearing halve [85]. EFFECTIVITY ALL 1) Use hand pressure to make an overlap of ¼ in. (6.4 mm) to the insert [8A] to keep its round shape. NOTE: This will keep the insert snug against the upper bearing halves. 2) Use the compressor assembly half [92] to hold the bearing closed during inner cylinder [12] installation. SUBTASK 32-21-11-420-024 CAUTION INSTALL THE COMPRESSOR ASSEMBLY BEFORE INSTALLATION OF THE INNER CYLINDER. DAMAGE TO THE THREADS OF THE OUTER CYLINDER AND THE UPPER BEARING ASSEMBLY CAN OCCUR WITHOUT THE TOOL. (2) Install the compressor assembly half [92]. (a) Install the compressor assembly half [92], such that it fits at the bottom of the outer cylinder [9]. (b) Install the strap assembly [75] around the outer cylinder [9] and connect the ends to the shoulder bolts on the side of the compressor assembly half [92]. 1) Tighten the strap assembly [75]. SUBTASK 32-21-11-420-014 CAUTION DO NOT LIFT THE AIRPLANE WITH THE AXLE JACK. DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR. (3) Install the inner cylinder [12] in the outer cylinder [9]: WARNING MAKE SURE A MINIMUM OF TWO PERSONS WILL HOLD THE INNER CYLINDER WHEN YOU DO THE SUBSEQUENT STEPS. THE INNER CYLINDER IS HEAVY. INJURY TO PERSONS OR DAMAGE TO THE EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR IF THE INNER CYLINDER IS NOT HELD PROPERLY. CAUTION BE CAREFUL NOT TO CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE INNER CYLINDER OR THE METERING PIN. DAMAGE TO THESE PARTS CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE SEALS. CAUTION MAKE SURE THE DOWEL PINS ON THE LOWER CENTERING CAM ARE ALIGNED WITH THE RECESSES IN THE OUTER CYLINDER. (a) Put the inner cylinder [12] in position to install in the outer cylinder [9]. NOTE: You can use the Centering Assembly C32016-35, or manually move the lower centering cam, to assist in aligning the lower centering cam dowel pins with the dowel pin recesses inside the outer cylinder. Align the dowel pins with the axle centerline or the gland nut tablock recesses on the outer cylinder. EFFECTIVITY ALL (b) Manually lift the inner cylinder [12], into the outer cylinder [9], until the top edge of the chrome surface of the inner cylinder [12] is level with the lower surface of the compressor assembly compressor assembly half [92]. NOTE: Use great care in installing the inner cylinder into the outer cylinder to keep from damaging the lower bearing carrier dowel pins that are loosely riveted to the carrier, and are easily caused to be detached from the carrier if acted upon with much force. (c) Use a floor jack to hold the inner cylinder [12] in position. SUBTASK 32-21-11-080-004 (4) Remove the compressor assembly half [92]: (a) Remove the strap assembly [75] from the outer cylinder [9] and compressor assembly half [92]. (b) Remove the compressor assembly half [92], from the outer cylinder [9]. SUBTASK 32-21-11-420-025 CAUTION MAKE SURE THAT THE DOWEL PINS ON THE LOWER CENTERING CAM ALIGN WITH THE GROOVES OF THE OUTER CYLINDER. IF NOT, DAMAGE CAN OCCUR. (5) Carefully put the thread protector insert [77] between the outer cylinder [9] and inner cylinder [12]. NOTE: The tread protector insert will expand and press against the outer cylinder, this will protect the static seals from the gland nut threads on the outer cylinder. SUBTASK 32-21-11-480-009 (6) Install the thread protector assembly [76]: (a) Install the thread protector assembly [76], so that it fits at the bottom of the outer cylinder [9]. (b) Install the strap assembly [75] around the outer cylinder [9] and connect the ends to the shoulder bolts on the side of the thread protector assembly [76]. 1) Tighten the strap assembly [75]. SUBTASK 32-21-11-480-010 (7) Install the seal puller assembly [73] around the inner cylinder [12] to support the bearing carrier. NOTE: You do not need to install the two puller screws, as the inner cylinder will push on the seal puller assembly and lower bearing carrier as the inner cylinder is pushed into place. The two plastic skid plates can be placed up right between the bearing carrier and scraper lock assembly to provide extra height to move the bearing carrier up into the outer cylinder. SUBTASK 32-21-11-580-008 CAUTION MAKE SURE THAT YOU HAVE THE DOWEL PINS ON THE LOWER CENTERING CAM ALIGNED WITH THE RECESSES IN THE OUTER CYLINDER OR THE AXLE CENTERLINE. IF NOT ALIGNED, IT CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE DOWEL PINS AND THE INNER CYLINDER. (8) Use two people to lift the inner cylinder assembly until you feel the dowels of the lower centering cam engage the grooves in the outer cylinder [9]. (b) Make sure that the static seals and backup rings stay in their positions as the lower bearing carrier [23] is installed. 1) You may apply a thin layer of fluid, D00467, or AFS-682 lubricant, D00589, to the elastomer ring [19], cap seal [20], and backup ring [21] to aid in keeping the backup rings in position during installation. NOTE: AFS-682 lubricant, D00589, will help keep the backup ring in its position. NOTE: The material is a very thick, tacky material and a large quantity can make the bearing carrier hard to install. 2) Use the minimum quantity of AFS-682 lubricant, D00589, necessary to keep the parts in their positions. 3) Remove unwanted AFS-682 lubricant, D00589. NOTE: If you apply too much AFS-682 lubricant, D00589, this can cause problems with assembly of the components. CAUTION DO NOT LET THE INNER CYLINDER TO LOWER WITHOUT THE THREAD PROTECTOR INSTALLED. DAMAGE TO THE SEALS CAN OCCUR. (c) Remove the thread protector assembly [76] when the lower surface of the lower bearing carrier [23], is aligned with the lower surface of the thread protector assembly [76]. NOTE: As you lift the inner cylinder, adjust the supporting jack to stay within ½ in. (13 mm) of the inner cylinder. SUBTASK 32-21-11-020-019 (9) Remove the puller assembly and skid plates. SUBTASK 32-21-11-020-020 (10) Remove the scraper retainer [79], and scraper lock scraper lock assembly, C32016-5 or -68, SPL-1379, from the gland nut [17]. (11) Apply a liberal amount of corrosion inhibiting material, G50136, to the threads of the gland nut [17] and to the threads of the outer cylinder [9]. (b) Wipe off excess corrosion inhibiting material, G50136, from the gland nut [17] and outer cylinder [9] joint after the gland nut installation is completed. SUBTASK 32-21-11-420-016 (13) Install the lockplate [16] for the gland nut [17] (Figure 802): WARNING USE NITRILE GLOVES FOR SKIN PROTECTION AGAINST CORROSION INHIBITOR MATERIAL, G50136. IF CORROSION INHIBITOR MATERIAL, G50136 GETS ON YOUR SKIN, IMMEDIATELY REMOVE IT WITH WATER. IF THIS MATERIAL GETS IN YOUR EYES, IMMEDIATELY FLUSH YOUR EYES WITH WATER AND GET MEDICAL AID. (c) Install the bolts [14] and washers [15]. (d) Tighten the bolts [14]. (e) Install MS20995C32 lockwire, G01048, on the bolts [14] (TASK 20-10-44-400-801). 32-21-11-960-803Scraper Ring ReplacementPDF p. 776

4. Scraper Ring Replacement (Figure 802, Figure 803)

A. General

(1) This task is used when the scraper ring is damaged and replacement is necessary but removal of the inner cylinder is not possible. (2) It is acceptable to operate the aircraft with a missing section of the energizer ring or other damage to the scraper ring. The scraper ring should be replaced with a new solid scraper ring or split scraper ring at the earliest maintenance opportunity to avoid excessive damage to the dynamic seal. If you do not have a split scraper ring available, you can cut a solid scraper ring or the damaged scraper ring to re-install it. NOTE: The installation of a split scraper ring is also a temporary repair and should be replaced when the nose landing gear is disassembled for other maintenance or overhaul.

SUBTASK 32-21-11-710-007 WARNING MAKE SURE THAT THE AREA BELOW THE AIRPLANE IS CLEAR OF PERSONNEL AND EQUIPMENT BEFORE YOU INFLATE OR DEFLATE THE SHOCK STRUT. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY, IT CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONNEL OR DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT. (3) Deflate the shock strut [4] for the nose landing gear. (a) Remove the cap assembly [1] for the gas valve [2] that is on the top of the shock strut [4]. WARNING DO NOT REMOVE THE VALVE BODY UNTIL YOU DEFLATE THE SHOCK STRUT FULLY. THE AIR PRESSURE CAN BLOW THE VALVE BODY OUT AND CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONNEL. (b) Loosen the swivel nut [3] a maximum of two turns. NOTE: Fluid in the shock strut can have bubbles when you release the pressure. 1) Deflate the shock strut [4] slowly to prevent the leakage of the fluid through the gas valve [2]. (c) Loosen the swivel nut [3] fully when all of the pressure in the shock strut [4] is released. NOTE: The shock strut is fully deflated when the dimension "X" is 13.9 in. (353 mm). SUBTASK 32-21-11-170-001 (4) Drain the hydraulic fluid from the shock strut [4]. (a) Remove the cap assembly [5] from the oil charging valve [6]. (b) Put a 5 gallon (19 liter) hydraulic fluid resistant container, STD-1110, in a position to catch the hydraulic fluid when the oil charging valve [6] is opened. (c) Install the drain equipment on the oil charging valve [6]. NOTE: The landing gear shock strut drain valve, SPL-1829, could also be used, but it will take much longer to drain the shock strut. 1) Cut a length of plastic tubing, sufficiently long to reach the container on the floor. 2) Insert a small allen wrench in the end of the length of tubing so that the long end of the allen wrench is flush with the end of the tube and the short end goes through the wall of the tube. 3) Install the tubing on the oil charging valve [6] so that the allen wrench goes into the check valve and holds it open to drain the hydraulic fluid. EFFECTIVITY ALL (d) Remove the drain equipment when you have removed all of the hydraulic fluid. 32-21-11-200-801Nose Landing Gear Shock Strut Seal Leakage CheckPDF p. 781

5. Nose Landing Gear Shock Strut Seal Leakage Check (Figure 801, Figure 802, Figure 803)

A. General

(1) This task gives the instructions to make sure that a shock strut is serviceable when you find fluid leakage on the inner cylinder. NOTE: During the initial landing cycles of a new landing gear it is usual to have hydraulic fluid streaks on the shock strut. These streaks are caused by hydraulic fluid applied to the shock strut seals during seal installation and will stop after more landing cycles occur. These streaks are different from the actual continuous drips that are the indication of shock strut seal leakage.

B. References

Reference Title 05-51-37-200-806 Phase I Inspection (P/B 201) 09-11-00-580-801 Maintenance Towing (P/B 201) 12-15-41-610-801 Nose Landing Gear Shock Strut Fluid Check (P/B 301) 12-21-21-640-802 Nose Landing Gear Lower End Components Servicing (P/B 301) 32-00-01-480-801 Landing Gear Downlock Pins Installation (P/B 201)

C. Location Zones

Zone Area 113 Area Above and Outboard of Nose Landing Gear Wheel Well - Left 114 Area Above and Outboard of Nose Landing Gear Wheel Well - Right 711 Nose Landing Gear Door - Left

D. Shock Strut Seal Leak Inspection

NOTE: If the inspection finds a fault on the scraper ring you must replace the damaged scraper ring. NOTE: The inner cylinder must be removed from the outer cylinder shock strut to replace the scraper ring. EFFECTIVITY ALL SUBTASK 32-21-11-480-004 WARNING MAKE SURE THE DOWNLOCK PINS ARE INSTALLED ON ALL THE LANDING GEAR. WITHOUT THE DOWNLOCK PINS, THE LANDING GEAR CAN RETRACT AND CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT. (1) If the downlock pins are not installed in the nose and main landing gear, do this task: Landing Gear Downlock Pins Installation, TASK 32-00-01-480-801. SUBTASK 32-21-11-210-001 (2) Inspect the shock struts for leakage. SUBTASK 32-21-11-210-002 (3) If you find leakage of the shock strut fluid on the inner cylinder, do the steps that follow to make sure that the shock strut is serviceable: (a) Check for leaks for 5 minutes: 1) Wipe the surface of the inner cylinder with a clean cloth to remove all of the fluid from the leak. 2) Monitor the inner cylinder where it touches the outer cylinder for 5 minutes. NOTE: Make sure that the extension of the inner cylinder does not change during this time. 3) Make a record of the location and the number of drops which come from the seals during the 5 minutes. (b) Tow the airplane to cause movement between the inner cylinder and the outer cylinder, do this task: Maintenance Towing, TASK 09-11-00-580-801. NOTE: The minimum distance the airplane must be moved is two airplane lengths. (c) Check for leaks for 5 minutes: 1) Wipe the surface of the inner cylinder with a clean cloth to remove all of the fluid from the leak. 2) Monitor the inner cylinder where it touches the outer cylinder for 5 minutes. NOTE: Make sure that the extension of the inner cylinder does not change during this time. 3) Make a record of the location and the number of drops which come from the seals during the 5 minutes. (d) Calculate the average of the number of drops which came from the seals during both of the 5 minute measurements. SUBTASK 32-21-11-210-003 (4) If the leakage stopped, do the steps that follow: (a) Continue to monitor the strut for leakage on subsequent landings. 1) If you see more signs of leakage, do the entire leak check procedure again. a) If you find a continuous leakage flow on subsequent landings, the shock strut [4] is not serviceable. EFFECTIVITY ALL CAUTION IF THE AIRPLANE MADE A LANDING WITH A DEFLATED OR FLAT STRUT, DO THE HARD LANDING INSPECTION. MAKE SURE THAT NO DAMAGE OCCURRED. A DEFLATED OR FLAT STRUT CAN CAUSE DAMAGE DURING A LANDING. 2) If you do not find leakage on subsequent landings, continue to examine the fluid level of the shock strut [4]. a) You must examine the fluid level in less than 3 days or 10 flight cycles, (Nose Landing Gear Shock Strut Fluid Check, TASK 12-15-41-610-801). b) If the nose landing gear shock strut [4] has low pressure or is deflated, do this task: Phase I Inspection, TASK 05-51-37-200-806. SUBTASK 32-21-11-210-004 (5) If there was leakage but the average was less than 20 drops during the two 5 minute periods, do the steps that follow: NOTE: 20 drops is equal to 1.0 cc. (a) Continue to monitor the strut for leakage on subsequent landings until you replace the seals. 1) If the leakage continues or increases, do the entire seal leak check procedure again. CAUTION IF THE AIRPLANE MADE A LANDING WITH A DEFLATED OR FLAT STRUT, DO THE HARD LANDING INSPECTION. MAKE SURE THAT NO DAMAGE OCCURRED. A DEFLATED OR FLAT STRUT CAN CAUSE DAMAGE DURING A LANDING. (b) If you do not find leakage on subsequent landings, examine the fluid level of the shock strut within 3 days or 10 flight cycles, (TASK 12-15-41-610-801). 1) If the nose landing gear shock strut has low pressure or is deflated, do this task: Phase I Inspection, TASK 05-51-37-200-806. (c) Continue to monitor the fluid level of the shock strut at no more than 3 day or 10 flight cycle intervals, until you replace the seals, (TASK 12-15-41-610-801). SUBTASK 32-21-11-210-005 (6) If the average leakage was more than 20 drops during the two 5 minute periods, but was not continuous, do the steps that follow: NOTE: 20 drops is equal to 1.0 cc. CAUTION IF THE AIRPLANE MADE A LANDING WITH A DEFLATED OR FLAT STRUT, DO THE HARD LANDING INSPECTION. MAKE SURE THAT NO DAMAGE OCCURRED. A DEFLATED OR FLAT STRUT CAN CAUSE DAMAGE DURING A LANDING. (a) Do this task: Nose Landing Gear Shock Strut Fluid Check, TASK 12-15-41-610-801. 1) If the nose landing gear shock strut has low pressure or is deflated, do this task: Phase I Inspection, TASK 05-51-37-200-806. (b) Continue to monitor the fluid level of the shock strut after each flight until you replace the seals. EFFECTIVITY ALL SUBTASK 32-21-11-210-006 (7) If the fluid leaked continuously during the 5 minute period, the shock strut is not serviceable and you must replace the shock strut seals.

D. Nose Gear Tow Fitting and Tow Fitting Bolt Installation

SUBTASK 32-21-14-916-001 (1) If the tow fitting bolt [1] installation is necessary, do these steps: WARNING USE NITRILE GLOVES FOR SKIN PROTECTION WHEN YOU USE COR￾BAN 27L. IF IT GETS ON YOUR SKIN, IMMEDIATELY REMOVE IT WITH WATER. IF THIS MATERIAL GETS IN YOUR EYES, IMMEDIATELY FLUSH YOUR EYES WITH WATER. GET MEDICAL AID. THIS MATERIAL CONTAINS FLAMMABLE AGENTS WHICH CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONNEL. (a) Apply a thin coat of Cor-Ban 27L Compound, G50237 or corrosion inhibiting material, G50136 (alternate) to the shank of the unplated bolt, bolt threads and thread reliefs of the bolt [1], and to the faces of the washer [2] and washer [5] prior to installation. Wipe off the excess. (b) Insert the tow fitting bolt [1] into the washer [2] and then into the tow fitting assembly [11]. (c) Install the washer [5] and the nut [6] to connect the tow fitting bolt [1] to the tow fitting assembly [11]. (d) Tighten the nut to 160 in-lb (18 N·m) to 190 in-lb (21 N·m) above run-on torque and back off to align the nearest castellation. (e) Install the pin [7]. (f) Lubricate the two lube fittings [12] with grease, D00633, or alternate grease, D00013. SUBTASK 32-21-14-916-002 (2) Do the steps that follow to install the tow fitting assembly [11] on the inner cylinder assembly: EFFECTIVITY ALL WARNING USE NITRILE GLOVES FOR SKIN PROTECTION WHEN YOU USE COR￾BAN 27L. IF IT GETS ON YOUR SKIN, IMMEDIATELY REMOVE IT WITH WATER. IF THIS MATERIAL GETS IN YOUR EYES, IMMEDIATELY FLUSH YOUR EYES WITH WATER. GET MEDICAL AID. THIS MATERIAL CONTAINS FLAMMABLE AGENTS WHICH CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONNEL. (a) Apply a thin coat of Cor-Ban 27L Compound, G50237 or corrosion inhibiting material, G50136 (alternate) to the shank of the unplated bolts [3], the bolt threads and bolt reliefs, and to the faces of the washer [4] and washer [10] prior to installation. Wipe off the excess Cor-Ban 27L Compound, G50237. (b) Hold the tow fitting assembly [11] in position. (c) Install the bolts [3] into the washers [4] and then into the tow fitting assembly [11]. (d) Install the washers [10], the nuts [9] to the bolts [3]. (e) Install self-locking nuts [9] and tighten the nuts [9] to within the torque range of 250 in-lb (28 N·m) to 300 in-lb (34 N·m) above the run-on torque. NOTE: If installation had a cotter pin, the cotter pin may be discarded. Do not back-off the self locking nuts after torquing. NOTE: The Aircraft Illustrated Parts Catalog (AIPC) lists bolts and nuts which are acceptable for use in the tow fitting to outer cylinder installation, however for best results use non-castellated nuts and bolts without cotter pin holes for the installation. NOTE: If a BACN10JC self-locking nut is used on a bolt that has a hole for a cotter pin, it is recommended that the nut not be used again after removal. The edges of the hole will make the self-locking feature unserviceable.

E. Put the airplane back to its usual condition.

E. Nose Landing Gear Drag Strut Removal

SUBTASK 32-21-21-020-002 (1) If necessary, disconnect the hydraulic hose [53] (UP-hose) and hydraulic hose [52] (DOWN-hose) connections from the rod end of the retract actuator [3]. NOTE: These steps are only necessary if the retract actuator will be removed. (a) Disconnect the hydraulic hose [53] (UP-hose) at the bracket on the retract actuator [3]. (b) Disconnect the hydraulic hose [52] (DOWN-hose) at the fitting on the retract actuator [3]. (c) Install the caps on the hydraulic hose [52] (DOWN-hose), hydraulic hose [53] (UP-hose), and fittings on the retract actuator [3]. ALL; AIRPLANES WITH OLD PIN ASSEMBLIES SUBTASK 32-21-21-020-003 (2) Disconnect the rod end of the retract actuator [3]. (a) Remove the cotter pin [50] from the bolt [16]. (b) Remove the nut [12] and washer [14] from the bolt [16]. (c) Remove the bolt [16] from the pin [9]. (d) Remove the nut [15] and washer [11] from the pin [9]. (e) Remove the pin [9] that holds the rod end of the retract actuator [3] and washers [18] from the upper drag strut [17]. ALL; AIRPLANES WITH NEW PIN ASSEMBLIES SUBTASK 32-21-21-020-014 (3) Disconnect the rod end of the retract actuator [3]. (a) Remove the nuts [46], washers [45], washers [44], bolts [43], and retainer [47] from the pin [48]. (b) Remove the pin [48] that holds the rod end of the retract actuator [3] and washers [18] from the upper drag strut [17]. ALL SUBTASK 32-21-21-020-004 (4) Disconnect the forward lock link [20]. NOTE: This step will also disconnect the lower drag strut from the upper drag strut. (a) Remove the cotter pin [13] from the bolt [22]. (b) Remove the nut [25] and washer [24] from the bolt [22]. (c) Remove the bolt [22] from the pin [19]. (d) Remove the nut [23] and washer [21] from the pin [19]. (e) Remove the pin [19] to disconnect the forward lock link [20] from the upper drag strut [17] and lower drag strut [10]. EFFECTIVITY ALL SUBTASK 32-21-21-020-005 WARNING MAKE SURE THAT YOU FULLY EXTEND THE SHOCK STRUT FOR THE NOSE LANDING GEAR BEFORE YOU DISCONNECT THE DRAG STRUT. IF YOU DO NOT FULLY EXTEND THE SHOCK STRUT, IT CAN MOVE QUICKLY AND CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONNEL AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT. (5) Disconnect the lower drag strut [10] from the shock strut [29]. (a) Remove the cotter pin [26] from the bolt [28]. (b) Remove the nut [33] and washer [32] from the bolt [28]. (c) Remove the bolt [28] from the pin [30]. (d) Remove the nut [27] and washer [31] from the pin [30]. (e) Remove the pin [30] that holds the lower drag strut [10] from the shock strut [29]. SUBTASK 32-21-21-480-003 (6) Use the retention strap, SPL-1871, to hold the shock strut [29] in the compressed position. SUBTASK 32-21-21-020-006 (7) Disconnect the upper drag strut [17] from the bracket [51]. NOTE: This step will also remove the bracket, that contains the down position sensor target. Keep the bracket for the installation procedure. (a) Remove the nut [34] and washer [35] from the bolt [36]. (b) Remove the bolt [36] and washer [35] to disconnect the upper drag strut [17] from the bracket [51]. (c) Remove the washer [35] from the bolt [36]. SUBTASK 32-21-21-020-007 (8) Remove the right trunnion pin [1] and left trunnion pin [2]. (a) Remove the cotter pin [38] from the bolt [40]. (b) Remove the nut [37] and washer [39] from bolt [40]. (c) Remove the bolt [40] that hold the right trunnion pin [1] and left trunnion pin [2] to the sidewall of the nose wheel well. (d) Remove the right trunnion pin [1] and left trunnion pin [2] to disconnect the upper drag strut [17] from the sidewall of the nose wheel well. NOTE: Use the Drag Strut Trunnion Pin puller, C32033-5, SPL-14478, and slide hammer, C32033-22, with slide screw, C32033-21, SPL-14479, to remove the trunnion pins from inboard side of the upper drag strut. ALL; AIRPLANES WITH PACKING PART NUMBER MS29513-031 OR MS29513-033 (e) Remove and discard the packing [42]. ALL SUBTASK 32-21-21-020-008 (9) Remove the upper drag strut [17] from the airplane.

SUBTASK 32-21-21-420-006 (17) If the retract actuator was removed, connect the hydraulic hose [52] (DOWN-hose) and hydraulic hose [53] (UP-hose) to the retract actuator [3]. (a) Tighten the B-nut on the hydraulic hose [52] (DOWN-hose) to 256.5 in-lb (29.0 N·m) - 283.5 in-lb (32.0 N·m). (b) Tighten the B-nut on the hydraulic hose [53] (UP-hose) to 133 in-lb (15.0 N·m) - 147 in-lb (16.6 N·m). (c) If it is necessary for the hydraulic hose [53] (UP-hose), install the clamp [7], screws [5], and washers [6] at the bracket to attach the tube [8] and reducer [4]. SUBTASK 32-21-21-720-001 (18) Do a post installation check of the nose landing gear down position sensor (TASK 32-61-51-400-801). NOTE: This step is necessary because the bracket, that contains the down position sensor target, was removed. EFFECTIVITY ALL

2. Nose Landing Gear Drag Strut Inspection

A. General

(1) This procedure give wear limits and repair data for the drag strut of the nose landing gear.

B. References

Reference Title 32-00-01-480-801 Landing Gear Downlock Pins Installation (P/B 201) 32-21-21-000-801 Nose Landing Gear Drag Strut Removal (P/B 401) SRM 53-10-90 Allowable Damage 1

C. Location Zones

Zone Area 115 Nose Landing Gear Wheel Well - Left 116 Nose Landing Gear Wheel Well - Right 713 Nose Landing Gear

D. Procedure

SUBTASK 32-21-21-480-004 WARNING MAKE SURE THE DOWNLOCK PINS ARE INSTALLED ON ALL THE LANDING GEAR. WITHOUT THE DOWNLOCK PINS, THE LANDING GEAR COULD RETRACT AND CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT. (1) If the downlock pins are not installed on all the landing gear, do this task: Landing Gear Downlock Pins Installation, TASK 32-00-01-480-801. SUBTASK 32-21-21-020-009 (2) Examine the upper drag brace bushings for these forms of damage: NOTE: It is not necessary to remove the nose landing gear drag brace strut assembly for a visual inspection for the following conditions: (a) corrosion (b) cracks in bushing or fillet seal (c) scratches along the rim of the bushing SUBTASK 32-21-21-410-001 (3) Use a feeler gage to check for 0.156 in. (3.962 mm) to 0.200 in. (5.080 mm) clearance between the structure support bushings and the nose landing gear drag strut upper trunnion bushings assemblies. NOTE: To have satisfactory results the feeler gage must display smooth transition while being installed or removed. (a) If the feeler gage can be installed and removed without force the check is satisfactory. EFFECTIVITY ALL (b) If the check is satisfactory, put the airplane back to its usual condition. (c) If the bushing display damage or smooth transition of the feeler gage can not be satisfied, do this task: Nose Landing Gear Drag Strut Removal, TASK 32-21-21-000-801. SUBTASK 32-21-21-200-001 (4) Refer to SRM 53-10-90 for the inspection and removal of damage to the nose landing gear drag strut fittings.

E. Prepare for the Removal

SUBTASK 32-21-24-480-001 WARNING MAKE SURE THAT THE DOWNLOCK PINS ARE INSTALLED ON ALL THE LANDING GEAR. WITHOUT THE DOWNLOCK PINS, THE LANDING GEAR CAN RETRACT. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONS, AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT. (1) If the downlock pins are not installed in the Nose Landing Gear (NLG) and Main Landing Gear (MLG), do this task: Landing Gear Downlock Pins Installation, TASK 32-00-01-480-801. EFFECTIVITY ALL SUBTASK 32-21-24-860-001 (2) For hydraulic system A, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Power Removal, TASK 29-11-00-860-805. SUBTASK 32-21-24-020-001 WARNING MAKE SURE THAT THE AREA BELOW THE AIRPLANE IS CLEAR OF PERSONNEL AND EQUIPMENT BEFORE YOU INFLATE OR DEFLATE THE SHOCK STRUT. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY, IT CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONNEL OR DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT. (3) Deflate the shock strut [4] for the NLG: (a) Remove the cap assembly [1] for the gas valve [2] which is on the top of the shock strut [4]. WARNING DO NOT REMOVE THE VALVE BODY UNTIL YOU DEFLATE THE SHOCK STRUT FULLY. THE AIR PRESSURE CAN BLOW THE VALVE BODY OUT AND CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONNEL. (b) Loosen the swivel nut [3] a maximum of two turns. NOTE: Fluid in the shock strut can have bubbles when you release the pressure. 1) Deflate the shock strut slowly to prevent the leakage of the fluid through the gas valve [2]. (c) Loosen the swivel nut [3] fully when all of the pressure in the shock strut [4] is released. NOTE: The shock strut is fully deflated when the dimension "X" is 13.9 in. (353 mm). SUBTASK 32-21-24-680-001 (4) Drain the hydraulic fluid from the shock strut [4]: NOTE: Very little fluid will come out. (a) Remove the cap assembly [5] from the oil charging valve [6]. (b) Put a 5 gallon (19 liter) hydraulic fluid resistant container, STD-1110, in a position to catch the hydraulic fluid when the oil charging valve [6] is opened. (c) Install the drain equipment on the oil charging valve [6]: NOTE: The tool, landing gear shock strut drain valve, SPL-1829, could also be used, but it will take much longer to drain the shock strut. 1) Cut a length of plastic tubing, long enough to reach the container on the floor. 2) Insert a small allen wrench in the end of the length of tubing, such that the long end of the allen wrench is flush with the end of the tube and the short end penetrates the wall of the tube. 3) Install the tubing on the oil charging valve [6] such that the allen wrench goes into the check valve and holds it open to drain the hydraulic fluid. (d) Remove the drain equipment when you have removed all of the hydraulic fluid. SUBTASK 32-21-24-580-001 (5) Lift the nose of the airplane until the shock strut [4] extends approximately 10 in. (254 mm), do this task: Lift the Airplane Nose with the Nose Jack at Jack Point D, TASK 07-11-21-580-801. EFFECTIVITY ALL 006, 007, 013, 014, 018-020, 043, 044, 056-063, 067-078, 081, 083-103, 111-114, 121-129, 131, 132, 135, 138-169, 174-179, 182-187, 189-203, 205-209, 212-220, 223, 224, 231-236, 239-298, 301-304, 306, 308, 315-317, 322-341, 343, 346-369 SUBTASK 32-21-24-020-005 (6) Remove the screw [28], washer [26], washer [27], and the nut [25] to disconnect the clamp from the taxi light assembly. (a) Disconnect the clamp with the electrical conduit attached. SUBTASK 32-21-24-020-024 (7) Remove the taxi light and housing (PAGEBLOCK 33-45-01/201). ALL SUBTASK 32-21-24-020-025 (8) Remove the tow fitting (TASK 32-21-14-000-801). SUBTASK 32-21-24-020-026 (9) Remove the NLG wheel and tire (TASK 32-45-21-000-801). 006, 007, 013, 014, 018-020, 043, 044, 056-063, 067-078, 081, 083-103, 111-114, 121-129, 131, 132, 135, 138-169, 174-179, 182-187, 189-203, 205-209, 212-220, 223, 224, 231-236, 239-298, 301-304, 306, 308, 315-317, 322-341, 343, 346-369 SUBTASK 32-21-24-020-006 (10) Remove the nut [29], and the washer [30] to disconnect the clamp from the inner cylinder [14]. (a) Disconnect the clamp with the electrical conduit attached. SUBTASK 32-21-24-020-007 (11) Remove the screw [50], washer [51], and the nut [52] to disconnect the clamp from the lower torsion link [53]. (a) Disconnect the clamp with the electrical conduit attached. SUBTASK 32-21-24-800-001 (12) Attach the electrical conduits, box assembly [32], and the wire harness plug for the taxi light to the outer cylinder [9] so that it is not in the way. ALL SUBTASK 32-21-24-020-009 (13) Do this task: Nose Landing Gear Lower Torsion Link Removal, TASK 32-21-31-000-802.

F. Inner Cylinder Removal

SUBTASK 32-21-24-020-010 (1) Disconnect the gland nut [18] from the outer cylinder [9] (Figure 401): (a) Remove the bolt [15], washer [16], and the lockplate [17] to release the gland nut [18]. (b) Use the gland nut wrench, SPL-1867, to disconnect the gland nut [18] from the outer cylinder [9]. 1) Keep the gland nut [18] in its position against the outer cylinder [9] after you have disconnected it from the outer cylinder [9]. SUBTASK 32-21-24-580-002 (2) Lift the nose of the airplane until there is enough room to install the scraper retainer, C32016-4 or -67, SPL-1378 [61] and the scraper lock assembly, C32016-5 or -68, SPL-1379 [56] on the gland nut [18], do this task: Lift the Airplane Nose with the Nose Jack at Jack Point D, TASK 07-11-21-580-801. EFFECTIVITY ALL SUBTASK 32-21-24-480-002 (3) Install the scraper retainer, C32016-4 or -67, SPL-1378 [61] and the scraper lock assembly, C32016-5 or -68, SPL-1379 [56] on the gland nut [18]. NOTE: This will make sure that the scraper ring for the gland nut does not come out of its groove. (a) Install the scraper retainer, C32016-4 or -67, SPL-1378 [61] on the gland nut [18]. (b) Install the scraper lock assembly, C32016-5 or -68, SPL-1379 [56] to hold the scraper retainer, C32016-4 or -67, SPL-1378 [61] in its position on the gland nut [18]. SUBTASK 32-21-24-020-011 (4) Move the gland nut [18] down at the inner cylinder [14]. (a) If the scraper ring [21] comes out of its groove, use the scraper plunger, C32016-2, SPL-1376 [62] and the scraper reducer, C32016-3, SPL-1377 [63] to install the scraper ring [21] back in its groove. SUBTASK 32-21-24-020-012 (5) Move the lower bearing carrier [20]: (a) Loosely install the seal puller assembly, C32016-6, SPL-4047 [55] around the inner cylinder [14]. (b) Push the seal puller assembly, C32016-6, SPL-4047 [55] up, such that it will install correctly at the bottom of the outer cylinder [9]. (c) Align the holes in the seal puller assembly, C32016-6, SPL-4047 [55] with the holes in the lower bearing carrier [20] for the puller screws [60]. (d) Install the carrier puller screws [60] to hold the seal puller assembly, C32016-6, SPL-4047 [55] to the lower bearing carrier [20]. (e) Tighten the retainer screws on each side of the seal puller assembly, C32016-6, SPL-4047 [55]. (f) Install the strap assy, C32017-60, SPL-3927 [57] around the axle and connect the ends to the shoulder bolts on each side of the seal puller assembly, C32016-6, SPL-4047 [55]. SUBTASK 32-21-24-580-003 (6) Lift the airplane until the lower bearing carrier [20] is completely out of the outer cylinder [9], (TASK 07-11-21-580-801). SUBTASK 32-21-24-020-013 (7) Remove the inner cylinder [14] from the outer cylinder [9]: (a) Remove the downlock pin from the NLG, do this task: Landing Gear Downlock Pins Removal, TASK 32-00-01-080-801. WARNING DO NOT PUT A PLUG IN THE OPEN PORTS OF THE RETRACT ACTUATOR. THE HYDRAULIC LINES CAN BREAK AND CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS OR DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT. (b) Disconnect the hydraulic lines from the retract actuator (TASK 32-21-21-000-801). (c) Push up on the lock link to move it from the locked overcenter position. (d) Optional: Connect a hydraulic pump to the retract actuator. NOTE: The pressure line from the pump must be connected to the Up port of the actuator. The return line to the pump must be connected to the Down port of the actuator. EFFECTIVITY ALL WARNING HOLD THE INNER CYLINDER WITH A ROPE BEFORE YOU CONNECT OR DISCONNECT THE CYLINDERS. IF YOU DO NOT HOLD THE INNER CYLINDER IN ITS POSITION, IT WILL FALL. THE INNER CYLINDER IS HEAVY AND CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONNEL OR DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT. CAUTION BE CAREFUL NOT TO CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE INNER CYLINDER OR THE METERING PIN. DAMAGE TO THESE PARTS CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE SEALS. (e) Slowly apply pressure to the retract actuator to remove the inner cylinder [14] from the outer cylinder [9]. This will move the NLG forward. (f) Remove the inner cylinder [14]. SUBTASK 32-21-24-840-001 WARNING MAKE SURE THAT A MINIMUM OF TWO PERSONS WILL HOLD THE INNER CYLINDER WHEN YOU DO THE SUBSEQUENT STEPS. THE INNER CYLINDER IS HEAVY. INJURY TO PERSONS OR DAMAGE TO THE EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR. (8) Hold the inner cylinder [14] in a vertical position. SUBTASK 32-21-24-040-001 (9) Move the control lever for the landing gear to OFF. NOTE: This will release the hydraulic pressure from the lock actuator of the NLG.

G. Remove the Components From the Inner Cylinder

NOTE: Do these steps if the inner cylinder you will install does not have these components installed. SUBTASK 32-21-24-020-014 (1) Remove the metering pin [11] from the inner cylinder [14]: (a) Use the metering pin and retainer ring equipment, SPL-1895, to remove the nut [12] and the retaining ring [67] from the inner cylinder [14]. (b) Remove the metering pin [11] from the inner cylinder [14]. (c) Remove the ring assembly [75] from the metering pin [11]. SUBTASK 32-21-24-020-015 (2) Remove the upper bearing carrier [68] and the recoil valve assembly from the top of the inner cylinder [14]: (a) Remove the upper bearing [8] from the upper bearing carrier [68]. NOTE: Pull the bearing apart slightly and slide it up and off the upper bearing carrier. (b) Remove the upper bearing carrier [68] halves from the inner cylinder [14]. (c) Remove the recoil valve ring [69]. (d) Remove the recoil valve [70] from the upper centering cam [10]. SUBTASK 32-21-24-020-016 (3) Remove the upper centering cam [10] and lower centering cam [13] from the inner cylinder [14]. (a) Remove the dowel retaining circlip [71] and the dowel [72] from the inner cylinder [14]. EFFECTIVITY ALL SUBTASK 32-21-24-020-017 (4) Remove the lower bearing carrier [20] from the inner cylinder [14]: (a) Use rubber mallet and lightly hit the bottom of the seal puller assembly, C32016-6, SPL-4047 [55] until the lower bearing carrier [20] can be pulled out off the top of the inner cylinder [14]. NOTE: The lower bearing carrier is coated with a dry lube film. The film may be worn and appear uneven, this is not cause for bearing carrier replacement. (b) Remove the puller screw [60] to disconnect the seal puller assembly, C32016-6, SPL-4047 [55] from the lower bearing carrier [20]. (c) Remove the seal puller assembly, C32016-6, SPL-4047 [55] from the lower bearing carrier [20]. (d) Put the lower bearing carrier [20] on a table or bench. SUBTASK 32-21-24-020-018 (5) Remove the seal retainer [19]: (a) Remove the bearing carrier pin [22] for the seal retainer [19]. (b) Move the seal retainer [19] away from the lower bearing carrier [20] to get access to the active dynamic seal. SUBTASK 32-21-24-900-001 (6) Install a new scraper ring [21] on the gland nut [18] if there is any sign of damage or wear on the old scraper ring [21]: NOTE: The scraper ring prevents dirt and debris from entering the shock strut when the inner and outer cylinder compress. (a) Remove the gland nut [18] from the inner cylinder [14]. (b) Remove the scraper retainer, C32016-4 or -67, SPL-1378 [61] and the scraper lock assembly, C32016-5 or -68, SPL-1379 [56] from the gland nut [18]. (c) Remove the old scraper ring [21] in its groove on the gland nut [18]. (d) Install the new scraper ring [21] in its groove on the gland nut [18]. (e) Make sure that you use the correct scraper configuration to be installed in its groove on the gland nut [18]. NOTE: There are two possible scraper configurations used for installation (Figure 401).

F. Install the Components on the Inner Cylinder

NOTE: Do these steps if the inner cylinder you will install does not have these components installed. SUBTASK 32-21-24-420-001 (1) Install the gland nut [18] on the inner cylinder [14]. (a) If the scraper ring [21] comes out of its groove, use the scraper plunger, C32016-2, SPL-1376 [62] and scraper reducer, C32016-3, SPL-1377 [63], to install the scraper ring [21] back in its groove. SUBTASK 32-21-24-420-002 (2) Install the seal retainer [19]: (a) Put the seal retainer [19] in its position on the lower bearing carrier [20]. (b) Align the pin holes in the seal retainer [19] with the pin holes in the lower bearing carrier [20]. (c) Install the bearing carrier pins [22] to connect the seal retainer [19] to the lower bearing carrier [20]. EFFECTIVITY ALL SUBTASK 32-21-24-840-002 WARNING MAKE SURE THAT A MINIMUM OF TWO PERSONS WILL HOLD THE INNER CYLINDER WHEN YOU DO THE SUBSEQUENT STEPS. THE INNER CYLINDER IS HEAVY. INJURY TO PERSONS OR DAMAGE TO THE EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR. (3) Hold the inner cylinder [14] in a vertical position. SUBTASK 32-21-24-480-003 (4) Install the dynamic seal guide, C32016-45, SPL-1382 [66], at the top of the inner cylinder [14]. SUBTASK 32-21-24-420-003 (5) Install the lower bearing carrier [20]: CAUTION MAKE SURE THAT THE BACKUP RINGS AND THE SEAL STAY TOGETHER WHEN YOU MOVE THE LOWER BEARING CARRIER. IF THE BACKUP RINGS AND THE SEAL MOVE APART, THEY WILL NOT INSTALL CORRECTLY. THIS CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE SEAL AND THE BACKUP RINGS. (a) Put the lower bearing carrier [20] in its position for installation on the inner cylinder [14]. (b) Use rubber mallet and lightly hit the top of the lower bearing carrier [20] until it passes the dynamic seal guide, C32016-45, SPL-1382 [66]. (c) Move the lower bearing carrier [20] down to the bottom of the inner cylinder [14]. SUBTASK 32-21-24-020-019 (6) Remove the dynamic seal guide, C32016-45, SPL-1382 [66], from the inner cylinder [14]. SUBTASK 32-21-24-420-004 (7) Install the following items: (a) Install the lower centering cam [13] on the inner cylinder [14]. (b) Install the dowels [72] in their position on the inner cylinder [14]. (c) Install the dowel retaining circlip [71] on the inner cylinder [14] and on the dowels [72] to hold the dowels [72] in their place. (d) Install the upper centering cam [10] on the inner cylinder [14]. (e) Install the upper bearing carrier [68] and recoil valve [70] on the inner cylinder [14]: 1) Install the recoil valve [70] on the top of the upper centering cam [10]. 2) Install the recoil valve ring [69] on the recoil valve [70] if it was removed. 3) Install the upper bearing carrier [68] on the inner cylinder [14]. (f) Install the upper bearing [8] on the upper bearing carrier [68] halves. 1) If the upper bearing [8] does not fit tightly around the bearing carrier [68], use the compressor assy half, C32016-10, SPL-1383 [73], to hold the bearing closed during inner cylinder [14] installation. 2) Make an overlap of ¼ in. (6 mm) to the upper bearing [8] to keep its round shape. SUBTASK 32-21-24-420-005 (8) Install the metering pin [11] in the inner cylinder [14] (View L, Figure 401): (a) Cover the ring assembly [75] fully with fluid, D50022, or fluid, D00467. (b) Wipe the metering pin [11] groove and adjacent surfaces with fluid, D50022, or fluid, D00467. EFFECTIVITY ALL (c) Install the ring assembly [75] into the metering pin [11] groove. 1) Position the scarf cuts diametrically opposite. (d) Install the retaining ring [67] and nut [12] on the metering pin [11]. 1) Apply a layer of fluid, D50022, or fluid, D00467, to the threads of the nut [12]. 2) Install the retaining ring [67] on the metering pin [11] with the flat lip against the mating face. 3) Use the metering pin and retainer ring equipment, SPL-1895, to compress the retaining ring [67] on the metering pin [11]. 4) Install the nut [12] to hold the retaining ring [67] compressed between the metering pin [11] and nut [12]. (e) Put the metering pin [11], with the retaining ring [67] and nut [12] installed, into the inner cylinder [14]. (f) Use the wrench assy, C32035-6, SPL-9679, and socket assy, C32035-3, SPL-9680, to loosen the nut [12] from the inside of the inner cylinder [14]. NOTE: This will allow the retaining ring to expand into the mating groove of the inner cylinder. (g) Use the metering pin and retainer ring equipment, SPL-1895, to tighten the nut [12] to 75 ft-lb (101.7 N·m) - 100 ft-lb (135.6 N·m).

G. Install the Inner Cylinder in the Outer Cylinder

SUBTASK 32-21-24-420-006 (1) Install the compressor assy half, C32016-10, SPL-1383 [73]: (a) Install the compressor assy half, C32016-10, SPL-1383 [73], such that it fits at the bottom of the outer cylinder [9]. (b) Install the strap assy, C32017-60, SPL-3927 [57], around the outer cylinder [9] and connect the ends to the shoulder bolts on the side of the compressor assy half, C32016-10, SPL-1383 [73]. 1) Tighten the strap assy, C32017-60, SPL-3927 [57]. SUBTASK 32-21-24-420-007 (2) Install the inner cylinder [14] in the outer cylinder [9]: CAUTION BE CAREFUL NOT TO CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE INNER CYLINDER OR THE METERING PIN. DAMAGE TO THESE PARTS CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE SEALS. (a) Put the inner cylinder [14] in position to install in the outer cylinder [9]. (b) If necessary, disconnect the hydraulic pump from the retract actuator. (c) Connect the hydraulic lines to the retract actuator (TASK 32-21-21-400-801). (d) Move the Nose Landing Gear (NLG) aft while you put the inner cylinder [14] into the outer cylinder [9]. (e) Push down on the lock link to move it to the locked overcenter position. (f) Install the downlock pin in the NLG, do this task: Landing Gear Downlock Pins Installation, TASK 32-00-01-480-801. SUBTASK 32-21-24-080-001 (3) Remove the compressor assy half, C32016-10, SPL-1383 [73]: EFFECTIVITY ALL (a) Remove the strap assy, C32017-60, SPL-3927 [57], around the outer cylinder [9] and to the shoulder bolts on the side of the compressor assy half, C32016-10, SPL-1383 [73]. (b) Remove the compressor assy half, C32016-10, SPL-1383 [73], from the outer cylinder [9]. SUBTASK 32-21-24-420-008 (4) Carefully put the thread protector half, C32016-21, SPL-1385 [59], between the outer cylinder [9] and inner cylinder [14]. NOTE: The thread protector will expand and press against the outer cylinder, this will protect the static seals from the gland nut threads on the outer cylinder. SUBTASK 32-21-24-480-004 (5) Install the thread protector assembly, C32016-11, SPL-1384 [58]: (a) Install the thread protector assembly, C32016-11, SPL-1384 [58], such that it fits at the bottom of the outer cylinder [9]. (b) Install the strap assy, C32017-60, SPL-3927 [57], around the outer cylinder [9] and connect the ends to the shoulder bolts on the side of the thread protector assembly, C32016-11, SPL-1384 [58]. 1) Tighten the strap assy, C32017-60, SPL-3927 [57]. SUBTASK 32-21-24-580-004 (6) Lift the NLG with an axle jack until the lower bearing carrier [20] moves into the recess between the inner cylinder [14] and outer cylinder [9] (TASK 07-11-03-580-802). (a) Make sure that the static seals stay in their positions as the lower bearing carrier [20] is installed. (b) Continue to lift the NLG with an axle jack until the shock strut extension is reduced to three or four inches (TASK 07-11-03-580-802). SUBTASK 32-21-24-020-020 (7) Remove the thread protector assembly, C32016-11, SPL-1384 [58], and thread protector half, C32016-21, SPL-1385 [59]. SUBTASK 32-21-24-020-021 (8) Remove the scraper retainer, C32016-4 or -67, SPL-1378 [61], and scraper lock assembly, C32016-5 or -68, SPL-1379, from the gland nut [18]. SUBTASK 32-21-24-640-001 WARNING DO NOT GET THE CORROSION-INHIBITING COMPOUND ON YOUR SKIN, IN YOUR EYES, OR ON YOUR CLOTHES. THE COMPOUND IS POISONOUS AND FLAMMABLE. USE APPROVED GLOVES, AND EYE PROTECTION. MAKE SURE THAT THERE IS GOOD AIRFLOW IN THE WORK AREA. KEEP THE COMPOUND AWAY FROM SPARKS AND FLAMES. THE COMPOUND CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONNEL AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT. (9) Apply a thin layer of corrosion inhibiting material, G50136, to these items: (a) The thread major and minor diameters of the gland nut [18]. (b) The thread major and minor diameters of the mating outer cylinder [9]. (c) The outer cylinder [9] thread relief. SUBTASK 32-21-24-420-009 (10) Install the gland nut [18]: EFFECTIVITY ALL (a) Move the gland nut [18] up on the inner cylinder [14] and engage the threads to the outer cylinder [9]. (b) Use the gland nut wrench, SPL-1867, to tighten the gland nut [18] to 100 ft-lb (135.6 N·m) - 125 ft-lb (169.5 N·m). (c) Remove and clean the unwanted corrosion inhibiting material, G50136, from the joint of the gland nut [18] and outer cylinder [9]. SUBTASK 32-21-24-420-010 (11) Install the lockplate [17] for the gland nut [18]: WARNING DO NOT GET THE CORROSION-INHIBITING COMPOUND ON YOUR SKIN, IN YOUR EYES, OR ON YOUR CLOTHES. THE COMPOUND IS POISONOUS AND FLAMMABLE. USE APPROVED GLOVES, AND EYE PROTECTION. MAKE SURE THAT THERE IS GOOD AIRFLOW IN THE WORK AREA. KEEP THE COMPOUND AWAY FROM SPARKS AND FLAMES. THE COMPOUND CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONNEL AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT. (a) Apply a thin layer of corrosion inhibiting material, G50136, to the shank and threads of bolts [15] and washers [16]. (b) Install the lockplate [17] in the holes which will put the tab of the lockplate [17] as close to the gland nut [18] slot as possible. 1) If it is necessary, loosen the gland nut [18] slightly to align slot in the gland nut [18] with the lockplate [17]. (c) Install the bolts [15] and washers [16]. (d) Tighten the bolts [15]. (e) Install MS20995C32 lockwire, G01048, on the bolts [15]. SUBTASK 32-21-24-420-016 (20) Install the oil charging valve [6]: (a) Remove and discard the old packing [7]. (b) Apply a thin layer of fluid, D00467, on the new packing [7]. D. Prepare for the Removal

SUBTASK 32-21-31-480-001 WARNING MAKE SURE THE DOWNLOCK PINS ARE INSTALLED ON ALL THE LANDING GEAR. WITHOUT THE DOWNLOCK PINS, THE LANDING GEAR CAN RETRACT AND CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT. (1) If the downlock pins are not installed on all the landing gear, do this task: Landing Gear Downlock Pins Installation, TASK 32-00-01-480-801.

E. Nose Landing Gear Upper Torsion Link Removal

SUBTASK 32-21-31-020-001 (1) Disconnect the box assembly [38] from the upper torsion link assembly [15]: NOTE: Disconnect the box assembly [38] with the electrical conduits attached. (a) Remove the screws [44] and washers [45] and remove the cover [46] from the box assembly [38]. (b) Remove the nuts [33] and the washers [34] from the bolts [36]. (c) Remove the bolts [36] and the washers [35] from the upper torsion link assembly [15]. (d) Remove the washers [35] from the bolts [36]. EFFECTIVITY ALL SUBTASK 32-21-31-020-002 (2) Remove the clamps [25] that hold the electrical conduits [22] to the bracket [26]: (a) Remove the screws [23] that hold the clamps [25] to the bracket [26]. (b) Remove the clamps [25] and the nut clips [24] from the bracket [26]. SUBTASK 32-21-31-020-003 (3) Remove the bracket [26] from the upper torsion link assembly [15]: (a) Remove the nuts [43] and the washers [42] from the bolts [39]. (b) Remove the bracket [26] and the washers [41] from the bolts [39]. (c) Remove the bolts [39] and the washers [40] from the upper torsion link assembly [15]. (d) Remove the washers [40] from the bolts [39]. SUBTASK 32-21-31-020-004 (4) Disconnect the sensor brackets [17] from the upper torsion link assembly [15]: NOTE: Disconnect the brackets [17] with the sensors [16] and the electrical conduits [22] attached. (a) Remove the nuts [21] and the washers [20] from the bolts [18]. (b) Remove the bolts [18] that hold the sensor brackets [17] to the upper torsion link assembly [15]. (c) Remove the washers [19] from the bolts [18]. (d) Isolate the sensor brackets [17] from the upper torsion link assembly [15]. 1) If it is necessary, use a string to hold the sensor brackets [17] and attach the string over the top of the outer cylinder. SUBTASK 32-21-31-480-002 (5) Use a rope to hold the upper end of the lower torsion link assembly [11] to the outer cylinder. NOTE: This task will hold the lower torsion link assembly [11] in its position when you remove and install the upper torsion link assembly [15] in the subsequent steps. SUBTASK 32-21-31-020-005 (6) Remove the upper torsion link assembly [15] from the nose landing gear: (a) Remove the cotter pin [14], nut [13] and the washer [12] from the apex pin [6]. (b) Remove the apex pin [6] to disconnect the upper torsion link assembly [15] from the lower torsion link assembly [11]. (c) Remove the cotter pin [2], nut [1] and the washer [3] from the torsion link pin [5]. (d) Remove the torsion link pin [5] to disconnect the upper torsion link assembly [15] from the steering collar [4]. (e) Isolate the box assembly [38] from the upper torsion link assembly [15]. 1) If it is necessary use a string to hold the box assembly [38] and attach the string to the outer cylinder. (f) Remove the upper torsion link assembly [15] from the airplane.

32-21-37-600-801CORROSION PREVENTIONPDF p. 871

2. CORROSION PREVENTION

A. Consumable Materials

Reference Description Specification G00009 Compound - Organic Corrosion Inhibiting BMS3-23 G01314 Tape - 3M Polyester Film Tape 8412

B. General Philosophy

SUBTASK 32-21-37-210-001 (1) The basic corrosion prevention philosophy is to make periodic inspections to preclude or detect the early stages of corrosion. Missing fasteners, white powdery or discolored deposits are evidence of the existence of corrosion which should alert operators that some corrective action is required. A corrosion prevention program should be initiated to prevent the accumulation of corrosive products in order to minimize the occurrence of corrosion. SUBTASK 32-21-37-210-002 (2) After the suspected areas are cleaned, a thorough inspection helps to ensure that protective finishes provided during manufacture remain intact. EFFECTIVITY ALL SUBTASK 32-21-37-210-003 (3) Where corrosion exists (noticeable bulges of the skin or white deposits of corrosion products at fastener heads of joint edges), refer to Structural Repair Manual for details of corrosion removal. SUBTASK 32-21-37-210-004 (4) For minor corrosion, to minimize the downtime of the airplane, the corrosion products should be cleaned off, followed by the application of a corrosion inhibiting compound into the affected area to slow the corrosion process. The finish system should be restored at the next maintenance opportunity.

C. Prevention Treatment

SUBTASK 32-21-37-610-001 (1) At the next maintenance opportunity, corrosion prevention treatment should be accomplished to the nose landing gear. SUBTASK 32-21-37-610-004 CAUTION DO NOT APPLY CORROSION INHIBITING COMPOUND ON GREASED JOINTS OR SEALED BEARINGS. THESE COMPOUNDS DISSOLVE GREASE AND OTHER LUBRICANTS. THEY ARE PENETRATING COMPOUNDS AND CAN GET AROUND THE SEALS AND INTO THE BEARINGS. (2) Do preventive measures to these components (Figure 201). NOTE: Apply corrosion inhibiting compound, G00009, to exposed outer surfaces only. Do not disassemble parts to apply the corrosion inhibiting compound. Do not spray into joints, linkages, pulleys, cables or bearings. (a) Shock struts (Oleo). Apply corrosion inhibiting compound, G00009, to exterior areas of the inner and outer cylinder with broken finish systems. All lugs, lug faces, connecting pins and fasteners should be sprayed with corrosion inhibiting compound. (b) Upper Drag Brace Links. Apply corrosion inhibiting compound, G00009, to exterior surface areas with broken finish systems. All lugs, lug faces, connecting pins, and fasteners should be sprayed with corrosion inhibiting compound, G00009. (c) Axle. Apply corrosion inhibiting compound, G00009, to outside surface areas of the axle. Make suitable nozzle extension and spray the inside surfaces of the axle. At wheel removal spray the exterior surfaces of axle cover by wheel except at bearing or journal surfaces. (d) Torsion Links. Apply corrosion inhibiting compound, G00009, to surface areas with broken finish systems. Lugs, lug faces, and connecting pins should be sprayed with corrosion inhibiting compound. (e) Trunnion. Apply corrosion inhibiting compound, G00009, to exterior surface areas with broken finish systems. Lugs, lug faces, connecting pins, fasteners, and trunnion bearing caps should be sprayed with corrosion inhibiting compound, G00009. (f) Lock Brace Assembly. Apply corrosion inhibiting compound, G00009, to surface areas of all components of the locking linkages with broken finish systems. Lugs, lug faces, and connecting pins should also be sprayed. SUBTASK 32-21-37-610-005 (3) The installation of polyester 3M 8412 tape, G01314, under corrosion resistant steel clamps is recommended at overhaul to minimize the risk of galvanic corrosion should the finish be damaged. EFFECTIVITY ALL

D. Frequency of Application

SUBTASK 32-21-37-610-002 (1) Periodic inspection is required to areas identified as susceptible to corrosion and should be consistent to the schedules specified in the Maintenance Planning Document. Operators must be aware of reported problems and areas of occurrences. SUBTASK 32-21-37-610-006 (2) Periodic application of corrosion inhibiting compound, G00009, is necessary to areas identified and should be consistent to the scheduled specified in the Maintenance Planning Document.

F. Nose Gear Axle Detailed Inspection

SUBTASK 32-21-71-490-001 WARNING MAKE SURE THAT THE DOWNLOCK PINS ARE INSTALLED ON ALL THE LANDING GEAR. WITHOUT THE DOWNLOCK PINS, THE LANDING GEAR CAN RETRACT. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONS, AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT. (1) If the downlock pins are not installed in the nose and main landing gear, do this task: Landing Gear Downlock Pins Installation, TASK 32-00-01-480-801. SUBTASK 32-21-71-000-001 (2) Remove the NLG wheel and tire assembly, do this task: Nose Landing Gear Wheel and Tire Assembly - Removal, TASK 32-45-21-000-801. SUBTASK 32-21-71-000-002 (3) For airplanes that use cotter pins [1], remove the cotter pins [1] in the axle spacer and remove the spacer from the axle. SUBTASK 32-21-71-010-001 (4) For airplanes that use lockwire, remove the lockwire in the axle spacer and remove the spacer from the axle. SUBTASK 32-21-71-200-001 (5) Examine the nose gear axles. (a) Make sure that the spacer is removed when you inspect for corrosion on the NLG axle. (b) Use a clean lint-free cloth, G01043, to remove grease and debris from the axle. 1) Do not use solvents or detergents to clean the axle. (c) Do a detailed visual inspection aided with a magnifying glass in the NLG axles for corrosion or cracks caused by corrosion. 1) Pay special attention to the area that was under the axle spacer, and most importantly, at the 6 o'clock position on the axle. 2) If corrosion is detected on a NLG axle, contact for disposition. NOTE: No corrosion is permitted on the axle. Corrosion can cause the axle to fracture and the wheel to depart the airplane. SUBTASK 32-21-71-600-001 WARNING DO NOT GET THE CORROSION-INHIBITING COMPOUND ON YOUR SKIN, IN YOUR EYES, OR ON YOUR CLOTHES. THE COMPOUND IS POISONOUS AND FLAMMABLE. USE APPROVED GLOVES, AND EYE PROTECTION. MAKE SURE THAT THERE IS GOOD AIRFLOW IN THE WORK AREA. KEEP THE COMPOUND AWAY FROM SPARKS AND FLAMES. THE COMPOUND CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONNEL AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT. CAUTION DO NOT APPLY CORROSION-INHIBITING COMPOUND ON GREASE JOINTS, OR SEALED BEARINGS. THESE COMPOUNDS REMOVE GREASE AND OTHER LUBRICANTS. THEY ARE PENETRATING COMPOUNDS. THEY WILL MOVE AROUND THE SEALS AND INTO THE BEARINGS. THIS WILL CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE BEARINGS, AND JOINTS. (6) Apply a light layer of Cor-Ban 27L Compound, G50237, (preferred) or corrosion inhibiting material, G50136, (alternate) to the area underneath the axle spacer. EFFECTIVITY ALL SUBTASK 32-21-71-420-001 (7) For airplanes that use cotter pins [1], make sure that the three cotter pins [1] are installed to hold the spacer on the axle. (a) Make sure that the three cotter pins [1] installed on the spacer do not touch the lower torsion link lug during wheel installation. SUBTASK 32-21-71-420-002 (8) For airplanes that use lockwire, make sure that MS20995C41 lockwire, G00440, is installed. (a) Make sure to bend the lockwire ends pigtails away from the inboard edge of the spacer (Figure 601). (b) Examine the completed installation to make sure that the lockwire ends do not touch the axle or the torsion link lugs. (c) Adjust the installed lockwire to make sure that the lockwire does not hit the landing gear parts during landing gear operations. NOTE: Spacers that use lockwire have six holes. SUBTASK 32-21-71-400-001 (9) Install the NLG wheel and tire assembly, do this task: Nose Landing Gear Wheel and Tire Assembly - Installation, TASK 32-45-21-400-801.
