D. Prepare for the Test

SUBTASK 32-35-00-480-005 WARNING MAKE SURE THE DOWNLOCK PINS ARE INSTALLED ON ALL LANDING GEAR. WITHOUT THE DOWNLOCK PINS, THE LANDING GEAR COULD RETRACT AND CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT. (1) Make sure the downlock pins are installed in the nose and main landing gear, do this task: Landing Gear Downlock Pins Installation, TASK 32-00-01-480-801. SUBTASK 32-35-00-860-050 (2) Do this task: Supply Electrical Power, TASK 24-22-00-860-811. SUBTASK 32-35-00-700-015 (3) Make sure that the manual extension release mechanism of the nose landing gear is free from contamination. SUBTASK 32-35-00-860-020 (4) Make sure the hydraulic power is off. Do this task, if necessary: Hydraulic System A or B Power Removal, TASK 29-11-00-860-805. SUBTASK 32-35-00-860-021 (5) Make sure the control lever for the landing gear is in the DN position.

E. Procedure

SUBTASK 32-35-00-860-022 (1) Put the control lever in the OFF position. SUBTASK 32-35-00-860-048 (2) Open the access door to the manual extension T handles. SUBTASK 32-35-00-700-004 (3) Pull the manual extension handle for the nose gear. (a) Make sure the full travel of the T handle is at least 21.0 in. (533.4 mm) (Detail C). SUBTASK 32-35-00-700-005 (4) Release the manual extension handle for the nose gear. (a) Make sure the handle returns to the stowed position without hesitation or binding. EFFECTIVITY ALL SUBTASK 32-35-00-480-006 (5) Attach a spring scale, STD-5505 to the manual extension T handle for the nose gear. SUBTASK 32-35-00-730-005 (6) Pull the manual extension handle for the nose gear. (a) Make sure the load to start the T handle from the seat has a minimum of 3.0 lbf (13.3 N) and a maximum of 7.0 lbf (31.1 N). (b) Make sure the load during the full travel of the T handle is not more than 15.0 lbf (66.7 N). NOTE: The T handle must be pulled upward and forward when you measure the load. This will simulate a person seated in the First Officer's seat. Do not pull the handle straight up. (c) Make sure the manual extension mechanism operates freely. SUBTASK 32-35-00-860-023 (7) Move the control lever for the landing gear to the DN position. SUBTASK 32-35-00-080-004 (8) Remove the spring scale, STD-5505 from the manual extension T handle for the nose gear. SUBTASK 32-35-00-860-037 (9) Pull the manual extension handle for the nose gear. NOTE: One person needs to be stationed in the nose landing gear wheel well. (10) Release the manual extension handle for the nose gear. NOTE: Observe the manual extension mechanism to make sure the release roller correctly resets to its retracted position. (a) Make sure the handle returns to the stowed position without hesitation or binding. SUBTASK 32-35-00-860-038 (11) Close the access door to the manual extension T handles.

F. Put the Airplane Back to its Usual Condition.

SUBTASK 32-35-00-860-025 (1) If electrical power is not necessary, do this task: Remove Electrical Power, TASK 24-22-00-860-812.

2. Hydraulic Brake System - Bleeding Upstream of the Antiskid Valves

A. General

(1) This task has instructions to bleed the brake system upstream of the antiskid valves. When the system is bled, the air in the brake lines or a component of the brake system is sent through the brake metering valves to the hydraulic reservoir by the return lines.

WITHOUT THE DOWNLOCK PINS, THE LANDING GEAR COULD RETRACT AND CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT. (1) If the downlock pins are not installed in the nose and main landing gear, do this task: Landing Gear Downlock Pins Installation, TASK 32-00-01-480-801. SUBTASK 32-41-00-480-002 (2) Do this task: Supply Electrical Power, TASK 24-22-00-860-811. SUBTASK 32-41-00-480-003 (4) Make sure the tires have chocks installed around them (CHOCK INSTALLATION, PAGEBLOCK 10-11-05/201). SUBTASK 32-41-00-860-001 (5) Release the parking brake. SUBTASK 32-41-00-840-001 (6) Do the steps that follow to bleed the normal brake system through the normal brake metering valves to return: (a) Push the brake pedals slowly through approximately one-half of their total travel and slowly release them. NOTE: Repeat this step several times. (b) Push both of the brake pedals fully to the stops and hold them there for 2 to 4 seconds and then release them. NOTE: Repeat this step 5 more times. (c) Make sure the brakes apply when you push on the brakes. (d) Push the brake pedals fully to the stops and set the parking brake. SUBTASK 32-41-00-860-002 (7) For the normal (System B) hydraulic system, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Power Removal, TASK 29-11-00-860-805. EFFECTIVITY ALL SUBTASK 32-41-00-790-002 WARNING KEEP PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT CLEAR OF THE FLIGHT CONTROL SURFACES, THE THRUST REVERSERS, AND THE LANDING GEAR. (8) For the alternate (System A) hydraulic system, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Pressurization, TASK 29-11-00-860-801. SUBTASK 32-41-00-840-002 (9) Do the steps that follow to bleed the alternate brake system through the alternate brake metering valves to return: (a) Push the brake pedals slowly through approximately one-half of their total travel and slowly release them. F. Normal (System B) Hydraulic Brake System Bleeding

SUBTASK 32-41-00-710-001 (1) To prepare to bleed the normal (System B) hydraulic brake system, do these steps: WARNING KEEP PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT CLEAR OF THE FLIGHT CONTROL SURFACES, THE THRUST REVERSERS, AND THE LANDING GEAR. THESE COMPONENTS CAN MOVE SUDDENLY WHEN YOU SUPPLY HYDRAULIC POWER. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT. (a) Use the hydraulic service cart to pressurize the normal (System B) hydraulic system to 800 psig (5516 kPa) (TASK 29-11-00-860-801). NOTE: We recommend that you use the hydraulic service cart because of the large volume of hydraulic fluid this procedure removes from the normal hydraulic system. NOTE: If you use the airplane's hydraulic supply, monitor the quantity of hydraulic fluid in the reservoir when you bleed the system. (b) Push the brake pedals slowly through approximately one-half of their total travel and slowly release them. NOTE: Repeat this step several times to remove the air from the brake lines upstream of the antiskid valves. EFFECTIVITY ALL (c) Push the two brake pedals fully to the stops and hold them there for 2 to 4 seconds and then release them. NOTE: Repeat this step 5 more times. (d) Push the brake pedals fully to the stops and set the parking brake. SUBTASK 32-41-00-710-002 (2) To bleed the air from each brake, do these steps for all four brakes (Figure 201): NOTE: We recommend you do all of the steps below for one brake before you start the steps again for the next brake. NOTE: There are two bleed valves on each brake, use the bleed valve to which you can get easy access. (a) Remove the screw [2] and washer [3] from the center of the bleeder screw [4]. (b) If installed, remove the lockwire from the bleed valve [1]. (c) Install the bleeder hose, SPL-15035, on the end of the bleeder screw [4]. (d) Put the free end of the bleeder hose, SPL-15035, into an oil resistant container (5 gal)(19 Liter), STD-1055. (e) Slowly loosen the bleeder screw [4] about one half turn. NOTE: This will let hydraulic fluid flow out of the bleeder hose, SPL-15035. (f) Let hydraulic fluid flow out of the bleeder hose, SPL-15035, until there are no air bubbles in the flow of hydraulic fluid. NOTE: The fluid can flow out of the hose very quickly and intermittently. (g) If the fluid flow stops, the brake fuse has set, to reset the fuse, do the steps that follow: 1) Close the bleeder screw [4]. 2) On the normal system fuse for the brake being bled, pull the fuse bypass lever and hold it in this bypass position for 5 seconds minimum (Figure 202). (h) Open the bleeder screw [4] and continue to bleed the brake until there are no air bubbles in the flow of hydraulic fluid. (i) If you will not bleed the alternate (System A) hydraulic system, do the steps that follow: 1) Remove the bleeder hose, SPL-15035, from the bleeder screw [4]. 006, 007, 013, 014, 018-020, 044, 056-063, 067-078, 081, 083-103, 111-114, 121-129, 131, 132, 135, 138-168, 174-179, 182-187, 189-203, 205-209, 212-220, 223, 224, 231-236, 239-298, 301-304, 306, 308, 315-317, 322-341, 343, 346-999 PRE SB 737-32-1429 AND PRE SB 737-32-1441; 169 PRE SB 737-32-1441 2) Tighten the bleeder screw [4] to 60 ±15 in-lb (6.8 ±1.7 N·m). 043; 006, 007, 013, 014, 018-020, 044, 056-063, 067-078, 081, 083-103, 111-114, 121-129, 131, 132, 135, 138-169, 174-179, 182-187, 189-203, 205-209, 212-220, 223, 224, 231-236, 239-298, 301-304, 306, 308, 315-317, 322-341, 343, 346-999 POST SB 737-32-1441 3) Tighten the bleeder screw [4] to 34 ±1 in-lb (3.84 ±0.15 N·m). 006, 007, 013, 014, 018-020, 043, 044, 056-063, 067-078, 081, 083-103, 111-114, 121-129, 131, 132, 135, 138-168, 174-179, 182-187, 189-203, 205-209, 212-220, 223, 224, 231-236, 239-298, 301-304, 306, 308, 315-317, 322-341, 343, 346-999 POST SB 737-32-1429 4) Tighten the bleeder screw [4] to 60.19 ±6.02 in-lb (6.8 ±0.7 N·m). 5) Apply a thin layer of hydraulic fluid, D00153, to the threads of the screw [2]. SUBTASK 32-41-00-870-001 (3) Release the brake pedals or the parking brake if it is set. SUBTASK 32-41-00-870-002 (4) Make sure that all of the normal (System B) hydraulic fuses are not set. (a) Operate the brake pedals several times. (b) Look for movement of the brake wear indicator pins to make sure that all of the brakes operate. SUBTASK 32-41-00-860-005 (5) Remove the external hydraulic pressure for the normal (System B) hydraulic system, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Power Removal, TASK 29-11-00-860-805. SUBTASK 32-41-00-870-003 (6) Make sure that the fluid in the normal (System B) hydraulic reservoir is at the correct level, do this task: Hydraulic Reservoir Servicing, TASK 12-12-00-610-801. 5. Normal (System B) Hydraulic System Brake Fuse Test (Figure 201, Figure 202)

A. General

(1) This task provides instructions to test each hydraulic brake fuse for the normal hydraulic brake system. There is one fuse for each brake for the normal hydraulic system. Each fuse must pass a specific quantity of hydraulic fluid before it closes. For this task, each brake for the main landing gear must be bled to check the fuse for that brake.

32-41-00-870-805Alternate (System A) Hydraulic System Brake Fuse TestPDF p. 1381

6. Alternate (System A) Hydraulic System Brake Fuse Test (Figure 201, Figure 202)

A. General

(1) This task provides instructions to test each hydraulic brake fuse for the alternate hydraulic brake system. There is one fuse for the two brakes on each main landing gear for the alternate hydraulic system. Each fuse must pass a specific quantity of hydraulic fluid before it closes. For this task, only one brake for the each main landing gear must be bled to check the fuse for that brake.

32-41-00-820-801Hydraulic Brake System - AdjustmentPDF p. 1385

2. Hydraulic Brake System - Adjustment (Figure 501)

A. General

(1) The landing gear brake system can be adjusted with the airplane on or off jacks. (2) The hydraulic pressure can be 'On' or 'Off' during adjustment. (3) The landing gear brake system must be adjusted with the brakes off. (4) If rig pin tools are not available, use pins that are 0.309 in. (7.85 mm) - 0.311 in. (7.90 mm) in diameter.

(c) Adjust the forward pushrod [2] on the brake pedal bus [1]. 1) Create a cross hair, consisting of two lines, with a fine tip felt pen at the junction of the two rods: NOTE: This will be a reference point for future adjustments. a) Make the cross-hair before the screws [28] are removed. b) Put one line horizontally across both tubes, halfway between the screw head and nut. c) Put the other line around the tube where the smaller tube meets the larger tube to complete the cross hair. d) Make sure that the pushrod end inspection hole is not open. 2) Loosen the jam nut [7] on the right end of the forward pushrod [2]. 3) Remove the screws [28], washers [29], and nuts [30] in the center of the pushrod [2]. a) Keep the screws [28], washers [29], and nuts [30] for the reassembly after the pushrod [2] adjustment. NOTE: It is necessary for the rig pin to remain installed for the cable adjustment. (e) Install rig pin LGB2, F70207-14, from rigging pin kit, SPL-1585, through the right beam structure and brake control bellcrank [4]. NOTE: It is necessary for the rig pin to remain installed for the cable adjustment. (f) Push the aft pushrod [2] to the left to take up the tolerance. (g) Push the right side crank arm clevis [11] to the left to take up the tolerance. (h) Align the right rod end [10] fastener with the right side crank arm clevis [11]: 1) Turn the rod end [10]. 2) Install the fastener. a) Do not install the washer or nut at this time. (i) Turn the pushrod [2] to lengthen or shorten the forward pushrod [2] to get the original cross hair position. 1) Install only one screw [28], washer [29], and nut [30] at this time. (b) For the locking clips [5] on the brake cables, do this task: Turnbuckle Locking Clips Removal, TASK 20-10-10-000-801. 32-41-00-710-801Normal and Alternate Brake Application - Functional TestPDF p. 1401

3. Normal and Alternate Brake Application - Functional Test

A. General

(1) This procedure does an operation test of these systems: (a) The operation of the brakes with hydraulic power supplied by the NORMAL (System B) brake hydraulic system. (b) The operation of the brakes with hydraulic power supplied by the ALTERNATE (System A) brake hydraulic system. (2) The brake pedal force and angle will also be checked in this task.

B. References

Reference Title 10-11-05 P/B 201 CHOCK INSTALLATION 29-11-00-860-801 Hydraulic System A or B Pressurization (P/B 201) 29-11-00-860-805 Hydraulic System A or B Power Removal (P/B 201) 32-00-01-480-801 Landing Gear Downlock Pins Installation (P/B 201)

Tool part numbers that are replaced or non-procurable are preceded by "Opt:", which stands for Optional. Zone Area 211 Flight Compartment - Left EFFECTIVITY ALL (Continued) Zone Area 212 Flight Compartment - Right 734 Left Main Landing Gear 744 Right Main Landing Gear

E. Prepare for the Procedure

SUBTASK 32-41-00-480-016 (1) Make sure that the tires have chocks installed around them (CHOCK INSTALLATION, PAGEBLOCK 10-11-05/201). SUBTASK 32-41-00-860-013 (2) Release the parking brake. SUBTASK 32-41-00-480-017 WARNING MAKE SURE THAT THE DOWNLOCK PINS ARE INSTALLED ON ALL THE LANDING GEAR. WITHOUT THE DOWNLOCK PINS, THE LANDING GEAR CAN RETRACT. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONS, AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT. (3) If the downlock pins are not installed in the nose and main landing gear, do this task: Landing Gear Downlock Pins Installation, TASK 32-00-01-480-801. SUBTASK 32-41-00-480-019 (4) Install one of the tools or equivalent on the captain's and the first officer's brake pedals: (a) push-pull digital force gauge, COM-1822, or (b) brake pedal measuring equipment, SPL-2555, or (c) brake pedal measuring equipment, SPL-11464. SUBTASK 32-41-00-480-020 (5) Install the pressure gauge, SPL-15031, or the optional gauge set, SPL-10813, on each brake. SUBTASK 32-41-00-710-007 (6) Use a digital protractor, STD-1232, to measure the angle of the brake pedals. SUBTASK 32-41-00-790-003 WARNING KEEP PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT CLEAR OF THE FLIGHT CONTROL SURFACES, THE THRUST REVERSERS, AND THE LANDING GEAR. THESE COMPONENTS CAN MOVE SUDDENLY WHEN YOU SUPPLY HYDRAULIC POWER. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT. (7) For the A or the B hydraulic systems, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Pressurization, TASK 29-11-00-860-801. (a) To test the normal (System B) brake system, only pressurize the system B hydraulic system. (b) To test the alternate (System A) brake system, only pressurize the system A hydraulic system. NOTE: The normal hydraulic system (System B) must not be pressurized for this test. EFFECTIVITY ALL

F. Procedure

NOTE: The steps that follow are applicable for the normal and alternate brake systems. The system that is tested depends on which hydraulic system is pressurized. SUBTASK 32-41-00-710-008 (1) Measure the brake pedal force and travel for each brake pedal. (a) Make sure that each pedal meets the requirements in Table 1. (b) Attach a digital protractor, STD-1232, to the brake pedal to measure the travel (position). 1) Make sure that the digital protractor, STD-1232, is set to zero. (c) Attach a spring scale or brake pedal measuring equipment, SPL-2555, to measure pedal forces. 1) Make sure that the force gage is set to zero. Table 1 *[1] *[2] Brake Pedal Travel (Deg) Brake Pedal Force Brake Pedal Force Brake Pressure 4.5 ± 1.5 28 ±3 lbf (125 ±14 N) 42 ±3 lbf (187 ±14 N) 400 ±50 psig (2758 ±345 kPa) *[1] The pedal force must be measured by the load that you apply perpendicular to the tip of the pedal, 8.25 in. (209.55 mm) from the brake pedal pivot. The brake pressure is the value shown at each brake gage. *[2] The pedal force must be measured with the J32001-64 equipment. The load on the J32001 is located 5.48 in. (139.19 mm) from the brake pedal pivot. The brake pressure is the value shown at each brake gage. (d) Push the captain’s left and right brake pedals until the brake force gage at each pedal shows the value in Table 1. (e) Hold the brake pedals in this position. (f) Make sure that the hydraulic pressure at each brake is within the specified pressure. (g) Make sure that the angle of the captain’s left and right brake pedals are 4.5 ± 1.5 degrees. (h) Release the captain’s brake pedals. (i) Make sure that the brakes fully release by observing that the brake pistons retract away from the heat sink. (j) Make sure that the angle of the captain's left and right brake pedals are 0.0 ± 0.50 degrees. (k) Push the captain’s brake pedals fully down. Make sure that the hydraulic pressure at each brake is 3000 ±150 psi (20,684 ±1034 kPa). (l) Release the captain’s brake pedals. (m) Make sure that the brakes fully release by observing that the brake pistons retract away from the brake heat sink. (n) Repeat the steps (1)(a) through (1)(l) using the first officer’s brake pedals. (o) For the A or the B hydraulic systems, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Power Removal, TASK 29-11-00-860-805. SUBTASK 32-41-00-080-001 (2) Remove the pressure gauge, SPL-15031, or the optional gauge set, SPL-10813, from each brake.

SUBTASK 32-41-00-480-022 (3) Do this task: Supply Electrical Power, TASK 24-22-00-860-811. SUBTASK 32-41-00-480-023 WARNING MAKE SURE THE DOWNLOCK PINS ARE INSTALLED ON ALL THE LANDING GEAR. WITHOUT THE DOWNLOCK PINS, THE LANDING GEAR COULD RETRACT AND CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT. (4) If the downlock pins are not installed in the nose and main landing gear, do this task: Landing Gear Downlock Pins Installation, TASK 32-00-01-480-801. IF YOU DO NOT INSTALL GROUND LOCK PINS, INJURY TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR. (6) Put the landing gear control lever in the UP position. SUBTASK 32-41-00-480-026 (11) If you are done with the maintenance, then remove the chocks from around the tires.

32-41-00-720-801Accumulator - Operational TestPDF p. 1405

5. Accumulator - Operational Test NOTE: This procedure is a scheduled maintenance task.

A. General

(1) This task has instructions to test the operation of the brake accumulator system. This will test the operation of the accumulator charging valve, the pressure transmitter, the accumulator isolation valve, and the accumulator pressure gauge.

B. References

Reference Title 10-11-05 P/B 201 CHOCK INSTALLATION 12-15-11-610-801 Check of the Brake Accumulator Pre-charge Pressure (P/B 301) 24-22-00-860-811 Supply Electrical Power (P/B 201) 24-22-00-860-812 Remove Electrical Power (P/B 201) 29-11-00-860-801 Hydraulic System A or B Pressurization (P/B 201) 29-11-00-860-805 Hydraulic System A or B Power Removal (P/B 201) 32-00-01-480-801 Landing Gear Downlock Pins Installation (P/B 201)

C. Location Zones

Zone Area 211 Flight Compartment - Left 212 Flight Compartment - Right 734 Left Main Landing Gear 744 Right Main Landing Gear EFFECTIVITY ALL

D. Procedure

SUBTASK 32-41-00-480-027 WARNING MAKE SURE THE DOWNLOCK PINS ARE INSTALLED ON ALL THE LANDING GEAR. WITHOUT THE DOWNLOCK PINS, THE LANDING GEAR CAN RETRACT AND CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT. (1) If the downlock pins are not installed in the nose and main landing gear, do this task: Landing Gear Downlock Pins Installation, TASK 32-00-01-480-801. SUBTASK 32-41-00-480-030 (2) Do this task: Supply Electrical Power, TASK 24-22-00-860-811. SUBTASK 32-41-00-480-029 (3) Make sure that the tires have chocks installed around them (CHOCK INSTALLATION, PAGEBLOCK 10-11-05/201). SUBTASK 32-41-00-860-018 (4) Release the parking brake. SUBTASK 32-41-00-860-019 (5) For the A and B hydraulic systems, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Power Removal, TASK 29-11-00-860-805. SUBTASK 32-41-00-840-003 (6) Fully push the brake pedals 12 times to remove hydraulic pressure from the brake accumulator. NOTE: You can look at the wear pin indicators on each brake to see that the brakes no longer actuate when the brake pedals are pushed. SUBTASK 32-41-00-710-026 (7) Permit approximately 5 minutes for the accumulator hydraulic pressure to become stabilized. SUBTASK 32-41-00-700-001 (8) To make sure that the brake accumulator has the correct pressure precharge, do this task: Check of the Brake Accumulator Pre-charge Pressure, TASK 12-15-11-610-801. SUBTASK 32-41-00-790-005 WARNING KEEP PERSONNEL AND EQUIPMENT AWAY FROM THE FLIGHT CONTROL SURFACES, THE THRUST REVERSERS, AND THE LANDING GEAR. THESE COMPONENTS CAN MOVE SUDDENLY WHEN YOU SUPPLY HYDRAULIC POWER. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONNEL AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT. (9) For the A and the B hydraulic systems, for at least 2 minutes, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Pressurization, TASK 29-11-00-860-801. SUBTASK 32-41-00-710-027 (10) Make sure that the pressure shown by the HYD BRAKE PRESS gauge on the First Officer's panel reads within 100 psig (689 kPa) of the hydraulic system 'B' pressure. (a) Write down the hydraulic system 'B' steady state pressure value. SUBTASK 32-41-00-710-028 (11) Make sure that the HYD BRAKE PRESS gauge on the First Officer's panel reads within 100 psig (689 kPa) of the brake accumulator pressure gauge on the rear bulkhead in the right main gear wheel well. EFFECTIVITY ALL SUBTASK 32-41-00-860-020 (12) For the B hydraulic systems, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Power Removal, TASK 29-11-00-860-805. SUBTASK 32-41-00-710-033 (13) Wait approximately one minute until the B hydraulic system pressure drops to less than 1000 psi (6895 kPa). SUBTASK 32-41-00-710-029 (14) Push the brake pedals to the stops 7 times while you observe the brake accumulator pressure. NOTE: Wait approximately 3 seconds after each time you apply the brakes. (a) Make sure that the brake accumulator pressure does not decrease with each brake application. SUBTASK 32-41-00-860-021 (15) For the A hydraulic systems, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Power Removal, TASK 29-11-00-860-805. SUBTASK 32-41-00-710-031 (16) Make sure that the HYD BRAKE PRESS gauge on the First Officer's panel reads within 150 psig (1034 kPa) of hydraulic system 'B' steady state pressure previously written down. SUBTASK 32-41-00-710-032 (17) Push the brake pedals to the stops 7 times while you observe the brake accumulator pressure. NOTE: Wait approximately 3 seconds after each time you apply the brakes. (a) Make sure that the brake accumulator pressure decreases with each brake application. SUBTASK 32-41-00-700-002 (18) To make sure that the brake accumulator has the correct pressure precharge, do this task: Check of the Brake Accumulator Pre-charge Pressure, TASK 12-15-11-610-801. SUBTASK 32-41-00-860-022 (19) Set the parking brake. SUBTASK 32-41-00-860-027 (20) If it is not necessary, remove electrical power. To do this, do this task: Remove Electrical Power, TASK 24-22-00-860-812.

D. Prepare for the Removal

SUBTASK 32-41-11-480-001 WARNING MAKE SURE THAT THE DOWNLOCK PINS ARE INSTALLED ON ALL THE LANDING GEAR. WITHOUT THE DOWNLOCK PINS, THE LANDING GEAR CAN RETRACT. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONS, AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT. (1) If the downlock pins are not installed in the nose and main landing gear, do this task: Landing Gear Downlock Pins Installation, TASK 32-00-01-480-801. SUBTASK 32-41-11-860-001 (2) For the A and B hydraulic systems, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Power Removal, TASK 29-11-00-860-805. SUBTASK 32-41-11-480-002 (3) Make sure that the tires have chocks installed around them (PAGEBLOCK 10-11-05/201). SUBTASK 32-41-11-860-002 (4) Release the parking brake. SUBTASK 32-41-11-860-003 (5) Fully push the captain's brake pedals twelve times to remove the pressure from the brake accumulator. EFFECTIVITY ALL SUBTASK 32-41-11-020-001 (6) Disconnect the hose half [1] of the quick disconnect from the brake half [7] of the quick disconnect. (a) Push the barrel [2] toward the brake and turn the barrel [2] clockwise to disengage the brake half [7] from the hose half [1]. (b) Pull up on the barrel [2] of the hose half [1] of the quick disconnect until the threads of the two halves are engaged. (c) Turn the barrel [2] counterclockwise to disconnect the hose half [1] from the brake half [7] of the quick disconnect.

E. Brake Disconnect Removal (Hose Half)

SUBTASK 32-41-11-020-002 (1) Disconnect the hydraulic hose [8] from the elbow fitting [9]. SUBTASK 32-41-11-480-003 (2) Install a cap/plug, STD-14686, on the hydraulic hose [8]. SUBTASK 32-41-11-020-006 (3) If it is necessary, remove the elbow fitting [9] from the hose half [1] of the quick disconnect.

F. Brake Disconnect Removal (Brake Half)

SUBTASK 32-41-11-020-007 (1) Cut and remove the lockwire or safety cable. SUBTASK 32-41-11-020-003 (2) Remove the bolt [3] and washer [4] that hold the brake half [7] of the quick disconnect to the brake. SUBTASK 32-41-11-020-004 (3) Remove the brake half [7] of the quick disconnect from the brake. SUBTASK 32-41-11-020-005 (4) Remove and discard the packing [6] and the rings [5] from the brake half [7] of the quick disconnect.

F. Brake Disconnect Installation

SUBTASK 32-41-11-420-004 (1) If it is necessary, install the elbow fitting [9] to the hose half [1] of the quick disconnect: (a) Apply a thin layer of hydraulic fluid, D00153, to the elbow threads of the hose half [1] of the quick disconnect. (b) Install the elbow fitting [9] to the hose half [1] of the quick disconnect. (c) Do not tighten the B-nut on the hose half [1] of the quick disconnect at this time. SUBTASK 32-41-11-420-001 (2) Brake Disconnect Installation (Hose Half): (a) Remove the cap/plug, STD-14686, from the hydraulic hose [8]. (b) Apply a thin layer of hydraulic fluid, D00153, to the hydraulic hose [8] threads and elbow fitting [9] threads. (c) Connect the hydraulic hose [8] to the elbow fitting [9], do not tighten at this time. EFFECTIVITY ALL (d) If it is necessary, loosen the B-nut of the hose half [1] of the quick disconnect. (e) Turn the elbow fitting [9] on the hose half [1] of the quick disconnect. Make sure that it is parallel to the oleo centerline or a maximum of ten degrees to the oleo centerline (away from the tire). CAUTION USE TWO WRENCHES TO TORQUE THE HOSE B-NUT. USE ONE TO HOLD THE ELBOW FITTING, AND THE OTHER TO TORQUE THE HOSE B-NUT. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY, DAMAGE TO THE EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR. CAUTION MAKE SURE THAT YOU DO NOT TWIST OR MAKE KINKS IN THE HOSE WHEN YOU TIGHTEN THE NUT. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY, DAMAGE TO THE EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR. (f) Tighten the B-nut on the hydraulic hose [8]. 1) Apply initial torque to 270 ±14 in-lb (31 ±2 N·m). 2) Loosen the B-nut on the hydraulic hose [8] to decrease the torque to zero. 3) Tighten the B-nut on the hydraulic hose [8] to 400 ±20 in-lb (45 ±2 N·m). (g) Tighten the B-nut on the elbow fitting [9] connection to hose half [1] quick disconnect. 1) Apply initial torque to 270 ±14 in-lb (31 ±2 N·m). 2) Loosen the B-nut on the hose half [1] of the quick disconnect to decrease the torque to zero. 3) Tighten the B-nut on the hose half [1] of the quick disconnect to 400 ±20 in-lb (45 ±2 N·m). (h) Apply torque stripes, G50411, or other special identification mark to the B-nuts. SUBTASK 32-41-11-420-002 (3) Brake Disconnect Installation (Brake Half): (a) Lubricate the new packing [6] and the two new rings [5] with hydraulic fluid, D00153. (b) Install the new packing [6] and the two new rings [5] on the brake half [7] of the quick disconnect. (c) Apply a thin layer of BATCO X8401-2 grease, D00571, to the brake half [7] of the disconnect. (d) Make sure that the BATCO X8401-2 grease, D00571, is on the diametral surface above the upper retaining ring and the lower surface of the mounting flange. (e) Install the brake half [7] of the quick disconnect on the brake. 1) Make sure that the alignment pin on the brake goes into the alignment hole in the brake half [7] of the quick disconnect. (f) Apply the BATCO X8401-2 grease, D00571, to the bolts [3]. (g) Install the bolts [3] and washers [4] that hold the brake half [7] of the quick disconnect to the brake. (h) Tighten the bolts [3] to 72 in-lb (8 N·m) - 82 in-lb (9 N·m). (i) Install MS20995C32 lockwire, G01048, or Safety Cable, G50466, on the bolts [3] in pairs. (j) Make sure that the MS20995C32 lockwire, G01048, or Safety Cable, G50466, passes through the lug hole to the other bolt head on each side of the disconnect (Figure 401). EFFECTIVITY ALL SUBTASK 32-41-11-420-003 (4) Install the hose half [1] of the quick disconnect to the brake half [7] of the quick disconnect on the brake. (a) Install the hose half [1] on the brake half [7]. 1) Turn the hose half [1] until the internal tangs align with the slots inside the brake half [7] and you can push the hose half down. 2) Push down on the barrel [2] and turn it clockwise to engage the threads. 3) Turn the barrel [2] clockwise until the lock in the bottom of the barrel [2] snaps onto the external lock on the brake half [7]. 4) Make sure that the elbow fitting [9] is ten degrees from parallel to the oleo centerline towards the shock strut. NOTE: This is to help prevent worn areas on the hoses. (b) Do a visual check to make sure that the lock on hose half [1] is fully and correctly engaged with the lock on the brake half [7].

SUBTASK 32-41-21-020-001 (1) Install a control cable clamp, SPL-1569, on the two cables that are connected to the control quad and shaft assy [22] that you will remove, this will keep light tension on the cables. NOTE: Light tension on the cables will prevent wind off on the cable drums and also make sure they do not move out from the pulley guides. SUBTASK 32-41-21-020-002 (2) Go to the access opening that is forward of the nose wheel well and do the following: (a) To remove the locking clip [1] from the turnbuckle [2] on the brake forward control cables [3] for the brake metering control quad and shaft assy [22] you will remove, do this task: Turnbuckle Locking Clips Removal, TASK 20-10-10-000-801. (b) Loosen the turnbuckle [2] for the forward control cable [3] to release the tension in the cable. SUBTASK 32-41-21-020-003 (3) Go to the access opening in the passenger floor and do the steps that follow: (a) Disconnect the forward control cable [3] from the control quad and shaft assy [22]: 1) Remove the pins [38], that holds the ends of the forward control cables [3], from the quad and shaft assy [22]. 2) Pull the fittings on the end of the forward control cables [3] from the control quad and shaft assy [22]. SUBTASK 32-41-21-020-004 (4) Go to the wheel well and remove components from the quadrant shaft as follows: (a) Do the steps that follow to disconnect the rod [6] from the crank [5]. 1) Remove the nut [4], the bolt [9], the washer [12], retainer [10], and the bushing [11]. 2) Remove the rod [6] end from its position in the crank [5]. (b) Do the steps that follow to remove the crank [5] from the quadrant shaft: EFFECTIVITY ALL 1) Remove the cotter pin [30], the nut [29], the washers [27], [28], and the spacer [26] from the quadrant shaft. 2) Remove the bolt [20], the washer [21], and the nut [23] from the crank [5] on the quadrant shaft. 3) Remove the crank [5] and the spacer [25] from the quadrant shaft. 4) Install the spacer [25], the spacer [26], the washers [27], [28], and the nut [29] back on to the quadrant shaft. NOTE: These parts are reinstalled to help keep the quadrant assembly in the support when you remove it. (c) Remove the four bolts [14], [17], and their washers [18], [15] that hold the control quad and shaft assy [22] to the pressure deck. SUBTASK 32-41-21-020-005 (5) Go to the access opening in the passenger floor and do the steps that follow: NOTE: It is necessary to have a person in the wheel well to turn the nuts [31], [33] while you hold the bolts [36], [37]. (a) Remove the four bolts [36], [37], their washers [32], [34], and their nuts [31], [33] that hold the control quad and shaft assy [22] to the pressure deck. 1) Make sure the person in the wheel well holds the rig pin bracket [13] and removes it when the bolts [36], [37] are removed. (b) Remove the control quad and shaft assembly [22] from the pressure deck.

G. Brake Metering Valve Installation Test

SUBTASK 32-41-31-790-001 (1) Do a leak check and operational check of the brake metering valve for each hydraulic system, do these steps: (a) For the normal (System B) hydraulic system: WARNING MAKE SURE ALL PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT ARE CLEAR OF THE FLIGHT CONTROLS SURFACES, THE THRUST REVERSERS, AND THE LANDING GEAR. THESE COMPONENTS CAN MOVE SUDDENLY WHEN YOU SUPPLY HYDRAULIC POWER. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT. 1) Do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Pressurization, TASK 29-11-00-860-801. 2) Fully push the captain's brake pedals twelve times. 3) Make sure that there are no leaks around the brake metering valve. 4) Check the brake wear indicators on the brakes to make sure that the brakes engaged. (b) For the alternate (System A) hydraulic system: WARNING MAKE SURE ALL PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT ARE CLEAR OF THE FLIGHT CONTROLS SURFACES, THE THRUST REVERSERS, AND THE LANDING GEAR. THESE COMPONENTS CAN MOVE SUDDENLY WHEN YOU SUPPLY HYDRAULIC POWER. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT. 1) Do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Pressurization, TASK 29-11-00-860-801. 2) Fully push the captain's brake pedals twelve times. 3) Make sure that there are no leaks around the brake metering valve. 4) Check the brake wear indicators on the brakes to make sure that the brakes engaged. EFFECTIVITY ALL SUBTASK 32-41-31-790-002 (2) Do a gear retract braking actuator check: WARNING MAKE SURE ALL PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT ARE CLEAR OF THE FLIGHT CONTROLS SURFACES, THE THRUST REVERSERS, AND THE LANDING GEAR. THESE COMPONENTS CAN MOVE SUDDENLY WHEN YOU SUPPLY HYDRAULIC POWER. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT. (a) For the normal (System B) and the alternate (System A) hydraulic system, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Pressurization, TASK 29-11-00-860-801. WARNING MAKE SURE THAT THE DOWNLOCK PINS ARE INSTALLED ON ALL THE LANDING GEAR. WITHOUT THE DOWNLOCK PINS, THE LANDING GEAR CAN RETRACT. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONS, AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT. (b) Move the control lever for the landing gear to the UP position. NOTE: Each gear door connects to each shock strut and only moves when that landing gear extends or retracts. (c) Check the brake wear indicators on the brakes to make sure that the brakes engaged. (d) Make sure that the valve assembly does not produce noise or unusual sound. (e) Make sure that there are no leaks around the brake metering valve. (f) Move the control lever for the landing gear to the DN position. (g) Check each brake’s pistons to make sure that all brakes are released. SUBTASK 32-41-31-710-001 (3) For each hydraulic system, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Power Removal, TASK 29-11-00-860-805. SUBTASK 32-41-31-710-002 (4) Bleed the hydraulic systems: (a) For the normal brake metering valves, do this task: Hydraulic Brake System - Bleeding Upstream of the Antiskid Valves, TASK 32-41-00-870-801. (b) For the alternate brake metering valves, do this task: Hydraulic Brake System - Bleeding Upstream of the Antiskid Valves, TASK 32-41-00-870-801.

I. Main Gear Wheel Brakes Bleeding and Installation Test

SUBTASK 32-41-41-860-011 WARNING KEEP PERSONNEL AND EQUIPMENT AWAY FROM THE FLIGHT CONTROL SURFACES, THE THRUST REVERSERS, AND THE LANDING GEAR. THESE COMPONENTS CAN MOVE SUDDENLY WHEN YOU SUPPLY HYDRAULIC POWER. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONNEL AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT. (1) For the normal (System B) hydraulic system, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Pressurization, TASK 29-11-00-860-801. SUBTASK 32-41-41-790-005 (2) Do these steps to do an operational check of all four brakes: NOTE: At least one person needs to be stationed near the main landing gear brakes. Repeat brake pedal application and release as needed to verify operation of each brake. (a) Push one set of brake pedals to the limit of travel to fully operate each brake assy [1]. (b) Set the parking brake. (c) Monitor the movement of each brake's pistons or wear pins to make sure that each brake assy [1] engaged. NOTE: If the brake wear pins move, the brakes will engage. (d) Wait two minutes. (e) Look for leaks around each brake assy [1] and at each brake disconnect [3]. (f) Release the parking brake. (g) Monitor the movement of each brake's pistons or wear pins to make sure that each brake assy [1] released. NOTE: If the brake wear pins move, the brakes will release. SUBTASK 32-41-41-870-002 (3) If the brakes do not feel normal, do this task: Normal (System B) Hydraulic Brake System - Bleeding, TASK 32-41-00-870-802. EFFECTIVITY ALL

EFFECTIVITY ALL 043; 006, 007, 013, 014, 018-020, 044, 056-063, 067-078, 081, 083-103, 111-114, 121-129, 131, 132, 135, 138-168, 174-179, 182-187, 189-203, 205-209, 212-220, 223, 224, 231-236, 239-298, 301-304, 306, 308, 315-317, 322-341, 343, 346-999 POST SB 737-32-1429 OR POST SB 737-32-1441; 169 POST SB 737-32-1441 (Continued) (a) Make sure that the surface finishes are in good condition. NOTE: Corrosion can occur quickly in some climates. SUBTASK 32-41-41-210-017 (5) Do a check for approximately the same brake running clearance between each brake piston and pressure plate (View A-A, Figure 604 or Figure 605 or Figure 606). (a) With the brake released, visually check to make sure that there is clearance between each brake piston and pressure plate. (b) Make sure that the running clearance between each brake piston and pressure plate is not less than 0.050 in. (1.270 mm). (c) If the running clearance is less than 0.050 in. (1.270 mm), replace the main landing gear brake to check the condition of the brake assembly springs (PAGEBLOCK 32-41-41/401). SUBTASK 32-41-41-210-012 (6) Check the visible areas of the brake heat sink (rotors, stators, pressure plate, and end plate) for oxidation damage (Figure 604 or Figure 605 or Figure 606). (a) Replace the carbon brakes if these conditions exist (Figure 604 or Figure 605 or Figure 606). 1) Examine the brakes for indentations or flaking carbon where the hydraulic brake pistons touch the carbon pressure plate. 2) Examine the brake and surrounding areas for unusual carbon debris such as chips or small pieces of carbon broken off of the rotors and stators. 3) Make sure that the metal rotor drive clips on the outside diameter of each carbon rotor do not show excessive movement and there is no loose flaking carbon near the clips. (b) Do a check for loose rotor drive clips and rivets. (c) Do a check for pieces of carbon that have broken off the carbon disks. (d) Do a check of the outside diameter of the stator disks for the correct 12 o’clock positions of their alignment grooves (Figure 604 or Figure 605 or Figure 606). NOTE: Most carbon brakes are configured with worn stator indicators. A worn stator indicator is a line machined in the stator at the 12 o’clock position of the heatsink. If this indicator is available on the heatsink, the indicator can be used as a visual reference to make sure that the stator does not rotate more than 0.25 in. (0.64 cm). NOTE: A stator groove that is not aligned is an indication of possible stator disk drive failure. NOTE: Manufacturing of alignment markings vary from brake supplier to brake supplier, not all brake assemblies have this indicator. 1) With one hand at the 3 o’clock position and the other hand at the 9 o’clock position, rotate each stator individually and see that the stator does not move more than 0.25 in. (0.64 cm) as measured on the outside diameter of the adjacent stators. 2) Replace the brake if any of the stators can be moved by hand beyond 0.25 in. (0.64 cm). EFFECTIVITY ALL 043; 006, 007, 013, 014, 018-020, 044, 056-063, 067-078, 081, 083-103, 111-114, 121-129, 131, 132, 135, 138-168, 174-179, 182-187, 189-203, 205-209, 212-220, 223, 224, 231-236, 239-298, 301-304, 306, 308, 315-317, 322-341, 343, 346-999 POST SB 737-32-1429 OR POST SB 737-32-1441; 169 POST SB 737-32-1441 (Continued) (e) If the carbon material in a damaged area is soft, flaking, or can be easily removed with a fingernail or plastic scraper, STD-765, replace the brake. NOTE: Carbon brake oxidation causes softness, flaking, and pieces to break off of the rotors and stators. Stains that are brown or orange are initial indications of possible oxidation. Oxidation damage normally occurs on the outside diameters of rotors and stators and non-wear surfaces of pressure plate and end plate and is easy to see. Oxidation damage can also occur on the inner diameter of the rotors and stators, end plate and pressure plate. SUBTASK 32-41-41-210-013 (7) Damage such as nicks, scratches, and gouges in the carbon that do not have cracks are acceptable provided that the carbon is not soft or flaking and cannot be scraped off with a fingernail or plastic scraper, STD-765. ALL SUBTASK 32-41-41-220-002 (8) Use the feeler gage to make sure that the axial free play is not more 0.03 in. (0.76 mm) from the bottom of the nut [7] to the brake lug [8]. (a) If the axial free play is more 0.03 in. (0.76 mm), tighten the nut [7]. SUBTASK 32-41-41-960-001 (9) If the degree of the conditions that are seen on the brake during the above inspections are significant enough, then replacement of the brake is necessary.

SUBTASK 32-41-51-480-001 WARNING MAKE CERTAIN THAT LANDING GEAR DOWNLOCK PINS ARE INSTALLED. PINS NOT INSTALLED MAY CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONNEL OR DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT. (1) If the downlock pins are not installed in the nose and main landing gear, do this task: Landing Gear Downlock Pins Installation, TASK 32-00-01-480-801. SUBTASK 32-41-51-480-002 (2) Make sure the tires have chocks installed around them (CHOCK INSTALLATION, PAGEBLOCK 10-11-05/201). SUBTASK 32-41-51-860-001 (3) Release the parking brake. WARNING MAKE SURE THAT YOU LOOSEN THE SWIVEL NUT FOR THE AIR VALVE A MAXIMUM OF TWO TURNS. AIR PRESSURE CAN BLOW THE VALVE OFF AND CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS. (b) Loosen the swivel nut [7] on the charging valve [8] a maximum of one complete turn counter-clockwise to release the gas pressure from the brake accumulator [1].

E. Brake Accumulator Removal

SUBTASK 32-41-51-020-001 (1) Do these steps to remove the brake accumulator [1]: (a) Disconnect the hydraulic line from the forward end of the brake accumulator [1]. (b) Install a plug on the hydraulic line and a cap on the hydraulic port of the brake accumulator [1]. (c) Disconnect the gas line from the aft end of the brake accumulator [1]. (d) Install a plug on the gas line and a cap in the gas port of the brake accumulator [1]. (e) Loosen the clamp nuts for the accumulator clamps (two locations). (f) Open the clamps. (g) Remove the brake accumulator [1] from the airplane. SUBTASK 32-41-51-020-002 (2) If the brake accumulator [1] you will install does not have the reducer [3] and the reducer [5] installed, do these steps: (a) Remove the reducer [3] and the reducer [5] from the brake accumulator [1]. (b) Remove and discard the packing [2] and the packing [4] from the applicable fitting. SUBTASK 32-41-51-480-003 (3) Install plugs in the ports of the brake accumulator [1].

F. Brake Accumulator Installation

SUBTASK 32-41-51-020-003 (1) Remove the caps or plugs from the ports of the brake accumulator [1]. SUBTASK 32-41-51-410-001 (2) If the reducer [3] and reducer [5] are not installed in the brake accumulator [1], do these steps: (a) Lubricate the new packing [2], new packing [4], reducer [3], and reducer [5] with hydraulic fluid, D00153, or MCS 352B fluid, D00054. (b) For the GAS end of the brake accumulator [1]: 1) Install the new packing [2] on the reducer [3]. 2) Install the reducer [3] in the GAS PORT of the brake accumulator [1]. 3) Tighten the reducer [3] to 180 in-lb (20.34 N·m) - 200 in-lb (22.60 N·m). (c) For the HYDRAULIC end of the brake accumulator [1]: 1) Install the new packing [4] on the reducer [5]. 2) Install the reducer [5] in the FLUID PORT of the brake accumulator [1]. 3) Tighten the reducer [5] to 855 in-lb (96.60 N·m) - 945 in-lb (106.77 N·m). SUBTASK 32-41-51-420-001 (3) Do the steps that follow to install the brake accumulator [1]: (a) Align the gas line with the reducer [3] on the brake accumulator [1] when you put the brake accumulator [1] in its position in the clamps. (b) Tighten the clamp nuts. (c) Connect the gas line from the charging valve [8] to the GAS PORT of the brake accumulator [1]. (d) Connect the hydraulic line to the FLUID PORT of the brake accumulator [1]. SUBTASK 32-41-51-420-002 (4) Do the steps that follow to put the brake accumulator [1] back to its usual condition: (a) Do this task: Hydraulic Brake Accumulator Servicing, TASK 12-15-11-420-801. 1) Make sure that the cap [6] is installed on the charging valve [8] and it has lockwire, G01505 (TASK 20-10-44-400-801). WARNING KEEP PERSONNEL AND EQUIPMENT CLEAR OF THE FLIGHT CONTROL SURFACES, THE THRUST REVERSERS, AND THE LANDING GEAR. THESE COMPONENTS CAN MOVE SUDDENLY WHEN YOU SUPPLY HYDRAULIC POWER. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT. (b) For the normal (System B) hydraulic system, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Pressurization, TASK 29-11-00-860-801. (c) Make sure that the gages for normal (System B) hydraulic system and the brake accumulator [1] indicate approximately 3000 psig (3000 psi). (d) Make sure that there is no leak at the connection for the hydraulic line on the brake accumulator [1]. (e) Apply a soap solution to the connection at the charging line. 1) Examine the connection for air bubbles. EFFECTIVITY ALL (f) If leakage is detected at the charging valve [8], do the following steps to remove and replace the charging valve [8]: 1) Make sure that the hydraulic reservoirs have been depressurized before you remove the charging valve [8] (TASK 29-09-00-860-802). 2) Remove the cap [6] on the charging valve [8] then slowly unscrew the swivel nut [7] to release any residual air pressure. 3) Remove lockwire from the charging valve [8] and manifold assembly. 4) Remove the charging valve [8] from the manifold assembly. 5) Remove and discard the packing [20] from the charging valve [8]. 6) Lubricate the new packing [20] with MCS 352B fluid, D00054, or hydraulic fluid, D00153. 7) Install the new packing [20] onto the charging valve [8]. 8) Install the charging valve [8] in manifold assembly port. a) Tighten the charging valve [8] to 100 in-lb (11 N·m) - 110 in-lb (12 N·m). 9) Install MS20995C47 lockwire, G50356, to the charging valve [8] and manifold assembly with the double twist method. 10) Install the cap [6] and tighten swivel nut [7] on the charging valve [8]. 11) Pressurize the pneumatic crossover manifold duct. 12) Use a solution of soap and water to make sure that no air leaks are at the charging valve [8]. 13) Release pressure from the pneumatic cross manifold duct. (g) To bleed the normal (System B) hydraulic system, do this task: Hydraulic Brake System - Bleeding Upstream of the Antiskid Valves, TASK 32-41-00-870-801.

G. Brake Accumulator Installation Test

SUBTASK 32-41-51-420-003 (1) Do these steps to do an operational check of the brake accumulator [1]. (a) Release pressure from the normal (System B) hydraulic system, do this task: Hydraulic Reservoirs Depressurization, TASK 29-09-00-860-802 or Hydraulic Reservoirs Depressurization, TASK 29-09-00-860-808. (b) Push and release the brake pedals fully a minimum of seven times. (c) Monitor the movement of the brake-wear indicators on each brake to make sure that the brakes work properly.

H. Put the Airplane Back to Its Usual Condition

THIS CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONS, AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT. (1) If the downlock pins are not installed in the nose and main landing gear, do this task: Landing Gear Downlock Pins Installation, TASK 32-00-01-480-801. SUBTASK 32-41-51-480-005 (2) Make sure that the tires have chocks installed around them (CHOCK INSTALLATION, PAGEBLOCK 10-11-05/201). SUBTASK 32-41-51-860-004 (3) For the A and B hydraulic systems, do this task: Hydraulic Reservoirs Depressurization, TASK 29-09-00-860-802 or Hydraulic Reservoirs Depressurization, TASK 29-09-00-860-808. SUBTASK 32-41-51-860-005 (4) Release the parking brake. SUBTASK 32-41-51-860-006 (5) Fully push the captain's brake pedals 12 times to remove the hydraulic pressure from the brake accumulator. SUBTASK 32-41-51-840-001 (6) Do these steps to remove the gas pressure from the brake accumulator: (a) Remove the cap [6] from the brake accumulator charging valve [8]. WARNING DO NOT LET THE VALVE TURN WITH THE SWIVEL NUT. THE PRESSURE IN THE ACCUMULATOR WILL DISENGAGE THE VALVE WITH EXPLOSIVE FORCE. INJURIES TO PERSONNEL AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR. (b) Loosen the swivel nut [7] on the charging valve [8] a maximum of one complete turn counter-clockwise to release the gas pressure from the brake accumulator [1]. (c) Make sure that the gage assembly [9] for the brake accumulator goes to zero. EFFECTIVITY ALL SUBTASK 32-41-51-020-004 (7) Do these steps to remove the gage assembly [9]. (a) Disconnect the gas line [10] from the gage assembly [9]. (b) Install a plug on the gas line [10]. (c) Remove the screws [11], washers [12], washers [13], and washers [14] from the airplane. (d) Remove the shield [16] from the airplane. (e) Remove the washers [13], washers [14], and spacers [15]. (f) Remove the gage assembly [9] from the airplane. 1) Remove the flange [18] from the gage assembly [9]. (g) Put a cap on the union [19] on the gage. SUBTASK 32-41-51-020-005 (8) If the replacement gage assembly [9] does not have a union [19] installed, then do these steps: (a) Remove the union [19] and packing [17] from the port of the gage. (b) Discard the packing [17].

E. Brake Accumulator Pressure Gage Installation

SUBTASK 32-41-51-080-001 (1) Remove the cap or plug from the port of the gage assembly [9] and the gas line [10]. SUBTASK 32-41-51-420-004 (2) If the replacement gage assembly [9] does not have a union [19] installed in the port, then do these steps: (a) Lightly lubricate new packing [17], the threads of gage assembly [9] and the threads of union [19] with hydraulic fluid, D00153 or MCS 352B fluid, D00054 (alternative). (b) Install the new packing [17] on to the union [19]. (c) Install the union [19] on the port of the gage. SUBTASK 32-41-51-420-005 (3) Do these step to install the gage assembly [9]. (a) Install the flange [18] on the gage assembly [9]. (b) Install the gage assembly [9] on the bracket in the right wheel well. EFFECTIVITY ALL WARNING USE NITRILE GLOVES FOR SKIN PROTECTION WHEN YOU USE COR￾BAN 27L. IF IT GETS ON YOUR SKIN, IMMEDIATELY REMOVE IT WITH WATER. IF THIS MATERIAL GETS IN YOUR EYES, IMMEDIATELY FLUSH YOUR EYES WITH WATER. GET MEDICAL AID. THIS MATERIAL CONTAINS FLAMMABLE AGENTS WHICH CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONNEL. (c) Apply a thin layer of Cor-Ban 27L Compound, G50237 (preferred) or corrosion inhibiting material, G50136 (alternative) to the faces of the washers [13], the faces of the washers [14] and the faces of the spacers [15]. Wipe off excess. (d) Install the spacers [15], washers [14], washers [13] on the flange [18]. NOTE: The rubber washers [14] should always be against the shield [16]. (e) Install the shield [16] on the spacers [15]. (f) Apply a thin layer ofCor-Ban 27L Compound, G50237 (preferred) or corrosion inhibiting material, G50136 (alternative) to the thread reliefs and threads of the screws [11], the faces of the washers [12], the faces of the washers [13], the faces of the washers [14]. Wipe off the excess. (g) Install the washers [14], the washers [13], washers [12], and screws [11]. NOTE: Install washers [13] until no more than one washer [13] is above the spacer to prevent movement of the shield [16]. Tighten without damage to washers [14]. (h) Connect the gas line [10] to the union [19] on the gage assembly [9].

(b) For the normal (System B) hydraulic system, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Pressurization, TASK 29-11-00-860-801. (c) Make sure that the gages for normal (System B) hydraulic system and the brake accumulator indicated approximately 3000 psig (20,684 kPa). (d) Make sure there is no leak at the connection for the line on the gage assembly [9]. (e) Apply a soap solution to the connection at the union [19]. 1) Examine the connection for air bubbles. (f) To bleed the normal (System B) hydraulic system, do this task: Hydraulic Brake System - Bleeding Upstream of the Antiskid Valves, TASK 32-41-00-870-801.

E. Brake System Relief Valve Installation

SUBTASK 32-41-71-420-001 (1) Do these steps to install the brake accumulator pressure relief valve [1]: (a) Remove the caps or plugs from the hydraulic lines. (b) Put the relief valve [1] in its position in the hydraulic line. (c) Connect the inboard hydraulic tee to the relief valve [1]. (d) Connect the outboard hydraulic line to the relief valve [1]. 1) Tighten the hydraulic line to 140 ±7 in-lb (15.8 ±0.8 N·m). (e) Put the clamp [2] in its position on the relief valve [1]. (f) Install the bolts [4] and the washers [3] to connect the clamp [2] to the airplane. SUBTASK 32-41-71-420-002 (2) Do the steps that follow to make sure the brake accumulator is in its usual condition: EFFECTIVITY ALL (a) Make sure the brake accumulator charge pressure is correct. NOTE: The brake accumulator charge pressure can be found on the placard located next to the brake accumulator pressure gage. (b) If the brake accumulator needs to be serviced, do this task: Hydraulic Brake Accumulator Servicing, TASK 12-15-11-420-801. 1) Make sure the cap is installed on the charging valve and it has lockwire, G01505 on it, do this task Lockwire, Cotter Pins, and Lockrings - Installation, TASK 20-10-44-400-801.

F. Brake Accumulator Pressure Relief Valve Leakage Test

SUBTASK 32-41-71-870-002 (1) Do the steps that follow to do a leakage check of the brake accumulator pressure relief valve: WARNING KEEP PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT CLEAR OF THE FLIGHT CONTROL SURFACES, THE THRUST REVERSERS, AND THE LANDING GEAR. THESE COMPONENTS CAN MOVE SUDDENLY WHEN YOU SUPPLY HYDRAULIC POWER. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT. (a) For the normal (System B) hydraulic system, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Pressurization, TASK 29-11-00-860-801. (b) Fully push the brake pedals twelve times to bleed the air out through the brake metering valves. NOTE: Wait approximately 5 seconds between each time that you push the brake pedals. (c) Make sure there are no leaks from the relief valve [1] when you bleed the brake system. (d) For the normal (System B) hydraulic system, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Power Removal, TASK 29-11-00-860-805.

SUBTASK 32-41-81-840-001 (4) To get access to the aft cable [2], forward cable [4], turnbuckles [3] and quadrant [5] (forward of nose wheel well), do this step: (a) Open this access panel: Number Name/Location 112A Forward Access Door SUBTASK 32-41-81-840-002 (5) Remove the passenger seats from station 706 through station 727, do this task: Passenger Seat - Removal, TASK 25-22-00-000-801. G. Hydraulic Brake Control Cable Removal

NOTE: The steps that follow are applicable for all of the brake control cables. SUBTASK 32-41-81-020-001 (1) In the forward compartment, forward of the nose wheel well, do these steps: (a) Install a control cable clamp, SPL-1569, on the cable (aft cable [2] or forward cable [4]) opposite the one you will remove to keep light tension on the cable (aft cable [2] or forward cable [4]). NOTE: Light tension on the aft cable or forward cable will prevent wind off on the cable drums. Light tension will also make sure that the cables do not move out of the quadrant guides. (b) Remove the locking clip [1] from the turnbuckle [3] on the aft cable [2], forward cable [4] (TASK 20-10-10-000-801). (c) Loosen the turnbuckle [3] for the aft cable [2], forward cable [4] to release the tension in the cable. EFFECTIVITY ALL 1) Make sure that you keep light tension on the aft cable [2] or forward cable [4] to keep the aft cable [2] or forward cable [4] in the quadrant [5] or quadrant [8] guides. (d) Disconnect the forward cable [4] from the quadrant [5]: 1) Remove the pin [7], that holds the end of the forward cable [4], from the quadrant [5]. 2) Pull the fitting on the end of the control forward cable [4] from the control quadrant [5]. 3) Remove the forward cable [4] from the quadrant [5]. SUBTASK 32-41-81-020-002 (2) In the passenger compartment, do these steps: (a) Disconnect the brake control aft cable [2] from the quadrant [8]: 1) Remove the pin [9], that holds the end of the aft cable [2], from the quadrant [8]. 2) Pull the fitting on the end of the control aft cable [2] from the control quadrant [8]. SUBTASK 32-41-81-020-003 (3) Attach the new aft cable [2] or forward cable [4], or a piece of string, STD-837, to the old aft cable [2]. NOTE: The new aft cable or forward cable must be pulled through the system to make the new aft cable or forward cable installation easy. If you remove the old aft cable or forward cable without attaching anything to it, installation of the new aft cable or forward cable will be very difficult. SUBTASK 32-41-81-020-004 (4) Remove the aft cable [2] or forward cable [4]: (a) Pull the old aft cable [2] or forward cable [4] out, that will pull the new aft cable [2] or forward cable [4], or string, STD-837, through the cable system at the same time. 1) Make sure that the new aft cable [2] or forward cable [4] has grease, D00633, applied to it before it is installed.

D. Brake Accumulator Isolation Valve Removal

SUBTASK 32-41-91-020-001 (1) Do these steps to remove the accumulator isolation valve [13]: (a) Disconnect the hydraulic line [1], hydraulic line [8], and elbow [11] from the accumulator isolation valve [13]. (b) Install the plugs in the hydraulic line [1], hydraulic line [8], and elbow [11]. (c) Install the caps on the reducer [2], reducer [7], and reducer [10] in the ports of the accumulator isolation valve [13]. (d) Remove the bolts [4] and washers [5] that attach the accumulator isolation valve [13] to the mating surface. (e) Remove the accumulator isolation valve [13] from the airplane. SUBTASK 32-41-91-020-002 (2) If the replacement accumulator isolation valve [13] does not have hydraulic fittings installed, do these steps: (a) Remove the reducer [2], reducer [7], reducer [10], and plugs [14] from the ports of the accumulator isolation valve [13]. 1) Remove the lockwire from the plugs [14]. (b) Remove and discard the packing [6], packing [9], and packings [3]. (c) Install plugs in the hydraulic ports of the accumulator isolation valve [13].

F. Brake Accumulator Isolation Valve Installation

SUBTASK 32-41-91-640-001 (1) If the reducer [2], reducer [7], reducer [10], plugs [14], packings [3], packing [6], and packing [9] are not installed, do these steps: (a) Lubricate the reducer [2], reducer [7], reducer [10], plugs [14], new packings [3], new packing [6], and new packing [9] with hydraulic fluid, D00153, or MCS 352B fluid, D00054. (b) Install the reducer [2], reducer [7], reducer [10], plugs [14], packings [3], packing [6], and packing [9] in their location on the accumulator isolation valve [13]. ALL; BRAKE ACCUMULATOR ISOLATION VALVE WITH PLUG P/N 274T4629-1 1) Tighten the reducer [2] to 270 ±14 in-lb (30.5 ±1.6 N·m). NOTE: The reducer is made of steel. ALL; BRAKE ACCUMULATOR ISOLATION VALVE WITH PLUG P/N 274T4629-4 2) Tighten the reducer [2] to 170 ±9 in-lb (19.2 ±1.0 N·m). NOTE: The reducer is made of aluminum alloy. ALL 3) Tighten the reducer [7] to 280 ±14 in-lb (31.6 ±1.6 N·m). 4) Tighten the reducer [10] to 280 ±14 in-lb (31.6 ±1.6 N·m). (c) Install MS20995NC32 lockwire, G50347, on the plugs [14] with the double-twist method. SUBTASK 32-41-91-420-001 (2) Do these steps to install the accumulator isolation valve [13]: (a) Put the accumulator isolation valve [13] on the mating surface. (b) Install the bolts [4] and washers [5] to attach the accumulator isolation valve [13] on the mating surface. (c) Remove the caps from the hydraulic ports of the accumulator isolation valve [13]. (d) Remove the plugs from the hydraulic line [1], hydraulic line [8], and elbow [11]. (e) Connect the hydraulic line [1], hydraulic line [8], and elbow [11] to the accumulator isolation valve [13]. 1) Tighten the hydraulic line [1] to 140 ±7 in-lb (15.8 ±0.8 N·m). 2) Tighten the hydraulic line [8] to 270 ±14 in-lb (30.5 ±1.6 N·m). 3) Tighten the elbow [11] to 270 ±14 in-lb (30.5 ±1.6 N·m).

G. Accumulator Isolation Valve Test

SUBTASK 32-41-91-870-003 (1) Do the steps that follow to make sure that the valve assembly does not leak: EFFECTIVITY ALL WARNING KEEP PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT CLEAR OF THE FLIGHT CONTROL SURFACES, THE THRUST REVERSERS, AND THE LANDING GEAR. THESE COMPONENTS CAN MOVE SUDDENLY WHEN YOU SUPPLY HYDRAULIC POWER. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT. (a) For the normal and alternate brake hydraulic systems, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Pressurization, TASK 29-11-00-860-801. (b) Make sure that the PRESS A, PRESS B, and BRAKE hydraulic connections on the accumulator isolation valve [13] do not leak. SUBTASK 32-41-91-870-002 (2) Bleed the brake hydraulic system: (a) Operate the brake pedals 6 times. NOTE: Operate the pedals slowly and wait a minimum of 5 seconds between each time you push the pedals. SUBTASK 32-41-91-860-003 (3) For the normal and alternate hydraulic systems, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Power Removal, TASK 29-11-00-860-805. SUBTASK 32-41-91-840-002 (4) Set the parking brakes. SUBTASK 32-41-91-840-003 (5) Remove the chocks from around the tires of all the landing gear.

D. Alternate Brake Selector Valve Removal

E. Gear Retract Braking Operational Test

SUBTASK 32-41-93-480-011 (1) Do these steps to install a pressure gage at each brake: (a) Disconnect the brake at the brake disconnect: 1) Push the barrel toward the brake and rotate the barrel clockwise to disengage the brake half from the hose half. 2) Pull up on the barrel of the brake disconnect away from the brake until the threads of the two halves are engaged. 3) Turn the barrel counterclockwise to disconnect the brake hose from the brake assembly. (b) Remove the brake bleeder assembly from the brake. NOTE: Each brake bleeder assembly has a bleeder valve installed in an adapter. The adapter is installed in the brake. (c) Install the pressure gauge, SPL-15031, or optional gauge set, SPL-10813, or gauge set, SPL-1819. (d) Connect the brake at the brake disconnect: 1) Turn the hose half of the brake disconnect until the internal tangs align with the slots inside the brake half of the brake disconnect and you can push the hose half down. 2) Push down on the barrel and turn it clockwise to engage the threads. 3) Turn the barrel clockwise until the slots in the bottom of the barrel snap into place on the external tangs on the brake half of the brake disconnect. (e) Do a visual check to make sure that the slots on the barrel are fully and correctly engaged with the tangs on the brake half of the brake disconnect. SUBTASK 32-41-93-790-003 WARNING KEEP PERSONNEL AND EQUIPMENT AWAY FROM THE FLIGHT CONTROL SURFACES, THE THRUST REVERSERS, AND THE LANDING GEAR. THESE COMPONENTS CAN MOVE SUDDENLY WHEN YOU SUPPLY HYDRAULIC POWER. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONNEL AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT. (2) For the normal (system B) and alternate (system A) hydraulic systems, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Pressurization, TASK 29-11-00-860-801. EFFECTIVITY ALL SUBTASK 32-41-93-860-007 WARNING MAKE SURE THAT THE DOWNLOCK PINS ARE INSTALLED IN ALL OF THE LANDING GEAR BEFORE YOU MOVE THE CONTROL LEVER. WITHOUT THE DOWNLOCK PINS, THE LANDING GEAR CAN RETRACT AND CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONNEL AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT. (3) Put the landing gear control lever in the UP position. SUBTASK 32-41-93-870-003 (4) Wait 2 seconds. SUBTASK 32-41-93-710-002 (5) Make sure that the hydraulic pressure at all brakes is 500 psig (3447 kPa) - 575 psig (3964 kPa). SUBTASK 32-41-93-710-003 (6) Put the landing gear control lever in the DOWN position. SUBTASK 32-41-93-710-004 (7) Make sure that the hydraulic pressure at all of the brakes is less than 60 psig (414 kPa). SUBTASK 32-41-93-860-020 (8) For the normal (system B) and alternate (system A) hydraulic systems, do this task: Hydraulic Reservoirs Depressurization, TASK 29-09-00-860-802. SUBTASK 32-41-93-480-012 (9) Do these steps to remove the pressure gages at each brake: (a) Disconnect the brake at the brake disconnect: 1) Pull up on the barrel of the brake disconnect. 2) Turn the barrel counterclockwise to disconnect the brake hose from the brake assembly. (b) Remove the pressure gauge, SPL-15031, or optional gauge set, SPL-10813, or gauge set, SPL-1819. (c) Install the brake bleeder assembly on the brake. NOTE: Each brake bleeder assembly has a bleeder valve installed in an adapter. The adapter is installed in the brake. (d) Connect the brake at the brake disconnect: 1) Turn the hose half of the brake disconnect until the internal tangs align with the slots inside the brake half of the brake disconnect and you can push the hose half down. 2) Push down on the barrel and turn it clockwise to engage the threads. 3) Turn the barrel clockwise until the slots in the bottom of the barrel snap into place on the external tangs on the brake half of the brake disconnect. (e) Do a visual check to make sure that the slots on the barrel are fully and correctly engaged with the tangs on the brake half of the brake disconnect. EFFECTIVITY ALL

THE INCORRECT CONNECTION OF THE VALVE CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE EQUIPMENT AND BRAKE SYSTEM MALFUNCTION. SUBTASK 32-41-95-790-001 (4) Bleed the hydraulic brake systems, these are the tasks: Normal (System B) Hydraulic Brake System - Bleeding, TASK 32-41-00-870-802, Alternate (System A) Hydraulic Brake System - Bleeding, TASK 32-41-00-870-803. (a) Make sure that there is no leakage from the valve assembly [5] as you bleed the brake hydraulic system.

E. Antiskid/Autobrake Control Unit Operational Test

SUBTASK 32-42-00-860-008 (1) Do the following steps for AACU: (a) Push and then release the RESET switch on the AACU. (b) Make sure that the display on the front panel of the AACU shows MEM CLR and then clears. (c) Set the AUTOBRAKE selector switch on the P2-2 panel to "OFF" then to position "1". NOTE: If the AUTOBRAKE DISARM light is on when you do three subsequent steps, the test will not successfully complete and one or more faults will show on the front panel of the AACU. (d) Push and hold the ENABLE/VERIFY switch on the AACU. (e) While you hold the ENABLE/VERIFY switch, push and hold the VERIFY switch on the AACU. (f) Release the ENABLE/VERIFY switch and the VERIFY switch at the same time. NOTE: The AACU display will flash WAIT during the test. (g) Make sure that you see the following indications: 1) Make sure that the AACU display shows TEST END after 10 - 20 seconds. EFFECTIVITY ALL ALL; AIRPLANES WITH AACU P/N 142-147 OR 42-935-X 2) Make sure that the ANTISKID INOP light on the P2-2 panel flashes two times. ALL; AIRPLANES WITH AACU P/N 142-219 3) Make sure that the ANTISKID INOP light on the P2-2 panel flashes four times. ALL 4) Make sure that the AUTOBRAKE DISARM light on the P2-2 panel is ON, then OFF, and then remains ON at the end of the test. (h) Set the autobrake selector switch to the OFF position.

SUBTASK 32-42-00-860-092 (1) For the normal (system B) and alternate (system A) hydraulic systems, do this task: Hydraulic Reservoirs Depressurization, TASK 29-09-00-860-802 or Hydraulic Reservoirs Depressurization, TASK 29-09-00-860-808. SUBTASK 32-42-00-480-004 (2) Make sure that the tires have chocks installed around them (PAGEBLOCK 10-11-05/201). SUBTASK 32-42-00-860-011 (3) Release the parking brake. SUBTASK 32-42-00-480-005 (4) Do these steps to install a pressure gage at each brake: (a) Disconnect the brake at the brake disconnect: 1) Push the barrel toward the brake and rotate the barrel clockwise to disengage the brake half from the hose half. EFFECTIVITY ALL 2) Pull up on the barrel of the brake disconnect away from the brake until the threads of the two halves are engaged. 3) Turn the barrel counterclockwise to disconnect the brake hose from the brake assembly. (b) Remove the brake bleeder assembly from the brake. NOTE: Each brake bleeder assembly has a bleeder valve installed in an adapter. The adapter is installed in the brake. (c) Install the pressure gauge, SPL-15031, or optional gauge set, SPL-10813. (d) Connect the brake at the brake disconnect: 1) Turn the hose half of the brake disconnect until the internal tangs align with the slots inside the brake half of the brake disconnect and you can push the hose half down. 2) Push down on the barrel and turn it clockwise to engage the threads. 3) Turn the barrel clockwise until the slots in the bottom of the barrel snap into place on the external tangs on the brake half of the brake disconnect. (e) Do a visual check to make sure that the slots on the barrel are fully and correctly engaged with the tangs on the brake half of the brake disconnect. SUBTASK 32-42-00-860-013 WARNING KEEP PERSONNEL AND EQUIPMENT CLEAR OF THE FLIGHT CONTROL SURFACES, THE THRUST REVERSERS, THE LANDING GEAR, AND THE DOORS FOR THE MAIN LANDING GEAR. THESE COMPONENTS CAN MOVE SUDDENLY WHEN YOU SUPPLY HYDRAULIC POWER. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY, DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT OR INJURY TO PERSONNEL CAN OCCUR. (5) For the normal (system B) hydraulic systems, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Pressurization, TASK 29-11-00-860-801. SUBTASK 32-42-00-860-014 (6) Disable the parking brake indication: (a) Open this circuit breaker and install safety tag: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-3 Row Col Number Name B 16 C01346 LANDING GEAR PARKING BRAKE SUBTASK 32-42-00-860-015 (7) Set the parking brake.

E. Normal Antiskid Valve Functional Test

SUBTASK 32-42-00-860-016 (1) Make sure that the hydraulic pressure at the controlled brake is within 200 psi (1379 kPa) of B hydraulic supply pressure. SUBTASK 32-42-00-860-017 (2) Do these steps for each antiskid valve that you removed: (a) Move the BRAKE TEST selector switch on the Antiskid/Autobrake Control Unit (AACU) to the wheel position for the brake valve that you will test. NOTE: See the top of the AACU for the brake number. (b) Push and hold the ENABLE/VERIFY switch on the AACU. EFFECTIVITY ALL (c) Push and hold the VERIFY switch on the AACU. (d) Release the ENABLE/VERIFY and the VERIFY switches at the same time. NOTE: The AACU display will show BRK X during the test, where X = the wheel number selected by the BRAKE TEST selector switch. (e) Make sure that the hydraulic pressure at the controlled brake is less than or equal to 150 psi (1034 kPa) for 5 to 10 seconds and then applies to within 200 psi (1379 kPa) of B hydraulic supply pressure. (f) Move the BRAKE TEST selector switch to the NORM position.

NOTE: The AACU display will show BRK X during the test, where X = the wheel number selected by the BRAKE TEST selector switch. EFFECTIVITY ALL 2) Turn the barrel counterclockwise to disconnect the brake hose from the brake assembly. (b) Remove the pressure gauge, SPL-15031, or optional gauge set, SPL-10813. E. Transducer Functional Test

SUBTASK 32-42-00-020-001 (1) Do these steps to remove the hubcap (Figure 503): EFFECTIVITY ALL (a) For an outboard wheel, turn the camlock fasteners 1/4-turn to disconnect the hubcap fairing from the outboard hubcap. (b) Remove and discard MS20995N32 lockwire, G50177, from the bolts of the outboard or inboard hubcap. (c) Remove the bolts and washers to disconnect the outboard or inboard hubcap from the wheel. (d) Remove the outboard or inboard hubcap from the wheel. SUBTASK 32-42-00-860-025 (2) Install the spin up adapter, SPL-1831, in a drill. SUBTASK 32-42-00-860-026 (3) Make sure that the hydraulic pressure at all brakes is equal to the system B pressure ±200 psi (1379 kPa). NOTE: This is to make sure that the antiskid system does not inadvertently release the brakes. SUBTASK 32-42-00-710-002 (4) Do these steps to test each wheel speed transducer: NOTE: A minimum of one person must be near the main landing gear brakes. WARNING KEEP PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT AWAY FROM THRUST REVERSERS. THE OPERATION OF THE WHEEL SPEED TRANSDUCER CAN CAUSE AUTOMATIC OPERATION OF THE STANDBY HYDRAULIC PUMP AND SUDDEN THRUST REVERSER MOVEMENTS. IF YOU DO NOT DO THIS, INJURY TO PERSONS OR DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR. (a) Use the spin up adapter, SPL-1831, and a variable speed drill to turn the wheel speed transducer between 250 and 2200 Revolutions Per Minute (RPM). NOTE: It is recommended to keep the wheel speed below 60 knots. If the aircraft is not in this condition, the standby hydraulic pump can operate automatically. (b) Visually make sure that the brake at the paired wheel is less than or equal to 150 psi (1034 kPa) (Table 501). NOTE: The wheels are numbered from the left to the right. Table 501/32-42-00-993-804 ANTISKID TRANSDUCER PAIRED WHEELS TRANSDUCER PAIRED WHEEL 1 4 2 3 3 2 4 1 (c) Stop the movement of the wheel speed transducer as quickly as possible. (d) Visually make sure that the brake at the controlled wheel is less than or equal to 150 psi (1034 kPa) (Table 502). EFFECTIVITY ALL Table 502/32-42-00-993-806 ANTISKID TRANSDUCER CONTROLLED WHEELS TRANSDUCER CONTROLLED WHEEL 1 1 2 2 3 3 4 4 (e) Wait 5 to 10 seconds. (f) Make sure that the hydraulic pressure at all brakes is equal to the system B pressure ±200 psi (1379 kPa). SUBTASK 32-42-00-420-001 CAUTION DO NOT TIGHTEN THE HUBCAP BOLTS TOO MUCH. MAKE SURE THAT THE HUBCAP IS IN THE CORRECT POSITION BEFORE YOU TIGHTEN THE BOLTS. TOO MUCH TORQUE WILL CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE BOLTS AND THE HUBCAP. (5) Do these steps to install the hubcap (Figure 503): (a) Turn the antiskid transducer dog inside the wheel such that the drive on the hubcap and the dog in the wheel will connect when the hubcap is installed. (b) Put the hubcap in its position on the wheel. 1) Visually make sure that the hubcap is flush with the wheel assembly. 2) Use a soft rubber mallet, STD-3906, to lightly tap the hubcap to make it flush. (c) Install the bolts and washers to connect the hubcap to the wheel. 1) Tighten the bolts to 50 in-lb (6 N·m) - 80 in-lb (9 N·m). (d) Install MS20995N32 lockwire, G50177, on the bolts with the double twist method TASK 20-10-44-400-801). (e) Do these steps for the outboard wheel: 1) Put the hubcap fairing on the hubcap. 2) Turn the camlock fasteners 1/4-turn to attach the hubcap fairing to the hubcap. SUBTASK 32-42-00-080-002 (6) Do these steps to remove the pressure gauges at each brake: (a) Disconnect the brake at the brake disconnect: 1) Pull up on the barrel of the brake disconnect. 2) Turn the barrel counterclockwise to disconnect the brake hose from the brake assembly. (b) Remove the pressure gauge, SPL-15031, or the optional gauge set, SPL-10813. (c) Install the brake bleeder assembly on the brake. NOTE: Each brake bleeder assembly has a bleeder valve installed in an adapter. The adapter is installed in the brake. (d) Connect the brake at the brake disconnect: 1) Turn the hose half of the brake disconnect until the internal tangs align with the slots inside the brake half of the brake disconnect and you can push the hose half down. 2) Push down on the barrel and turn it clockwise to engage the threads. EFFECTIVITY ALL 3) Turn the barrel clockwise until the slots in the bottom of the barrel snap into place on the external tangs on the brake half of the brake disconnect. (e) Do a visual check to make sure the slots on the barrel are fully and correctly engaged with the tangs on the brake half of the brake disconnect.

SUBTASK 32-42-00-860-035 (1) Do these steps for each antiskid valve that you removed or test: NOTE: One person must be at the Main Landing Gear (MLG) brakes to monitor the movement of the brake pistons or wear pins. SUBTASK 32-42-00-480-016 (9) Do these steps to install a pressure gage at each brake: (a) Disconnect the brake at the brake disconnect: 1) Pull up on the barrel of the brake disconnect. 2) Turn the barrel counterclockwise to disconnect the brake hose from the brake assembly. (b) Remove the brake bleeder assembly from the brake. NOTE: Each brake bleeder assembly has a bleeder valve installed in an adapter. The adapter is installed in the brake. (c) Install the pressure gauge on the brake bleed port. (d) Connect the brake at the brake disconnect: EFFECTIVITY ALL 1) Turn the hose half of the brake disconnect until the internal tangs align with the slots inside the brake half of the brake disconnect and you can push the hose half down. 2) Push down on the barrel and turn it clockwise to engage the threads. 3) Turn the barrel clockwise until the slots in the bottom of the barrel snap into place on the external tangs on the brake half of the brake disconnect. (e) Do a visual check to make sure that the slots on the barrel are fully and correctly engaged with the tangs on the brake half of the brake disconnect. SUBTASK 32-42-00-010-002 (11) To get access to the Antiskid/Autobrake Control Unit (AACU), on the E1-3 shelf, do this step: (a) Open this access panel: Number Name/Location 117A Electronic Equipment Access Door SUBTASK 32-42-00-860-048 (12) Set the BRAKE TEST selector switch, on the AACU, to the A/B position. NOTE: In Steps (11) through (15), if the AUTO BRAKE DISARM light is ON when you push the ENABLE/VERIFY switches, the test will not successfully complete and the display on the front panel of the AACU will show "BRK ####." SUBTASK 32-42-00-860-049 (13) Do the steps that follow for AUTO BRAKE selector position 1. (a) Set the AUTO BRAKE selector switch, on the P2-2 panel, to the OFF position then to the 1 position. (b) Push and then release the RESET switch on the AACU. NOTE: The display on the front panel of the AACU will show "MEM CLR". (c) Push and hold the ENABLE/VERIFY switch on the AACU. (d) While you hold the ENABLE/VERIFY switch, push and hold the VERIFY switch on the AACU. (e) Release the ENABLE/VERIFY switch and the VERIFY switch at the same time. NOTE: The AACU display will show BRK A/B1 during the test. (f) Make sure that the hydraulic pressure at any brake is 1250 ±250 psi (8618 ±1724 kPa) for approximately 10 to 30 seconds, then is 300 ±250 psi (2068 ±1724 kPa) for approximately 5 to 20 seconds, and then is less than 150 psi (1034 kPa). (g) Make sure that the AUTO BRAKE DISARM light, on the P2-2 panel, comes on. (h) Set the AUTO BRAKE selector switch, on the P2-2 panel, to the OFF position. SUBTASK 32-42-00-860-050 (14) Do the steps that follow for AUTO BRAKE selector position 2. EFFECTIVITY ALL (a) Set the AUTO BRAKE selector switch, on the P2-2 panel, to the 2 position.
