(d) Release the ENABLE/VERIFY switch and the VERIFY switch at the same time. NOTE: The AACU display will show BRK A/B2 during the test. (e) Make sure that the hydraulic pressure at any brake is 1500 ±250 psi (10,342 ±1724 kPa) for approximately 10 to 30 seconds, then is 300 ±250 psi (2068 ±1724 kPa) for approximately 5 to 20 seconds, and then is less than 150 psi (1034 kPa). (f) Make sure that the AUTO BRAKE DISARM light, on the P2-2 panel, comes on. (g) Set the AUTO BRAKE selector switch, on the P2-2 panel, to the OFF position. SUBTASK 32-42-00-860-051 (15) Do the steps that follow for AUTO BRAKE selector position 3. (a) Set the AUTO BRAKE selector switch, on the P2-2 panel, to the 3 position. (b) Push and hold the ENABLE/VERIFY switch on the AACU. (c) While you hold the ENABLE/VERIFY switch, push and hold the VERIFY switch on the AACU. (d) Release the ENABLE/VERIFY switch and the VERIFY switch at the same time. NOTE: The AACU display will show BRK A/B3 during the test. (e) Make sure that the hydraulic pressure at any brake is 2000 ±250 psi (13,790 ±1724 kPa) for approximately 10 to 30 seconds, then is 300 ±250 psi (2068 ±1724 kPa)for approximately 5 to 20 seconds, and then is less than 150 psi (1034 kPa). (f) Make sure that the AUTO BRAKE DISARM light, on the P2-2 panel, comes on. (g) Set the AUTO BRAKE selector switch, on the P2-2 panel, to the OFF position. SUBTASK 32-42-00-860-052 (16) Do the steps that follow for AUTO BRAKE selector position MAX. (a) Set the AUTO BRAKE selector switch, on the P2-2 panel, to the MAX position. (b) Push and hold the ENABLE/VERIFY switch on the AACU. (c) While you hold the ENABLE/VERIFY switch, push and hold the VERIFY switch on the AACU. (d) Release the ENABLE/VERIFY switch and the VERIFY switch at the same time. NOTE: The AACU display will show BRK A/B4 during the test. (e) Make sure that the hydraulic pressure at any brake is 3000 ±250 psi (20,684 ±1724 kPa) for approximately 10 to 30 seconds, then is 300 ±250 psi (2068 ±1724 kPa) for approximately 5 to 20 seconds, and then is less than 150 psi (1034 kPa). (f) Make sure that the AUTO BRAKE DISARM light, on the P2-2 panel, comes on. (g) Set the AUTO BRAKE selector switch, on the P2-2 panel, to the OFF position. SUBTASK 32-42-00-860-053 (17) Do the steps that follow for AUTO BRAKE selector position RTO. (a) Set the AUTO BRAKE selector switch, on the P2-2 panel, to the RTO position. (b) Push and hold the ENABLE/VERIFY switch on the AACU. EFFECTIVITY ALL (c) While you hold the ENABLE/VERIFY switch, push and hold the VERIFY switch on the AACU. (d) Release the ENABLE/VERIFY switch and the VERIFY switch at the same time. NOTE: The AACU display will show BRK RTO during the test. (e) Make sure that the hydraulic pressure at any brake is 3000 ±250 psi (20,684 ±1724 kPa) for approximately 15 to 45 seconds, then decays to less than 150 psi (1034 kPa). (f) Make sure that the AUTO BRAKE DISARM light, on the P2-2 panel, comes on. (g) Set the AUTO BRAKE selector switch, on the P2-2 panel, to the OFF position. SUBTASK 32-42-00-860-079 (18) Do the steps that follow to test the brake metered pressure switches. (a) Set the AUTO BRAKE selector switch, on the P2-2 panel, to the 1 position. (b) Push and hold the left brake pedal to the stop. (c) Make sure that the AUTO BRAKE DISARM light, on the P2-2 panel, comes on. (d) Set the AUTO BRAKE selector switch, on the P2-2 panel, to the OFF position and then set it back to the 1 position. (e) Push and hold the right brake pedal to the stop. (f) Make sure that the AUTO BRAKE DISARM light, on the P2-2 panel, comes on. SUBTASK 32-42-00-860-054 (19) Set the AUTO BRAKE selector switch, on the P2-2 panel, to the OFF position. E. Transducer Operational Test

SUBTASK 32-42-00-020-002 (1) If the hubcap is installed, do these steps to remove the hubcap (Figure 503): (a) For an outboard wheel, turn the camlock fasteners 1/4-turn to disconnect the hubcap fairing from the outboard hubcap. (b) Remove and discard MS20995N32 lockwire, G50177, from the bolts of the outboard or inboard hubcap. (c) Remove the bolts and washers to disconnect the outboard or inboard hubcap from the wheel. (d) Remove the outboard or inboard hubcap from the wheel. SUBTASK 32-42-00-020-003 (2) Do the steps that follow to check the mechanical condition of the transducer and drive coupling: (a) Turn the transducer drive coupling while you do a check to make sure that you do not have these conditions: 1) Free play in the bearing for the transducer drive coupling. 2) A drive shaft for the transducer drive coupling that is bent. SUBTASK 32-42-00-860-075 (3) Install the spin up adapter, SPL-1831, in a drill. SUBTASK 32-42-00-710-004 (4) Do these steps for each wheel speed transducer that you will test: NOTE: One person must be at the Main Landing Gear (MLG) brakes to monitor the movement of the brake pistons or wear pins. This is to make sure that the correct brake releases and engages. WARNING KEEP PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT AWAY FROM THRUST REVERSERS. THE OPERATION OF THE WHEEL SPEED TRANSDUCER CAN CAUSE AUTOMATIC OPERATION OF THE STANDBY HYDRAULIC PUMP AND SUDDEN THRUST REVERSER MOVEMENTS. IF YOU DO NOT DO THIS, INJURY TO PERSONS OR DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR. (a) Use the spin up adapter, SPL-1831, and a variable speed drill to turn the wheel speed transducer between 250 and 2200 Revolutions Per Minute (RPM). NOTE: We recommend that you keep the wheel speed below 60 knots. If the aircraft is not in this condition, the standby hydraulic pump can operate automatically. (b) Observe the movement of the brake pistons or wear pins to make sure that the brake at the paired wheel releases (Table 503). NOTE: The wheels are numbered from the left to the right. EFFECTIVITY ALL Table 503/32-42-00-993-805 ANTISKID TRANSDUCER PAIRED WHEELS TRANSDUCER PAIRED WHEEL 1 4 2 3 3 2 4 1 (c) Stop the movement of the wheel speed transducer as quickly as possible. (d) Observe the movement of the brake pistons or wear pins to make sure that the brake at the controlled wheel releases momentarily and then reapplies again in 5 to 10 seconds (Table 504). Table 504/32-42-00-993-808 ANTISKID TRANSDUCER CONTROLLED WHEELS TRANSDUCER CONTROLLED WHEEL 1 1 2 2 3 3 4 4 SUBTASK 32-42-00-420-002 CAUTION DO NOT TIGHTEN THE HUBCAP BOLTS TOO MUCH. MAKE SURE THAT THE HUBCAP IS IN THE CORRECT POSITION BEFORE YOU TIGHTEN THE BOLTS. TOO MUCH TORQUE WILL CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE BOLTS AND THE HUBCAP. (5) Do these steps to install the hubcap (Figure 503): (a) Turn the antiskid transducer dog inside the wheel such that the drive on the hubcap and the dog in the wheel will connect when the hubcap is installed. (b) Put the hubcap in its position on the wheel. 1) Visually make sure that the hubcap is flush with the wheel assembly. a) Use a soft rubber mallet, STD-3906, to lightly tap the hubcap to make it flush. (c) Install the bolts and washers to connect the hubcap to the wheel. 1) Tighten the bolts to 50 in-lb (6 N·m) - 80 in-lb (9 N·m). (d) Install MS20995N32 lockwire, G50177, on the bolts with double twist method (TASK 20-10-44-400-801). (e) Do these steps for the outboard wheel: 1) Put the hubcap fairing on the hubcap. 2) Turn the camlock fasteners 1/4-turn to attach the hubcap fairing to the hubcap.

SUBTASK 32-42-11-860-005 (1) Make sure that these circuit breakers are open and have safety tags: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-3 Row Col Number Name E 16 C00196 LANDING GEAR ANTISKID INBD E 18 C00195 LANDING GEAR ANTISKID OUTBD SUBTASK 32-42-11-860-002 (2) If the support [11] came out of the axle, install the support in the axle with the slot on the back of the support at the top. SUBTASK 32-42-11-420-001 (3) Do these steps to install the transducer [14]: (a) Before you connect the electrical connector [12] to the back of the transducer [14], examine the electrical connector [12] for corrosion. WARNING DO THE STEPS BELOW IF THE AIRPLANE OPERATES WHERE DEICING FLUID THAT CONTAINS POTASSIUM FORMATE OR POTASSIUM ACETATE IS USED. ALSO, DO THE STEPS FOR ALL AIRPLANES THAT YOU FOUND CORROSION IN THE ELECTRICAL CONNECTORS IN THE MAIN WHEEL WELL. THE ELECTRICAL CONNECTORS ARE IN A SYSTEM THAT IS NECESSARY FOR SAFE FLIGHT. (b) If there was corrosion, correct the problem (SWPM 20-60-03). (c) Apply the D5026NS or ZC-026 compound, G50171, to the connector (SWPM 20-60-03). (d) Wind the electrical wire so that the overall coil diameter is approximately 50% of the internal diameter of the landing gear axle diameter. NOTE: If not coiled, the wire bundle section inside the axle is somewhat stiff and may result in hard contact with the inside of the axle. (e) Connect the electrical connector [12] to the back of the transducer [14]. NOTE: Use the label on each electrical connector/wire to find the correct position from the inboard or the outboard transducer. CAUTION DO NOT PULL OR TWIST THE WIRE HARNESS WHEN YOU INSTALL THE TRANSDUCER IN THE AXLE. YOU CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE WIRES AND THE ANTISKID TRANSDUCER. (f) Install the transducer [14] in the axle. 1) Install the transducer [14] in the assembly with the tab on the back of the transducer aligned with the slot inside the support [11]. (g) Do these steps to install the locknut [13]: 1) Install the locknut [13] in its position in the support. 2) Tighten the locknut [13] to 40 ft-lb (54 N·m) - 60 ft-lb (81 N·m) with the locknut wrench set, SPL-1873. 3) Loosen the locknut [13] to 0 ft-lb (0 N·m). 4) Tighten the locknut [13] to 30 ft-lb (41 N·m). EFFECTIVITY ALL 5) Install the MS20995C32 lockwire, G01048, between the locknut [13] and lockwire holes in the support [11] (TASK 20-10-44-400-801). SUBTASK 32-42-11-860-003 (4) Remove the safety tags and close these circuit breakers: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-3 Row Col Number Name E 16 C00196 LANDING GEAR ANTISKID INBD E 18 C00195 LANDING GEAR ANTISKID OUTBD SUBTASK 32-42-11-860-004 (5) Do this task: Transducer Operational Test, TASK 32-42-00-710-802. SUBTASK 32-42-11-420-002 (6) Do these steps to install the bolts [10] to lock the support [11] to the axle assembly: (a) Install the bolts [10] with the head to the inside of the axle. (b) Install the washers [9] and nuts [8]. (c) Do a check of the self locking nuts (TASK 20-50-11-910-801). (d) Tighten the nuts [8] to 63 in-lb (7.1 N·m) - 67 in-lb (7.6 N·m). SUBTASK 32-42-11-420-003 CAUTION DO NOT TIGHTEN THE HUBCAP BOLTS TOO MUCH. MAKE SURE THAT THE HUBCAP IS IN THE CORRECT POSITION BEFORE YOU TIGHTEN THE BOLTS. TOO MUCH TORQUE WILL CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE BOLTS AND THE HUBCAP. (7) Do these steps to install the hubcap [3]: (a) Turn the transducer drive coupling the inside the wheel assembly [1] such that the drive on the hubcap [3] and the dog in the wheel will connect when the hubcap [3] is installed. (b) Put the hubcap [3] in its position on the wheel assembly [1]. 1) Turn it if it is necessary to engage the drive on the hubcap [3] with the drive coupling on the transducer [14]. (c) See the hubcap [3] flush with the wheel assembly [1]. NOTE: Use a soft mallet to lightly tap the hubcap to make it flush. (d) Install the bolts [6] and washers [7] to attach the hubcap [3] to the wheel assembly [1]. (e) Tighten the bolts [6] to 50 in-lb (6 N·m) - 80 in-lb (9 N·m). (f) Install MS20995C32 lockwire, G01048, on the bolts [6] (TASK 20-10-44-400-801). (g) Do these steps for the outboard wheel: 1) Put the hubcap fairing [5] on the hubcap [3]. 2) Turn the CAM-LOCs [4] fasteners 1/4 turn to attach the hubcap fairing [5] to the hubcap [3].

D. Antiskid Valve Removal

CAUTION BE CAREFUL WHEN YOU DISCONNECT THE HYDRAULIC LINES, UNIONS, FILTERS, AND CHECK VALVES FROM THE ANTISKID VALVES. DAMAGE TO THE ANTISKID VALVES CAN OCCUR. SUBTASK 32-42-31-020-001 (1) Disconnect the electrical connector [14] from the antiskid control valve [6]. SUBTASK 32-42-31-020-002 (2) For the UPR normal antiskid control valve [6], do these steps: (a) Disconnect the pressure hydraulic line [17] and pressure hydraulic line [20] from the filter [4]. (b) Disconnect the return hydraulic line [16] from the union [12]. (c) Disconnect the brake hydraulic line [15] from the union [12]. EFFECTIVITY ALL 006, 007, 013, 014, 018-020, 043, 044, 056-063, 067-078, 081, 083-103, 111-114, 121-129, 131, 132, 135, 138-169, 174-179, 182-187, 189-203, 205-209, 212-220, 223, 224, 231-236; 239-298, 301-304, 306, 308, 315-317, 322-341, 343, 346-999 PRE SB 737-32-1528 (Continued) SUBTASK 32-42-31-020-011 (3) For the LWR normal antiskid control valve [6], do these steps: (a) Disconnect the pressure hydraulic line [20] from the filter [4]. (b) Disconnect the return hydraulic line [16] and return hydraulic line [21] from the union [12]. (c) Disconnect the brake hydraulic line [22] from the union [12]. SUBTASK 32-42-31-020-005 (4) For the alternate antiskid control valve [6], do these steps: (a) Disconnect the pressure hydraulic line [25] and pressure hydraulic line [26] from the filter [4]. (b) Disconnect the return hydraulic line [24] from the check valve [13]. (c) Disconnect the brake hydraulic line [23] from the union [12]. SUBTASK 32-42-31-420-007 (5) Install the caps or plugs on the hydraulic lines. SUBTASK 32-42-31-020-003 (6) Remove the bolts [8] and washers [7] to remove the antiskid control valve [6] from the airplane. SUBTASK 32-42-31-020-004 (7) If the normal replacement antiskid control valve [6] does not have hydraulic fittings installed, do these steps: (a) Remove the unions [12] and packings [5]. (b) Remove the filter [11] and packing [10]. (c) Remove the filter [4] and packing [5]. (d) Discard the packings [5] and packing [10]. SUBTASK 32-42-31-020-012 (8) If the alternate replacement antiskid control valve [6] does not have hydraulic fittings installed, do these steps: (a) Remove the union [12] and packing [5]. (b) Remove the filter [11] and packing [10]. (c) Remove the check valve [13] and packing [5]. (d) Remove the filter [4] and packing [5]. (e) Discard the packings [5] and packing [10]. SUBTASK 32-42-31-480-004 (9) Install plugs in the ports of the antiskid control valve [6].

F. Antiskid Valve Installation

SUBTASK 32-42-31-080-001 (1) Remove the plugs from the ports of the antiskid control valve [6]. SUBTASK 32-42-31-420-001 (2) If the replacement antiskid control valve [6] does not have hydraulic fittings installed, do these steps: (a) Lubricate the hydraulic union [12], check valve [13], filter [4], filter [11], packing [10], and packings [5] for the antiskid control valve [6] with hydraulic fluid, D00153. (b) Install the new packings [5] on the hydraulic fittings and install the new packing [10] on the filter [11]. (c) Install the fittings in the antiskid control valve [6]. 1) Install the filter [11] in the brake port of the antiskid control valve [6]. a) Tighten the filter [11] to 475 in-lb (53.7 N·m) - 525 in-lb (59.3 N·m). 2) Install the hydraulic union [12] in the brake port of the antiskid control valve [6]. a) Tighten the hydraulic union [12] to 256 in-lb (28.9 N·m) - 284 in-lb (32.1 N·m). 3) Install the fitting in the return port. a) For the normal antiskid valves, install the hydraulic union [12] in the return port of the normal antiskid control valve [6]. <1> Tighten the hydraulic union [12] to 161 in-lb (18.2 N·m) - 179 in-lb (20.2 N·m). b) For the alternate antiskid valves, install the hydraulic check valve [13] in the return port of the alternate antiskid control valve [6]. <1> Tighten the hydraulic check valve [13] to 161 in-lb (18.2 N·m) - 179 in-lb (20.2 N·m). 4) Install the hydraulic filter [4] in the pressure port of the antiskid control valve [6]. a) Tighten the hydraulic filter [4] to 257 in-lb (29.0 N·m) - 285 in-lb (32.2 N·m). 5) Install MS20995C20 lockwire, G50225, or cable, G50264, on the filter [4] and filter [11]. SUBTASK 32-42-31-100-001 (3) Do the steps below to help get a good electrical bond between the antiskid control valve [6] and bracket: (a) To fully clean the mating surface of the bracket and antiskid control valve [6], do this task: Hand Clean Metal Surfaces with Abrasives, TASK 20-10-34-120-801. EFFECTIVITY ALL 006, 007, 013, 014, 018-020, 043, 044, 056-063, 067-078, 081, 083-103, 111-114, 121-129, 131, 132, 135, 138-169, 174-179, 182-187, 189-203, 205-209, 212-220, 223, 224, 231-236; 239-298, 301-304, 306, 308, 315-317, 322-341, 343, 346-999 PRE SB 737-32-1528 (Continued) 1) Clean the valve body and mating bracket surfaces at a minimum of two of the four lugs (Figure 402). a) Do not clean more than the specified areas to prevent possible corrosion problems. (b) For all cleaned areas, and if there is any damage to the finish on the antiskid control valve [6], manually apply coating, C00064. SUBTASK 32-42-31-420-002 WARNING USE NITRILE GLOVES FOR SKIN PROTECTION WHEN YOU USE COR-BAN 27L. IF IT GETS ON YOUR SKIN, IMMEDIATELY REMOVE IT WITH WATER. IF THIS MATERIAL GETS IN YOUR EYES, IMMEDIATELY FLUSH YOUR EYES WITH WATER. GET MEDICAL AID. THIS MATERIAL CONTAINS FLAMMABLE AGENTS WHICH CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONNEL. (4) Apply Cor-Ban 27L Compound, G50237 (preferred), or corrosion inhibiting material, G50136 (alternate), to all of the areas of the fastener hole. SUBTASK 32-42-31-390-002 (5) Apply sealant, A00247, to the cleaned areas faying surfaces. NOTE: If necessary, you can apply the sealant for this procedure in a maximum interval of no more than eight weeks. SUBTASK 32-42-31-420-006 (6) Hold the antiskid control valve [6] in its position on the airplane. SUBTASK 32-42-31-420-003 (7) Install the bolts [8] and washers [7] that hold the antiskid control valve [6] to the airplane. (a) Make sure that you install the bolts [8] and washers [7] immediately. SUBTASK 32-42-31-080-003 (8) Measure the electrical bonding resistance between the body of the antiskid control valve [6] and bracket (SWPM 20-20-00). (a) Use an intrinsically safe approved bonding meter, COM-1550. (b) Make sure that the electrical bonding resistance is 0.0025 ohms (2.5 milliohms) or less. SUBTASK 32-42-31-390-001 (9) Apply sealant, A00247, to the edge of the antiskid control valve [6] around the mating surface, do this task: Fillet Seal Application, TASK 51-31-00-390-804. (7) For the normal (system B) hydraulic system, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Pressurization, TASK 29-11-00-860-801. SUBTASK 32-42-61-860-013 (8) Set the BRAKE TEST selector switch on the Antiskid/Autobrake Control Unit to A/B. NOTE: In Steps (10) through (14), if the AUTOBRAKE disarm light is on when you push the enable/verify switches, the test will not successfully complete and the display on the front panel of the Antiskid/Autobrake Control Unit will show “BRK ####”. SUBTASK 32-42-61-860-014 (9) Do the steps that follow for autobrake selector position “1”. (a) Set the autobrake selector switch on the P2-2 panel to “OFF” then to the “1” position. (b) Push and then release the RESET switch on the Antiskid/Autobrake Control Unit. NOTE: The display on the front panel of the Antiskid/Autobrake Control Unit will show “MEM CLR”. (c) Push and hold the ENABLE/VERIFY switch on the Antiskid/Autobrake Control Unit. (d) While you hold the ENABLE/VERIFY switch, push and hold the VERIFY switch on the Antiskid/Autobrake Control Unit. (e) Release the ENABLE/VERIFY switch and the VERIFY switch at the same time. NOTE: The Antiskid/Autobrake Control Unit display will show BRK A/B1 during the test. (f) Make sure the AUTOBRAKE DISARM light on the P2-2 panel comes on. (g) Set the autobrake selector switch on the P2-2 panel to”OFF”. SUBTASK 32-42-61-860-015 (10) Do the steps that follow for autobrake selector position “2”. (a) Set the autobrake selector switch on the P2-2 panel to “2”. (b) Push and hold the ENABLE/VERIFY switch on the Antiskid/Autobrake Control Unit. EFFECTIVITY ALL (c) While you hold the ENABLE/VERIFY switch, push and hold the VERIFY switch on the Antiskid/Autobrake Control Unit. (d) Release the ENABLE/VERIFY switch and the VERIFY switch at the same time. NOTE: The Antiskid/Autobrake Control Unit display will show BRK A/B2 during the test. (e) Make sure the AUTOBRAKE DISARM light on the P2-2 panel comes on. (f) Set the autobrake selector switch on the P2-2 panel to “OFF”. SUBTASK 32-42-61-860-016 (11) Do the steps that follow for autobrake selector switch “3”. (a) Set the autobrake selector switch on the P2-2 panel to “3”. (b) Push an hold the ENABLE/VERIFY switch on the Antiskid/Autobrake Control Unit. (c) While you hold the ENABLE/VERIFY switch, push and hold the VERIFY switch on the Antiskid/Autobrake Control Unit. (d) Release the ENABLE/VERIFY switch and the VERIFY switch at the same time. NOTE: The Antiskid/Autobrake Control Unit display will show BRK A/B3 during the test. (e) Make sure the AUTOBRAKE DISARM light on the P2-2 panel comes on. (f) Set the autobrake selector switch on the P2-2 panel to “OFF”. SUBTASK 32-42-61-860-017 (12) Do the steps that follow for the autobrake selector position “MAX”. (a) Set the autobrake selector switch on the P2-2 panel to “MAX”. (b) Push and hold the ENABLE/VERIFY switch on the Antiskid/Autobrake Control Unit. (c) While you hold the ENABLE/VERIFY switch, push and hold the VERIFY switch on the Antiskid/Autobrake Control Unit. (d) Release the ENABLE/VERIFY switch and the VERIFY switch at the same time. NOTE: The Antiskid/Autobrake Control Unit display will show BRK A/B4 during the test. (e) Make sure the AUTOBRAKE DISARM light on the P2-2 panel comes on. (f) Set the autobrake selector switch on the P2-2 panel to “OFF”. SUBTASK 32-42-61-860-018 (13) Do the steps that follow for autobrake selector position “RTO”. (a) Set the autobrake selector switch on the P2-2 panel to “RTO”. (b) Push and hold the ENABLE/VERIFY switch on the Antiskid/Autobrake Control Unit. (c) While you hold the ENABLE/VERIFY switch, push and hold the VERIFY switch on the Antiskid/Autobrake Control Unit. (d) Release the ENABLE/VERIFY switch and the VERIFY switch at the same time. NOTE: The Antiskid/Autobrake Control Unit display will show BRK RTO during the test. (e) Make sure the AUTOBRAKE DISARM light on the P2-2 panel comes on. (f) Set the autobrake selector switch on the P2-2 panel to “OFF”. SUBTASK 32-42-61-860-019 (14) Do the steps that follow to test the brake metered pressure switches. (a) Set the autobrake selector switch on the P2-2 panel to “1”. (b) Push and hold the left brake pedal to the stop. (c) Verify that the AUTOBRAKE DISARM light on the P2-2 panel comes on. EFFECTIVITY ALL (d) Set the autobrake selector switch on the P2-2 panel to “OFF” and then set it back to “1”. (e) Push and hold the right brake pedal to the stop. (f) Verify that the AUTOBRAKE DISARM light on the P2-2 panel comes on. SUBTASK 32-42-61-860-020 (15) Set the autobrake selector switch on the P2-2 panel to “OFF”. SUBTASK 32-42-61-860-021 (16) Set the BRAKE TEST selector switch on the Antiskid/Autobrake Control Unit to NORM.

(a) Make sure that the air charging valve stays open until the reservoir air pressure gauge shows 0 psi (0 kPa). NOTE: This step makes sure that the reservoirs fully release pressure. SUBTASK 32-42-71-860-008 (4) Release the parking brake. EFFECTIVITY ALL SUBTASK 32-42-71-840-002 (5) Operate the brake pedals until the gage at the brake accumulator shows no change in the pressure. F. Autobrake Pressure Control Module Installation

SUBTASK 32-42-81-080-001 (1) Remove the caps/plugs, STD-14686, from the ports of the autobrake pressure control module [20]. SUBTASK 32-42-81-420-001 (2) If the replacement autobrake pressure control module [20] does not have hydraulic fittings installed, do these steps: (a) Lubricate the unions [13], union [18], and packings [14] for the autobrake pressure control module [20] with hydraulic fluid, D00153. (b) Install the packings [14] on the unions [13] and union [18]. (c) Install the unions [13] and union [18] in the autobrake pressure control module [20]. 1) Tighten the unions [13] and union [18] to 360 ±18 in-lb (40.7 ±2.0 N·m). SUBTASK 32-42-81-100-001 (3) To help get a good electrical bond between the autobrake pressure control module [20] and module bracket, do these steps: (a) To fully clean the mating surface of the bracket and autobrake pressure control module [20], do this task: Hand Clean Metal Surfaces with Abrasives, TASK 20-10-34-120-801. (b) Manually apply coating, C00064, to all of the cleaned areas of the bracket. ALL; AIRPLANES WITH PARKER HANNIFIN CORP AUTOBRAKE CONTROL MODULE P/N 78169, -01, -02, -03, -04 (c) Fay surface seal the valve assembly to the bracket with sealant, A02315. ALL SUBTASK 32-42-81-420-002 (4) Install the autobrake pressure control module [20]. EFFECTIVITY ALL WARNING USE NITRILE GLOVES FOR SKIN PROTECTION WHEN YOU USE COR￾BAN 27L. IF IT GETS ON YOUR SKIN, IMMEDIATELY REMOVE IT WITH WATER. IF THIS MATERIAL GETS IN YOUR EYES, IMMEDIATELY FLUSH YOUR EYES WITH WATER. GET MEDICAL AID. THIS MATERIAL CONTAINS FLAMMABLE AGENTS WHICH CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONNEL. (a) Apply Cor-Ban 27L Compound, G50237 (preferred), or corrosion inhibiting material, G50136 (alternate), to the bolts [3] and washers [4] that hold the autobrake pressure control module [20] to the bracket. (b) Install the bolts [3] and washers [4] to hold the autobrake pressure control module [20] to the bracket. (c) Measure the electrical bonding resistance between the autobrake pressure control module [20] and bracket (SWPM 20-20-00). 1) Use an intrinsically safe approved bonding meter, COM-1550. 2) Make sure that the resistance is not more than 0.0025 ohms (2.5 milliohms). (d) Remove the caps/plugs, STD-14686, from the hydraulic line (brake port) [2], hydraulic line (return port) [9], and hydraulic line (pressure port) [11]. (e) Connect the hydraulic lines to the unions [13] and union [18] on the autobrake pressure control module [20]. 1) Tighten the B-nuts on the hydraulic line (brake port) [2], hydraulic line (return port) [9], and hydraulic line (pressure port) [11] to 170 ±9 in-lb (19.2 ±1.0 N·m). (f) Examine the electrical connector [1], electrical connector [6], electrical connector [7], and electrical connector [8] for corrosion. WARNING DO THE STEPS BELOW IF THE AIRPLANE OPERATES WHERE DEICING FLUID THAT CONTAINS POTASSIUM FORMATE OR POTASSIUM ACETATE IS USED. ALSO, DO THE STEPS FOR ALL AIRPLANES THAT YOU FOUND CORROSION IN THE ELECTRICAL CONNECTORS IN THE MAIN WHEEL WELL. THE ELECTRICAL CONNECTORS ARE IN A SYSTEM THAT IS NECESSARY FOR SAFE FLIGHT. 1) If there is corrosion, correct the problem (SWPM 20-60-03). 2) Apply D5026NS or ZC-026 compound, G50171, to the electrical connector [1], electrical connector [6], electrical connector [7], and electrical connector [8] (SWPM 20-60-03). (g) Connect the electrical connector [1], electrical connector [6], electrical connector [7], and electrical connector [8] to the autobrake pressure control module [20]. SUBTASK 32-42-81-390-001 (5) Apply a fillet seal with sealant, A02315, around the mounting points between the autobrake pressure control module [20] and bracket (SWPM 20-20-00, Section 14E). EFFECTIVITY ALL

E. Prepare for the Removal

SUBTASK 32-42-81-480-005 WARNING MAKE SURE THE DOWNLOCK PINS ARE INSTALLED ON ALL THE LANDING GEAR. WITHOUT THE DOWNLOCK PINS, THE LANDING GEAR COULD RETRACT AND CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT. (1) If the downlock pins are not installed in the nose and main landing gear, do this task: Landing Gear Downlock Pins Installation, TASK 32-00-01-480-801. SUBTASK 32-42-81-480-006 (2) Make sure that the tires have chocks installed around them, do one of these tasks: • Chock Installation in Winds or Wind Gusts to a Maximum of 35 Knots, TASK 10-11-05-500-801 • Chock Installation in Winds More than 35 Knots - Handling, TASK 10-11-05-500-802. SUBTASK 32-42-81-860-005 (3) Remove pressure from the normal (system B) and alternate (system A) hydraulic systems, do this task: Hydraulic Reservoirs Depressurization, TASK 29-09-00-860-802 or Hydraulic Reservoirs Depressurization, TASK 29-09-00-860-808. (a) Make sure that the air charging valve stays open until the reservoir air pressure gauge shows 0 psi (0 kPa). NOTE: This step makes sure that the reservoirs fully release pressure. SUBTASK 32-42-81-860-006 (4) Release the parking brake. SUBTASK 32-42-81-840-002 (5) Operate the brake pedals until the gage at the brake accumulator shows no change in the pressure. NOTE: You will have to fully depress, hold for 2 seconds, and release the brake pedals approximately 14 times to completely release the pressure from the accumulator. This will prevent high-pressure fluid spray when replacing components within the hydraulic brake system. (a) After you operate the brake pedals approximately 14 times, open the air charging valve until the reservoir air pressure gauge shows 0 psi (0 kPa) (TASK 29-09-00-860-802 or TASK 29-09-00-860-808). (b) Close the air charging valve (TASK 29-09-00-860-802 or TASK 29-09-00-860-808). SUBTASK 32-42-81-860-010 (6) Set the parking brake. EFFECTIVITY ALL SUBTASK 32-42-81-860-007 (7) Open these circuit breakers and install safety tags: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-3 Row Col Number Name A 16 C01345 LANDING GEAR AUTOBRAKE BITE CONT 2 A 18 C00583 LANDING GEAR AUTOBRAKE BITE CONT 1 E 16 C00196 LANDING GEAR ANTISKID INBD E 18 C00195 LANDING GEAR ANTISKID OUTBD SUBTASK 32-42-81-020-021 (8) Remove the lockwire from the applicable Line Replaceable Unit (LRU).

F. Solenoid Valve Removal

SUBTASK 32-42-81-020-005 (1) Remove the screws [25] and washers [26] that connect the solenoid valve assembly [12] to the autobrake pressure control module [20]. SUBTASK 32-42-81-480-007 CAUTION WHEN YOU REMOVE THE SOLENOID VALVE FROM THE MODULE, MAKE SURE THE VALVE IS KEPT IN A VERTICAL POSITION. IF THE VALVE IS NOT KEPT IN A VERTICAL POSITION, DAMAGE TO THE CONNECTOR PINS CAN OCCUR. CAUTION WHEN YOU REMOVE THE SOLENOID VALVE AND THE GASKET, MAKE SURE THAT CONTAMINATION CAN NOT GO INTO THE MODULE'S OPEN PORTS. DAMAGE TO THE VALVE CAN OCCUR IF LET CONTAMINATION GO INTO THE PORTS. (2) Remove the solenoid valve assembly [12] from the autobrake pressure control module [20]. SUBTASK 32-42-81-480-008 (3) Remove the packing [24] from the solenoid valve assembly [12]. (a) Discard the packing [24]. SUBTASK 32-42-81-020-006 (4) Remove the gasket [27] from the autobrake pressure control module [20]. SUBTASK 32-42-81-480-009 (5) Install the cap/plug, STD-14686, in the port of the solenoid valve assembly [12].

G. Servo Valve Removal

SUBTASK 32-42-81-020-007 (1) Disconnect the electrical connector [7] from the servo valve assembly [10]. SUBTASK 32-42-81-020-008 (2) Remove the screws [22] and washers [23] (if applicable) that connect the servo valve assembly [10] to the autobrake pressure control module [20]. EFFECTIVITY ALL SUBTASK 32-42-81-480-010 CAUTION MAKE SURE THAT CONTAMINATION CAN NOT GO INTO THE MODULE'S OPEN PORTS WHEN YOU REMOVE THE SERVO VALVE AND GASKET. DAMAGE TO THE VALVE CAN OCCUR IF YOU LET CONTAMINATION GO INTO THE PORTS. (3) Remove the servo valve assembly [10] from the autobrake pressure control module [20]. SUBTASK 32-42-81-020-009 (4) Remove the gasket [21]. SUBTASK 32-42-81-480-011 (5) Install the caps/plugs, STD-14686, in the ports of the servo valve assembly [10].

H. Pressure Switch Removal

NOTE: These steps apply to the pressure switch of the solenoid valve and the pressure switch of the servo valve. SUBTASK 32-42-81-020-010 (1) Disconnect the electrical connector [1] or electrical connector [6] from the pressure switch [5]. SUBTASK 32-42-81-480-012 (2) Remove the pressure switch [5] from the autobrake pressure control module [20]. SUBTASK 32-42-81-480-013 (3) Remove the packing [16], packing [17] (if applicable), and retainers [15] from the pressure switch [5]. (a) Discard the packing [16] and packing [17] (if applicable). SUBTASK 32-42-81-480-014 (4) Install the cap/plug, STD-14686, in the port of the pressure switch [5]. ALL; AIRPLANES WITH PARKER HANNIFIN CORP AUTOBRAKE CONTROL MODULE P/N 78169, -01, -02, -03, -04

I. Filter Removal

SUBTASK 32-42-81-020-011 (1) Remove the filter bowl [28] from the autobrake pressure control module [20]. SUBTASK 32-42-81-020-017 (2) Remove the retainers [33] and packing [34] from the filter bowl [28]. (a) Discard the packing [34]. SUBTASK 32-42-81-020-018 (3) Remove the filter [32] from the autobrake pressure control module [20]. SUBTASK 32-42-81-020-019 (4) Remove the retainers [30] and packing [31] from the filter [32]. (a) Discard the packing [31]. SUBTASK 32-42-81-480-023 (5) Install the cap/plug, STD-14686, in the port of the filter bowl [28]. ALL

G. Solenoid Valve Installation

SUBTASK 32-42-81-420-006 (1) Install the packing [24] on the solenoid valve assembly [12]. SUBTASK 32-42-81-480-018 (2) Remove the cap/plug, STD-14686, from the port of the solenoid valve assembly [12]. SUBTASK 32-42-81-480-019 WARNING USE NITRILE GLOVES FOR SKIN PROTECTION WHEN YOU USE COR-BAN 27L. IF IT GETS ON YOUR SKIN, IMMEDIATELY REMOVE IT WITH WATER. IF THIS MATERIAL GETS IN YOUR EYES, IMMEDIATELY FLUSH YOUR EYES WITH WATER. GET MEDICAL AID. THIS MATERIAL CONTAINS FLAMMABLE AGENTS WHICH CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONNEL. (3) Apply Cor-Ban 27L Compound, G50237, (preferred) or corrosion inhibiting material, G50136, (optional) to the screws [25]. SUBTASK 32-42-81-020-012 (4) Install the solenoid valve gasket [27] on the autobrake pressure control module [20]. SUBTASK 32-42-81-020-013 (5) Put the solenoid valve assembly [12] in its position on the autobrake pressure control module [20]. SUBTASK 32-42-81-420-007 (6) Install the screws [25] and washers [26] to connect the solenoid valve assembly [12] to the autobrake pressure control module [20]. (a) Tighten the screws [25] to 75 in-lb (8.47 N·m) - 80 in-lb (9.04 N·m) in a crisscross sequence. 1) Starting with the screw [25] closest to the nearest mounting bolt [3] for the autobrake pressure control module [20], tighten all bolts to 5 in-lb (0.56 N·m) - 10 in-lb (1.13 N·m), then to 35 in-lb (3.95 N·m) - 40 in-lb (4.52 N·m), and then to the final torque. SUBTASK 32-42-81-420-009 (7) Use a 0.0015 in. (0.0381 mm) shim stock to examine the gasket [27] for gaps. (a) No gaps more than 0.0015 in. (0.0381 mm) are permitted. NOTE: This applies to gaps on either side of the gasket. There must be no gap in excess of 0.0015 in. (0.0381 mm) between the solenoid valve and the gasket and between the valve module and the gasket.

SUBTASK 32-42-81-480-020 (1) Remove the caps/plugs, STD-14686, from the ports of the servo valve assembly [10]. (a) Tighten the screws [22] to 75 in-lb (8.47 N·m) - 80 in-lb (9.04 N·m) in a crisscross sequence. 1) Starting with the screw [22] closest to the solenoid valve assembly [12], tighten all screws [22] to 5 in-lb (0.56 N·m) - 10 in-lb (1.13 N·m), then to 35 in-lb (3.95 N·m) - 40 in-lb (4.52 N·m), and then to the final torque. SUBTASK 32-42-81-420-012 (6) Use a 0.0015 in. (0.0381 mm) shim stock to examine the gasket [21] for gaps. (a) No gaps more than 0.0015 in. (0.0381 mm) are permitted. NOTE: This applies to gaps on either side of the gasket. There must be no gap in excess of 0.0015 in. (0.0381 mm) between the servo valve and the gasket and between the valve module and the gasket. WARNING DO THE STEPS BELOW IF THE AIRPLANE OPERATES WHERE DEICING FLUID THAT CONTAINS POTASSIUM FORMATE OR POTASSIUM ACETATE IS USED. ALSO, DO THE STEPS FOR ALL AIRPLANES THAT YOU FOUND CORROSION IN THE ELECTRICAL CONNECTORS IN THE MAIN WHEEL WELL. THE ELECTRICAL CONNECTORS ARE IN A SYSTEM THAT IS NECESSARY FOR SAFE FLIGHT. ALL; AIRPLANES WITH WOODWARD HRT AUTOBRAKE CONTROL MODULE P/N 20102060-101, -102, -103 SUBTASK 32-42-81-420-014 (2) Install the packing [17] in the middle groove of the pressure switch [5]. E. Prepare for the Adjustment

SUBTASK 32-44-00-480-001 WARNING MAKE SURE THE DOWNLOCK PINS ARE INSTALLED ON ALL THE LANDING GEAR. WITHOUT THE DOWNLOCK PINS, THE LANDING GEAR COULD RETRACT AND CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT. F. Parking Brake System - Adjustment

SUBTASK 32-44-00-820-005 (1) Adjust the pawls [11] of the parking brake (Figure 501): (a) Push the two brake pedals fully to the pedal steps, and hold them in position. (b) Extend the pawls [11] one turn at a time until the parking brake can not be set. (c) Retract the pawls [11] 1 to 2 turns to set adjustment or until you get a clearance of 0.04 in. (1.0 mm) - 0.10 in. (2.5 mm) between the pawl [11] and bushing [12]. (d) Make sure that the parking brake can be set from the captain's and first officer's seat. (e) If necessary, adjust the pawls [11] (retract one turn at a time) until the parking brake can be set from the captain's or first officer's seat. NOTE: The more the pawls are retracted, the larger the parking brake bleed-down rate will be. (f) Lock the adjustment. (g) Release the brake pedals. SUBTASK 32-44-00-820-002 (2) Adjust the pawl stop (Figure 501): (a) Turn the bellcranks [13] until the bushings [12] are at their closest point to the aft edge of the pawls [11]. (b) Adjust the pawl stop until the clearance between the aft edge of the pawls [11] and the bushings [12] is 0.16 in. (4.1 mm) – 0.20 in. (5.1 mm): 1) Remove the nut [7] from the pawl stop assembly. 2) Remove the bumper [4], screw [5], and washer [6] from the pawl stop bracket [8]. 3) Add or remove washers [6] until you get the correct clearance. 4) Install the bumper [4], screw [5], and washer [6] on the pawl stop bracket [8]. 5) Install the nut [7] on the pawl stop assembly. (c) Release the bellcrank [13]. SUBTASK 32-44-00-820-003 (3) Adjust the parking brake lever [42] (Figure 501, Figure 502): (a) Install a rig pin LGB2, from rigging pin kit, SPL-1585, through the jackshaft rig pin hole [15] and switch support bracket [18]. (b) Install rig pin LGB1, from rigging pin kit, SPL-1585, through the brake control bell cranks rig pin hole [3] rig pin hole and the left beam structure rig pin hole [49]. (c) Remove the cotter pin [47], washer [46], and the pin [45] from the parking brake lever [42] and the rod [44]. (d) Loosen the jamnut [48] on the bottom of the rod [44]. EFFECTIVITY ALL (e) Adjust the length of the rod [44] until the stop surface of the parking brake lever [42] is against the top of the control stand when the pin [45] is installed. NOTE: If the parking brake rod is adjusted with this method, the rod itself must be turned in full 360 degree turns. The rod assembly is orientation sensitive. (f) Tighten the jamnut [48] on the rod [44]. (g) Install the pin [45], washer [46], and the cotter pin [47] to hold the parking brake lever [42] to the rod [44]. (h) Make sure that the parking brake lever [42] moves smoothly. (i) Remove the rig pin from rigging pin kit, SPL-1585, the jackshaft rig pin hole [15] and the switch support bracket [18]. (j) Remove the rig pin LGB1 from rigging pin kit, SPL-1585, the left beam structure rig pin hole [49] and the hole on the brake control bell cranks rig pin hole [3] rig pin hole. SUBTASK 32-44-00-820-004 (4) Adjust the parking brake latch switch [17] (Figure 501, Figure 502): (a) Make sure that the rudder pedals are released. (b) Pull the parking brake lever [42] on the control stand, until it stops, and hold it in this position. (c) Make sure that the switch actuator [16] lightly contacts the rod end. (d) Make sure that the parking brake light [43], next to the parking brake lever [42], does not turn on. (e) If the switch [17] does not operate in the correct range, do these steps: 1) Install the rig pin LGB1, from rigging pin kit, SPL-1585, to the brake control bell cranks rig pin hole [3] on captain side and left beam structure rig pin hole [49]. 2) Loosen the screws [19] or nuts [20] that hold the switch actuator [16] and switch [17] to the structure. 3) Rotate the pawls [11] until they touch the bellcrank bushing [12]. 4) Adjust the switch actuator [16] until the switch actuator roller [21] touches the end of the rod [1]. 5) Continue to rotate switch [17] until the switch clicks. 6) Back of the switch slightly until the switch clicks 7) Tighten the screws [19] or nuts [20] to 2 in-lb (0.2 N·m) - 3 in-lb (0.3 N·m) above the run-on torque value. 8) Remove the rig pin LGB1, from rigging pin kit, SPL-1585. (f) Push the two rudder pedals and set the parking brake. (g) Make sure that the parking brake light [43] next to the parking brake lever [42] turns on. NOTE: The parking brake light should turn on between 35 and 45 degrees of parking brake lever travel from the released position. (h) Release the parking brake. (i) Make sure that parking brake light [43] goes off. (j) Make sure that the parking brake lever [42] returns to its usual position without assistance. (k) Set the parking brake. EFFECTIVITY ALL SUBTASK 32-44-00-860-004 (5) Close this access panel: Number Name/Location 112A Forward Access Door

E. Procedure

SUBTASK 32-44-00-790-001 WARNING KEEP PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT CLEAR OF THE FLIGHT CONTROL SURFACES, THE THRUST REVERSERS, AND THE LANDING GEAR. THESE COMPONENTS CAN MOVE SUDDENLY WHEN YOU SUPPLY HYDRAULIC POWER. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT. (1) For the B hydraulic system, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Pressurization, TASK 29-11-00-860-801. SUBTASK 32-44-00-720-001 (2) Make sure that the pressure shown on the HYD BRAKE PRESS gage is approximately the same as the B hydraulic system pressure. NOTE: The HYD BRAKE PRESS gage is in the flight compartment on the main instrument panel for the first officer. SUBTASK 32-44-00-710-001 (3) Do these steps for the captain's brake pedals: (a) Push the two brake pedals fully to their stops and set the parking brake. (b) Release the brake pedals. (c) Make sure the parking brake engages. (d) Make sure the parking brake light on the control stand is on. (e) Look at the pistons on each brake to see that the brakes are engaged. (f) Release the parking brake. (g) Make sure the parking brake light on the control stand is off. (h) Look at the pistons on each brake to see that the brakes are not engaged. (i) For the B hydraulic system, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Power Removal, TASK 29-11-00-860-805 (j) Fully push the captain's brake pedals twelve times to remove the pressure from the brake accumulator. (k) Push the two brake pedals fully to their stops and set the parking brake. (l) Release the brake pedals. (m) Make sure the parking brake engages. (n) Make sure the parking brake light on the control stand is on. EFFECTIVITY ALL (o) Look at the pistons on each brake to see that the brakes are not engaged. (p) Release the parking brake. WARNING KEEP PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT CLEAR OF THE FLIGHT CONTROL SURFACES, THE THRUST REVERSERS, AND THE LANDING GEAR. THESE COMPONENTS CAN MOVE SUDDENLY WHEN YOU SUPPLY HYDRAULIC POWER. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT. (q) For the B hydraulic system, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Pressurization, TASK 29-11-00-860-801. (r) Push the left brake pedal fully to the stop. (s) Pull the parking brake lever on the control stand. (t) Make sure the parking brake will not engage. (u) Make sure the parking brake light on the control stand is off. (v) Look at the pistons on each brake to see that the brakes on the left gear are engaged and the brakes on the right gear are not engaged. (w) Release the left brake pedal. (x) Push the right brake pedal fully to the stop. (y) Pull the parking brake lever on the control stand. (z) Make sure the parking brake will not engage. (aa) Make sure the parking brake light on the control stand is off. (ab) Look at the pistons on each brake to see that the brakes on the right gear are engaged and the brakes on the left gear are not engaged. (ac) Release the right brake pedal. SUBTASK 32-44-00-710-002 (4) Do these steps for the first officer's brake pedals: (a) Push the two brake pedals fully to their stops and set the parking brake. (b) Release the brake pedals. (c) Make sure the parking brake engages. (d) Release the parking brake. (e) Push the left brake pedal fully to the stop. (f) Pull the parking brake lever on the control stand. (g) Make sure the parking brake will not engage. (h) Release the left brake pedal. (i) Push the right brake pedal fully to the stop. (j) Pull the parking brake lever on the control stand. (k) Make sure the parking brake will not engage. (l) Release the right brake pedal. SUBTASK 32-44-00-080-001 (5) Remove rig pins R1 and R2 from the rudder pedal shaft [2]. EFFECTIVITY ALL SUBTASK 32-44-00-720-002 (6) Do this task: Parking Brake Hold Check, TASK 32-44-00-790-801.

32-44-00-790-801Parking Brake Hold CheckPDF p. 1754

4. Parking Brake Hold Check NOTE: This procedure is a scheduled maintenance task.

A. General

(1) This task includes these steps: (a) Parking brake system bleed down test - parking brake set (b) Parking brake system bleed down test - parking brake released.

B. References

Reference Title 10-11-05 P/B 201 CHOCK INSTALLATION 29-11-00-860-801 Hydraulic System A or B Pressurization (P/B 201) 29-11-00-860-805 Hydraulic System A or B Power Removal (P/B 201) 32-00-01-480-801 Landing Gear Downlock Pins Installation (P/B 201)

C. Location Zones

Zone Area 211 Flight Compartment - Left 734 Left Main Landing Gear 744 Right Main Landing Gear

D. Prepare for the Check

SUBTASK 32-44-00-480-007 WARNING MAKE SURE THAT THE DOWNLOCK PINS ARE INSTALLED ON ALL THE LANDING GEAR. WITHOUT THE DOWNLOCK PINS, THE LANDING GEAR CAN RETRACT. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONS, AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT. (1) If the downlock pins are not installed in the nose and main landing gear, do this task: Landing Gear Downlock Pins Installation, TASK 32-00-01-480-801. SUBTASK 32-44-00-480-008 (2) Make sure the tires have chocks installed around them (PAGEBLOCK 10-11-05/201). SUBTASK 32-44-00-860-007 (3) Release the parking brake. SUBTASK 32-44-00-860-008 (4) For the A and B hydraulic systems, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Power Removal, TASK 29-11-00-860-805. SUBTASK 32-44-00-870-001 (5) Push the Captain's or the First Officer's left and right toe brake pedals to the stops several times until the brakes no longer actuate. NOTE: This will release the hydraulic pressure at the accumulator. (a) Check the pistons on each brake to make sure that the brakes no longer actuate when the brake pedals are pushed. EFFECTIVITY ALL SUBTASK 32-44-00-860-009 (6) Make sure that the brake accumulator Nitrogen charge is correct. NOTE: Correct charge pressure from the accumulator placard are located on the rear bulkhead in the right main gear wheel well. SUBTASK 32-44-00-790-002 WARNING KEEP PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT CLEAR OF THE FLIGHT CONTROL SURFACES, THE THRUST REVERSERS, AND THE LANDING GEAR. THESE COMPONENTS CAN MOVE SUDDENLY WHEN YOU SUPPLY HYDRAULIC POWER. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT. (7) To pressurize B hydraulic system to 3000 ±150 psig (20,684 ±1034 kPa), do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Pressurization, TASK 29-11-00-860-801. SUBTASK 32-44-00-860-010 (8) Set the parking brake. NOTE: This step keeps the brake system pressurized with the accumulator. SUBTASK 32-44-00-720-003 (9) Wait at least 10 minutes for the accumulator temperature to stabilize.

E. Parking Brake Hold Check - Parking Brake Set

SUBTASK 32-44-00-720-004 (1) Write down the pressure shown on the PRESS gage for the brake accumulator. NOTE: The PRESS gage is located on the rear bulkhead in the right main gear wheel well. SUBTASK 32-44-00-860-011 (2) For the B hydraulic systems, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Power Removal, TASK 29-11-00-860-805. NOTE: This will leave the accumulator charged and pressurized. (a) Record the initial time when the B hydraulic system pressure is removed. SUBTASK 32-44-00-710-003 (3) Do a check of the brake pressure at the end of any of the time periods that follow. If the necessary pressure drop for one time period is not within the limits, use the next time period. NOTE: It is permitted to read the brake pressure from the brake pressure gage in the cockpit, or the brake accumulator gage in the wheel well. (a) After 10 minutes, the pressure drop should be less than 100 psi (689 kPa). (b) After 30 minutes, the pressure drop should be less than 300 psi (2068 kPa). (c) After 1 hour, the pressure drop should be less than 500 psi (3447 kPa). (d) After 8 hours, the pressure should be greater than 1200 psi (8274 kPa) minimum. SUBTASK 32-44-00-780-001 (4) If the brake accumulator pressure drops faster than permitted, do a check for leaks in the accumulator system. SUBTASK 32-44-00-780-002 (5) The trouble shooting of the brake system can be delayed until the next convenient maintenance period if the conditions that follow are met: (a) With the parking brake set, make sure that the brake accumulator pressure drop is less than 800 psi (5516 kPa) in the first 30 minutes. EFFECTIVITY ALL (b) The system passes the parking brake hold check - parking brake released. SUBTASK 32-44-00-860-012 (6) Release the parking brake. SUBTASK 32-44-00-720-005 (7) Push the Captain's or First Officer's left and right toe brake pedals to the stops 7 times while observing the brake pistons on all of the brakes. NOTE: Wait approximately 3 seconds each time you apply the brakes. (a) Make sure that the brake pistons compress and release each of the 7 times the pedals are pushed.

F. Parking Brake Hold Check - Parking Brake Released

SUBTASK 32-44-00-790-003 WARNING KEEP PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT CLEAR OF THE FLIGHT CONTROL SURFACES, THE THRUST REVERSERS, AND THE LANDING GEAR. THESE COMPONENTS CAN MOVE SUDDENLY WHEN YOU SUPPLY HYDRAULIC POWER. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT. (1) Pressurize B hydraulic system to 3000 ±150 psig (20,684 ±1034 kPa), do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Pressurization, TASK 29-11-00-860-801. SUBTASK 32-44-00-720-006 (2) Wait at least 10 minutes for the accumulator temperature to stabilize. SUBTASK 32-44-00-720-007 (3) Write down the pressure shown on the PRESS gage for the brake accumulator. NOTE: The PRESS gage is located on the rear bulkhead in the right main gear wheel well. SUBTASK 32-44-00-860-013 (4) For the B hydraulic systems, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Power Removal, TASK 29-11-00-860-805. NOTE: This will leave the accumulator charged and pressurized. (a) Record the initial time when the B hydraulic system pressure is removed. SUBTASK 32-44-00-780-003 (5) Do a check of the brake pressure at 30 minutes after the test start. (a) Make sure that the pressure decrease of the brake accumulator is less than 450 psi (3103 kPa). SUBTASK 32-44-00-780-004 (6) If the brake accumulator pressure drops faster than permitted, do a check the accumulator system for leaks. EFFECTIVITY ALL

G. Put the Airplane Back to Its Usual Condition

F. Parking Brake Shutoff Valve Installation

SUBTASK 32-44-21-080-001 (1) Remove the plugs or caps from the ports of the parking brake shutoff valve assy [5]. SUBTASK 32-44-21-420-001 (2) If the replacement parking brake shutoff valve assy [5] does not have hydraulic fittings installed, do these steps: (a) Lubricate the reducer [3], reducer [7] and packings [4] for the parking brake shutoff valve assy [5] with hydraulic fluid, D00153, or MCS 352B fluid, D00054. (b) Install the packing [4] on the reducer [3]. (c) Install the reducer [3] in the parking brake shutoff valve assy [5]. (d) Install the packing [4] on the reducer [7]. (e) Install the reducer [7] in the parking brake shutoff valve assy [5]. SUBTASK 32-44-21-100-001 (3) Do the steps below to help get a good electrical bond between the valve assy [5] and the support bracket: (a) To fully clean the mating surface of the support bracket and the valve assy [5], do this task: Hand Clean Metal Surfaces with Abrasives, TASK 20-10-34-120-801. (b) For all cleaned areas, and if there is any damage to the finish on the valve assy [5], manually apply coating, C00064. SUBTASK 32-44-21-390-001 WARNING USE NITRILE GLOVES FOR SKIN PROTECTION WHEN YOU USE COR-BAN 27L. IF IT GETS ON YOUR SKIN, IMMEDIATELY REMOVE IT WITH WATER. IF THIS MATERIAL GETS IN YOUR EYES, IMMEDIATELY FLUSH YOUR EYES WITH WATER. GET MEDICAL AID. THIS MATERIAL CONTAINS FLAMMABLE AGENTS WHICH CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONNEL. (4) Apply a layer of the Cor-Ban 27L Compound, G50237, (preferred) or corrosion inhibiting material, G50136, (alternate), to the threads and the shank of each bolt [2]. (a) Do not let the Cor-Ban 27L Compound, G50237, or corrosion inhibiting material, G50136, dry before you install the bolts [2]. (b) Install the bolts [2] when the Cor-Ban 27L Compound, G50237, or corrosion inhibiting material, G50136, is wet. EFFECTIVITY ALL SUBTASK 32-44-21-390-003 WARNING USE NITRILE GLOVES FOR SKIN PROTECTION AGAINST CORROSION INHIBITOR MATERIAL, G50136. IF CORROSION INHIBITOR MATERIAL, G50136 GETS ON YOUR SKIN, IMMEDIATELY REMOVE IT WITH WATER. IF THIS MATERIAL GETS IN YOUR EYES, IMMEDIATELY FLUSH YOUR EYES WITH WATER AND GET MEDICAL AID. THIS MATERIAL CONTAINS VERY POISONOUS AND FLAMMABLE AGENTS WHICH CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONNEL. (5) Apply a layer of corrosion inhibiting material, G50136, to the mating surface of the mounting bracket. NOTE: Do not let corrosion inhibiting material, G50136, dry before the bolts installation. SUBTASK 32-44-21-420-002 (6) Hold the parking brake shutoff valve assy [5] in its position on the airplane. SUBTASK 32-44-21-420-003 (7) Install the bolt [2] and washer [1] which hold the parking brake shutoff valve assy [5] to the airplane. SUBTASK 32-44-21-210-001 (8) Make sure that there is squeeze-out around mating surfaces of the support bracket and parking brake shutoff valve assy [5]. SUBTASK 32-44-21-100-002 WARNING USE NITRILE GLOVES FOR SKIN PROTECTION AGAINST CORROSION INHIBITOR MATERIAL, G50136. IF CORROSION INHIBITOR MATERIAL, G50136 GETS ON YOUR SKIN, IMMEDIATELY REMOVE IT WITH WATER. IF THIS MATERIAL GETS IN YOUR EYES, IMMEDIATELY FLUSH YOUR EYES WITH WATER AND GET MEDICAL AID. THIS MATERIAL CONTAINS VERY POISONOUS AND FLAMMABLE AGENTS WHICH CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONNEL. (9) If it is necessary, remove the excess of corrosion inhibiting material, G50136, with a dry lint-free cloth, G01043. NOTE: The stains of the corrosion inhibiting material, G50136, remaining in crevices are acceptable. SUBTASK 32-44-21-760-001 (10) Use an intrinsically safe approved bonding meter, COM-1550, to measure the electrical resistance between the valve assy [5] and the bracket. (a) Make sure that the resistance is less than 0.0025 ohms. (b) If the measured resistance is not less than 0.0025 ohms, do the steps to clean the mating surfaces of the bracket and valve assy [5]. (c) Apply coating, C00064, again. SUBTASK 32-44-21-080-002 (11) Remove the caps or plugs from the elbow and the tee fitting. SUBTASK 32-44-21-420-004 (12) Connect the tee fitting to the reducer [3] on the parking brake shutoff valve assy [5]. SUBTASK 32-44-21-420-005 (13) Connect the elbow to the reducer [7] on the parking brake shutoff valve assy [5]. EFFECTIVITY ALL SUBTASK 32-44-21-420-006 (14) Before you connect the electrical connector [6] to the parking brake shutoff valve assy [5], examine the connector for corrosion. WARNING DO THE STEPS BELOW IF THE AIRPLANE OPERATES WHERE DEICING FLUID THAT CONTAINS POTASSIUM FORMATE OR POTASSIUM ACETATE IS USED. ALSO, DO THE STEPS FOR ALL AIRPLANES THAT YOU FOUND CORROSION IN THE ELECTRICAL CONNECTORS IN THE MAIN WHEEL WELL. THE ELECTRICAL CONNECTORS ARE IN A SYSTEM THAT IS NECESSARY FOR SAFE FLIGHT. (a) If there was corrosion, correct the problem SWPM 20-60-03. (b) Apply the D5026NS or ZC-026 compound, G50171, to the connector (SWPM 20-60-03). (15) Connect the electrical connector [6] to the parking brake shutoff valve assy [5]. SUBTASK 32-44-21-860-004 (16) Remove the safety tag and close this circuit breaker: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-3 Row Col Number Name B 16 C01346 LANDING GEAR PARKING BRAKE

G. Parking Brake Shutoff Valve Installation Test

SUBTASK 32-44-21-790-001 (1) Do these steps to do a leak check of the parking brake shutoff valve assy [5]: WARNING KEEP PERSONNEL AND EQUIPMENT AWAY FROM THE FLIGHT CONTROL SURFACES, THE THRUST REVERSERS, DRIVE MECHANISMS AND THE LANDING GEAR. THESE COMPONENTS CAN MOVE SUDDENLY WHEN YOU OPERATE THEM WITH ELECTRICAL OR HYDRAULIC POWER. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONNEL AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT. SUBTASK 32-44-21-710-002 (3) Do these steps to do a check of the parking brake shutoff valve assy [5] installation: (a) Set the parking brake. (b) Make sure that the parking brake light on the captain's control stand comes on. (c) Release the parking brake. (d) Make sure that the parking brake light is off. D. Deflate the Tire

SUBTASK 32-45-00-480-001 WARNING MAKE SURE THAT THE DOWNLOCK PINS ARE INSTALLED ON ALL THE LANDING GEAR. WITHOUT THE DOWNLOCK PINS, THE LANDING GEAR CAN RETRACT. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONS, AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT. (1) If the downlock pins are not installed in the nose and main landing gear, do this task: Landing Gear Downlock Pins Installation, TASK 32-00-01-480-801. SUBTASK 32-45-00-480-005 (2) Make sure that the wheel and tire assembly is clear of the ground before you deflate the tire, do the task that applies for the nose or the main landing gear: EFFECTIVITY ALL (a) Do this task: Lift the Main Landing Gear Axles with the Axle Jacks, TASK 07-11-03-580-801. (b) Do this task: Lift the Airplane Nose Landing Gear with the Axle Jack at Jack Point E, TASK 07-11-03-580-802. SUBTASK 32-45-00-480-002 (3) Remove the valve cap [1] from the wheel and tire. SUBTASK 32-45-00-840-001 WARNING DEFLATE THE TIRE BEFORE YOU REMOVE THE WHEEL AND TIRE ASSEMBLY. OR, DO AN INSPECTION OF THE WHEEL AND TIRE TO MAKE SURE THAT THEY ARE SAFE. AIR PRESSURE CAN CAUSE AN EXPLOSION OF THE DAMAGED WHEEL AND TIRE COMPONENTS. INJURIES TO PERSONNEL, AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR. WARNING MAKE SURE THAT ALL PERSONNEL ARE CLEAR OF THE INFLATION VALVE ASSEMBLY PATH WHILE YOU REMOVE IT. IF THE INFLATION VALVE ASSEMBLY EJECTS WHILE YOU REMOVE IT, INJURY TO PERSONNEL CAN OCCUR. (4) Deflate the tire with the small bore tire deflator, COM-4046 or large bore tire deflator, COM-1524. NOTE: Always go near the wheels from the front or rear. NOTE: If the tire is hot, let the tire cool before you deflate it. WARNING DO NOT LOOSEN OR REMOVE THE VALVE BODY UNDER PRESSURE. THE VALVE CAN BLOW OUT CAUSING INJURY TO PERSONNEL. (a) If you cannot use the usual procedure to deflate the tire because the valve core is damaged, do these steps: 1) Turn the valve assembly slowly in a counterclockwise direction until there is gas leakage through the boss. 2) At the same time, push lightly on the valve assembly. 3) After all of the gas has been released, remove the valve assembly from the tire.

D. Tires Inspection

SUBTASK 32-45-00-480-004 WARNING MAKE SURE THE DOWNLOCK PINS ARE INSTALLED ON ALL THE LANDING GEAR. WITHOUT THE DOWNLOCK PINS, THE LANDING GEAR CAN RETRACT AND CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT. (1) If the downlock pins are not installed in the nose and main landing gear, do this task: Landing Gear Downlock Pins Installation, TASK 32-00-01-480-801. SUBTASK 32-45-00-220-002 (2) Do this task: Landing Gear Tire Pressure Check and Tire Servicing, TASK 12-15-51-780-801. SUBTASK 32-45-00-210-009 (3) Do the steps that follow and examine the tires (Figure 601, Figure 602): (a) Examine the tires for air leaks, abrasions, unusual worn areas, cuts, and flat spots. (b) Examine the tires for the presence of contaminants. 1) Keep the tires clean of contaminants such as oils, fuels, hydraulic fluids, aircraft cleaning agents, and greases. 2) Cover the tire if these or other potentially harmful chemicals spill on the tire. 3) Wipe off the tire with a soapy solution if the tire becomes contaminated. 4) The tire should be removed from service as soon as practical if the surface of the tire appears soft, spongy, or there are bulges present. (c) Remove the tires that have the conditions that follow: 1) Cuts or weather cracks in the grooves, the tread, shoulders or sidewalls that exceed the limits in (Figure 602). 2) Blisters, bulges, or other signs of ply separation in the tread, shoulder or sidewall area. 3) Tires with a flat spot which shows the tread reinforcement ply (bias) or cut protector (radial). NOTE: If the tread reinforcement ply (bias) or the cut protector (radial) shows, the tire should be replaced as soon as possible. If necessary, the tire may be used for a small number of landings until it is replaced. However, you may not be able to retread the tire if you leave the tire in service too long with this condition. 4) Other types of damage which can cause tire problems. (d) Examine the tires for worn areas: 1) Measure the depth of the tire tread groove at three points that are equally apart. 2) If the average depth of any groove is 1/32 inch (0.79 mm) or less, the tire must be replaced at the next convenient maintenance opportunity. 3) If the tread belt ply (radial) or carcass ply (bias) shows at any location, the tire is not serviceable and must be replaced. EFFECTIVITY ALL 4) If the tread is worn so that the cut protector (radial) or tread reinforcement ply (bias) shows at any location, the tire must be replaced at the next convenient maintenance opportunity. NOTE: If the cut protector (radial) or tread reinforcement ply (bias) shows, the tire should be replaced as soon as possible. If necessary, the tire may be used for a small number of landings until it is replaced. However, you may not be able to retread the tire if you leave the tire in service too long with this condition.

E. Prepare for the Inspection

SUBTASK 32-45-00-020-002 (1) If not previously done, perform the following tasks as applicable: (a) For the Main Landing Gear: Main Landing Gear Wheel and Tire Assembly Removal, TASK 32-45-11-000-801. (b) For the Nose Landing Gear: Nose Landing Gear Wheel and Tire Assembly - Removal, TASK 32-45-21-000-801.

F. Wheel Bearings Inspection

SUBTASK 32-45-00-020-003 (1) Remove the bearing cone from the bearing cup (Figure 603). EFFECTIVITY ALL SUBTASK 32-45-00-210-014 (2) Put the bearing cone in a clean area. (a) Make sure that no unwanted materials get into the bearing cone while setting it aside. SUBTASK 32-45-00-210-011 (3) Examine the internal and external surfaces of the bearing cup and cone for water or any other unwanted material in the grease. (a) If water or unwanted material is found in the grease, remove and replace the entire wheel assembly. NOTE: It is normal for the grease color to change from red or light brown to dark brown, gray, or black. Grease color is not a cause to reject unless the grease color is white. White color is an indication that grease contains unwanted water. SUBTASK 32-45-00-210-012 (4) Examine the internal and external surfaces of the bearing cup and cone for any obvious signs of cracking, flat spots or damage. (a) If cracking, flat spots or damage is found, remove and replace the entire wheel assembly, including the wheel bearing cone. SUBTASK 32-45-00-100-001 (5) Wipe off the grease only from the cup race with a lint-free cloth, G00834. (a) Remove only enough grease to get a clear view of bearing cup race surface. (b) Do not use solvents to clean the bearing cup race surface. SUBTASK 32-45-00-210-013 (6) Visually examine the cup race with a flashlight for marks, discoloration or corrosion. See (Figure 604) for examples of marks and discolorations. (a) If no defects are found, do the steps: 1) Re-apply a thin layer of bearing grease Aeroshell 22 grease, D00378, Mobil 28 grease, D00233 or Mobil Aviation Grease SHC 100 grease, D50005 to the surface of the cup race. 2) Re-insert the wheel bearing cone into the bearing cup. (b) If discoloration, texture or surface corrosion is found, attempt to remove it by gently using Scotch-Brite 7447 pad, G51224 or Scotch-Brite 7448 pad, G50492. Perform this task for no longer than 2 minutes. 1) Equivalent abrasive papers or cloths to the ones given inhere (with a grade between 600 to 1000) can be used instead. 2) Do not use wire metal brushes, rotary brushes or flappers of any kind to perform this task. (c) After the area has been reworked, slowly slide a ball point pen, a non-metallic scraper/pick or a bare fingernail along the whole cup race surface to feel for abnormalities: 1) If texture is felt, remove and replace the entire wheel assembly including the wheel bearing cone. 2) If corrosion is still present, remove and replace the entire wheel assembly including the wheel bearing cone. 3) If no texture is felt, do the steps: EFFECTIVITY ALL a) Re-apply a thin layer of bearing grease Aeroshell 22 grease, D00378, Mobil 28 grease, D00233 or Mobil Aviation Grease SHC 100 grease, D50005 to the surface of the cup race. b) Re-insert the wheel bearing cone into the bearing cup.

G. Put the Airplane Back to Its Usual Condition

SUBTASK 32-45-00-840-002 (1) Do as applicable: (a) For the Main Landing Gear: Main Landing Gear Wheel and Tire Assembly Installation, TASK 32-45-11-400-801. (b) For the Nose Landing Gear: Nose Landing Gear Wheel and Tire Assembly - Installation, TASK 32-45-21-400-801.

D. Tire Inflation Valve Removal

SUBTASK 32-45-08-420-001 (1) Install landing gear downlocks, do this task: Landing Gear Downlock Pins Installation, TASK 32-00-01-480-801. SUBTASK 32-45-08-420-002 (2) Install chocks around all tires (CHOCK INSTALLATION, PAGEBLOCK 10-11-05/201). EFFECTIVITY ALL SUBTASK 32-45-08-580-001 (3) Raise axle on jack so that there is clearance between the wheel and tire assembly and the ground, do these tasks: • Lift the Main Landing Gear Axles with the Axle Jacks, TASK 07-11-03-580-801, • Lift the Airplane Nose Landing Gear with the Axle Jack at Jack Point E, TASK 07-11-03-580-802. SUBTASK 32-45-08-840-001 WARNING MAKE SURE THAT YOU DEFLATE THE TIRE BEFORE YOU REMOVE THE VALVE. IF YOU DO NOT DEFLATE THE TIRE, VALVE PARTS CAN COME OUT OF THE VALVE AT A HIGH VELOCITY WHEN YOU TRY TO REMOVE THE VALVE. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONNEL. WARNING MAKE SURE THAT ALL PERSONNEL ARE CLEAR OF THE INFLATION VALVE ASSEMBLY PATH WHILE YOU REMOVE IT. IF THE INFLATION VALVE ASSEMBLY EJECTS WHILE YOU REMOVE IT, INJURY TO PERSONNEL CAN OCCUR. WARNING BE VERY CAREFUL WHEN DEFLATING TIRES TO PREVENT INJURY TO PERSONNEL FROM A FLYING INFLATION VALVE CAP AND/OR VALVE CORE. CAUTION MAKE SURE THAT THE DEFLATED TIRE THAT IS ON THE AXLE DOES NOT TOUCH THE GROUND. IF THE TIRE DOES TOUCH THE GROUND, THE TIRE'S BEAD SEAT CAN MOVE OUT OF ITS POSITION AND BECOME UNSEATED. THE UNSEATED BEAD SEAT CAN CAUSE LEAKAGE WHICH THEN CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE TIRE AND WHEEL. (4) Deflate the tire with small bore tire deflator, COM-4046 or large bore tire deflator, COM-1524, do this task: Add Nitrogen or Air to the Tire, TASK 12-15-51-610-802. SUBTASK 32-45-08-020-002 (5) If it is necessary, remove the lockwire from the valve. SUBTASK 32-45-08-020-003 (6) Remove the valve from the wheel.

F. Tire Inflation Valve Installation

SUBTASK 32-45-08-210-001 (1) Do a check of the port in the wheel half for cracks, burrs, or scratches propagating from the port. (a) If cracks, burrs, or scratches are present, remove the wheel and the tire. SUBTASK 32-45-08-420-006 (2) If the main and nose wheel assemblies used the tire pressure sensor as an inflation valve [2], do these steps: NOTE: There are two configurations available for the tire inflation valve: • A standard valve • A combination inflation valve/pressure sensor. (a) For the Goodrich wheel assembly, do these steps: 1) Apply a thin layer of grease, D00504, for the orange or red packing [1], or PST 525 silicone grease, D50113, for the black packing [1]. 2) Prevent contact packing [1] with the thread of the inflation valve [2]. 3) Use a socket wrench, STD-7044, to install the inflation valve [2] on the wheel. 4) Tighten the tire inflation valve [2] to 150 in-lb (16.9 N·m) - 200 in-lb (22.6 N·m). 5) Make sure that the red mark on the tire is aligned with the inflation valve [2]. NOTE: The red dot identifies the lightest area of the tire. 6) If it is necessary, install MS20995C32 lockwire, G01048, between the inflation valve [2] and the outboard wheel. EFFECTIVITY ALL (b) For the Safran wheel assembly, do these steps: 1) Apply a thin layer of vaseline, D50395, for the red packing [1], or PST 525 silicone grease, D50113, for the black packing [1]. 2) Apply Loctite 242 adhesive, A50584, or Loctite 243 adhesive, A50585, to the inflation valve [2] threads. NOTE: It is necessary to install and tighten the inflation valve within 1 minute of the application of retaining compound. If it is tightened after 1 minute of the application of retaining compound, the bond of the retaining compound will not be satisfactory and inflation valve must be removed and installed again. 3) Do not let the primer or retaining compound touch the packing [1]. 4) Use a socket wrench, STD-7044, to install the inflation valve [2] on the wheel. 5) Tighten the tire inflation valve [2] to 150 in-lb (16.9 N·m) - 200 in-lb (22.6 N·m). a) Make sure that the inflation valve [2] was tightened within 1 minute after application of compound. 6) Make sure that the red mark on the tire is aligned with the inflation valve [2]. NOTE: The red dot identifies the lightest area of the tire. SUBTASK 32-45-08-420-003 (3) If the inflation valve [2] is not a combination valve and tire pressure sensor, do these steps to install the inflation valve [2]: (a) Install the inflation valve [2] to the main wheel assembly. 1) For the Goodrich main wheel assembly, do these steps: a) Apply a thin layer of grease, D00504, for the orange or red packing [1] or PST 525 silicone grease, D50113, for the black packing [1]. b) Prevent contact packing [1] with the thread of the inflation valve [2]. c) Tighten the tire inflation valve [2]. <1> For wheel assemblies with steel brakes, tighten the inflation valve [2] to 165 in-lb (18.6 N·m)-200 in-lb (22.6 N·m). <2> For wheel assemblies with carbon brakes, tighten the inflation valve [2] to 210 in-lb (23.7 N·m). d) Install MS20995C32 lockwire, G01048, between the inflation valve [2] and the outer wheel. 2) For the Safran main wheel assembly, do these steps: a) Apply a thin layer of vaseline, D50395, for the red packing [1], or PST 525 silicone grease, D50113, for the black packing [1]. b) Apply Loctite 242 adhesive, A50584, or Loctite 243 adhesive, A50585, to the tire inflation valve [2] thread. c) Prevent contact packing [1] with the thread of the inflation valve [2]. d) Tighten the tire inflation valve [2] to 182.7 in-lb (20.6 N·m) - 197.9 in-lb (22.4 N·m). 3) For the Honeywell main wheel assembly, do these steps: a) Install the packing [1] on the inflation valve [2]. b) Tighten the tire inflation valve [2] to 150 in-lb (16.9 N·m) - 200 in-lb (22.6 N·m). c) If it is necessary, install MS20995C32 lockwire, G01048. EFFECTIVITY ALL (b) Install the inflation valve [2] to the nose wheel assembly. 1) For the Goodrich nose wheel assembly, do these steps: a) Apply a thin layer of grease, D00504, for the orange or red packing [1], or PST 525 silicone grease, D50113, for the black packing [1]. b) Prevent contact packing [1] with the thread of the inflation valve [2]. c) Tighten the tire inflation valve [2] to 175 in-lb (19.8 N·m). 2) For the Safran nose wheel assembly, do these steps: a) Apply a thin layer of vaseline, D50395, for the red packing [1], or PST 525 silicone grease, D50113, for the black packing [1]. b) Prevent contact packing [1] with the thread of the inflation valve [2]. c) Tighten the tire inflation valve [2] to 143.4 in-lb (16.2 N·m) - 175.2 in-lb (19.8 N·m). 3) For the Honeywell nose wheel assembly, do these steps: a) Install the packing [1] on the inflation valve [2]. b) Tighten the tire inflation valve [2] to 150 in-lb (17 N·m) - 200 in-lb (23 N·m). c) If it is necessary, install MS20995C32 lockwire, G01048. SUBTASK 32-45-08-580-002 (4) Inflate the tire (TASK 12-15-51-610-802).

G. Tire Inflation Valve Installation Test

SUBTASK 32-45-08-210-002 (1) Using a bubble soap solution, check for leaks around the base of the tire inflation valve [2].

H. Put the Airplane Back to Its Usual Condition

SUBTASK 32-45-08-580-003 (1) Lower aircraft (TASK 07-11-03-580-801, TASK 07-11-03-580-802).

D. Prepare for the Removal

SUBTASK 32-45-11-480-003 WARNING MAKE SURE THAT THE DOWNLOCK PINS ARE INSTALLED IN ALL OF THE LANDING GEAR. WITHOUT THE DOWNLOCK PINS, THE LANDING GEAR CAN RETRACT AND CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT. (1) Make sure that the downlock pins are installed in the nose and main landing gear (PAGEBLOCK 32-00-01/201). SUBTASK 32-45-11-480-002 (2) Make sure that the tires have chocks installed around them (PAGEBLOCK 10-11-05/201). SUBTASK 32-45-11-860-001 (3) Make sure that the parking brake is released. SUBTASK 32-45-11-580-001 (4) Lift the wheel and tire assemblies with jacks until they are clear of the ground, do this task: Lift the Main Landing Gear Axles with the Axle Jacks, TASK 07-11-03-580-801. SUBTASK 32-45-11-860-002 (5) Make sure that the parking brake is set. NOTE: When you set the parking brake, the brake rotors will be aligned for wheel installation. EFFECTIVITY ALL SUBTASK 32-45-11-840-001 WARNING DEFLATE THE TIRE BEFORE YOU REMOVE THE WHEEL AND TIRE ASSEMBLY. OR, DO AN INSPECTION OF THE WHEEL AND TIRE TO MAKE SURE THAT THEY ARE SAFE. AIR PRESSURE CAN CAUSE AN EXPLOSION OF THE DAMAGED WHEEL AND TIRE COMPONENTS. INJURIES TO PERSONNEL, AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR. WARNING REMOVE ONLY ONE WHEEL AND TIRE ASSEMBLY FROM THE MAIN LANDING GEAR AT A TIME. IF YOU REMOVE THE TWO WHEEL AND TIRE ASSEMBLIES AT THE SAME TIME, STRUCTURAL DAMAGE AND INJURY TO PERSONS CAN OCCUR IF THE AIRPLANE FALLS. (6) Do the following steps to examine the tire and wheel assembly to see if it is safe to remove without tire deflation, or deflate the tire: NOTE: If you will not install the same wheel and tire assembly, deflate the tire to prevent transporting an inflated tire. (a) Inspect the outboard wheel and tire assembly [1] and/or the inboard wheel and tire assembly [17] to see if it has the conditions that follow: 1) Inspect the tires and make sure that there are no air leaks, abrasions, unusual worn areas, cuts or flat spots, do this task: Tires - Inspection, TASK 32-45-00-700-803. 2) Inspect the wheels and make sure that there is no evidence of wheel damage, including corrosion, loose or damaged or missing tire bolts or tire nuts, overheat damage or cracks, do this task: Wheels Fast Check (Wheel Installed on the Airplane), TASK 32-45-00-700-801. 3) If the wheel and tire assembly has any of the conditions in the above steps, you must deflate the tire. WARNING MAKE SURE THAT ALL PERSONNEL ARE CLEAR OF THE INFLATION VALVE ASSEMBLY PATH WHILE YOU REMOVE IT. IF THE INFLATION VALVE ASSEMBLY EJECTS WHILE YOU REMOVE IT, INJURY TO PERSONNEL CAN OCCUR. CAUTION MAKE SURE THAT THE DEFLATED TIRE THAT IS ON THE AXLE DOES NOT TOUCH THE GROUND. IF THE TIRE DOES TOUCH THE GROUND, THE TIRE'S BEAD SEAT CAN MOVE OUT OF ITS POSITION AND BECOME UNSEATED. THE UNSEATED BEAD SEAT CAN CAUSE LEAKAGE WHICH THEN CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE TIRE AND WHEEL. CAUTION DO NOT USE TOO MUCH FORCE ON THE VALVE CORE. THE CORE PARTS CAN MOVE AND THE SLEEVE AND THE LOWER END OF THE POPPET WILL STAY IN THE VALVE STEM. IF PARTS STAY IN THE VALVE STEM, DAMAGE CAN OCCUR TO THE VALVE STEM. (b) Deflate the tire with the small bore tire deflator, COM-4046, or large bore tire deflator, COM-1524. NOTE: If the wheel and tire are not damaged, it is acceptable to leave approximately 50 psi (345 kPa) or 25% of the service pressure in the tire while deflating. Leaving approximately 50 psi (345 kPa) or 25% of the service pressure in the tire can prevent damage to the tire when the wheel and tire are transported. EFFECTIVITY ALL 1) Use the 0-300 psig (0-2069 kpa) tire pressure gauge, STD-1132, to measure the tire pressure (TASK 12-15-51-780-801). (c) If you cannot use the usual procedure to deflate the tire because the valve core is damaged, do these steps: 1) Turn the valve assembly slowly in a counterclockwise direction until there is gas leakage through the boss. 2) At the same time, push lightly on the valve assembly. 3) After all of the gas has been released, remove the valve assembly from the tire.

E. Main Landing Gear Wheel and Tire Assembly Removal

SUBTASK 32-45-11-020-001 (1) Remove the hubcap [3] from the outboard wheel and tire assembly [1] or hubcap [18] from the inboard wheel and tire assembly [17], do these steps for the applicable wheel: (a) For the outboard wheel and tire assembly [1], turn the cam-locs [4] 1/4 turn to disconnect the hubcap fairing [5] from the hubcap [3]. (b) Remove the lockwire from the bolts [6] (TASK 20-10-44-000-801). (c) Remove the bolts [6] and washers [7] to disconnect the hubcap from the wheel. (d) Remove the hubcap from the wheel. SUBTASK 32-45-11-020-002 (2) Remove the outboard wheel and tire assembly [1] or inboard wheel and tire assembly [17], do these steps for the applicable wheel: (a) Remove the nuts [8], washers [9], and bolts [10] that hold the axle nut [16] to the axle. WARNING DO NOT PUT FINGERS IN THE LIGHTENING HOLES OF THE WHEEL RETAINING NUT SOCKET TOOL WHEN YOU REMOVE OR INSTALL THE WHEEL RETAINING NUT. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONS. (b) Remove the nut [16] with the socket, SPL-1865. (c) Remove the retention washer [15]. (d) Install the thread protector assembly, of the thread protector, SPL-1876, or the thread protector, SPL-14320, (for undersized threads) on the axle threads. Table 401/32-45-11-993-801 Main Landing Gear (MLG) - Thread Protector for Kit C32022* Optional Part # (Kit) Actual Tool # C32022-15 C32022-16 C32022-17 C32022-18 C32022-23 C32022-26 C32022-32 C32022-33 C32022-38 C32022-40 C32022-39 C32022-42 (e) Use the wheel/brake changer dolly, COM-1818, to lift and remove the outboard wheel and tire assembly [1]. (f) Mark the reason for the tire removal on the tire to aid the inspectors when they examine the tire. EFFECTIVITY ALL (g) Remove the wheel and tire assembly. (h) Install the axle protector assembly, of the thread protector, SPL-1876, on the axle.
