G. Prepare for the Installation

SUBTASK 32-45-11-840-003 (1) Do these steps to prepare for installation: (a) Remove the axle protector assembly, of the thread protector, SPL-1876, from the axle. (b) Remove all the old grease from the axle. (c) Remove all the old grease from the inner diameter of the brake. WARNING MAKE SURE THAT CORRECT PERSONAL PROTECTIVE EQUIPMENT IS USED FOR EYES DURING INSTALLATION AND REMOVAL OF THE BRAKE ASSEMBLY. IF CORRECT PERSONAL PROTECTIVE EQUIPMENT IS NOT USED BRAKE DUST CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSON. (d) Do an inspection of the brake. NOTE: Do this inspection with special attention to the whole circumference of each rotor for the signs of a broken rotor drive clip(s). 1) Do this task: Main Landing Gear Brake Check (Wheel Removed from the Airplane), TASK 32-41-41-700-803. (e) Do an inspection of the axle. (f) Examine the antiskid transducer drive components in the axle and hubcap [3], and hubcap [18] for damage. EFFECTIVITY ALL (g) If the wheel is not new, inspect the bearings, seals, and other parts of the wheel assembly. (h) If the tire is not new, do a tire inspection. 1) Do this task: Tires - Inspection, TASK 32-45-00-700-803. (i) If it is necessary to install the wheel inboard and outboard bearing assemblies, do these steps: 1) Apply Aeroshell 22 grease, D00378, or Mobil 28 grease, D00233, or Mobil Aviation Grease SHC 100 grease, D50005, to all of the parts of the bearing assemblies. CAUTION MAKE SURE THE CORRECT BEARING IS INSTALLED IN THE OUTSIDE OF THE WHEEL. INSTALLATION OF THE INNER BEARING IN THE OUTER BEARING WHEEL LOCATION CAN CAUSE WHEEL DAMAGE. 2) Install the inner bearing [12] in the inner side of the wheel and the outer bearing [13] in the outer side of the wheel. CAUTION INSTALL THE CORRECT GREASE SEAL IN THE EXTERNAL PART OF THE WHEEL. INSTALLATION OF THE INNER GREASE SEAL IN THE OUTER GREASE SEAL WHEEL LOCATION CAN CAUSE SEAL DAMAGE. 3) Install the grease seal [11] in the inner side of the wheel and the grease seal [14] in the outer side of the wheel. 4) If part of the assembly, install the retaining ring [19] in the inner side of the wheel and the retaining ring [20] in the outer side of the wheel. NOTE: Some wheel assemblies may not have the retaining rings as part of the configuration, or they may look different from those illustrated. (j) If using the torque multiplier, inspect the tools before use: NOTE: This method must only be used if only one engineer is available. 1) Obtain the torque multiplier rig, SPL-15334 (P/N WHEELCHANGEKIT), socket, SPL-1865, and 110 ft-lbf pre-set torque wrench, SPL-15335 (PART OF WHEELCHANGEKIT). 2) Check the tooling is serviceable. 3) Check there are no damaged parts. 4) Make sure that the jack extends and retracts. 5) Make sure that the torque multiplier is secure, free to turn and has no damage. 6) If you suspect the torque multiplier is unserviceable (U/S), do not use and return to stores with a U/S label.

H. Main Landing Gear Wheel and Tire Assembly Installation

SUBTASK 32-45-11-420-001 (1) Do these steps to install the outboard wheel and tire assembly [1] or inboard wheel and tire assembly [17]: EFFECTIVITY ALL CAUTION DO NOT APPLY GREASE TO THE AREA BETWEEN THE AXLE BEARINGS. HIGH TEMPERATURES IN THIS AREA DURING A LANDING CAN CAUSE ALL GREASE IN THIS AREA TO BURN. THIS CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO WHEELS, TIRES, AND BRAKES. (a) Apply a thin layer of Aeroshell 22 grease, D00378, or Mobil 28 grease, D00233, or Mobil Aviation Grease SHC 100 grease, D50005, to the inner diameter surface of the two bearings where they will touch the axle. (b) Apply a thin layer of Aeroshell 22 grease, D00378, Mobil 28 grease, D00233, or Mobil Aviation Grease SHC 100 grease, D50005, to the faces of the washer [15] and nut [16], and to the axle threads. (c) Apply a thin layer of Aeroshell 22 grease, D00378, Mobil 28 grease, D00233, or Mobil Aviation Grease SHC 100 grease, D50005, on the axle where the axle will touch the wheel bearings. WARNING MAKE SURE THAT CORRECT PERSONAL PROTECTIVE EQUIPMENT IS USED FOR EYES DURING INSTALLATION AND REMOVAL OF THE BRAKE ASSEMBLY. IF CORRECT PERSONAL PROTECTIVE EQUIPMENT IS NOT USED BRAKE DUST CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSON. (d) If you need to align the brake disks, do these steps: 1) Release the parking brake. CAUTION MAKE SURE THE BRAKE ROTORS ARE ALIGNED. DAMAGE TO THE ROTORS CAN OCCUR IF THE DRIVE KEYS ON THE WHEEL HIT ROTORS DURING INSTALLATION. 2) Align the brake disks. 3) Set the parking brake. NOTE: This will keep the brake rotors aligned. (e) Make sure that the thread protector assembly, of the thread protector, SPL-1876, or thread protector, SPL-14320, (for undersized threads) is installed. (f) Install the outboard wheel and tire assembly [1] with the wheel/brake changer dolly, COM-1818. 1) Make sure that the rotor drive keys on the wheel fully engage the key slots in the brake rotors. (g) Remove the thread protector assembly, of the thread protector, SPL-1876, or thread protector, SPL-14320, (for undersized threads) from the axle threads. CAUTION MAKE SURE YOU FIRMLY PUSH BOTH THE WHEEL AND LOCK WASHER ALL THE WAY ONTO THE AXLE UNTIL THE WHEEL IS SEATED PRIOR TO INSTALLING AND TIGHTENING THE AXLE NUT. MAKE SURE THAT THE LOCKTANG IS FIRMLY ENGAGED IN THE KEYWAY GROOVE IN THE AXLE. DO NOT USE THE AXLE NUT TO PUSH THE WHEEL AND LOCK WASHER INTO POSITION. FAILURE TO FOLLOW THIS CAN CAUSE THE WHEEL TO BE LOOSE AND CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE EQUIPMENT. (h) Install the washer [15]. EFFECTIVITY ALL (i) Install the nut [16]. (j) Release the parking brake. (k) Do these steps to tighten the nut [16] with the torque multiplier (Figure 401 or Figure 402 or Figure 403 or Figure 404): NOTE: This method must only be used if only one engineer is available. 1) Obtain the torque multiplier rig, SPL-15334 (P/N WHEELCHANGEKIT), socket, SPL-1865, and 110 ft-lbf pre-set torque wrench, SPL-15335 (PART OF WHEELCHANGEKIT). a) Check the condition of the 110 ft-lbf pre-set torque wrench, SPL-15335 (PART OF WHEELCHANGEKIT), before use. 2) Set up the torque multiplier rig, SPL-15334 (P/N WHEELCHANGEKIT), and make sure that the ground is level. 3) Align the socket, SPL-1865, with the nut [16]. a) Make sure that the socket, SPL-1865, and the nut [16] are fully engaged. 4) Hold the torque multiplier rig, SPL-15334 (P/N WHEELCHANGEKIT), down securely by applying foot pressure to the frame where “FOOT STEP” is marked. NOTE: Foot pressure is applied to prevent possible nut socket disengagement. CAUTION WHEN YOU USE A 110 FT-LBS (149 N-M) PRESET TORQUE WRENCH, DO NOT EXCEED THE PRESET TORQUE VALUE. IF YOU USE MORE THAN THAT VALUE, IT CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE AIRCRAFT. 5) Use the 110 ft-lbf pre-set torque wrench, SPL-15335 (PART OF WHEELCHANGEKIT), to tighten the nut [16]. NOTE: The 110 ft-lbf pre-set torque wrench, SPL-15335 (PART OF WHEELCHANGEKIT), used with the torque multiplier will produce an applied torque of 550 ft-lb (746 N·m) to the nut [16]. WARNING DO NOT PUT FINGERS IN THE LIGHTENING HOLES OF THE WHEEL RETAINING NUT SOCKET TOOL WHEN YOU REMOVE OR INSTALL THE WHEEL RETAINING NUT. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONS. (l) Do these steps to tighten the nut [16] with the socket, SPL-1865, and torque wrench, STD-1021: 1) While you turn the wheel, tighten the nut [16] to 500 ft-lb (678 N·m) - 600 ft-lb (813 N·m). 2) Stop the wheel. 3) While you turn the wheel, loosen the nut [16] to almost zero torque. NOTE: The function is to keep the bearing seated. a) If the nut [16] is set to zero torque, re-seat the wheel. 4) While you turn the wheel, tighten the nut [16] to 150 ft-lb (203 N·m). 5) If the holes for bolt [10] do not align, continue to tighten the nut [16] to align the holes. a) Do not tighten the nut [16] to more than 300 ft-lb (407 N·m). NOTE: The holes will align every 6 degrees that you turn the nut. EFFECTIVITY ALL (m) Do these steps to install the two bolts [10] to lock the nut [16] to the outboard wheel and tire assembly [1]: 1) Install the two bolts [10] with the heads to the inside of the axle. 2) Install the washers [9] and nuts [8]. 3) Check the self locking nuts (TASK 20-50-11-910-801). 4) Tighten the nuts [8] to 65 ±2 in-lb (7.3 ±0.2 N·m). NOTE: This is per Standard Torque Values, TASK 20-50-11-910-801 to have the lowest maximum value when both nuts and the bolts can be tightened. SUBTASK 32-45-11-420-002 CAUTION DO NOT TIGHTEN THE HUBCAP BOLTS TOO MUCH. MAKE SURE THAT THE HUBCAP IS IN THE CORRECT POSITION BEFORE YOU TIGHTEN THE BOLTS. TOO MUCH TORQUE WILL CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE BOLTS AND THE HUBCAP. (2) Install the hubcap [3] or hubcap [18]. (a) Do these steps to install the hubcap [3]: 1) Turn the antiskid transducer dog [2] inside the outboard wheel and tire assembly [1] such that the drive on the hubcap [3] and antiskid transducer dog [2] in the wheel will connect when the hubcap [3] is installed. 2) Put the hubcap [3] in its position on the outboard wheel and tire assembly [1]. 3) Make sure that the hubcap [3] flush with the outboard wheel and tire assembly [1]. a) Use a soft mallet to lightly tap the hubcap [3] to make it flush. 4) Install the bolts [6] and washers [7] to connect the hubcap [3] to the outboard wheel and tire assembly [1]. a) Tighten the bolts [6] to 50 in-lb (5.65 N·m) - 80 in-lb (9.04 N·m). 5) Install the lockwire on the bolts [6] (TASK 20-10-44-400-801). NOTE: The installation of the lockwire is acceptable on the fasteners that are over 6 in. (15 cm) apart at this location. 6) Put the hubcap fairing [5] on the hubcap [3]. 7) Turn the cam-locs [4], 1/4 turn to attach the hubcap fairing [5] to the hubcap [3]. (b) Do these steps to install the hubcap [18]: 1) Turn the antiskid transducer dog [2] inside the inboard wheel and tire assembly [17] such that the drive on the hubcap [18], and the antiskid transducer dog [2] in the wheel will connect when the hubcap [18] is installed. 2) Put the hubcap [18] in its position on the inboard wheel and tire assembly [17]. 3) Make sure that the hubcap [18] flush with the inboard wheel and tire assembly [17]. a) Use a soft mallet to lightly tap the hubcap [18] to make it flush. 4) Install the bolts [6] and washers [7] to connect the hubcap [18] to the inboard wheel and tire assembly [17]. a) Tighten the bolts [6] to 50 in-lb (5.65 N·m) - 80 in-lb (9.04 N·m). 5) Install the lockwire on the bolts [6] (TASK 20-10-44-400-801). EFFECTIVITY ALL SUBTASK 32-45-11-610-002 (3) Make sure that the landing gear tire pressure is within the servicing limits (TASK 12-15-51-780-801).

I. Put the Airplane Back to Its Usual Condition

SUBTASK 32-45-11-580-002 WARNING MAKE SURE THE AREA AROUND THE TIRES IS CLEAR OF PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT. IF THE AREA AROUND THE TIRES IS NOT CLEAR, INJURIES TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR. (1) Lower the axle and remove the jacks (TASK 07-11-03-580-801).

C. Location Zones

Zone Area 713 Nose Landing Gear

D. Prepare for the Removal

SUBTASK 32-45-21-860-002 (1) Make sure that the parking brake is set. EFFECTIVITY ALL SUBTASK 32-45-21-480-001 WARNING MAKE SURE THAT THE DOWNLOCK PINS ARE INSTALLED ON ALL THE LANDING GEAR. WITHOUT THE DOWNLOCK PINS, THE LANDING GEAR CAN RETRACT. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONS, AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT. (2) Make sure that the landing gear downlock downlock equipment, SPL-1880, and NLG towing lever pin, SPL-1499, are installed, do this task: Landing Gear Downlock Pins Installation, TASK 32-00-01-480-801. SUBTASK 32-45-21-480-002 (3) Make sure that the tires of Main Landing Gear (MLG) have the wheel chock, COM-1505, installed around them (PAGEBLOCK 10-11-05/201). SUBTASK 32-45-21-580-001 (4) Make sure to lift the nose landing gear and wheel and tire assembly with jacks until they are clear of the ground (TASK 07-11-03-580-802). SUBTASK 32-45-21-840-001 WARNING DEFLATE THE TIRE BEFORE YOU REMOVE THE WHEEL AND TIRE ASSEMBLY. OR, DO AN INSPECTION OF THE WHEEL AND TIRE TO MAKE SURE THAT THEY ARE SAFE. AIR PRESSURE CAN CAUSE AN EXPLOSION OF THE DAMAGED WHEEL AND TIRE COMPONENTS. INJURIES TO PERSONNEL, AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR. WARNING REMOVE ONE WHEEL AND THE TIRE ASSEMBLY FROM THE NOSE LANDING GEAR AT A TIME. IF YOU REMOVE THE TWO WHEEL AND THE TIRE ASSEMBLIES AT THE SAME TIME, THE AIRPLANE CAN FALL. STRUCTURAL DAMAGE AND INJURY TO PERSONNEL CAN OCCUR. (5) Do the following steps to examine the tire and wheel assembly to see if it is safe to remove without tire deflation, or deflate the tire (TASK 32-45-00-000-801): NOTE: If you will not install the same tire and wheel assembly, deflate the tire to prevent transporting an inflated tire. (a) Inspect the wheel and tire assembly [1] to see if it has the conditions that follow: 1) Inspect the tires and make sure that there are no air leaks, abrasions, unusual worn areas, cuts or flat spots, do this task: Tires - Inspection, TASK 32-45-00-700-803. 2) Inspect the wheels and make sure that there is no evidence of wheel damage, including corrosion, loose or damaged or missing tie bolts or tie nuts, overheat damage or cracks, do this task: Wheels Fast Check (Wheel Installed on the Airplane), TASK 32-45-00-700-801. NOTE: If the wheel and tire assembly has any of the conditions in the above steps, you must deflate the tire. WARNING MAKE SURE THAT ALL PERSONNEL ARE CLEAR OF THE INFLATION VALVE ASSEMBLY PATH WHILE YOU REMOVE IT. IF THE INFLATION VALVE ASSEMBLY EJECTS WHILE YOU REMOVE IT, INJURY TO PERSONNEL CAN OCCUR. EFFECTIVITY ALL (WARNING PRECEDES) WARNING BE CAREFUL WHEN DEFLATING TIRES, A FLYING INFLATION VALVE CAP AND CORE CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT AND INJURY TO PERSONNEL. CAUTION MAKE SURE THAT THE DEFLATED TIRE THAT IS ON THE AXLE DOES NOT TOUCH THE GROUND. IF THE TIRE DOES TOUCH THE GROUND, THE TIRE'S BEAD SEAT CAN MOVE OUT OF ITS POSITION AND BECOME UNSEATED. THE UNSEATED BEAD SEAT CAN CAUSE LEAKAGE WHICH THEN CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE TIRE AND WHEEL. (b) Deflate the tire with the small bore tire deflator, COM-4046, or large bore tire deflator, COM-1524. NOTE: If the wheel and tire are not damaged, it is acceptable to leave approximately 50 psi (345 kPa) or 25% of the service pressure in the tire while deflating. Leaving approximately 50 psi (345 kPa) or 25% of the service pressure in the tire can prevent damage to the tire when the wheel and tire is transported. 1) Use the 0-300 psig (0-2069 kpa) tire pressure gauge, STD-1132, to measure the tire pressure (TASK 12-15-51-780-801). (c) If you cannot use the usual procedure to deflate the tire because the valve core is damaged, do these steps: 1) Turn the valve assembly slowly in a counterclockwise direction until there is gas leakage through the boss. 2) At the same time, push lightly on the valve assembly. 3) After all of the gas has been released, remove the valve assembly from the tire.

E. Nose Landing Gear Wheel and Tire Assembly Removal

SUBTASK 32-45-21-020-001 (1) Do these steps to remove the wheel and tire assembly [1]: (a) Remove the lockwire from the screws [4]. (b) Remove the screws [4] that hold the axle nut [3] to the axle. (c) Remove the axle nut [3] with the NLG socket, C32012-3, SPL-1817, from the kit socket, SPL-1865. (d) Remove the washer [2]. CAUTION MAKE SURE THAT THE AXLE THREAD PROTECTOR IS INSTALLED BEFORE YOU REMOVE THE WHEEL/TIRE ASSEMBLY. IF YOU REMOVE THE TIRE ASSEMBLY WITHOUT THE AXLE THREAD PROTECTOR INSTALLED, DAMAGE TO THE THREADS OR THE TIRE ASSEMBLY CAN OCCUR. (e) Install the thread protector assembly, of the thread protector, SPL-1877, on the axle threads. NOTE: You can use tape to hold the thread protector to the axle if it is necessary. EFFECTIVITY ALL Table 401/32-45-21-993-801 Nose Landing Gear (NLG) - Thread Protector for Kit C32022-20 Optional Part # (Kit) Actual Tool # C32022-35 C32022-36 C32022-20 C32022-21 C32022-2 C32022-5 (f) If the axle has undersized threads, install the thread protector, SPL-14582, on the axle threads. NOTE: You can use tape to hold the thread protector to the axle. CAUTION MAKE SURE TO KEEP CLEARANCE BETWEEN THE NOSE-WHEEL INNER BEARING AND PAINTED SURFACES OF THE NOSE GEAR AXLE DURING REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION. FRICTION CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO NOSE-WHEEL AXLE PAINT AND OTHER EQUIPMENT. (g) Use the wheel/brake changer dolly, COM-1818, to lift and remove the wheel and tire assembly [1]. (h) Remove the wheel and tire assembly [1]. (i) Mark the reason for the tire removal on the tire to aid the inspectors when they examine the tire.

Zone Area 713 Nose Landing Gear

G. Prepare for the Installation

SUBTASK 32-45-21-000-002 (1) Do these steps to prepare for installation: (a) Remove the axle thread thread protector, SPL-1877, or thread protector, SPL-14582, from the axle. (b) Remove all the old grease from the axle. (c) If the wheel is not new, inspect the bearings, seals, and other parts of the wheel assembly. (d) If the tire is not new, do a tire inspection (TASK 32-45-00-700-803). (e) Do these steps if the component of the nose wheel assembly (the bearings, the seals, and other parts) need to be installed: 1) Apply Aeroshell 22 grease, D00378, or Mobil 28 grease, D00233, or Mobil Aviation Grease SHC 100 grease, D50005, to the inner bearing [8], outer bearing [9], grease seal [7] and grease seal [10]. CAUTION MAKE SURE THE CORRECT BEARING IS INSTALLED IN THE OUTSIDE OF THE WHEEL. INSTALLATION OF THE INNER BEARING IN THE OUTER BEARING WHEEL LOCATION CAN CAUSE WHEEL DAMAGE. EFFECTIVITY ALL (CAUTION PRECEDES) CAUTION MAKE SURE TO KEEP CLEARANCE BETWEEN THE NOSE-WHEEL INNER BEARING AND PAINTED SURFACES OF THE NOSE GEAR AXLE DURING REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION. FRICTION CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO NOSE-WHEEL AXLE PAINT AND OTHER EQUIPMENT. 2) Install the inner bearing [8] on the inner side of the wheel and the outer bearing [9] on the outer side of the wheel. a) Make sure that the inner bearing is installed on the wheel side opposite inflation valve. CAUTION MAKE SURE THAT YOU INSTALL THE CORRECT GREASE SEAL IN THE OUTER SIDE OF THE WHEEL. IF YOU INSTALL THE INNER GREASE SEAL IN THE OUTER GREASE SEAL LOCATION, YOU CAN CAUSE SEAL DAMAGE. 3) Install the grease seal [7] on the inner side of the wheel and the grease seal [10] on the outer side of the wheel. a) Make sure that the tab of grease seal fits indentation of cutout in wheel housing. 4) Install the retaining ring [11] on the inner side of the wheel and the retaining ring [12] on the outer side of the wheel.

H. Nose Landing Gear Wheel and Tire Assembly Installation

SUBTASK 32-45-21-420-001 (1) Do these steps to install the wheel and tire assembly [1]: (a) Inspect the axles for nicks, gouges, and damaged chrome plate. (b) If the axle spacer is removed, do a general visual inspection of the axles for corrosion (TASK 32-21-71-200-803). CAUTION MAKE SURE THAT THE SPACER IS CORRECTLY INSTALLED ON THE AXLE. THE SPACER CAN MOVE WHEN THE WHEEL AND TIRE ASSEMBLY IS REMOVED. IF IT IS NOT IN ITS CORRECT POSITION, THE WHEEL AND TIRE ASSEMBLY WILL NOT INSTALL CORRECTLY. THIS CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT. (c) Make sure that the axle spacer [5] is installed on the axle. NOTE: The axle spacer is inboard of the wheel on the axle. The inner bearing will touch the spacer when the wheel is installed. 1) For airplanes that use cotter pins, make sure that the three new cotter pins [6] are installed to hold the spacer on the axle. NOTE: If you did not remove the axle spacer and it is installed correctly, it is not necessary to replace the three cotter pins [6]. a) Examine the cotter pins [6] installation to make sure that they do not touch the torsion link lug during wheel installation. NOTE: An axle spacer that uses cotter pins has 3 holes. EFFECTIVITY ALL 2) For airplanes that use lockwire, make sure that MS20995C41 lockwire, G00440, is installed. NOTE: If you did not remove the axle spacer and it is installed correctly, it is not necessary to replace the lockwire. a) Make sure that to bend the lockwire ends pigtails away from the inboard edge of the spacer (Figure 401). b) Examine the completed installation to be sure that the lockwire ends do not touch the axle, or the torsion link lugs. c) If necessary, adjust the lockwire to make sure that it does not touch the landing gear parts during landing gear operations. NOTE: An axle spacer that uses lockwire has six holes. WARNING DO NOT APPLY GREASE TO THE AREA BETWEEN THE AXLE BEARINGS. HIGH TEMPERATURES IN THIS AREA DURING A LANDING CAN CAUSE ALL GREASE IN THIS AREA TO BURN. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONNEL AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT. (d) Apply a thin layer of Aeroshell 22 grease, D00378, or Mobil 28 grease, D00233, or Mobil Aviation Grease SHC 100 grease, D50005, to the face and outer diameter of the spacer [5]. (e) Apply a thin layer of Aeroshell 22 grease, D00378, or Mobil 28 grease, D00233, or Mobil Aviation Grease SHC 100 grease, D50005, to the inner diameter surface of the two bearings where they will touch the axle. (f) Apply a thin layer of Aeroshell 22 grease, D00378, or Mobil 28 grease, D00233, or Mobil Aviation Grease SHC 100 grease, D50005, to the faces of the washer [2] and the axle nut [3], and to the axle threads. (g) Apply a thin layer of Aeroshell 22 grease, D00378, or Mobil 28 grease, D00233, or Mobil Aviation Grease SHC 100 grease, D50005, on the axle where the axle will touch the wheel bearings. (h) Install the thread protector, thread protector, SPL-1877, or thread protector, SPL-14582 (if the axle undersized threads). (i) Use the wheel/brake changer dolly, COM-1818, to install the wheel and tire assembly [1]. (j) Install the wheel and tire assembly [1]. (k) Remove the thread protector assembly, of the thread protector, SPL-1877, from the axle threads. (l) Align the key of the washer with the keyway of the axle and install the washer [2]. (m) Install the axle nut [3]. (n) Do these steps to torque the axle nut [3] with the NLG socket, C32012-3, SPL-1817, from kit socket, SPL-1865: 1) While you turn the wheel, torque the axle nut [3] to 80 ft-lb (108 N·m) - 100 ft-lb (136 N·m). a) Stop the wheel. b) While you turn the wheel, loosen the axle nut [3] to almost zero torque. c) While you turn the wheel, torque the axle nut [3] to 30 ft-lb (41 N·m). EFFECTIVITY ALL d) Continue to tighten the axle nut [3] until two bolt holes in the nut align with two threaded holes in the washer [2]. NOTE: Do not torque the nut over 60 ft-lb (81 N·m). (o) Install the two lock screws [4] to lock the axle nut [3] to the washer [2]. 1) Torque the two lock screws [4] to 31.0 in-lb (3.5 N·m) - 38.0 in-lb (4.3 N·m). (p) Install MS20995C32 lockwire, G01048, or MS20995NC32 lockwire, G50347, or MS20995N32 lockwire, G50177, on the lock screws [4]. (q) Make sure that the tire pressure is a minimum of half the correct pressure (TASK 12-15-51-780-801).

I. Put the Airplane Back to Its Usual Condition

SUBTASK 32-45-21-580-003 (1) Lower the axle and remove the jacks (TASK 07-11-03-580-802). SUBTASK 32-45-21-020-002 (2) Remove the NLG towing lever pin, SPL-1499, from the nose wheel steering mechanism (TASK 32-00-01-080-801). SUBTASK 32-45-21-000-001 (3) Do this task: Landing Gear Tire Pressure Check and Tire Servicing, TASK 12-15-51-780-801.

32-45-31-000-801Nose Wheel Spin Brake Lining - RemovalPDF p. 1859

2. Nose Wheel Spin Brake Lining - Removal (Figure 201)

A. References

Reference Title 32-00-01 P/B 201 LANDING GEAR DOWNLOCK PINS - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES

B. Location Zones

Zone Area 115 Nose Landing Gear Wheel Well - Left 116 Nose Landing Gear Wheel Well - Right

C. Nose Wheel Spin Brake Lining Removal

SUBTASK 32-45-31-480-002 WARNING MAKE SURE THAT THE DOWNLOCK PINS ARE INSTALLED IN ALL OF THE LANDING GEAR. WITHOUT THE DOWNLOCK PINS, THE LANDING GEAR CAN RETRACT AND CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT. (1) Make sure that the downlock pins are installed in the nose and main landing gear (PAGEBLOCK 32-00-01/201). SUBTASK 32-45-31-020-001 (2) Remove the screws [6], washers [1], and nuts [2] that hold the spin brake lining [5] to the spin brake spring [3]. SUBTASK 32-45-31-020-002 (3) Remove the spin brake lining [5] and spacers [4].

32-45-31-400-801Nose Wheel Spin Brake Lining - InstallationPDF p. 1862

3. Nose Wheel Spin Brake Lining - Installation (Figure 201)

A. Consumable Materials

Reference Description Specification A00247 Sealant - Pressure And Environmental - Chromate Type BMS5-95

B. Expendables/Parts

AMM Item Description AIPC Reference AIPC Effectivity 5 Spin brake lining 32-22-11-02-060 ALL

C. Location Zones

Zone Area 115 Nose Landing Gear Wheel Well - Left 116 Nose Landing Gear Wheel Well - Right

D. Procedure

SUBTASK 32-45-31-420-001 (1) Apply sealant, A00247 to the six locations on the spin brake spring [3] where you will install the spacers [4]. SUBTASK 32-45-31-420-002 (2) Hold the spin brake lining [5] in its position on the spin brake spring [3]. SUBTASK 32-45-31-420-003 (3) Do these steps for each screw [6]: (a) Install two spacers [4] between the block and the spin brake spring [3] where you will install the screw [6]. (b) Install the screw [6] and washer [1] through the spin brake lining [5], spacers [4], and the spin brake spring [3]. (c) Install the washer [1] and the nut [2] on the screw [6].

32-45-31-700-801Nose Wheel Spin Brake Lining InspectionPDF p. 1862

4. Nose Wheel Spin Brake Lining Inspection (Figure 201)

A. Location Zones

Zone Area 115 Nose Landing Gear Wheel Well - Left 116 Nose Landing Gear Wheel Well - Right

B. Procedure

SUBTASK 32-45-31-220-001 (1) Measure the distance from the head of each bolt [6] to the wear surface of the spin brake lining [5]. SUBTASK 32-45-31-350-001 (2) If this distance you measured is less than 0.060 inches (1.524 mm) you must replace that spin brake lining [5]: EFFECTIVITY ALL These are the tasks: • Nose Wheel Spin Brake Lining - Removal, TASK 32-45-31-000-801, • Nose Wheel Spin Brake Lining - Installation, TASK 32-45-31-400-801.

(1) If the downlock pins are not installed in the nose and main landing gear, do this task: Landing Gear Downlock Pins Installation, TASK 32-00-01-480-801. SUBTASK 32-51-00-860-051 WARNING REMOVE HYDRAULIC POWER FOR THE NOSE WHEEL STEERING BEFORE YOU DO THE CHECK. HYDRAULIC POWER CAN CAUSE THE NOSE WHEELS TO MOVE. INJURIES TO PERSONNEL AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR. (2) For hydraulic system A, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Power Removal, TASK 29-11-00-860-805. SUBTASK 32-51-00-010-012 (3) Open these access panels to get access to the nose wheel steering system mechanism and cable turnbuckles: Number Name/Location 113AC Fwd Nose Wheel Well Upper Access Panel EFFECTIVITY ALL (Continued) Number Name/Location 113AW Forward Nose Wheel Well Panel 113BW Forward Nose Wheel Well Panel (a) Do this task: Nose Wheel Well Access Panels - Removal, TASK 53-14-01-020-801.

G. General Check of the Adjustment of the Nose Wheel Steering System

SUBTASK 32-51-00-820-014 (1) Make sure that the tension in the cables NGPP-A and NGPP-B is such that the load necessary to deflect the cable 0.45 in. (11.4 mm) to 0.55 in. (14.0 mm) downward at the turnbuckle is 16 lbf (71.2 N) to 22 lbf (97.9 N) (as measured with a spring scale, STD-5505). SUBTASK 32-51-00-820-015 (2) Use a low tension cable tensiometer, COM-1553, to make sure that the tension in the cables NWS-A and NWS-B is in tolerance (Table I, Figure 501). SUBTASK 32-51-00-480-015 (3) Install these rig pins, rigging pin kit, SPL-1585, as follows: (a) Rig pin NS2 in the Captain's control wheel drum. (b) Rig pin NS1 in the interconnect quadrant. (c) Rig pin NS5 in the interconnect eccentric drum. Do the following steps: 1) Do this task: Put the Airplane in the Air Mode, TASK 32-09-00-860-801. 2) Make sure that the interconnect eccentric drum rig pin hole and bracket rig pin slot line up. 3) Install rig pin NS5. (d) Rig pin R3 in the rudder forward quadrant. (e) Rig pin NS4 in the summing mechanism bracket at the steering metering valve. SUBTASK 32-51-00-820-016 (4) Make sure that all the rig pins have a free fit. NOTE: The rig pins have a free fit if you can install or remove them with two fingers. Some resistance is permitted. SUBTASK 32-51-00-080-010 (5) Remove all the rig pins. SUBTASK 32-51-00-080-015 (6) Do this task: Return the Airplane to the Ground Mode, TASK 32-09-00-860-802. SUBTASK 32-51-00-730-037 (7) With the control wheel in the center position, make sure that the steering angle is 0 +/-1.5 degrees on the decal that is on the nose gear shock strut. NOTE: If the decal is not on the nose gear shock strut, then use the illustration in Figure 501 to make a decal with tape. SUBTASK 32-51-00-210-003 (8) Examine all of the adjustable rod ends to make sure there is correct thread engagement. NOTE: The end of the rod end must cover at least 50 percent of the inspection hole. EFFECTIVITY ALL SUBTASK 32-51-00-210-004 (9) After the cables are adjusted, the cable cannot touch the pulley or quadrant flanges for the full travel of the cables. NOTE: The cables must stay in the plane of the pulley or quadrant within +/-2 degrees. SUBTASK 32-51-00-410-007 (10) Close these access panels: Number Name/Location 113AC Fwd Nose Wheel Well Upper Access Panel 113AW Forward Nose Wheel Well Panel 113BW Forward Nose Wheel Well Panel (a) Do this task: Nose Wheel Well Access Panels - Installation, TASK 53-14-01-420-801.

G. Adjust the Interconnect Mechanism for the Rudder Pedals

SUBTASK 32-51-00-020-001 (1) Remove the turnbuckle locking clips from the turnbuckles on the NGPP-A and NGPP-B cables. SUBTASK 32-51-00-020-002 (2) Remove the nut [7], washer [6], and bolt [5] to disconnect the idler rod on the rudder pedal interconnect mechanism from the structure. SUBTASK 32-51-00-220-001 (3) Make sure the rotary actuator is turned in the counter-clockwise direction with the index marks aligned to show that it is in the air mode. SUBTASK 32-51-00-480-021 (4) Install rig pins NS1 and NS5. Do the following steps: (a) Install the rig pin NS1, rigging pin kit, SPL-1585. (b) Do this task: Put the Airplane in the Air Mode, TASK 32-09-00-860-801. 1) Make sure the interconnect eccentric drum rig pin hole and bracket rig pin slot line up. (c) Install rig pin NS5 SUBTASK 32-51-00-820-003 (5) Adjust the tension in cables NGPP-A and NGPP-B until the load necessary to move the cable 0.45 in. (11.4 mm) to 0.55 in. (14.0 mm) downward at the turnbuckle is 16 lbf (71.2 N) to 22 lbf (97.9 N) (as measured with a spring scale, STD-5505). NOTE: It is not necessary to allow for the temperature because the NGPP cables are very short. SUBTASK 32-51-00-080-001 (6) Remove the rig pin NS5. EFFECTIVITY ALL SUBTASK 32-51-00-710-001 (7) Operate the rotary actuator five times from the air mode, (do this task: Put the Airplane in the Air Mode, TASK 32-09-00-860-801), back to the ground mode, (do this task: Return the Airplane to the Ground Mode, TASK 32-09-00-860-802), and back again. (a) Make sure the rotary actuator changes from the air mode to the ground mode, and back again each time. SUBTASK 32-51-00-210-001 (8) Make sure that the rig pin NS5 fits freely. Do the following steps: (a) Do this task: Put the Airplane in the Air Mode, TASK 32-09-00-860-801. (b) Make sure the interconnect eccentric drum rig pin hole and bracket rig pin slot line up. (c) Make sure rig pin NS5 can be installed and removed freely. SUBTASK 32-51-00-820-024 (9) Make sure the tension in the cables NGPP-A and NGPP-B is such that the load necessary to move the cable 0.45 in. (11.4 mm) to 0.55 in. (14.0 mm) at the turnbuckle is 16 lbf (71.2 N) to 22 lbf (97.9 N) (as measured with a spring scale, STD-5505). (a) If it is necessary, adjust the cable turnbuckles until the rig pin NS5 is free and the tension in the cables is correct. SUBTASK 32-51-00-820-002 (10) Adjust the length of the idler rod, if it is necessary, so that the bolt [5] fits freely when it is installed through the rod end and the structure. (a) Install the bolt [5], washer [6], and nut [7] to attach the idler rod to the structure. SUBTASK 32-51-00-080-013 (11) Make sure the rig pin NS1 fits freely. SUBTASK 32-51-00-080-014 (12) Remove rig pin NS1. SUBTASK 32-51-00-420-008 (13) Install the turnbuckle locking clips on the turnbuckles for the NGPP-A and NGPP-B cables. SUBTASK 32-51-00-410-009 (14) Close these access panels: Number Name/Location 113AC Fwd Nose Wheel Well Upper Access Panel 113AW Forward Nose Wheel Well Panel 113BW Forward Nose Wheel Well Panel (a) Do this task: Nose Wheel Well Access Panels - Installation, TASK 53-14-01-420-801. SUBTASK 32-51-00-860-044 (15) Do this task: Return the Airplane to the Ground Mode, TASK 32-09-00-860-802.

G. Check the Adjustment of the Steering System of the Nose Wheel

SUBTASK 32-51-00-820-020 (1) Make sure that the conditions of this check are satisfactory, if they are not, do this task (TASK 32-51-00-820-802). EFFECTIVITY ALL SUBTASK 32-51-00-730-038 (2) Make sure that the steering angle is 0 +/-1.5 degrees on the decal that is on the nose gear shock. NOTE: The inner cylinder centering cam will put the nose wheels in the center position when the airplane is lifted on jacks. Manual assistance may be necessary to make sure that the nose gear and cam is in the center position. NOTE: If the decal is not on the nose gear shock strut, then use the illustration in Figure 501 to make a decal with tape. SUBTASK 32-51-00-860-058 WARNING MAKE SURE THAT ALL PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT ARE CLEAR OF CONTROL SURFACES, CABLES, AND LANDING GEAR AREAS. PRESSURIZATION OF A HYDRAULIC SYSTEM CAN MOVE CONTROL SURFACES, CABLES, LANDING GEAR, AND LANDING GEAR DOORS. MOVEMENT OF CONTROL SURFACES, CABLES, LANDING GEAR, AND LANDING GEAR DOORS CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT. (3) For hydraulic system A, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Pressurization, TASK 29-11-00-860-801. SUBTASK 32-51-00-730-039 (4) Make sure that the nose gear stays centered. NOTE: If the nose gear moves when the hydraulic system is pressurized, the nose gear steering is not adjusted correctly. There is a disagreement between the steering system and the mechanical centerline position of the nose gear centering cams. SUBTASK 32-51-00-820-021 (5) Make sure that the tension in the cables NWS-A and NWS-B is in tolerance (Table I, Figure 501). SUBTASK 32-51-00-010-004 (6) Remove the screws [8], washers [9], and summing mechanism cover [10]. SUBTASK 32-51-00-010-026 (7) Do these steps that follow to get access to the Captain's rig pin hole for the control wheels: (a) Remove the screw [15] from the access cover [14]. (b) Turn the access cover [14] counterclockwise to get access to the rig pin hole. SUBTASK 32-51-00-480-018 (8) Make sure that you can install the rig pins, rigging pin kit, SPL-1585, that follow: NOTE: The steering system has a 1 - 2 degree dead band in the center position. 32-51-00-820-802Nose Wheel Steering System AdjustmentPDF p. 1888

6. Nose Wheel Steering System Adjustment (Figure 501, Figure 502)

A. General

(1) This task provides instructions to do the adjustment of the steering system of the nose wheel. (a) There three methods to perform this task: 1) Method 1: Airplane on Ground (off Jacks). a) Method 1 requires removal of the torsion link apex pin to disconnect the steering mechanism from the wheel assembly. 2) Method 2: Airplane on Jacks. EFFECTIVITY ALL a) Method 2 requires the Nose Landing Gear (NLG) to be compressed while the airplane is jacked. 3) Method 3: Airplane on Grease Plate. a) Method 3 does not need removal of the torsion pin. The grease plate will prevent tire scuffing when the NLG is turned left or right.

32-51-00-820-807Nose Wheel Steering System Adjustment (Adjusting Steering Metering Valve Input Rod Method)PDF p. 1900

7. Nose Wheel Steering System Adjustment (Adjusting Steering Metering Valve Input Rod Method) (Figure 501)

A. General

(1) This procedure is to be used only after rigging in accordance with the usual rigging procedure (TASK 32-51-00-820-802). (2) This task provides a procedure for adjusting the steering system rigging based on the recorded amount of rudder trim required to counteract a steering pulling condition as measured during ground maneuvers. (3) This is a procedure for adjusting single and dual tiller steering systems only if necessary to improve steering centering characteristics. Prior to making steering adjustments, pilot evaluation of the rudder trim needed to center the steering system, must be recorded. Fewer than 2 units of rudder trim is required for acceptable centering. One (1) unit of rudder trim is equivalent to ¼ degree of steered angle or 0.02 in. (0.05 cm) on the steering marker. The rudder trim that produces satisfactory centering characteristics is used to readjust the steering control system. Initial rigging requires the steering to center equally about the “0” mark when returning from turns from the right and left. After completion of this procedure, the steering does not have to center equally about the “0” mark.

SUBTASK 32-51-00-860-091 (1) For hydraulic system A, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Pressurization, TASK 29-11-00-860-801. SUBTASK 32-51-00-080-016 (2) Remove the NLG towing lever pin, SPL-1499. SUBTASK 32-51-00-210-011 (3) Verify that the rudder trim is set to zero (“0”) (+/- 1/4°). SUBTASK 32-51-00-710-003 (4) Using the rudder pedals, cycle the system to the left and right and allow it to return to center from each direction. NOTE: Note the relationship on the indicator mark on the back of the steering collar to the zero (“0”) mark on the decal. There will be a difference in this relationship when returning from the left or returning from the right of up to 1 degree, 0.06 in. (0.15 cm) on the decal, due to the dead band in the steering valve. SUBTASK 32-51-00-860-092 (5) Set the rudder trim (+/- 1/4°) to the setting the pilot noted for acceptable centering characteristics. SUBTASK 32-51-00-710-004 (6) Using the rudder pedals, cycle the system to the left and right and allow it to return to center from each direction. NOTE: Note these relationships of the indicator mark on the back of the steering collar to the zero (“0”) mark on the decal. These are the positions to which the steering must return after adjustments are made. EFFECTIVITY ALL SUBTASK 32-51-00-860-093 (7) Set the rudder trim back to zero (“0") (+/- 1/4°). SUBTASK 32-51-00-860-094 (8) For hydraulic system A, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Power Removal, TASK 29-11-00-860-805. SUBTASK 32-51-00-860-095 WARNING ONLY USE THE CORRECT PIN FOR THE AIRPLANE MODEL. IF YOU USE AN INCORRECT PIN, THE HYDRAULIC STEERING CAN OPERATE. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONNEL AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT. (9) Move the towing lever to the "TOW" position and install the NLG towing lever pin, SPL-1499. SUBTASK 32-51-00-820-032 (10) Make sure that you can install the rig pins from the rigging pin kit, SPL-1585, that follow: (a) Rig pin NS2 in the Captain's control wheel drum. (b) Rig pin NS4 in the summing mechanism bracket at the steering metering valve. (c) Make sure that the rig pins have a free fit. NOTE: The rig pins must have a free fit when you install or remove them. Some resistance is permitted. SUBTASK 32-51-00-000-002 (11) Loosen the jamnuts on the input rod. SUBTASK 32-51-00-820-033 (12) Based on the setting the pilot noted for acceptable centering characteristics, adjust the length of the input rod to correct the steering pulling condition. NOTE: Turning the hexagonal barrel between the rod ends clockwise when facing aft, lengthens the control rod. One complete revolution clockwise changes the steering angle approximately equivalent to one unit of left rudder trim. One complete revolution counterclockwise changes the steering angle approximately equivalent to one unit of right rudder trim. SUBTASK 32-51-00-420-011 (13) Tighten the jamnuts. SUBTASK 32-51-00-860-096 (14) For hydraulic system A, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Pressurization, TASK 29-11-00-860-801. SUBTASK 32-51-00-860-097 (15) Remove the NLG towing lever pin, SPL-1499, from the towing lever. SUBTASK 32-51-00-710-005 (16) Cycle the system to the left and right using the rudder pedals and allow it to return to center from each direction. SUBTASK 32-51-00-200-006 (17) Compare the centering to what was noted earlier in the task when the rudder was cycled around the trim point the pilot had set. SUBTASK 32-51-00-860-098 (18) If satisfactory, do this task to remove hydraulic system A pressure: Hydraulic System A or B Power Removal, TASK 29-11-00-860-805. EFFECTIVITY ALL SUBTASK 32-51-00-420-014 (19) Install the safety wire on the input rod. (a) Make sure that the safety wire tail is on the aft end of the steering valve input rod when installed. SUBTASK 32-51-00-200-005 (20) Make sure that the rig pin NS2 in the Captain's control wheel drum does not bind. NOTE: It is not necessary for rig pin NS4 in the summing mechanism bracket at the steering metering valve to fit freely.

G. Put the Airplane Back to Its Usual Condition

SUBTASK 32-51-00-420-015 (1) If it was disconnected, reconnect the nose gear torsion links at the apex bolt (TASK 32-21-31-400-803).

32-51-00-700-801Nose Wheel Steering System TestPDF p. 1903

8. Nose Wheel Steering System Test (Figure 501, Figure 503)

A. General

(1) This task gives instructions to do the test of the steering system of the nose wheel. (a) There are two methods to perform this task: 1) Method 1: On Ground/Grease Plates 2) Method 2: Airplane on Jacks. (2) The test of the steering system of the nose wheel includes the tests that follow: (a) A steering centering test to make sure that the steering metering valve is in the null position when the nose gear is mechanically centered (b) A normal steering response test (c) A control wheel torque test (d) A test of the nose gear turn radius and response to the full rudder pedal input (e) A tow test of the nose gear steering to make sure that the nose gear will turn freely with the tow lever in the tow position (f) A test of the alternate steering system (g) An air/ground mode test. (3) The steering system of the nose wheel must be adjusted correctly before you do the system test. (4) The rig pins are from the rigging pin kit, SPL-1585.

B. References

F. Prepare to Test the Steering System of the Nose Wheel

SUBTASK 32-51-00-610-002 (1) Do servicing on the hydraulic system before you do the test, do this task: Hydraulic Reservoir Servicing, TASK 12-12-00-610-801. EFFECTIVITY ALL SUBTASK 32-51-00-480-028 WARNING MAKE SURE THAT THE DOWNLOCK PINS ARE INSTALLED IN ALL OF THE LANDING GEAR. WITHOUT THE DOWNLOCK PINS, THE LANDING GEAR CAN RETRACT AND CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT. (2) Make sure that the downlock pins are installed in the nose and main landing gear (PAGEBLOCK 32-00-01/201). SUBTASK 32-51-00-580-013 (3) Do this task: Lift the Airplane Nose with the Nose Jack at Jack Point D, TASK 07-11-21-580-801. SUBTASK 32-51-00-730-057 (4) For Method 2, make sure that the torsion links are connected at apex. NOTE: It is not necessary to connect conduit and clamps at this time if they are already loose or disconnected. SUBTASK 32-51-00-860-101 (5) Do this task: Supply Electrical Power, TASK 24-22-00-860-811. SUBTASK 32-51-00-860-012 (6) For hydraulic system A, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Power Removal, TASK 29-11-00-860-805. SUBTASK 32-51-00-860-013 (7) Make sure that the control lever for the landing gear is in the DN position. SUBTASK 32-51-00-860-014 (8) Make sure that the NOSE WHEEL STEERING ALTERNATE switch is in the NORM position. SUBTASK 32-51-00-860-015 (9) Make sure that these circuit breakers are closed: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-3 Row Col Number Name C 15 C01355 LANDING GEAR AIR/GND SYS 2 C 16 C01356 LANDING GEAR AIR/GND SYS 1 D 17 C01027 LANDING GEAR NOSE GEAR STEER

G. Do the Steering Centering Test

SUBTASK 32-51-00-860-016 (1) Remove the NLG towing lever pin, SPL-1499, from the towing lever and permit the lever to move to the PRESSURE ON position. SUBTASK 32-51-00-860-017 (2) Make sure that the rig pin R3 fits freely in the rudder quadrant. NOTE: This will show that the rudder pedals are in the neutral position. SUBTASK 32-51-00-730-002 (3) Make sure that the steering angle is 0 +/-1.5 degrees on the decal that is on the nose gear shock. NOTE: The inner cylinder centering cam will put the nose wheels in the center position when the airplane is lifted on jacks. Manual assistance could be necessary to make sure that the nose gear and cam is in the center position. EFFECTIVITY ALL (a) If the decal is not on the nose gear shock strut, make a decal with tape (Figure 501). SUBTASK 32-51-00-860-018 WARNING MAKE SURE ALL PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT ARE CLEAR OF THE FLIGHT CONTROLS SURFACES, THE THRUST REVERSERS, AND THE LANDING GEAR. THESE COMPONENTS CAN MOVE SUDDENLY WHEN YOU SUPPLY HYDRAULIC POWER. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT. (4) For hydraulic system A, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Pressurization, TASK 29-11-00-860-801. SUBTASK 32-51-00-730-003 (5) Make sure that the nose gear stays centered. NOTE: If the nose gear moves when the hydraulic system is pressurized, the nose gear steering is not adjusted correctly. There is a disagreement between the steering system and the mechanical centerline position of the nose gear centering cams. SUBTASK 32-51-00-860-079 (6) For hydraulic system A, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Power Removal, TASK 29-11-00-860-805.

H. Do the Test of the Normal Steering Response

SUBTASK 32-51-00-480-012 (1) For method 1, make sure that the greased plates are under the nose wheels. SUBTASK 32-51-00-480-027 (2) For method 1, if necessary, do this task: Lower the Airplane Nose Off of the Jack, TASK 07-11-21-580-802. SUBTASK 32-51-00-860-099 CAUTION MAKE SURE THAT YOU PUT THE TORSION LINK TO KEEP CLEARANCE AT THE GEAR DOORS AND UPPER STEERING SLEEVE. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY, THE TORSION LINK CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE AFT OF THE GEAR DOORS AND THE PRIMARY/SECONDARY AIR/GROUND SENSORS. (3) For method 2, do these steps to disconnect the torsion link apex joint: WARNING ONLY USE THE CORRECT PIN FOR THE AIRPLANE MODEL. IF YOU USE AN INCORRECT PIN, THE HYDRAULIC STEERING CAN OPERATE. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONNEL AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT. (a) Install the NLG towing lever pin, SPL-1499, through the towing lever. NOTE: The NLG towing lever pin, SPL-1499, holds the towing lever in the TOW position. (b) Disconnect the torsion link apex joint, do this task: Nose Landing Gear Torsion Link Disconnection, TASK 32-21-31-000-803 1) Put the airplane in ground mode. 2) To avoid damage during operation, remove the bracket that attaches the conduit to the Nose Landing Gear (NLG) landing/taxi light, and other clamps on torsion links. 3) Secure the torsion link assembly to avoid damage during the operation. (c) Remove the NLG towing lever pin, SPL-1499, from the towing lever. EFFECTIVITY ALL SUBTASK 32-51-00-860-078 WARNING MAKE SURE ALL PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT ARE CLEAR OF THE FLIGHT CONTROLS SURFACES, THE THRUST REVERSERS, AND THE LANDING GEAR. THESE COMPONENTS CAN MOVE SUDDENLY WHEN YOU SUPPLY HYDRAULIC POWER. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT. (4) For hydraulic system A, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Pressurization, TASK 29-11-00-860-801. (a) Make sure that at least one of the main gears is in the ground mode. NOTE: The air/ground system needs two inputs to transition into the ground mode. SUBTASK 32-51-00-730-047 (5) Do the steps that follow to make sure that the captain's control wheel operates correctly: (a) Turn the captain's control wheel to operate the nose wheel steering through at least 6 complete cycles, and make sure that it operates freely and smoothly. NOTE: One cycle of the system is from center to full right, then to full left, then back to center. (b) Make sure that there is no leakage of hydraulic fluid from the nose gear steering tubing and fittings from the landing gear selector valve to the valves on the steering actuators. (c) Turn the nose wheels with the captain's control wheel from the center position to the LEFT (CCW) stop position. 1) Make sure that the steering angle is 78 +/-2 degrees on the decal that is on the nose gear shock strut. (d) Release the captain's control wheel and let it return to the center position. 1) Make sure that the steering angle is at 0 +/-1 degree. (e) Turn the nose wheels with the captain's control wheel from the center position to the RIGHT (CW) stop position. 1) Make sure that the steering angle is 78 +/-2 degrees on the decal that is on the nose gear shock strut. (f) Release the captain's control wheel and let it return to the center position. 1) Make sure that the steering angle is at 0 +/-1 degree.

I. Do the Test for Control Wheel Torque

SUBTASK 32-51-00-010-002 (1) Use the control wheel to turn the nose wheels from the center position to the LEFT (CCW) until the steering angle is 70 +/-7 degrees. NOTE: Secure the torsion link assembly to avoid damage during the operation. (a) Hold this position. SUBTASK 32-51-00-480-007 (2) Install a spring scale at 5.0 in. (127.0 mm) radius on the control wheel. SUBTASK 32-51-00-730-014 (3) Measure the tangential force that is necessary to turn the control wheel to the left (CCW, 78 degrees) and stop just before you touch the control wheel stop. (a) Make sure that the force on the control wheel is between 9 lbf (40.0 N) and 15 lbf (66.7 N). EFFECTIVITY ALL SUBTASK 32-51-00-080-008 (4) Remove the spring scale from the control wheel. SUBTASK 32-51-00-730-035 (5) Use the control wheel to turn the nose wheels from the center position to the RIGHT (CW) until the steering angle is 70 +/-7 degrees. (a) Hold this position. SUBTASK 32-51-00-480-013 (6) Install the spring scale at 5.0 in. (127.0 mm) radius on the control wheel. SUBTASK 32-51-00-730-036 (7) Measure the tangential force that is necessary to turn the control wheel to the right (CW, 78 degrees) and stop just before you touch the control wheel stop. (a) Make sure that the force on the control wheel is between 9 lbf (40.0 N) and 15 lbf (66.7 N). SUBTASK 32-51-00-730-016 (8) Release the control wheel and let it go back to the neutral (center) position. SUBTASK 32-51-00-080-004 (9) Remove the spring scale from the control wheel.

J. Do the Test of Nose Gear Turn Radius and Response to Full Rudder Pedal Input

SUBTASK 32-51-00-480-008 (1) For method 2, make sure that airplane nose gear is in the ground mode. (a) Make sure that at least one of the main gears is in ground mode. NOTE: The air/ground system needs two inputs to transition into the ground mode. Both of the nose gear sensors are in ground mode by installing actuator (target) on ground proximity sensor or holding the upper torsion link in the ground position. SUBTASK 32-51-00-730-060 WARNING BEFORE YOU MOVE THE RUDDER PEDALS, MAKE SURE THE AREA AROUND THE RUDDER IS CLEAR OF ALL PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT. THIS WILL PREVENT INJURY TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT. (2) Push the captain's left rudder pedal fully. (a) Make sure that the steering angle is 7 +/- 1 degrees left turn on the decal that is on the nose gear shock strut. SUBTASK 32-51-00-730-018 (3) Release the rudder pedals. (a) Make sure that the steering angle is at the center, 0 +/- 1 degrees, on the decal that is on the nose gear shock strut. SUBTASK 32-51-00-730-019 WARNING BEFORE YOU MOVE THE RUDDER PEDALS, MAKE SURE THE AREA AROUND THE RUDDER IS CLEAR OF ALL PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT. THIS WILL PREVENT INJURY TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT. (4) Push the captain's right rudder pedal fully. EFFECTIVITY ALL (a) Make sure that the steering angle is 7 +/- 1 degrees right turn on the decal that is on the nose gear shock strut. SUBTASK 32-51-00-730-020 (5) Release the rudder pedals. (a) Make sure that the steering angle is at the center, 0 +/- 1 degrees, on the decal that is on the nose gear shock strut.

K. Do the Nose Gear Steering Tow Test

SUBTASK 32-51-00-860-048 WARNING ONLY USE THE CORRECT PIN FOR THE AIRPLANE MODEL. IF YOU USE AN INCORRECT PIN, THE HYDRAULIC STEERING CAN OPERATE. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONNEL AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT. (1) Move the towing lever to the "TOW" position and install the NLG towing lever pin, SPL-1499. SUBTASK 32-51-00-860-063 (2) For method 1, remove the apex pin from the torsion links. SUBTASK 32-51-00-860-100 (3) Move the steering system manually with the upper torsion link, approximately 10 degrees to the left and right, and then return it to the center position. (a) If necessary, install the extension bar, SPL-7306, on the nose landing gear to rotate the steering system. NOTE: If the towing valve does not remove pressure from the steering valve, you cannot move the steering system manually with the upper torsion link. You must then replace the steering valve. SUBTASK 32-51-00-080-005 WARNING MAKE SURE THAT THE NOSE WHEEL STEERING SYSTEM IS IN THE CENTER POSITION. WHEN HYDRAULIC POWER IS ON AND THE TOWING LEVER LOCKPIN IS REMOVED, THE STEERING COLLAR AND TOP TORSION LINK WILL TURN QUICKLY TO CENTER. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONNEL AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT. (4) If installed, remove the extension bar, SPL-7306, from the NLG. SUBTASK 32-51-00-860-089 (5) For method 1, install the apex pin in the torsion links (TASK 32-21-31-400-803). SUBTASK 32-51-00-080-017 (6) Remove the NLG towing lever pin, SPL-1499, from the towing lever and permit the lever to move to the PRESSURE ON position. SUBTASK 32-51-00-730-022 (7) Make sure that the steering system operates normally with the control wheel.

L. Do the Test of the Alternate Steering System

SUBTASK 32-51-00-860-049 (1) For hydraulic system A, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Power Removal, TASK 29-11-00-860-805. EFFECTIVITY ALL SUBTASK 32-51-00-010-028 (2) To get access to the P92 panel, open this access door: Number Name/Location 117A Electronic Equipment Access Door SUBTASK 32-51-00-860-035 WARNING WHEN YOU OPEN THE P91 AND P92 PANELS, MAKE SURE THAT THE OUTER DOOR STAYS AS OPEN AS POSSIBLE. IF THE OUTER DOOR TURNS IN, THE ATTACHED DOOR COMPONENTS COULD TOUCH THE INNER DOOR COMPONENTS. THIS CAN CAUSE AN ARC CONDITION WHEN YOU SUPPLY POWER. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY, DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT AND INJURY TO PERSONNEL CAN OCCUR. WARNING DO NOT TOUCH THE CONDUCTORS IN THE P91 AND P92 PANELS. BE CAREFUL WHEN YOU GET ACCESS TO THE CIRCUIT BREAKERS ON THE INNER SIDE OF THE P91 AND P92 PANELS (ROW F). IF IT IS POSSIBLE, REMOVE AIRPLANE ELECTRICAL POWER FIRST. THE P91 AND P92 PANELS HAVE HIGH VOLTAGES AND CURRENTS. ELECTRICAL VOLTAGE AND CURRENT CAN KILL YOU OR CAUSE INJURIES. (3) Open this circuit breaker and install safety tag: Power Distribution Panel Number 2, P92 Row Col Number Name F 2 C01449 STANDBY HYDRAULIC PUMP SUBTASK 32-51-00-860-036 (4) Make sure that the hydraulic system B reservoir is full, do this task: Hydraulic Reservoir Servicing, TASK 12-12-00-610-801. SUBTASK 32-51-00-860-037 (5) For hydraulic system B, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Pressurization, TASK 29-11-00-860-801. SUBTASK 32-51-00-860-038 (6) Make sure that these circuit breakers are closed: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-2 Row Col Number Name C 15 C00799 HYD SYS LDG GR SYS XFR VALVE SEC C 16 C00781 HYD SYS LDG GR SYS XFR VALVE PRI SUBTASK 32-51-00-730-024 (7) Put the NOSE WHEEL STEERING ALTERNATE switch, on the captain's P1 panel, to the ALT position. SUBTASK 32-51-00-730-026 (8) Make sure that the steering system operates normally with the control wheel. SUBTASK 32-51-00-730-029 (10) Make sure that the steering system does not operate normally with the control wheel. EFFECTIVITY ALL

M. Do the Test of Air/Ground Mode and Normal Steering Response

SUBTASK 32-51-00-580-017 (1) For method 1, do this task: Lift the Airplane Nose with the Nose Jack at Jack Point D, TASK 07-11-21-580-801. SUBTASK 32-51-00-430-001 (2) For method 2, do these steps to connect the torsion link apex pin: WARNING ONLY USE THE CORRECT PIN FOR THE AIRPLANE MODEL. IF YOU USE AN INCORRECT PIN, THE HYDRAULIC STEERING CAN OPERATE. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONNEL AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT. (a) Install the NLG towing lever pin, SPL-1499, through the towing lever. NOTE: The NLG towing lever pin, SPL-1499, holds the towing lever in the TOW position. (b) Connect the torsion link apex pin, do this task: Nose Landing Gear Torsion Link Connection, TASK 32-21-31-400-803. (c) Remove the NLG towing lever pin, SPL-1499, from the towing lever. SUBTASK 32-51-00-730-050 (3) With the nose gear shock strut fully extended, make sure that the steering rotary actuator is in the air mode as follows: (a) The index marks on the rotary actuator pulley and housing are aligned. (b) The pulley on the rotary actuator is turned fully counter-clockwise. SUBTASK 32-51-00-730-051 (4) With the airplane on jacks, do this task: Lift the Airplane Nose Landing Gear with the Axle Jack at Jack Point E, TASK 07-11-03-580-802. (a) Use the nose gear axle jack to compress the nose gear shock strut 1.90 in. (48.3 mm) to 2.10 in. (53.3 mm) and make sure that the rotary actuator stays in the air mode. NOTE: The dimensions given in this test are all measured from the bottom of the inner diameter of the outer cylinder. NOTE: Nose gear axle jack required only for testing while the airplane is jacked. SUBTASK 32-51-00-730-052 (5) Continue to compress the nose gear shock strut until the rotary actuator changes to the ground mode. SUBTASK 32-51-00-730-053 (6) Extend the nose gear shock strut back to 1.90 in. (48.3 mm) - 2.10 in. (53.3 mm) of compression and make sure that the rotary actuator moves back to the air mode in 8 seconds or less. SUBTASK 32-51-00-430-002 (7) Install bracket and clamps for NLG landing/taxi light conduit. SUBTASK 32-51-00-730-055 (8) Do this task: Lower the Airplane Nose Off of the Jack, TASK 07-11-21-580-802. SUBTASK 32-51-00-730-056 (9) Make sure that the rotary actuator changes to the ground mode. EFFECTIVITY ALL

(6) Remove the safety tag and close this circuit breaker: Power Distribution Panel Number 2, P92 Row Col Number Name F 2 C01449 STANDBY HYDRAULIC PUMP EFFECTIVITY ALL SUBTASK 32-51-00-410-026 (7) Close this access panel: Number Name/Location 117A Electronic Equipment Access Door SUBTASK 32-51-00-580-007 (8) For method 1, do this task: Lift the Airplane Nose with the Nose Jack at Jack Point D, TASK 07-11-21-580-801. F. Clean the Towing Lever Assembly

SUBTASK 32-51-11-100-001 CAUTION DO NOT TRY TO DISASSEMBLE THE TOWING LEVER PLUNGER TO CLEAN IT. DAMAGE TO INTERNAL COMPONENTS WILL OCCUR. (1) Use a clean cloth, moistened in alcohol, B00130, to clean the towing lever [1], crank [2], and plunger [3] to remove dirt, grease, and grime. NOTE: Isopropyl alcohol is the most effective cleaner that will not damage the valve seals and finishes. (a) If it is necessary, disassemble the crank [2] and towing lever [1] as follows: 1) Remove the cotter pin [7], nut [6], washers [5], and bolt [4] from the crank [2]. a) Discard the cotter pin [7]. 2) Remove the towing lever [1]. 3) Remove the crank [2] and washer [8] from the valve housing. 4) Clean the bushings in the valve housing and area in between them. 5) Install the crank [2] into the valve housing. 6) Install the washer [8] and towing lever [1] onto the crank [2] splines. a) Orient splines so that the bolt [4] can be installed through the hole in the towing lever [1]. b) Use a rig pin, from the rigging pin kit, SPL-1585, to line up the holes in the manifold and crank [2]. 7) Install the bolt [4] with washer [5] under head through the towing lever [1] and crank [2]. NOTE: Installation direction of the bolt is optional. 8) Install the washer [5] and nut [6]. a) Install a rig pin, from the rigging pin kit, SPL-1585, to hold the towing lever [1] in place. 9) Tighten the nut [6] to 40 in-lb (4.5 N·m) - 45 in-lb (5.1 N·m), as required, to line up the slot in the nut [6] with the hole in the bolt [4]. 10) Install the new cotter pin [7]. SUBTASK 32-51-11-212-001 (2) Check the operation of the towing lever [1] and plunger [3]. NOTE: Lubrication of the towing lever or plunger is not recommended as this will attract dirt and grime. (a) Make sure that the towing lever [1] and plunger [3] return to the normal position when released. (b) Make sure that there is no external leakage or evidence of instability, sticking or binding of the towing lever [1].

F. Steering Metering Valve Removal

SUBTASK 32-51-11-010-001 (1) Remove the screws [4] and washers [5] that hold the summing mechanism cover [10] to the summing mechanism bracket. EFFECTIVITY ALL SUBTASK 32-51-11-010-002 (2) Remove the screws [9] and washers [5] that hold the support bracket to the valve assembly [7]. SUBTASK 32-51-11-020-002 (3) Loosen the cable NWS-A [1], cable NWS-B [2], and cable NWS-A/B [8] at the turnbuckles [3]. SUBTASK 32-51-11-020-003 (4) Remove the nut [23], washer [5], bushing [24], and bolt [25] to disconnect the link assembly [6] from the input lever on the valve assembly [7]. SUBTASK 32-51-11-020-004 (5) Disconnect the hydraulic lines [11] from the valve assembly [7]. SUBTASK 32-51-11-480-003 (6) Install caps in the hydraulic lines [11] and plugs in the ports on the valve assembly [7]. SUBTASK 32-51-11-020-010 (7) Remove the lockwire from the bolts [20]. SUBTASK 32-51-11-020-005 (8) Remove the bolts [20] and washers [18] that hold the valve assembly [7] to the top and bottom support plates. SUBTASK 32-51-11-020-006 (9) Remove the nuts [14], washers [15], washers [18], and bolts [19] that hold the valve assembly [7] to the top support plate. SUBTASK 32-51-11-020-007 CAUTION THE STEERING METERING VALVE IS TOP HEAVY. THE VALVE WILL FLIP OUT OF YOUR HOLD. BE CAREFUL NOT TO DROP AND DAMAGE THE STEERING METERING VALVE. (10) Remove the nuts [16], bolts [22], washers [21], and clamps [17] that attach the swivel valves to the steering actuator trunnions and carefully remove the valve assembly [7]. (a) Make sure that the area around and in the trunnions is clean before the hydraulic ports are open. NOTE: This is to prevent contamination. The hydraulic ports will be open when you remove the swivel valves from the actuator trunnions. (b) Install lockwire in the top of the swivel valves to keep them in the valve assembly [7]. CAUTION DO NOT REMOVE THE SWIVEL VALVES FROM THE STEERING METERING VALVE. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY, DAMAGE TO THE MATING SURFACES OF THE SWIVEL VALVES AND THE STEERING METERING VALVE CAN OCCUR. 1) Do not remove the swivel valves from the valve assembly [7]. SUBTASK 32-51-11-480-004 (11) Install caps in the open hydraulic ports for the swivel valves (that are part of the valve assembly [7]) and actuator trunnions. SUBTASK 32-51-11-020-008 (12) Remove the unions [12] and packings [13] from the valve assembly [7]. EFFECTIVITY ALL SUBTASK 32-51-11-480-005 (13) Install plugs in the ports.

G. Steering Metering Valve Installation

SUBTASK 32-51-11-600-001 CAUTION THE STEERING METERING VALVE IS TOP HEAVY. THE VALVE WILL FLIP OUT OF YOUR HOLD. BE CAREFUL NOT TO DROP AND DAMAGE THE STEERING METERING VALVE. (1) Do these steps to prepare the valve assembly [7] for installation: (a) Lubricate the new packings [13] and unions [12] with hydraulic fluid, D00153. (b) Install the packings [13] and unions [12] in the valve assembly [7]. (c) Apply hydraulic fluid, D00153, to the transfer tubes in the actuator trunnions. (d) Install the new O-rings [28] and new packing [27] on both of the ferrule [26] between the valve assembly [7] and steering cylinders. SUBTASK 32-51-11-620-001 WARNING USE NITRILE GLOVES FOR SKIN PROTECTION WHEN YOU USE COR-BAN 27L. IF IT GETS ON YOUR SKIN, IMMEDIATELY REMOVE IT WITH WATER. IF THIS MATERIAL GETS IN YOUR EYES, IMMEDIATELY FLUSH YOUR EYES WITH WATER. GET MEDICAL AID. THIS MATERIAL CONTAINS FLAMMABLE AGENTS WHICH CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONNEL. CAUTION DO NOT APPLY CORROSION-INHIBITING COMPOUND ON GREASE JOINTS, OR SEALED BEARINGS. THESE COMPOUNDS REMOVE GREASE AND OTHER LUBRICANTS. THEY ARE PENETRATING COMPOUNDS. THEY WILL MOVE AROUND THE SEALS AND INTO THE BEARINGS. THIS WILL CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE BEARINGS, AND JOINTS. (2) Apply corrosion preventive Cor-Ban 27L Compound, G50237 (preferred), or corrosion inhibiting material, G50136 (alternate), to the faying surfaces of all four mounting feet on the valve assembly [7]. SUBTASK 32-51-11-620-002 (3) Apply a thin layer of the corrosion preventive Cor-Ban 27L Compound, G50237 (preferred), or corrosion inhibiting material, G50136 (alternate), to these items: (a) The shank of the bolts [19] (b) The shank, threads, and thread reliefs of the bolts [20] (c) The threads of the nuts [14] (d) The splines and faces of the washers [15] and washers [18]. (e) The threads of the bolts [22]. EFFECTIVITY ALL SUBTASK 32-51-11-020-009 CAUTION MAKE SURE THAT THE OFFSET HOLE PATTERN IN THE SWIVEL VALVES FOR THE VALVE ASSEMBLY ARE CORRECTLY ALIGNED WITH THE MATING HOLE PATTERN IN THE ACTUATOR TRUNNION. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY, IT IS POSSIBLE THAT THE STEERING SYSTEM WILL NOT OPERATE CORRECTLY AND YOU CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE STEERING SYSTEM. (4) Put the swivel valves for the valve assembly [7] into the steering actuator trunnions and make sure the offset hole pattern in the swivel valves is aligned with the mating hole pattern in the left and right trunnions. SUBTASK 32-51-11-420-002 (5) Install the clamps [17], washers [21], bolts [22], and nuts [16] to attach the valve assembly [7] to the actuator trunnions. (a) If it is installed, remove the lockwire from the swivel valves. (b) Tighten the bolts [22] to 20 in-lb (2.3 N·m) - 25 in-lb (2.8 N·m). SUBTASK 32-51-11-420-003 (6) Install the bolts [19], washers [15], washers [18], and nuts [14] to attach the valve assembly [7] to the top support plate. SUBTASK 32-51-11-420-004 (7) Install the bolts [20] and washers [18] to attach the valve assembly [7] to the top and bottom support plates. SUBTASK 32-51-11-420-025 (8) Install MS20995NC20 lockwire, G02166, on the bolts [20] (TASK 20-10-44-400-801). SUBTASK 32-51-11-420-010 (9) Install the screws [9] and washers [5] that hold the support bracket to the valve assembly [7]. SUBTASK 32-51-11-480-006 (10) Make sure that these rig pins from the rigging pin kit, SPL-1585, set are installed: (a) Rig pin 2 in the steering tiller for the nose wheel (b) Rig pin NS1 in the rudder pedal interconnect quadrant (c) Rig pin 4 in the summing mechanism. SUBTASK 32-51-11-420-005 (11) Install the bushing [24], bolt [25], washer [5], and nut [23] to attach the link assembly [6] to the input lever on the valve assembly [7]. (a) Adjust the link assembly [6] until you can easily install bolt [25]. (b) Remove the rig pin 4 from the summing mechanism. SUBTASK 32-51-11-080-001 (12) Remove the caps from the hydraulic lines [11] and ports on the valve assembly [7]. SUBTASK 32-51-11-420-006 (13) Connect the hydraulic lines [11] to the valve assembly [7]. SUBTASK 32-51-11-420-023 (14) Tighten the B-nuts on the hydraulic lines [11] to 270 ±14 in-lb (31 ±2 N·m). EFFECTIVITY ALL SUBTASK 32-51-11-420-007 (15) Tighten the cable NWS-A [1], cable NWS-B [2], and cable NWS-A/B [8] at the turnbuckles [3] and adjust the tension. NOTE: This task will make you perform the required system test. Look for hydraulic leaks when you do this. (a) Tighten the cables and adjust the tension, do this task: Nose Wheel Steering System Adjustment, TASK 32-51-00-820-802. SUBTASK 32-51-11-080-002 (16) Remove these rig pins: (a) Rig pin 2 in the steering tiller for the nose wheel (b) Rig pin NS 1 in the rudder pedal interconnect quadrant. SUBTASK 32-51-11-410-001 (17) Close these access panels: (Nose Wheel Well Access Panels - Installation, TASK 53-14-01-420-801) Number Name/Location 113AC Fwd Nose Wheel Well Upper Access Panel 113AW Forward Nose Wheel Well Panel SUBTASK 32-51-11-420-011 (18) Do a test on the steering system of the nose wheel, do the following steps from this task: Nose Wheel Steering System Test, TASK 32-51-00-700-801: • General • Prepare the Airplane for Testing • Do the Test of the Normal Steering Response • Do the Test for the Control Wheel Torque • Do the Test of Nose Gear Turn Radius and Response to Full Rudder Pedal Input • Do the Nose Gear Steering Tow Test • Put the Airplane in its Usual Condition. (a) Make sure that there is no leakage. SUBTASK 32-51-11-420-008 (19) Put the summing mechanism cover [10] in position and install the screws [4] and washers [5].

E. Steering Metering Valve Removal

SUBTASK 32-51-11-010-004 (1) Remove the screws [4] and washers [5] that hold the summing mechanism cover [10] to the summing mechanism bracket. SUBTASK 32-51-11-010-005 (2) Remove the screws [9] and washers [5] that hold the support bracket to the valve assembly [7]. SUBTASK 32-51-11-020-013 (3) Use the cable clamp, SPL-13966, to remove the tension in steering cables NWS-A and NWS-B between the trunnion and the link assembly (Figure 403). NOTE: You may need to remove one of the slider bolts in order to install the base plate over the cables. (a) Position the base plate against the trunnion, with steering cables positioned in the base plate grooves. NOTE: Use the Lock-Trunnion Nut to align the base plate into position. (b) Tighten the clamp bolts evenly to 70 in-lb (8 N·m) - 80 in-lb (9 N·m) onto the clamp plate. (c) Turn only the tension bolt until the clamp carrier contacts the head of the slider bolts. 1) Make sure that you do not exceed a maximum of 0.10 in. (0.25 cm) of cable stretch. SUBTASK 32-51-11-020-014 (4) Remove the pulleys [30] to loosen cable assembly [29]. (a) Remove the nuts [34], washers [33], washers [35], bolts [32], cable guards [31], and pulleys [30] from their brackets. SUBTASK 32-51-11-020-015 (5) Remove the nut [23], washer [5], bushing [24], and bolt [25] to disconnect the link assembly [6] from the input lever on the valve assembly [7]. SUBTASK 32-51-11-020-016 (6) Disconnect the hydraulic lines [11] from the valve assembly [7]. SUBTASK 32-51-11-480-011 (7) Install caps in the hydraulic lines [11] and plugs in the ports on the valve assembly [7]. SUBTASK 32-51-11-020-017 (8) Remove the lockwire from the bolts [20]. SUBTASK 32-51-11-020-018 (9) Remove the bolts [20] and washers [18] that hold the valve assembly [7] to the top and bottom support plates. EFFECTIVITY ALL SUBTASK 32-51-11-020-019 (10) Remove the nuts [14], washers [15], washers [18], and bolts [19] that hold the valve assembly [7] to the top support plate. SUBTASK 32-51-11-020-020 CAUTION THE STEERING METERING VALVE IS TOP HEAVY. THE VALVE WILL FLIP OUT OF YOUR HOLD. BE CAREFUL NOT TO DROP AND DAMAGE THE STEERING METERING VALVE. (11) Remove the nuts [16], bolts [22], washers [21], and clamps [17] that attach the swivel valves to the steering actuator trunnions and carefully remove the valve assembly [7]. (a) Make sure that the area around and in the trunnions is clean before the hydraulic ports are open. NOTE: This is to prevent contamination. The hydraulic ports will be open when you remove the swivel valves from the actuator trunnions. (b) Install lockwire in the top of the swivel valves to keep them in the valve assembly [7]. CAUTION DO NOT REMOVE THE SWIVEL VALVES FROM THE STEERING METERING VALVE. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY, DAMAGE TO THE MATING SURFACES OF THE SWIVEL VALVES AND THE STEERING METERING VALVE CAN OCCUR. 1) Do not remove the swivel valves from the valve assembly [7]. SUBTASK 32-51-11-480-012 (12) Install caps in the open hydraulic ports for the swivel valves (that are part of the valve assembly [7]) and actuator trunnions. SUBTASK 32-51-11-020-021 (13) Remove the unions [12] and packings [13] from the valve assembly [7]. SUBTASK 32-51-11-480-013 (14) Install plugs in the ports.

F. Steering Metering Valve Installation

SUBTASK 32-51-11-600-002 (1) Do these steps to prepare the valve assembly [7] for installation: EFFECTIVITY ALL (a) Lubricate the new packings [13] and unions [12] with hydraulic fluid, D00153. (b) Install the packings [13] and unions [12] in the valve assembly [7]. (c) Apply hydraulic fluid, D00153, to the transfer tubes in the actuator trunnions. (d) Install the new O-rings [28] and new packing [27] on both of the ferrule [26] between the valve assembly [7] and steering cylinders. SUBTASK 32-51-11-620-003 WARNING USE NITRILE GLOVES FOR SKIN PROTECTION WHEN YOU USE COR-BAN 27L. IF IT GETS ON YOUR SKIN, IMMEDIATELY REMOVE IT WITH WATER. IF THIS MATERIAL GETS IN YOUR EYES, IMMEDIATELY FLUSH YOUR EYES WITH WATER. GET MEDICAL AID. THIS MATERIAL CONTAINS FLAMMABLE AGENTS WHICH CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONNEL. CAUTION DO NOT APPLY CORROSION-INHIBITING COMPOUND ON GREASE JOINTS, OR SEALED BEARINGS. THESE COMPOUNDS REMOVE GREASE AND OTHER LUBRICANTS. THEY ARE PENETRATING COMPOUNDS. THEY WILL MOVE AROUND THE SEALS AND INTO THE BEARINGS. THIS WILL CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE BEARINGS, AND JOINTS. (2) Apply corrosion preventive Cor-Ban 27L Compound, G50237 (preferred), or corrosion inhibiting material, G50136 (alternate), to the faying surfaces of all four mounting feet on the valve assembly [7]. SUBTASK 32-51-11-620-004 (3) Apply a thin layer of the corrosion preventive Cor-Ban 27L Compound, G50237 (preferred), or corrosion inhibiting material, G50136 (alternate), to these items: (a) The shank of the bolts [19] (b) The shank, threads, and thread reliefs of the bolts [20] (c) The threads of the nuts [14] (d) The splines and faces of the washers [15] and washers [18]. (e) The threads of the bolts [22]. SUBTASK 32-51-11-020-022 CAUTION CORRECTLY ALIGN THE INDEX PINS ON THE SWIVEL VALVES WITH THE MATING HOLES IN THE ACTUATOR TRUNNION. IF YOU DO NOT, YOU CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE STEERING SYSTEM. (4) Put the swivel valves for the valve assembly [7] into the steering actuator trunnions and make sure that the offset hole pattern in the swivel valves is aligned with the mating hole pattern in the left and right trunnions. SUBTASK 32-51-11-420-014 (5) Install the clamps [17], washers [21], bolts [22], and nuts [16] to attach the valve assembly [7] to the actuator trunnions. (a) If it is installed, remove the lockwire from the swivel valves. (b) Tighten the bolts [22] to 20 in-lb (2.3 N·m) - 25 in-lb (2.8 N·m). SUBTASK 32-51-11-420-015 (6) Install the bolts [19], washers [15], washers [18], and nuts [14] to attach the valve assembly [7] to the top support plate. EFFECTIVITY ALL SUBTASK 32-51-11-420-016 (7) Install the bolts [20] and washers [18] to attach the valve assembly [7] to the top and bottom support plates. SUBTASK 32-51-11-420-026 (8) Install MS20995NC20 lockwire, G02166, on the bolts [20] (TASK 20-10-44-400-801). SUBTASK 32-51-11-420-017 (9) Install the screws [9] and washers [5] that hold the support bracket to the valve assembly [7]. SUBTASK 32-51-11-480-014 (10) Make sure that this rig pin from the rigging pin kit, SPL-1585, set is installed: (a) Rig pin 4 in the summing mechanism. SUBTASK 32-51-11-420-018 (11) Install the bushing [24], bolt [25], washer [5], and nut [23] to attach the link assembly [6] to the input lever on the valve assembly [7]. (a) Adjust thelink assembly [6] until you can easily install bolt [25]. (b) Remove the rig pin 4 from the summing mechanism. SUBTASK 32-51-11-080-003 (12) Remove the caps from the hydraulic lines [11] and the ports on the valve assembly [7]. SUBTASK 32-51-11-420-019 (13) Connect the hydraulic lines [11] to the valve assembly [7]. SUBTASK 32-51-11-420-024 (14) Tighten the B-nuts on the hydraulic lines [11] to 270 ±14 in-lb (31 ±2 N·m). SUBTASK 32-51-11-420-020 (15) Install the pulleys [30]. (a) Put the cable assembly [29] in the groove of the pulleys [30]. (b) Install the pulleys [30], cable guards [31], bolts [32], washers [33], washers [35], and nuts [34] on their brackets on the top of the outer cylinder. SUBTASK 32-51-11-080-004 (16) Remove the cable clamp, SPL-13966. SUBTASK 32-51-11-420-021 (17) Do a test on the steering system of the nose wheel, do the following steps from this task: Nose Wheel Steering System Test, TASK 32-51-00-700-801: • General • Prepare the Airplane for Testing • Do the Test of the Normal Steering Response • Do the Test for the Control Wheel Torque • Do the Test of Nose Gear Turn Radius and Response to Full Rudder Pedal Input • Do the Nose Gear Steering Tow Test • Put the Airplane in its Usual Condition. (a) Make sure that there is no leakage. SUBTASK 32-51-11-420-022 (18) Put the summing mechanism cover [10] in position and install the screws [4] and washers [5].

NOTE: The nose of the airplane is lifted with jacks to find the center position of the nose landing gear and steering collar. This will help correctly install the cables for the nose gear steering system. The internal centering cam of the shock strut is used to find the center position of the nose landing gear and steering collar. If the jacks are not available you can use grease plates under the nose wheels to put the nose gear and steering collar in the center position. NOTE: As an optional procedure, to put the nose landing gear and steering collar in the center position without jacks, tow the airplane a minimum of 12 ft (4 m) in a straight line before it is parked.
